An abnormality of the intestinal rotation and fixation that normally occurs during the development of the gut. This can lead to volvulus, or twisting of the intestine that causes obstruction and necrosis.
Greater than normal amounts of fat in the feces. This is a result of malabsorption of lipids in the small intestine and results in frothy foul-smelling fecal matter that floats.

A disorder of esophageal motility characterized by the inability of the lower esophageal sphincter to relax during swallowing and by inadequate or lacking peristalsis in the lower half of the body of the esophagus.
Paroxysmal, recurrent episodes of vomiting.
The passage of fresh (red) blood per anus, usually in or with stools. Most rectal bleeding comes from the colon, rectum, or anus.
An intermittent form of abdominal pain.
An abnormal connection (fistula) between the esophagus and the trachea.
lay_en: Abnormal connection between trachea and esophagus

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the intestine in which part of the intestine invaginates (telescopes) into another part of the intestine.
An abnormality of the stomach.
Decreased strength of the muscle layer of stomach, which leads to a decreased ability to empty the contents of the stomach despite the absence of obstruction.
Abnormal intestinal contractions, such as spasms and intestinal paralysis, related to the loss of the ability of the gut to coordinate muscular activity because of endogenous or exogenous causes.
Abnormal twisting of a portion of intestine around itself or around a stalk of mesentery tissue.

Atrophic gastritis (AG) is a histopathological entity that is characterized by chronic inflammation of the gastric mucosa with loss of gastric glandular cells and replacement by intestinal-type epithelium, pyloric-type glands, and fibrous tissue.

Colitis refers to an inflammation of the colon and is often used to describe an inflammation of the large intestine (colon, cecum and rectum). Colitides may be acute and self-limited or chronic, and broadly fit into the category of digestive diseases.
Bleeding from the intestines.
An abnormality of the peritoneum.
Inflammation of the peritoneum.
Vomiting that ejects the gastric contents with great force.
An erosion of the mucous membrane in a portion of the duodenum.
A neurological anomaly with gross overeating associated with an abnormally strong desire or need to eat.
An ulcer, that is, an erosion of an area of the gastric mucous membrane.
Angiectasia of lymph vessels (i.e., dilatation of lymphatic vessels) in the intestines.
Hypoplasia of the pancreas.
Acute obstruction of the intestines preventing passage of the contents of the intestines.
An abnormality of the vasculature.
A head tremor of moderate speed (3 to 4 Hz) in the anterior-posterior direction.
Reduced intensity of muscle tendon reflexes in the lower limbs. Reflexes are elicited by stretching the tendon of a muscle, e.g., by tapping.

terms.en: Paresis of extensor muscles of the big toe

terms.def_en: Telangiectasia affecting the gastrointestinal tract.
lay_en: Small, enlarged blood vessels near skin

terms.def_en: The presence of cell death (necrosis) affecting the liver.
Involuntary fecal soiling in adults and children who have usually already been toilet trained.

Celiac disease (CD) is an autoimmune condition affecting the small intestine, triggered by the ingestion of gluten, the protein fraction of wheat, barley, and rye. Clinical manifestations of CD are highly variable and include both gastrointestinal and non-gastrointestinal features. The hallmark of CD is an immune-mediated enteropathy. This term is included because the occurrence of CD is seen as a feature of a number of other diseases.
The presence of fibrosis of that part of the liver with congenital onset.
lay_en: Excessive buildup of connective tissue and scarring of liver at birth

terms.def_en: Progressive destruction of the small-to-medium bile ducts of the intrahepatic biliary tree, which leads to progressive cholestasis and often end-stage liver disease.
A type of hepatic necrosis that is concentrated around the necrosis of hepatocytes localized around the intrahepatic branch of portal vein.
Low Blood Pressure, vascular hypotension.
An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the aortic root.
lay_en: Bulge in wall of root of large artery that carries blood away from heart

terms.def_en: An abnormal increase in the diameter of an artery or vein, either as a diffuse dilatation or as a localized, sac-like outpouching of the vessel wall (aneurysm).
lay_en: Wider than typical opening or gap

terms.def_en: Enlarged and tortuous veins.

A condition characterized by patchy atheromas or atherosclerotic plaques which develop in the walls of medium-sized and large arteries and can lead to arterial stenosis with reduced or blocked blood flow.

An overriding aorta is a congenital heart defect where the aorta is positioned directly over a ventricular septal defect, instead of over the left ventricle. The result is that the aorta receives some blood from the right ventricle, which reduces the amount of oxygen in the blood. It is one of the four conditions of the Tetralogy of Fallot. The aortic root can be displaced toward the front (anteriorly) or directly above the septal defect, but it is always abnormally located to the right of the root of the pulmonary artery. The degree of override is quite variable, with 5-95% of the valve being connected to the right ventricle.
An anomaly of vein.
Formation of a blot clot in a deep vein. The clot often blocks blood flow, causing swelling and pain. The deep veins of the leg are most often affected.
lay_en: Blood clot in a deep vein

terms.en: Venous varicosities of celiac and mesenteric vessels
terms.def_en: Elongated and tortuous mesenteric veins, which comprise the inferior mesenteric vein and the superior mesenteric vein.
syn_en: Venous varicosities of coeliac and mesenteric vessels

terms.en: Right aortic arch with mirror image branching
terms.def_en: The aortic arch crosses the right mainstem bronchus and not the left mainstem bronchus, but does not result in the creation of a vascular ring. The first branch is the left brachiocephalic artery which divides into the left carotid artery and left subclavian artery, the second branch is the right carotid artery, the third branch is the right subclavian artery.
An anomalous configuration of blood vessels that shunts arterial blood directly into veins without passing through the capillaries and that is located in the gastrointestinal tract.
Abnormality of the absorption of fat from the gastrointestinal tract.
Inflammation of blood vessel.
Sclerosis (hardening) of the arteries with increased thickness of the wall of arteries as well as increased stiffness and a loss of elasticity.

In type IV atherosclerotic lesions a dense accumulation of extracellular lipid occupies an extensive but well-defined region of the intima. This type of extracellular lipid accumulation is known as the lipid core. A fibrous tissue increase is not a feature, and complications such as defects of the lesion surface and thrombosis are not present. The type IV lesion is also known as atheroma. Type IV is the first lesion considered advanced in this classification because of the severe intimal disorganization caused by the lipid core. The characteristic core appears to develop from an increase and the consequent confluence of the small isolated pools of extracellular lipid that characterize type III lesions. The increase in lipid is believed to result from continued insudation from the plasma. Type IV lesions, when they first appear in younger people, are found in the same locations as adaptive intimal thickenings of the eccentric type. Thus, atheroma is, at least initially, an eccentric lesion.
Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation in an artery that originates from the abdominal aorta.
Restriction of arterial blood supply to the brain associated with insufficient oxygenation to support the metabolic requirements of the tissue.
lay_en: Disruption of blood oxygen supply to brain

terms.def_en: Inflammation of a superficial vein associated with venous thrombosis (blood clot formation within the vein).

Budd-Chiari syndrome (BCS) is caused by obstruction of hepatic venous outflow at any level from the small hepatic veins to the junction of the inferior vena cava (IVC) with the right atrium, 1 and occurs in 1/100,000 of the general population worldwide. The most common presentation is with ascites, but can range from fulminant hepatic failure (FHF) to asymptomatic forms. Obstruction of hepatic venous outflow is mainly caused by primary intravascular thrombosis, which can occur suddenly or be repeated over time, accompanied by some revascularization, accounting for the variable parenchymal hepatic damage and histologic presentation. Budd-Chiari syndrome is thus a disease, but since it occurs as a manifestation of several other diseases, this term is kept for the present for convenience.
A type of hypertension associated with pheochromocytoma.

terms.en: Arteriovenous fistulas of celiac and mesenteric vessels
syn_en: Arteriovenous fistulas of coeliac and mesenteric vessels

terms.def_en: Respiratory difficulty as newborn.
An abnormality of the bony pelvic girdle, which is a ring of bones connecting the vertebral column to the femurs.
lay_en: Abnormal shape of pelvic girdle bone
syn_en: Abnormality of pelvic girdle bone morphology

terms.def_en: The presence of extra bones within a cranial suture. Wormian bones are irregular isolated bones which appear in addition to the usual centers of ossification of the cranium.
syn_en: Islands of bone within cranial sutures

terms.def_en: Aortic dissection refers to a tear in the intimal layer of the aorta causing a separation between the intima and the medial layers of the aorta.
lay_en: Tear in inner wall of large artery that carries blood away from heart

terms.def_en: The presence of an abnormal lateral curvature of the spine.
A general term describing features characterized by abnormal development of bones and connective tissues.
An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to bone.
A disorder of bone growth affecting the vertebrae and the ends of the long bones (epiphyses).

lay_en: Abnormal development of end part of bone
Abnormal development of the ends of long bones in arms and legs

terms.def_en: An abnormally increased tendency to fractures of bones caused by an abnormal reduction in bone strength that is generally associated with an increased risk of fracture.
An increased tendency to fractures following trauma, with fractures occurring without pain.

lay_en: Delayed maturation of end part of long bone

terms.def_en: An organ or organ-system abnormality that consists of uncontrolled autonomous cell-proliferation which can occur in any part of the body as a benign or malignant neoplasm (tumor).
A cancer originating in lymphocytes and presenting as a solid tumor of lymhpoid cells.

Pheochromocytomas (also known as chromaffin tumors) produce, store, and secrete catecholamines. Pheochromocytomas usually originate from the adrenal medulla but may also develop from chromaffin cells in or about sympathetic ganglia. A common symptom of pheochromocytoma is hypertension owing to release of catecholamines.
The presence of a nephroblastoma, which is a neoplasm of the kidney that primarily affects children.

A carotid body tumor (also called paraganglionoma or chemodectoma) is a tumor found in the upper neck at the branching of the carotid artery. They arise from the chemoreceptor organ (paraganglion) located in the adventitia of the carotid artery bifurcation.

A malignant bone tumor that usually develops during adolescence and usually affects the long bones including the tibia, femur, and humerus. The typical symptoms of osteosarcoma comprise bone pain, fracture, limitation of motion, and tenderness or swelling at the site of the tumor.
The presence of a basal cell carcinoma of the skin.

Coxa valga is a deformity of the hip in which the angle between the femoral shaft and the femoral neck is increased compared to age-adjusted values (about 150 degrees in newborns gradually reducing to 120-130 degrees in adults).
Trilobar skull configuration when viewed from the front or behind.
An abnormal narrowing of the foramen magnum.
Abnormality of the sella turcica, a saddle-shaped depression in the sphenoid bone at the base of the human skull.

terms.it: Sella turcica a forma di J
terms.def_en: A deformity of the sella turcica whereby the sella extends further anterior than normal such that the anterior clinoid process appears to overhang it, giving the appearance of the letter J on imaging of the skull.
Increased width of the skull.

Abnormality of the morphology (structure) of the calvaria (skullcap), that is, of that part of the skull that is made up of the superior portions of the frontal bone, occipital bone, and parietal bones and covers the cranial cavity that contains the brain.
syn_en: Abnormality of the shape of calvarium

terms.def_en: The presence of an abnormally thick calvaria.
An abnormality of the frontal sinus, one of the mucosa-lined, normally air-filled paranasal sinuses of the bones of the skull. The frontal sinus is located within the frontal bone.
Aplasia of frontal sinus.
Aplasia of the paranasal sinuses.
An abnormal enlargement of the sella turcica.

A developmental malformation of the occipital bone and upper end of the cervical spine, in which the latter appears to have pushed the floor of the occipital bone upward such that there is an abnormal flattening of the skull base.
syn_en: Increased basal angle of skull base
Obtuse basal angle of skull base

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the base of the skull, which forms the floor of the cranial cavity and separates the brain from other facial structures. The skull base is made up of five bones: the ethmoid, sphenoid, occipital, paired frontal, and paired parietal bones, and is subdivided into 3 regions: the anterior, middle, and posterior cranial fossae. The petro-occipital fissure subdivides the middle cranial fossa into 1 central component and 2 lateral components.
Increased bone density of the skull base without significant changes in bony contour.
Any abnormality of the parietal bone of the skull.
syn_en: Abnormality of the parietal bone of skull

terms.def_en: The presence of symmetrical and circular openings (foramina) in the parietal bone ranging in size from a few millimeters to several centimeters wide.
syn_en: Persistent foramina of the parietal bones
Symmetrical, oval defects in the parietal bone

terms.def_en: Any abnormality of the foramen magnum.
An abnormal increase in the size of the foramen magnum.
An abnormality of the process of ossification of the skull.
lay_en: Abnormality of bone formation of cranium

terms.def_en: The presence of a high and narrow palate.
lay_en: Narrow, highly arched roof of mouth

terms.def_en: The presence of small (ca. 0.5-1.0 mm) dilated blood vessels near the surface of the mucous membranes of the palate.
lay_en: Telangiectasia of the roof of the mouth
Spider veins of the roof of the mouth

terms.def_en: Unusual prominence of the median palatal raphe, which is the ridge formed by the fusion of the two plates of the skull that form the hard palate.
lay_en: Prominent central ridge on roof of the mouth

terms.def_en: A depression located at an oral commissure.
lay_en: Lip pits at corners of the mouth
Pits at the corners of the lips

terms.def_en: Increased depth of the median tongue furrow.
A morphological abnormality of the mouth in which the angle of the mouth is downturned. The oral commissures are positioned inferior to the midline labial fissure.
An abnormality of the immune system.
Enlargement (swelling) of a lymph node.
Increased susceptibility to bacterial infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of bacterial infection.
Increased susceptibility to infections as manifested by repeated bouts of infection.

terms.it: Diminuzione del livello di IgA circolanti
terms.def_en: Decreased levels of immunoglobulin A (IgA).
Failure of the immune system to protect the body adequately from infection, due to the absence or insufficiency of some component process or substance.
An increased susceptibility to abscess formation, as manifested by a medical history of recurrent abscesses.

terms.en: Absence of bactericidal oxidative respiratory burst in phagocytes
terms.def_en: An absence of the phase of elevated metabolic activity, during which oxygen consumption increases, that occurs in neutrophils, monocytes, and macrophages shortly after phagocytosing material. An enhanced uptake of oxygen leads to the production, by an NADH dependent system, of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals, which play a part in microbiocidal activity.
Increased susceptibility to Aspergillus infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Aspergillus infection.
A chronic, relapsing, inflammatory, and often febrile multisystemic disorder of connective tissue, characterized principally by involvement of the skin, joints, kidneys, and serosal membranes.
Increased susceptibility to Staphylococcus aureus infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Staphylococcus aureus infection.
Recurrent or persistent superficial Candida infections of the skin, mucous membranes, and nails.
syn_en: Chronic candidiasis of mucosa, skin and nails

terms.def_en: Lymphadenopathy (enlargement of lymph nodes) owing to hyperplasia of follicular (germinal) centers.
A chronic form of lymphadenopathy that is not related to infection.

Abnormal decrease of apoptosis by peripheral blood T cells in an in vitro culture, compared to a healthy control sample. May be either spontaneous, induced by UV, X-ray, FasL or other agens. Commonly measured by surface expression of phosphatidyl serine labelled by Annexin V, but other methods such as staning of cleaved Caspases may be used by different laboratories.
Underdevelopment of the lymph nodes.
A structural lymph node abnormality.

lay_en: Increased thickness of bone of skull base

terms.def_en: Underdevelopment of frontal sinus.
Increased susceptibility to Escherichia coli infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Escherichia coli infection.
Increased susceptibility to Serratia infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Serratia infection.
Increased susceptibility to Klebsiella infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Klebsiella infection.
Increased susceptibility to enteroviral infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of enteroviral infection.
A thickened white patch on the oral mucosa that cannot be rubbed off.

terms.en: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness
terms.it: Insufficienza respiratoria dovuta a debolezza muscolare
lay_en: Decreased lung function due to weak breathing muscles
syn_en: Decreased respiratory function due to muscle weakness
Respiratory distress due to muscle weakness
Respiratory failure due to muscle weakness

terms.def_en: Rickets is divided into two major categories including calcipenic and phosphopenic. Hypophosphatemia is described as a common manifestation of both categories. Hypophosphatemic rickets is the most common type of rickets that is characterized by low levels of serum phosphate, resistance to ultraviolet radiation or vitamin D intake. There are several issues involved in hypophosphatemic rickets such as calcium, vitamin D, phosphorus deficiencies. Moreover, other disorder can be associated with its occurrence such as absorption defects due to pancreatic, intestinal, gastric, and renal disorders and hepatobiliary disease. Symptoms are usually seen in childhood and can be varied in severity. Severe forms may be linked to bowing of the legs, poor bone growth, and short stature as well as joint and bone pain. Hypophosphatemic rickets are associated with renal excretion of phosphate, hypophosphatemia, and mineral defects in bones. The familial type of the disease is the most common type of rickets.

Osteomalacia is a general term for bone weakness owing to a defect in mineralization of the protein framework known as osteoid. This defective mineralization is mainly caused by lack in vitamin D. Osteomalacia in children is known as rickets.
A decreased rate of skeletal maturation. Delayed skeletal maturation can be diagnosed on the basis of an estimation of the bone age from radiographs of specific bones in the human body.
An abnormal curvature of the spine in both a coronal (lateral) and sagittal (back-to-front) plane.
Abnormal thinning of the cortical region of bones.
Osteomyelitis is an inflammatory process accompanied by bone destruction and caused by an infecting microorganism.

A pathologic fracture occurs when a bone breaks in an area that is weakened secondarily to another disease process such as tumor, infection, and certain inherited bone disorders. A pathologic fracture can occur without a degree of trauma required to cause fracture in healthy bone.
The repeated occurrence of bone fractures (implying an abnormally increased tendency for fracture).

Degeneration (wear and tear) of articular cartilage, i.e., of the joint surface. Joint degeneration may be accompanied by osteophytes (bone overgrowth), narrowing of the joint space, regions of sclerosis at the joint surface, or joint deformity.

Joint hypermobility (ability of a joint to move beyond its normal range of motion) affecting many or all joints of the body. In individuals with Joint hypermobility at multiple sites (usually five or more), the term generalized joint hypermobility is preferred.
Presence of more than one exostosis. An exostosis is a benign growth the projects outward from the bone surface. It is capped by cartilage, and arises from a bone that develops from cartilage.
Any morphological abnormality of cartilage.
Punctate (speckled, dot-like) deposition of calcium of calcium salts in the articular cartilage (cartilage located in joints).
A structural anomaly of the trachea.
Weakness or softness of the cartilage in the walls of the bronchial tubes.
Increased resistance to the passage of air in the upper airway.

terms.it: Infezioni ricorrenti del tratto respiratorio inferiore
terms.def_en: An increased susceptibility to lower respiratory tract infections as manifested by a history of recurrent lower respiratory tract infections.
Weakness of the cartilage in the trachea and the bronchi, resulting in a floppy (non-rigid) airway. Affected persons may have difficulties to maintain patency of the airways.
Calcification (abnormal deposits of calcium) in the tracheal tissues.

terms.it: Infezioni ricorrenti del tratto respiratorio superiore
terms.def_en: An increased susceptibility to upper respiratory tract infections as manifested by a history of recurrent upper respiratory tract infections (running ears - otitis, sinusitis, pharyngitis, tonsillitis).
syn_en: Recurrent upper respiratory and lower respiratory infections

terms.def_en: Very rapid breathing.
lay_en: Increased respiratory rate or depth of breathing

terms.def_en: A reduction in the amount of air transported into the pulmonary alveoli by breathing, leading to hypercapnia (increase in the partial pressure of carbon dioxide).

An abnormal reduction on the vital capacity, which is defined as the total lung capacity (volume of air in the lungs at maximal inflation) less the residual volume (i.e., volume of air in the lungs following maximal exhalation) of the lung.
An anomaly of the rhythm or depth of breathing.
Abnormal function of the respiratory system.
Osteolysis refers to the destruction of bone through bone resorption with removal or loss of calcium.
One or more flexion contractures (a bent joint that cannot be straightened actively or passively) that are present at birth.
Multiple congenital contractures in different body areas.
Exaggerated anterior convexity of the thoracic vertebral column.

lay_en: Dumbbell shaped wide portion of long bone

terms.def_en: Coxa vara includes all forms of decrease of the femoral neck shaft angle (the angle between the neck and the shaft of the femur) to less than 120 degrees.
Any abnormality of bones of the arms or legs.
An abnormality of the leg.
An abnormality of the knee joint or surrounding structures.
An abnormally increased extension of the knee joint, so that the knee can bend backwards.
An abnormality of the arm.
An abnormality of the radius.
Any anomaly of the structure of the femur.
The presence of a tail-like skin appendage located adjacent to the sacrum.

An anomalous radiographic appearance of the developing pelvis, in which the greater ischiadic noth (incisura ischiadica major) is shallow and the pelvis takes on the appearance said to resemble a halberd (a weapon especially of the 15th and 16th centuries consisting typically of a battle-ax and pike mounted on a handle).
Displacement of the femur from its normal location in the hip joint.
Joint pain.
An abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) pattern of calcifications in soft tissues within or surrounding bones (as observed on radiographs).

Disseminated multifocal hemangiomatous or lymphangiomatous lesions of the skeleton. The lesions are lytic, well-defined, round or oval lesions within the medullary cavity, and they have an intact cortex, and manifest variable peripheral sclerosis and may exhibit endosteal scalloping.
syn_en: Lytic cystic lesions in appendicular bones

terms.def_en: Inspiration of a foreign object into the airway.
Eversion of the posterior bladder wall through the congenitally absent lower anterior abdominal wall and anterior bladder wall.
An increased susceptibility to bronchitis as manifested by a history of recurrent bronchitis.
Abnormal function of a sphincter of the urinary bladder.
Inflammation of a lymph node.
Increased susceptibility to fungal infections as manifested by multiple episodes of fungal infection.

Abnormal increase or decrease of total or subset T cell count. T cells are commonly characterized as CD3+ lymphocytes, or their subpopulations, in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group, measured ex vivo. These may include both TCR alpha/beta and gamma/delta T cells.
A structural abnormality of B cells.
Impaired production of memory cells, the B cells that persist for years or an entire lifetime and which confer rapid and enhanced response to secondary challenge.
The presence of normal overall immunoglobulin levels with deficiency of specific immunoglobulins directed against bacterial polysaccharides.
syn_en: Depressed antibody response to polysaccharide antigens

terms.en: Absence of lymph node germinal center
terms.def_en: Absence of germinal centers in lymph nodes. Germinal centers are the parts of lymph nodes in which B lymphocytes proliferate, differentiate, mutate through somatic hypermutation and class switch during antibody responses.
syn_en: Absence of lymph node germinal centre

terms.def_en: An abnormally decreased level of immunoglobulin M (IgM) in blood.

terms.it: Elevata percentuale di cellule T regolatorie CD4-negative, CD8-negative e alfa-beta
terms.def_en: Abnormal increase of double negative (DN) CD3+CD4-CD8- T cells, measured as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.
syn_en: Elevated proportion of CD4-negative, CD8-negative T cells
Increased number of CD4-/CD8- T cells expressing alpha/beta T-cell receptors

terms.en: Increased HLA-DR+ CD4+ T cell proportion
terms.def_en: Abnormal increase of the activated HLA-DR+ CD4+ T cell subpopulation, measured as percentage of total CD4+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.
syn_en: Increased HLA DR+ CD4+ T cell proportion
Increased HLA DR+ T cell proportion
Increased proportion of HLA DR+ T cells

terms.def_en: The legs angle inward, such that the knees are close together and the ankles far apart.
The presence of a meningioma, i.e., a benign tumor originating from the dura mater or arachnoid mater.
lay_en: Noncancerous growth of membranes covering brain

terms.def_en: The presence of squamous cell carcinoma of the skin.
The presence of a melanoma, a malignant cancer originating from pigment producing melanocytes. Melanoma can originate from the skin or the pigmented layers of the eye (the uvea).
The presence of a carcinoma of the urinary bladder.
Clonal hematopoietic stem cell disorders characterized by dysplasia (ineffective production) in one or more hematopoietic cell lineages, leading to anemia and cytopenia.
The presence of a medullary carcinoma of the thyroid gland.
Underdevelopment of the ilium ala.
An abnormality of the ilium, the largest and uppermost bone of the pelvis.
Decreased width of the wing (or ala) of the ilium (which is the large expanded portion which bounds the greater pelvis laterally).
Widening of the ilium ala, that is of the wing of the ilium, combined with external rotation, leading to a flared appearance of the iliac wing.

Obstructive Sleep Apnea is a condition characterized by the obstruction of the airway and pauses in breathing during sleep, which occur multiple times throughout the night. It is related to the relaxation of muscle tone that typically happens during sleep, leading to a partial collapse of the soft tissues in the airway and causing airflow obstruction.
Apnea resulting from depression of the respiratory centers in the medulla oblongata. There is a lack of respiratory effort rather than obstruction of airflow.

terms.en: Apneic episodes precipitated by illness, fatigue, stress
terms.def_en: Recurrent episodes of apnea that are precipitated by factors such as illness, fatigue, or stress.
syn_en: Episodic apnea induced by febrile illness or stress

terms.def_en: Perceived difficulty to breathe that occurs with exercise or exertion and improves with rest.
lay_en: Shortness of breathing upon physical activity

terms.def_en: Episodes of very rapid breathing.
An abnormal reduction in alveolar ventilation occurring during sleep. This is characterized by a rise in arterial carbon dioxide.
A severe form of respiratory insufficiency characterized by inadequate gas exchange such that the levels of oxygen or carbon dioxide cannot be maintained within normal limits.
Abnormally increased variability of the size of the vertebral bodies.
Recurrent bouts of sudden, severe apnea that may be life-threatening.

Hyperventilation refers to an increased pulmonary ventilation rate that is faster than necessary for the exchange of gases. Hyperventilation can result from increased frequency of breathing, an increased tidal volume, or both, and leads to an excess intake of oxygen and the blowing off of carbon dioxide.
A kind of neoplasm of the liver that originates from immature liver precursor cells and macroscopically is composed of tissue resembling fetal or mature liver cells or bile ducts.

A rapidly growing embryonic tumor arising in the posterior part of the cerebellar vermis and neuroepithelial roof of the fourth ventricle in children. More rarely, medulloblastoma arises in the cerebellum in adults.
A tumor that develops in the retrostyloid compartment of the parapharyngeal space, arising from an island of paraganglion tissue derived from the neural crest that is located on the vagus nerve.
The presence of an ependymoma of the central nervous system.
The presence of a carcinoma of the thyroid gland.
The presence of a leiomyosarcoma of the uterus.
A benign epithelial tumor derived from intrinsic cells of the adenohypophysis (anterior pituitary).
A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the pancreas.
The presence of a papillary adenocarcinoma of the thyroid gland.
A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the liver.
A benign tumor of the parathyroid gland that can cause hyperparathyroidism.
The concentration of potassium(1+) in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
The concentration of calcium in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
The concentration of sodium in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
An increased amount of bilirubin in the blood.
The concentration of phosphate ion in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
syn_en: Elevated phosphate ion level in blood
Increased phosphate ion level in blood

terms.def_en: Microscopic hematuria detected by dipstick or microscopic examination of the urine.
lay_en: Small amount of blood in urine

terms.def_en: An increased concentration of all types of amino acid in the urine.

terms.it: Elevata concentrazione di transaminasi epatiche circolanti
terms.def_en: Elevations of the levels of SGOT and SGPT in the serum. SGOT (serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase) and SGPT (serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase) are transaminases primarily found in the liver and heart and are released into the bloodstream as the result of liver or heart damage. SGOT and SGPT are used clinically mainly as markers of liver damage.
The concentration of methylmalonic acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
syn_en: Elevated methylmalonic acid level in blood
Increased methylmalonic acid level in blood

terms.def_en: Presence of myoglobin in the urine.
An increased concentration of chloride in the urine.
An abnormality of chromosome segregation.
The concentration of magnesium in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
The concentration of magnesium in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

High levels of ketone bodies (acetoacetic acid, beta-hydroxybutyric acid, and acetone) in the urine. Ketone bodies are insignificant in the blood and urine of normal individuals in the postprandial or overnight-fasted state.
The concentration of corticotropin, also known as adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), is below the lower limit of normal in the blood circulation.
An abnormality of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

terms.it: Aumento della concentrazione proteica nel liquor
terms.def_en: Increased concentration of protein in the cerebrospinal fluid.
The presence in the serum of an autoantibody directed against the Fc portion of IgG.

terms.it: Elevata concentrazione di ormone stimolante la tiroide in circolo
terms.def_en: Increased concentration of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) in the blood circulation.
An abnormal functionality of the thyroid gland.
An increased concentration of histidine in the urine.

terms.en: Decreased activity of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex
terms.it: Diminuzione dell'attività del complesso piruvato deidrogenasi
syn_en: Decreased activity of the PDH complex

terms.def_en: Reduced sensitivity of end organs to thyroid hormone characterized by elevated serum levels of free thyroid hormone with nonsuppressed thyroid stimulating hormone.
syn_en: Elevated serum levels of free thyroid hormone with nonsuppressed TSH

terms.def_en: A reduction in aldehyde oxidase level.
Ventral hernia refers to a condition in which abdominal contents protrude through a weakened portion of the abdominal wall.
An abnormal reduction in sensation in the distal portions of the extremities.
syn_en: Distal sensory impairment in lower limbs
Distal sensory impairment of the lower extremities
Distal sensory loss, upper and lower limbs

terms.def_en: Absence of one half of the vertebral body.
An abnormal accentuation of the inward curvature of the spine in the lumbar region.
lay_en: Excessive inward curvature of lower spine

terms.def_en: Over curvature of the thoracic region, leading to a round back or if sever to a hump.
Decreased height of the intervertebral disk.
Exaggerated convexity of the cervical vertebral column, causing the cervical spine to bow outwards and take on a rounded appearance.
A developmental defect leading to the union of two adjacent vertebrae.
A congenital anomaly characterized by a joining (fusion) of two or more cervical vertebral bodies with one another.
Congenital absence of a part of the vermis of cerebellum.

lay_en: Compression fracture of a vertebral body

terms.def_en: A granulomatous inflammation leading to multiple granuloma formation, which is a specific type of inflammation. A granuloma is a focal compact collection of inflammatory cells, mononuclear cells predominating, usually as a result of the persistence of a non-degradable product and of active cell mediated hypersensitivity.
Altered immune function characterized by lymphoid proliferation, immune activation, and excessive autoreactivity often leading to autoimmune/inflammatory complications.
An impairment of the class-switch recombination process that normally leads B lymphocytes to produce IgG, IgA, or IgE.
The occurrence of an immune reaction against the organism's own cells or tissues.

Delay in cutaneous immune reaction to specific antigens mediated not by antibodies but by cells. The delayed hypersensitivity test is an immune function test measuring the presence of activated T cells that recognize a specific antigen and is performed by injecting a small amount of the antigen into the skin. The area of the injection is examined 48-72 hours thereafter.
Inability to react to a delayed hypersensitivity skin test.
syn_en: Absence of delayed hypersensitivity skin test
Lack of delayed skin hypersensitivity reaction

terms.def_en: Abnormal positioning in which the elbows are turned out.
A positional abnormality marked by outward bowing of the legs in which the knees stay wide apart when a person stands with the feet and ankles together.

terms.en: Absent microvilli on the surface of peripheral blood lymphocytes
terms.def_en: Absence of the fingerlike protrusive, actin-dependent structures found on the surface of peripheral blood lymphocytes.
Decreased ability to react to a delayed hypersensitivity skin test.
syn_en: Decreased reactivity to skin test antigens

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the lower arm.
An abnormal osseous union (fusion) between the radius and the ulna.

terms.en: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the central nervous system
terms.def_en: Absence or underdevelopment of tissue in the central nervous system.
A bending or abnormal curvature affecting a long bone of the leg.
Bowing (abnormal curvature) of the femur.
An abnormality of the calf, i.e. of the posterior part of the lower leg.
A bending or abnormal curvature of the tibia.
The presence of abnormally small extremities.
lay_en: Smaller or shorter than typical limbs

terms.def_en: Underdevelopment of the radius.
A bending or abnormal curvature of the radius.
lay_en: Bowing of outer large bone of the forearm
syn_en: Bowing of radius bone of the forearm

terms.def_en: An elbow contracture that limits the ability of the elbow joint to be extended (straightened), meaning that the elbow is fixed in an flexed (bent) position.
syn_en: Fixed flexion at the elbow joint

terms.def_en: Absence of the fibula.
An anomaly of the calf bone (fibula), one of the two bones of the calf.
Abnormality of the tibia (shinbone).
The kneecap normally is located within the groove termed trochlea on the distal femur and can slide up and down in it. Patellar dislocation occurs if the patella fully dislocates out of the groove.
The presence of a carcinoma of the breast.
A benign neoplasm that usually arises from the sympathetic trunk in the mediastinum, representing a tumor of the sympathetic nerve fibers arising from neural crest cells.

Neuroblastoma is a solid tumor that originate in neural crest cells of the sympathetic nervous system. Most neuroblastomas originate in the abdomen, and most abdominal neuroblastomas originate in the adrenal gland. Neuroblastomas can also originate in the thorax, usually in the posterior mediastinum.
Prolongation of the time taken for a standardized skin cut of fixed depth and length to stop bleeding.
Abnormality originating in one or more muscles, i.e., of the set of muscles of body.
A morphological abnormality of epiphyses whereby they are abnormally outwardly curving (protuberant).
The presence of a splayed (i.e.,flared) metaphyseal segment of one or more long bones.
lay_en: Flared wide portion of long bone
syn_en: marked metaphyseal flaring of long bones

terms.def_en: Abnormal widening of the metaphyseal regions of long bones.
lay_en: Broad wide portion of long bone

terms.def_en: Abnormality of the wrist, the structure connecting the hand and the forearm.
Metaphyseal cupping refers to an inward bulging of the metaphyseal profile giving the metaphysis a cup-like appearance.
Underdevelopment of the ulna.

terms.en: Bowing of limbs due to multiple fractures
terms.it: Inarcamento degli arti dovuto a fratture multiple
terms.def_en: Curvature of the shafts of the long bones due to multiple fractures.
syn_en: Bowed limbs due to multiple fractures

terms.def_en: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of the metaphyses.
lay_en: Irregular wide portion of a long bone

terms.def_en: One or more abnormally short long bone.
Shortening of the middle parts of the limbs (forearm and lower leg) in relation to the upper and terminal segments.
lay_en: Disproportionately short middle portion of limb

terms.def_en: An anomaly of the joint that connects the foot with the leg.
Bending of the diaphysis (shaft) of the ulna.
An elevation in bone density in one or more diaphyses. Sclerosis is normally detected on a radiograph as an area of increased opacity.
lay_en: Increased bone density in shaft of long bone

terms.def_en: Increase in size of one or more joints.
Underdevelopment of the fibula.
An abnormal osseous union (fusion) between the radius and the humerus.
lay_en: Fusion of upper and lower arm bones

terms.def_en: Dislocation of the distal humerus out of the elbow joint, where the radius, ulna, and humerus meet.
An abnormality of the shoulder, which is defined as the structures surrounding the shoulder joint where the humerus attaches to the scapula.
Chronic reduction in active and passive mobility of the shoulder joint due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevents normal movement.
Abnormality of the patella (knee cap).
Partial dislocation of the head of the radius.
Abnormal increase in size of one or more metaphyses.
lay_en: Enlarged wide portion of a long bone

terms.def_en: Amelia of all four limbs.
Underdevelopment of the patella.
Reduced ability to extend (straighten) the knee joint.

An anomaly related to partial closure, or failure of development of the ulnar side of the distal radial growth plate, which results in an arrest of epiphyseal growth of the medial and volar portions of the distal radius. This leads to shortening of the radius and relative overgrowth of the ulna.
Abnormal flatness (decreased height) of epiphyses.
The concentration of calcium in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
The concentration of albumin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
An increased concentration of glucose in the blood.
A decreased concentration of protein in the blood.
An increased concentration of glucose in the urine.
The concentration of lipid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.en: Defective DNA repair after ultraviolet radiation damage

terms.def_en: An increased concentration of 4-hydroxy-L-proline in the urine.
An increased concentration of potassium(1+) in the urine.
A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint.
An increased tendency to fractures of the long bones (Mainly, the femur, tibia, fibula, humerus, radius, and ulna).
Disproportionately long fibulae.
Small hands and feet.

terms.en: Hypoplasia of the capital femoral epiphysis
terms.def_en: Underdevelopment of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
lay_en: Underdevelopment of the innermost thighbone end part

terms.def_en: Trophic changes occurring in a limb.
Limitation of the extension of the hip, i.e., decreased ability to straighten the hip joint and thereby increase the angle between torso and thigh; moving the thigh or top of the pelvis backward.
An abnormal shortening of the femur.
Relatively increased growth of the fibula compared to that of the tibia.
Reduced diameter of a long bone.
An abnormal increase in the carrying angle, which is the angle he long axis of the extended forearm as it lies lateral to the long axis of the arm.
An abnormality of compact bone (also known as cortical bone), which forms the dense surface of bones.

terms.en: Protuberances at ends of long bones
terms.def_en: The presence of multiple protuberances (bulges, or knobs) at the ends of the long bones.
lay_en: Protuberances at ends of long bones

terms.def_en: Loss of bone mass occurring beneath the periosteum (the periosteum is the connective-tissue membrane that surrounds all bones except at the articular surfaces). This process may create a serrated and lace-like appearance in periosteal cortical bone.
Any deviation from the normal concentration of cholesterol in the blood circulation.
An increased concentration of glycine in the urine.
An increased excretion of phosphates in the urine.
An abnormality of the composition of urine or the levels of its components.
Abnormality of the homeostasis (concentration) of a monoatomic ion.

terms.it: Concentrazione anormale di aminoacidi in circolo
terms.def_en: Any deviation from the normal concentration of amino acid in the blood circulation.
lay_en: Abnormality of serum amino acid levels
syn_en: Abnormality of serum amino acid level

terms.def_en: The concentration of chloride in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
Abnormal rhythm of the heart.
Concentration of a hormone in the blood circulation outside of normal limits.

Overproduction of the hormone of cortisol by the adrenal cortex, resulting in a characteristic combination of clinical symptoms termed Cushing syndrome, with truncal obesity, a round, full face, striae atrophicae and acne, muscle weakness, and other features.
Any deviation from the normal concentration of lipid in the blood circulation.
A contracture (chronic loss of joint motion due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin) that prevent normal movement of one or more joints of the limbs.
An increased concentration of cholesterol in the blood.

Reduced activity of coagulation factor VIII. Factor VIII (fVIII) is a cofactor in the intrinsic clotting cascade that is activated to fVIIIa in the presence of minute quantities of thrombin. fVIIIa acts as a receptor, for factors IXa and X.
Excretion in urine of proteins of a size smaller than albumin (molecular weight 69 kD).
An abnormally decreased calcium concentration in the urine.
An abnormal buildup of lactic acid in the body, leading to acidification of the blood and other bodily fluids.
An abnormality of the myelination of motor and sensory peripheral nerves. These are axons for motor nerves and dendrites for sensory nerves in the strict anatomic sense.
An increased concentration of cystine in the urine.

An abnormality of the spinocerebellar tracts, a set of axonal fibers originating in the spinal cord and terminating in the ipsilateral cerebellum. The spinocerebellar tract convey information to the cerebellum about limb and joint position (proprioception). They comprise the ventral spinocerebellar tract, the anterior spinocerebellar tract, and the posterior spinocerebellar tract.
An abnormality of the conduction of electrical impulses by peripheral (motor or sensory) nerves. This finding is elicited by a nerve conduction study (NCS).
syn_en: Sensory and motor nerve conduction abnormalities

terms.def_en: Level of proline in the urine anove the upper limit of normal.
An increased amount of nitrogen in the form of urea in the blood.
A reduction in the circulating levels of all the major classes of immunoglobulin. is characterized by profound decreases in all classes of immunoglobulin with an absence of circulating B lymphocytes.

terms.en: T-wave inversion in the right precordial leads

terms.it: Aumento della concentrazione di colesterolo LDL
terms.def_en: The concentration of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
syn_en: Elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol level in blood
Increased low-density lipoprotein cholesterol level in blood

terms.def_en: A increased concentration of serotonin in the blood.
The concentration of adenosylcobalam in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal. Adenosylcobalamin is one of the active forms of vitamin B12.
An decreased concentration of cholesterol in the blood.
An abnormally high level of uric acid in the urine.
The concentration of glutaric acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
An elevated urinary concentration of cystathionine.
An abnormal increased in the concentration of corticotropin, also known as adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), in the blood.

terms.it: Elevata concentrazione di fosfatasi alcalina in circolo
terms.def_en: Abnormally increased serum levels of alkaline phosphatase activity.
An abnormally low urinary specific gravity, i.e., reduced concentration of solutes in the urine.
Increased excretion of oxalates in the urine.
syn_en: Increased level of oxalate in urine

terms.en: Abnormal isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin
terms.it: Focalizzazione isoelettrica anormale della transferrina sierica
terms.def_en: Glycosylated transferrin concentrations can be measured in serum as a marker of N-linked glycosylation fidelity. In the traditional nomenclature for congenital disorders of glycosylation, absence of entire glycans was designated type I, and loss of one or more monosaccharides as type II. These terms are retained for historical reasons but for new annotations the precise glycosylation defect should be recorded.
Increased relative concentration of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvic acid in the urine.
An increased concentration of 5-aminolevulinic acid (CHEBI:17549) in the urine.

Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) deficiency (IGD) is characterized by inappropriately low serum concentrations of the gonadotropins LH (luteinizing hormone) and FSH (follicle-stimulating hormone) in the presence of low circulating concentrations of sex steroids (primarily testosterone or estradiol). GnRH is not typically assayed directly because it is released in pulses from the hypothalamus, and its concentration can fluctuate rapidly and in a complex pattern that makes single blood measurements less informative than the pituitary's response.

terms.it: Elevato livello di ormone paratiroideo circolante
terms.def_en: An abnormal increased concentration of parathyroid hormone.
Increased concentration of taurine in the urine.
An increased concentration of carnosine in the urine.

An increased level of a dibasic amino acid in the urine. Dibasic amino acids are usually referred to simply as basic aminoacids because they contain basic side chains at neutral pH. These are arginine (Arg), lysine (Lys), and histidine (His).
An abnormality of the acetabulum, i.e., the Acetabular part of hip bone, which together with the head of the femur forms the hip joint.
An anomaly of the the pubic bone, i.e., of the ventral and anterior of the three principal components (pubis, ilium, ischium) of the hip bone.
Underdevelopment of the pubis, which together with the ilium and the ischium, is one of the three bones that make up the hip bone.
An anomaly of the ischium, which forms the lower and back part of the hip bone.
Underdevelopment of the ischium, which forms the lower and back part of the hip bone.
A shift from the normally round (convex) appearance of the iliac wing towards a square-like appearance.
Intrapelvic bulging of the medial acetabular wall.

Flattening of the superior part of the acetabulum, which is a cup-shaped cavity at the base of the hipbone into which the ball-shaped head of the femur fits. The acetabular roof thereby appears horizontal rather than arched, as it normally does.
Abnormally increased width of the pubic symphysis is the midline cartilaginous joint uniting the superior rami of the left and right pubic bones.
Reduced ability to move the femur outward to the side.

The sacroiliac joint in the bony pelvis connects the sacrum and the ilium of the pelvis, which are joined by strong ligaments. The notch is located directly superior to the joint. This term refers to a reduction in the height of the notch.
The presence of nipples that instead of pointing outward are retracted inwards.
Underdevelopment of the breast.
Distance from nasion to subnasale more than two standard deviations above the mean, or alternatively, an apparently increased length from the nasal root to the nasal base.
The presence of a notch in the margin of the ala nasi.
It is characterized by one or more symptoms including sneezing, itching, nasal congestion, and rhinorrhea.
Decreased superior-inferior length of the nasal bridge, which is the saddle-shaped area that includes the nasal root and the lateral aspects of the nose.
lay_en: Decreased length of bridge of nose

terms.def_en: Distance from nasion to subnasale more than two standard deviations below the mean, or alternatively, an apparently decreased length from the nasal root to the nasal tip.
A disorder of muscle unrelated to impairment of innervation or neuromuscular junction.

terms.it: Fibre muscolari di colore rosso stracciato
terms.def_en: An abnormal appearance of muscle fibers observed on muscle biopsy. Ragged red fibers can be visualized with Gomori trichrome staining as irregular and intensely red subsarcolemmal zones, whereas the normal myofibrils are green. The margins of affect fibers appear red and ragged. The ragged-red is due to the accumulation of abnormal mitochondria below the plasma membrane of the muscle fiber, leading to the appearance of a red rim and speckled sarcoplasm.
Breakdown of muscle fibers that leads to the release of muscle fiber contents (myoglobin) into the bloodstream.
The presence of skeletal muscular atrophy (which is also known as amyotrophy).
syn_en: Neurogenic muscle atrophy, especially in the lower limbs

terms.def_en: Abnormal decrease of neutrophil oxidative burst, commonly measured through oxidation of dihydrorhodamine (DHR) using flow cytometry or through nitroblue tetrazolium test (NBT) using optical microscopy, upon stimulation with phorbol-12-myristate-13-acetate (PMA), E. coli or other ligands.
syn_en: Reduced reactive oxygen species production in neutrophils

terms.en: Intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material
terms.def_en: The intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent storage material.

terms.en: Curvilinear intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material
terms.def_en: An intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material in a curved pattern.
syn_en: Intracellular curvilinear profiles on ultrastructural analysis

terms.def_en: Pathological deposition of calcium salts in one or more arteries.

terms.en: Fingerprint intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material
terms.def_en: An intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material in a trabecular or fingerprint-like pattern.
A decreased rate of pyruvate carboxylase activity.
An abnormality of Krebs cycle metabolism that is characterized by a decreased rate of methylmalonyl-CoA mutase activity.

terms.it: Aumento del livello di IgE in circolo
terms.def_en: An abnormally increased overall level of immunoglobulin E in blood.

terms.en: Deficient excision of UV-induced pyrimidine dimers in DNA
Prolonged G2 phase of cell cycle

terms.def_en: An increased concentration of dicarboxylic acid in the urine.
A diffuse form of amyloidosis.
The concentration of glutamine in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
An increased concentration of orotic acid in the urine.
The concentration of ethylmalonic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
A type of chromosomal aberration characterized by reduced resistance of chromosomes to change or deterioration.

terms.en: Chromosomal breakage induced by crosslinking agents
terms.it: Rottura cromosomica indotta da agenti reticolanti
terms.def_en: Increased amount of chromosomal breaks in cultured blood lymphocytes or other cells induced by treatment with DNA cross-linking agents such as diepoxybutane and mitomycin C.
syn_en: Chromosomal breakage induced by mitomycin C

terms.def_en: The concentration of methylcobalamin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal. Methylcobalamin is a form of vitamin B12.

terms.en: Increased cellular sensitivity to UV light

terms.def_en: Decreased activity of coagulation factor V.

terms.en: Rectilinear intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material
terms.def_en: An intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material in a straight or rectilinear pattern.
The concentration of sodium in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
The concentration of tyrosine in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.it: Diminuzione della concentrazione di colesterolo HDL
terms.def_en: The concentration of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
syn_en: Decreased high-density lipoprotein cholesterol level in blood
Reduced high-density lipoprotein cholesterol level in blood

terms.def_en: The concentration of carnitine in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
An increased concentration of methionine in the blood.

terms.it: Elevata concentrazione di creatina chinasi in circolo
terms.def_en: The activity of creatine kinase in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
syn_en: Elevated creatine kinase level in blood
Increased creatine kinase level in blood

terms.it: Aumento del livello di IgG circolanti
terms.def_en: An abnormally increased level of immunoglobulin G in blood.
The concentration of pepsinogen I in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
An increased level of phosphoethanolamine (synonym: O-phosphoethanolamine) in the urine.
syn_en: Increased level of O-phosphoethanolamine in urine

terms.def_en: Abnormally elevated level of the enzyme phosphoribosyl pyrophosphatesynthetase, which catalyzes the synthesis of PP-ribose-P from ATP and ribose-5-phosphate.
Underdevelopment of part or all of the external reproductive organs.
Location of the urethral opening on the inferior aspect of the penis.
Increased size of the ridge of tissue that extends along the midline of the scrotum.

terms.en: Gonadal tissue inappropriate for external genitalia or chromosomal sex

terms.def_en: Aplasia of the vagina.
An abnormality of the process of DNA repair, that is, of the process of restoring DNA after damage.

An abnormality of the coagulation cascade, which is comprised of the contact activation pathway (also known as the intrinsic pathway) and the tissue factor pathway (also known as the extrinsic pathway) as well as cofactors and regulators.

terms.it: Elevata concentrazione di creatinina in circolo
terms.def_en: An increased amount of creatinine in the blood.
The concentration of hydroxyproline in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.it: Aumento del livello di IgA circolanti
terms.def_en: An abnormally increased level of immunoglobulin A in blood.
The presence in serum of antibodies against smooth muscle.
A type of hyperbilirubinemia with neonatal onset.
syn_en: High blood bilirubin levels in neonate

terms.def_en: An abnormal decrease in orotidine 5'-phosphate decarboxylase level.
A increased concentration of arginine in the urine.
Distention of the abdomen.
Abnormal increased size of the viscera of the abdomen.
An abnormality of the hip bone.

Lack of full passive range of motion (restrictions in flexion, extension, or other movements) of the hip joint resulting from structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and/or skin.
Underdeveloped acetabulae.
Reduced side to side width of the pelvis.
A benign growth the projects outward from the bone surface of the pelvis. Exostoses are capped by cartilage, and arise from a bone that develops from cartilage.
An abnormally squared appearance of the bony pelvis, a normally rounded or basin-shaped structure.
Widening of the femoral head and neck.

terms.it: Aumento della concentrazione di ferritina in circolo
terms.def_en: Increased concentration of ferritin in the blood circulation.
Concentration or activity of alkaline phosphatase outside the upper or lower limtis of normal in the blood circulation.
The concentration of cystathionine in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
A functional anomaly of mitochondria.
A decreased concentration of leptin in the blood.
An increased concentration of threonine in the urine.
An increased concentration of lysine in the urine.
The closed form of spina bifida with incomplete closure of a vertebral body with intact overlying skin.
When viewed in lateral radiographs, vertebral bodies have a roughly rectangular configuration. This term applies if the vertebral body appears rounded or oval.
An irregular surface of the vertebral end plates, which are normally relatively smooth.
Complete bilateral fractures of the pars interarticularis resulting in the anterior slippage of the vertebra.
lay_en: Displacement of one backbone compared to another

terms.def_en: Spondylolysis is an osseous defect of the pars interarticularis, thought to be a developmental or acquired stress fracture secondary to chronic low-grade trauma.
Congenital synostosis between two or more adjacent vertebrae (partial or complete fusion of adjacent vertabral bodies).
Reduced ability to move the vertebral column with a resulting limitation of neck and trunk flexion.
Abnormally increased curvature (anterior concavity) of the lumbar or cervical spine.
A partial dislocation of one or more intervertebral joints in the cervical vertebral column.

Abnormal structure of the odontoid process, which is a part of the C2 or axis vertebra and forms pivot of the structures forming the craniovertebral junction. The odontoid process is also known as the dens of the axis.
Developmental hypoplasia of the dens of the axis.

Abnormal form of vertebral body, which is the central cylindrical portion of the vertebra that together with other structures such as the vertebral arch, pedicles, laminae, spinous process, transverse processes, and articular facets makes up a vertebra.
syn_en: Abnormal form of the vertebral bodies

terms.def_en: A butterfly vertebra (sagittal cleft vertebra or anterior rachischisis) is a sagittal defect in the vertebral body caused by failure of fusion of the two lateral chondrification centers during embryogenesis. The name is based on the appearance of the two hemivertebrae emerging as butterfly wings from the central cleft on x-ray.
Any abnormality of the cervical vertebral column.
A partial dislocation of the atlantoaxial joints.
Generalized weakness or decreased strength of the muscles, affecting both distal and proximal musculature.
Weakness of the limb-girdle muscles (also known as the pelvic and shoulder girdles), that is, lack of strength of the muscles around the shoulders and the pelvis.
Pain in muscle.
Reduced strength of the axial musculature (i.e., of the muscles of the head and neck, spine, and ribs).
An abnormal structure of the hairshaft, i.e., of the nongrowing portion of a hair that protrudes from the skin.

terms.en: Hair shafts flattened at irregular intervals and twisted through 180 degrees about their axes

terms.def_en: Any anomaly in the composite material or the layered arrangement of the bony skeleton.
The activity of beta-hexosaminidase in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
An abnormal increase in catecholamine concentration in the blood.
An abnormality of the process of endochondral ossification, which is a type of replacement ossification in which bone tissue replaces cartilage.

The prothrombin consumption test measures the formation of intrinsic thromboplastin by determining the residual serum prothrombin after blood clotting is complete. If there is a defect in the process, less prothrombin will be converted to thrombin than normal (less prothrombin is consumed). This test may be abnormal with conditions including deficiency of factors VIII or IX, with circulating anticoagulants, thrombocytopenia.

terms.en: Focal necrosis of right ventricular muscle cells

terms.def_en: A type of megaloblastic anemia that improves upon administration of pyrimidine supplements such as uridylic acid and cytidylic acid.
syn_en: Anaemia corrected by uridylic acid and cytidylic acid
Anemia corrected by uridylic acid and cytidylic acid

terms.def_en: The formation of bullae (blisters) with cleavage in the lamina lucida layer of the skin.
syn_en: Subepidermal blistering with cleavage in the lamina lucida

terms.def_en: Reduced level of the enzyme glutathione synthetase, which catalyzes the last step in the synthesis of glutathione and a deficiency results in low levels of glutathione. Acidosis is due to reduced feedback inhibition of gamma-glutamyl cysteine synthetase in the gamma-glutamyl cycle, which ultimately leads to overproduction and accumulation of 5-oxoproline.
An abnormally increased level of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaric acid in the urine.
The concentration of noradrenaline in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
An increased concentration of alanine in the blood.

terms.it: Bassa velocità di esterificazione del colesterolo
terms.def_en: A reduction in the rate of cholesterol esterification.
An decreased level of renin in the blood.

terms.en: Endopolyploidy on chromosome studies of bone marrow
terms.def_en: An increase in the number of chromosome sets per cell in bone marrow cells.
An abnormality of amino acid metabolism characterized by a decreased level of propionyl-CoA carboxylase.
The concentration of threonine in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
An increased concentration of an amino acid in the urine.
lay_en: Increased levels of animo acids in urine

terms.def_en: A reduction in the level of thymic horomone.
An increased concentration of cystine within cells. This finding can be demonstrated on leukocytes, but is not specific to blood cells.
Decreased concentration of sulfate in the urine.
An increased concentration of tryptophan in the urine.

terms.it: Aumento della concentrazione di colesterolo VLDL
terms.def_en: The concentration of very-low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
syn_en: Elevated very-low-density lipoprotein cholesterol level in blood
Increased very-low-density lipoprotein cholesterol level in blood

terms.def_en: A left-right reversal (or mirror reflection) of the anatomical location of the viscera of the abdomen.
Joint pain affecting the hip.

lay_en: Abnormal neck or head of thigh bone
syn_en: Abnormality of the femoral neck or head region

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the femoral neck (which is the process of bone, connecting the femoral head with the femoral shaft).
An abnormality of the femoral head.
An abnormal flattening of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
lay_en: Flat end part of innermost thighbone

terms.en: Enlargement of the proximal femoral epiphysis
terms.def_en: An abnormal enlargement of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
lay_en: Enlarged end part of innermost thighbone

terms.def_en: A narrowing of the sacrosciatic notch, i.e., the deep indentation in the posterior border of the hip bone at the point of union of the ilium and ischium.

An abnormal gait pattern that arises from weakness of the pretibial and peroneal muscles due to a lower motor neuron lesion. Affected patients have footdrop and are unable to dorsiflex and evert the foot. The leg is lifted high on walking so that the toes clear the ground, and there may be a slapping noise when the foot strikes the ground again.
A pattern of simultaneous degeneration and regeneration of axons (see comment).

terms.en: Decreased number of peripheral myelinated nerve fibers
terms.it: Diminuzione del numero di fibre nervose periferiche mielinizzate
terms.def_en: A loss of myelinated nerve fibers in the peripheral nervous system (in general, this finding can be observed on nerve biopsy).
syn_en: Decreased number of large and small myelinated fibers
Decreased number of large and small myelinated fibres
Decreased number of peripheral myelinated nerve fibres

terms.def_en: Repeated episodes of segmental demyelination and remyelination lead to the accumulation of supernumerary Schwann cells around axons, which is referred to as onion bulb formation. This finding affects peripheral nerves.
Atrophic changes of axons of the peripheral nervous system.

terms.en: Decreased number of large peripheral myelinated nerve fibers
terms.def_en: A reduced number of large myelinated nerve fibers.
syn_en: Decreased number of large peripheral myelinated nerve fibres
Loss of larger myelinated nerve fibers
Loss of larger myelinated nerve fibres

terms.def_en: Increased susceptibility to fatigue.
An axonal neuropathy of peripheral sensory nerves.
A phenomenon whereby patients are not able to stand up without the use of the hands owing to weakness of the proximal muscles of the lower limbs.
Wasting of thenar muscles, which are located on palm of the hand at the base of the thumb.
Sudden and involuntary contractions of one or more muscles.
Dilated, glial-lined cavity in spinal cord. This cavity does not communicate with the central canal, and usually is between the dorsal columns unilaterally or bilaterally along the side of the cord.

terms.en: Generalized hypotonia due to defect at the neuromuscular junction
syn_en: Generalised hypotonia due to defect at the neuromuscular junction

terms.en: Abnormal synaptic transmission at the neuromuscular junction
terms.def_en: Any abnormality of the neuromuscular junction, which is the synapse between the motor end plate of a motor neuron and the skeletal muscle fibers.

terms.it: Formazione di bulbi di cipolla della lamina basale
terms.def_en: A type of onion bulb formation prominently affecting the area of the basal lamina.
syn_en: Basal lamina 'onion bulb' formations on nerve biopsy

terms.def_en: Abnormal sensations such as tingling, pricking, or numbness of the skin with no apparent physical cause.
An abnormal reduction in the amplitude of the miniature endplate potentials, i.e. the postsynaptic response to transmitter released from an individual vesicle at the neuromuscular junction.

terms.en: EMG: decremental response of compound muscle action potential to repetitive nerve stimulation
terms.it: EMG: risposta decrescente del potenziale d'azione del muscolo composto alla stimolazione nervosa ripetitiva
terms.def_en: A compound muscle action potential (CMAP) is a type of electromyography (EMG). CMAP refers to a group of almost simultaneous action potentials from several muscle fibers in the same area evoked by stimulation of the supplying motor nerve and are recorded as one multipeaked summated action potential. This abnormality refers to a greater than normal decrease in the amplitude during the course of the investigation.
syn_en: EMG: decremental response of CMAP to repetitive nerve stimulation

terms.en: Distal sensory impairment of all modalities
terms.def_en: Reduced ability to sense pain, temperature, touch, vibration stimuli in the distal regions of the extremities.
syn_en: Distal sensory loss to all modalities

terms.def_en: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of the proximal metaphysis of the femur.
An anomaly of the atlantoaxial joint, i.e., of the joint between the first (atlas) and second (axis) cervical vertebrae.
Partial dislocation of the atlantoaxial joint.
An abnormal narrowing of the spinal canal.
Frontal schisis (cleft or cleavage) of vertebral bodies.
An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the back.
An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the lower back.
An abnormality related to a defect of vertebral separation during development.
Reduced amount of myelin in the central nervous system resulting from defective myelinogenesis.

terms.it: Diminuzione della velocità di conduzione dei nervi motori
terms.def_en: A type of decreased nerve conduction velocity that affects the motor neuron.
An abnormal prolongation of the miniature endplate potentials, i.e. the postsynaptic response to transmitter released from an individual vesicle at the neuromuscular junction.
Absence of the Achilles reflex (also known as the ankle jerk reflex), which can normally be elicited by tapping the tendon is tapped while the foot is dorsiflexed.
A reduction in the size of nerve terminals.
Evidence of chronic denervation on electromyography.
The presence of characteristic findings of denervation on electromyography (fibrillations, positive sharp waves, and giant motor unit potentials).
A reduction in the number of axons in the peripheral nervous system.

terms.it: Diminuzione della velocità di conduzione del nervo sensoriale
terms.def_en: Reduced speed of conduction of the action potential along a sensory nerve.
Sudden and involuntary contractions of one or more muscles brought on by exposure to cold temperatures.
The presence of axonal regeneration following a previous axonal lesion.

terms.en: Increased rate of premature chromosome condensation
terms.def_en: An increased rate of premature chromosome condensation.
The concentration of iron cation in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
syn_en: Elevated iron cation level in blood
Increased iron cation level in blood

terms.def_en: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against neutrophils.
The presence in the serum of autoantibodies directed against thrombocytes.

terms.en: Elevated circulating long chain fatty acid concentration
terms.def_en: Increased concentration of long-chain fatty acids in the blood circulation.

terms.en: Low urinary cyclic AMP response to PTH administration

terms.def_en: Abnormal results of investigations using electromyography (EMG).
The presence of abnormal electromyographic patterns indicative of myopathy, such as small-short polyphasic motor unit potentials.

terms.en: Polyclonal elevation of circulating IgM concentration
terms.def_en: A heterogeneous increase in IgM immunoglobulins characterized by a diffuse band on serum electrophoresis.
Undetectable serum immunoglobulin A level at a value < 5 mg/dL (0.05 g/L).
Excretion of peptides conjugated to sialic acid in the urine.

Lipofuscin, a generic term applied to autofluorescent lipopigment, is a mixture of protein and lipid that accumulates in most aging cells, particularly those involved in high lipid turnover (e.g., the adrenal medulla) or phagocytosis of other cell types (e g., the retinal pigment epithelium or RPE; macrophage). This term pertains if there is an increase in the extraneuronal accumulation of lipofuscin (also known as autofluorescent lipoprotein) more than expected for the age of the patient.

terms.en: Paradoxical increased cortisol secretion on dexamethasone suppression test

terms.def_en: Abnormally increased movement at the junction between the first cervical (atlas) and the second cervical (axis) vertebrae as a result of either a bony or ligamentous anomaly.
An abnormality of one or more of the vertebrae.
Defective structure and function of myelin sheaths. Dysmyelination is distinguished from demyleination where there is destruction or damage of previously normal myelination.

Paralysis of voluntary muscles means loss of contraction due to interruption of one or more motor pathways from the brain to the muscle fibers. Although the word paralysis is often used interchangeably to mean either complete or partial loss of muscle strength, it is preferable to use paralysis or plegia for complete or severe loss of muscle strength, and paresis for partial or slight loss. Motor paralysis results from deficits of the upper motor neurons (corticospinal, corticobulbar, or subcorticospinal). Motor paralysis is often accompanied by an impairment in the facility of movement.
Hyperexcitability of the neuromuscular system related to abnormally low level of calcium in the blood, resulting in carpopedal or generalized spasms.
A type of weakness that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.
syn_en: Generalised muscle weakness due to defect at the neuromuscular junction
Generalized muscle weakness due to defect at the neuromuscular junction
Proximal muscle weakness due to defect at the neuromuscular junction

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the primary sensation that is mediated by peripheral nerves (pain, temperature, touch, vibration, joint position). The word hypoesthesia (or hypesthesia) refers to a reduction in cutaneous sensation to a specific type of testing.
An abnormality characterized by disruption of the normal functioning of peripheral axons.
A segmental pattern of demyelination and regeneration (remyelination) affecting peripheral nerves.

Electromyographic (EMG) findings characteristic of axonal neuropathy, with normal or slightly decreased nerve conduction velocities, normal or slightly prolonged distal latencies, but significantly reduced motor potentials and sensory amplitudes. There may be spontaneous activity upon needle EMG studies, such as increased insertional activity, positive sharp waves, and fibrillation potentials.
Weakness of the muscles of the arms.

Upturning of the big toe (and sometimes fanning of the other toes) in response to stimulation of the sole of the foot. If the Babinski sign is present it can indicate damage to the corticospinal tract.
An abnormally increased diphosphate(4-) concentration in the urine. Diphosphate(4-), as ester with two phosphate groups, is also known as pyrophosphate.
An elevated concentration of a gonadotropin hormone (stimulating hormone or luteinizing hormone) in the urine, consistent with the diagnosis of primary hypogonadism.
The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against nuclei or nuclear components.
Cellular accumulation of GM2 gangliosides.

terms.it: Aumento del livello di IgM circolanti
terms.def_en: An abnormally increased level of immunoglobulin M in blood.
A kind of short stature in which different regions of the body are shortened to differing extents.
A mild degree of short stature, more than -2 SD but not more than -3 SD from mean corrected for age and sex.
A kind of short stature in which different regions of the body are shortened to a comparable extent.
A severe degree of short stature, more than -4 SD from the mean corrected for age and sex.

terms.en: Reduced ratio of renal calcium clearance to creatinine clearance
terms.def_en: A reduction of the ratio of renal calcium clearance to creatinine clearance to below 0.01.
lay_en: Reduced ration of kidney calcium clearance to creatinine clearance
syn_en: Reduced ration of renal Ca clearance to creatinine clearance
Reduced ration of renal Ca2+ to creatinine clearance

terms.en: Deficiency or absence of cytochrome b(-245)
syn_en: Deficiency or absence of cytochrome b

terms.it: Statura bassa sproporzionata rispetto al tronco
