terms.def_en: A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short trunk but a average-sized limbs.
A reduction in methionine synthase activity.
Formation of crystals owing to an increased concentration of orotic acid in the urine.
An increased concentration of prostaglandin in the urine.

terms.it: Elevata concentrazione di calcitonina in circolo
terms.def_en: Concentration of calcitonin, a 32-amino acid polypeptide hormone that is produced primarily by the parafollicular cells of the thyroid, in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

terms.en: Parathormone-independent increased renal tubular calcium reabsorption
terms.def_en: An increase in the reabsorption of calcium by the renal tubulus that is not associated with increased parathormone levels.
syn_en: Parathormone-independent increased renal tubular Ca reabsorption
Parathormone-independent increased renal tubular Ca2+ reabsorption

terms.def_en: The concentration of glutaric acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
syn_en: Elevated glutaric acid level in blood
Increased glutaric acid level in blood

terms.def_en: Level of ornithine in the urine above the upper limit of normal.
Decreased level of acetaldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH). ALDH and alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH) are the primary enzymes involved in alcohol metabolism.
An abnormal reduction in xanthine dehydrogenase level.
An increased amount of 3-methylglutaconic acid in the urine.
An abnormality of Krebs cycle metabolism that is characterized by a decreased rate of fumarate hydratase activity.
The concentration of uric acid in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
syn_en: Decreased uric acid level in blood
Reduced uric acid level in blood

terms.def_en: An increased level of iduronate-2-sulfatase activity in the blood.

An impairment in the rate and degree to which platelets aggregate after the addition of an agonist that stimulates platelet clumping. Platelet aggregation is measured using aggregometer to measure the optical density of platelet-rich plasma, whereby platelet aggregation causes the plasma to become more transparent.
Excretion of glycosaminoglycan in the urine. Glycosaminoglycans are long unbranched polysaccharides consisting of a repeating disaccharide unit.
The concentration of pyruvate in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
A functional motor deficit where individuals whose responses to the challenges of exercise fail to achieve levels considered normal for their age and gender.

terms.it: Debolezza dei muscoli del cingolo scapolare
terms.def_en: The shoulder, or pectoral, girdle is composed of the clavicles and the scapulae. Shoulder-girdle weakness refers to lack of strength of the muscles attaching to these bones, that is, lack of strength of the muscles around the shoulders.

terms.en: Subsarcolemmal accumulations of abnormally shaped mitochondria
terms.def_en: An abnormally increased number of mitochondria in the cytoplasma adjacent to the sarcolemma (muscle cell membrane), whereby the mitochondria also possess an abnormal morphology.
Any abnormality of the soft tissues, including both connective tissue (tendons, ligaments, fascia, fibrous tissues, and fat).
Localized fluid retention and tissue swelling caused by a compromised lymphatic system, affecting mainly the legs.
Reduced ability to climb stairs.
A condition in which muscles cannot be moved quickly without accompanying pain or spasm.
Atrophy (wasting) affecting primary type 2 muscle fibers. This feature in general can only be observed on muscle biopsy.

Fiber splitting or branching is a common finding in human and rat skeletal muscle pathology. Fiber splitting refers to longitudinal halving of the complete fiber, while branching originates from a regenerating end of a necrotic fiber as invaginations of the sarcolemma. In fiber branching, one end of the fiber remains intact as a single entity, while the other end has several branches.

terms.en: Increased variability in muscle fiber diameter
terms.it: Aumento della variabilità del diametro delle fibre muscolari
terms.def_en: An abnormally high degree of muscle fiber size variation. This phenotypic feature can be observed upon muscle biopsy.
syn_en: Increased variability in muscle fiber size
Increased variability in muscle fibre diameter
Increased variability in muscle fibre size
Increased variation in muscle fiber size
Increased variation in muscle fibre size

terms.def_en: Rhabdomyolysis induced by a viral infection.

The term dystrophy means abnormal growth. However, muscular dystrophy is used to describe primary myopathies with a genetic basis and a progressive course characterized by progressive skeletal muscle weakness and wasting, defects in muscle proteins, and histological features of muscle fiber degeneration (necrosis) and regeneration. If possible, it is preferred to use other HPO terms to describe the precise phenotypic abnormalities.

terms.it: Lunghezza alla nascita inferiore al 3° percentile

terms.def_en: The concentration of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
syn_en: Decreased low-density lipoprotein cholesterol level in blood
Reduced low-density lipoprotein cholesterol level in blood

terms.def_en: The presence of a folate sensitive fragile site at chromosome Xq28.

An increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). The ESR is a test that measures the distance that erythrocytes have fallen after one hour in a vertical column of anticoagulated blood under the influence of gravity. The ESR is a nonspecific finding. An elevation may indicate inflammation or may be caused by any condition that elevates fibrinogen.
An increased concentration of prostaglandin E2 in the blood.
A decreased level of glucose-6-phosphate isomerase.
Absence of molybdenum cofactor(2-), a cofactor for enzymes including sulfite oxidase, xanthine oxidoreductase, and aldehyde oxidase.
Increased concentration of proprionic acid in the blood circulation.
The concentration of citrulline in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
Increased concentration of total (conjugated and unconjugated) bilirubin in the blood.

A positive response to the regitine blocking test consisting of a substantial reduction in blood pressure following administration of regitine, indicative of the presence of increased levels of epinephrine and norepinephrine in the circulation, which is seen in pheochromocytoma-associated hypertension.
An abnormally increased sodium concentration in the cytosol.
Lack of urothione (the urinary metabolite of molybdenum cofactor) in the urine.
Increased concentration of 4-hydroxyphenylacetic acid in the urine.

terms.en: Foam cells with lamellar inclusion bodies
terms.it: Cellule schiumose con corpi di inclusione lamellari
terms.def_en: The presence of foam cells that contain lamellar inclusion bodies.
Increased cytoplasmic staining of fibroblasts with toluidine blue.
If positive, the ferric chloride test indicates an increased concentration of phenols in the urine or blood.
The presence of circulating autoantibodies to phospholipids.
Increased concentration of trimethylamine in the urine.
Congenital lack of development of the muscles, which are then replaced by a mixture of dense fat and fibrous tissue.

terms.en: Loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue in limbs
terms.it: Perdita di tessuto adiposo sottocutaneo negli arti
terms.def_en: Loss (disappearance) of previously present subcutaneous fat tissue in arm or leg.
lay_en: Loss of fat tissue below the skin in limbs
syn_en: Loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue from extremities

terms.def_en: Activity or concentration of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
The concentration of epinephrine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
The presence of foam cells, a type of macrophage that localizes to fatty deposits on blood vessel walls, in the central nervous system.
The presence of free hemoglobin in the urine.

terms.it: Profilo dell'isoforma di transferrina di tipo I
terms.def_en: Abnormal transferrin isoform profile consistent with a type I congenital disorder of glycosylation. In the traditional nomenclature for congenital disorders of glycosylation, absence of entire glycans was designated type I, and loss of one or more monosaccharides as type II.
syn_en: Abnormal isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin, type I pattern
Isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin consistent with CDG type I

terms.def_en: Abnormally reduced sulfite oxidase level.

Increased time to coagulation in the partial thromboplastin time (PTT) test, a measure of the intrinsic and common coagulation pathways. Phospholipid, and activator, and calcium are mixed into an anticoagulated plasma sample, and the time is measured until a thrombus forms.
Abnormally increased concentration of hydrogencarbonate in the urine.
A deficiency of the electron transfer flavoprotein-ubiquinone oxidoreductase.
An increased concentration of lactic acid in the urine.

Abnormality of glycosidase enzyme activity. Glycoside hydrolases (GHs), including glycosidases and transglycosidases. These enzymes constitute 113 protein families that are responsible for the hydrolysis and/or transglycosylation of glycosidic bonds.

The presence of foam cells, a type of macrophage that localizes to fatty deposits on blood vessel walls, where they ingest low-density lipoproteins and become laden with lipids, giving them a foamy appearance.
Recurring episodes of myoglobinuria, i.e., of the presence of myoglobin in the urine. This is usually a consequence of rhabdomyolysis, i.e., of the destruction of muscle tissue.

Metachromasia (also known as metachromacy) is a characteristic color change which certain aniline dyes exhibit when bound to particular substances or when concentrated in solution. For example, the basic dye toluidine blue becomes distinctly pink when bound to cartilage matrix. In the sense used here, the metachromasia refers to a change in color not observed with normal tissues, anomalous staining with the cationic dyes toluidine blue O and Alcian blue resulting from excessive amounts of the polyanionic glycosaminoglycans.
An abnormal reduction in dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (NADP+) level.
An abnormality of glycoprotein metabolism related to a decreased level of alpha-1,6-mannosylglycoprotein 2-beta-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase activity.
Reduced level of the enzyme beta-glucosidase, an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of glucosylceramide into ceramide and glucose.

Accumulation of granular osmiophilic material in blood vessel walls. Osmiophilic material becomes black upon staining with osmium tetroxide. Deposition of granular osmiophilic material (GOM) is the vascular pathological hallmark of CADASIL, which is the most prevalent hereditary small vessel disease and is caused by missense mutations in the NOTCH3 gene. GOM have been shown to contain NOTCH3 ectodomain (NOTCH3ECD) and extracellular matrix proteins, and can be visualized ultrastructurally in the tunica media of small arteries and capillaries. These electron dense GOM deposits are located in the basement membrane of mural cells, i.e. vascular smooth muscle cells and pericytes. In both manifest and pre-manifest CADASIL patients, GOM deposits are present not only in brain vessels, but also in vessels of other organs, such as the skin.
A decreased concentration of methionine in the blood.

terms.en: Amyotrophy of the musculature of the pelvis
terms.def_en: Muscular atrophy affecting the muscles of the pelvis.

terms.it: Fibre muscolari scheletriche a nucleazione centrale
terms.def_en: An abnormality in which the nuclei of sarcomeres take on an abnormally central localization (or in which this feature is found in an increased proportion of muscle cells).
An abnormally reduced activity of the enzyme cytochrome C oxidase in muscle tissue.
syn_en: Cytochrome c oxidase deficiency in skeletal muscle
Decreased activity of cytochrome C oxidase in muscle tissue
Decreased skeletal muscle cytochrome c oxidase activity

terms.def_en: The presence of multiple deletions of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA).
Reduced strength and weakness of the muscles of the arms and legs.
Abnormal protrusion of the scapula away from the surface of the back.
Muscular atrophy affecting muscles in the distal portions of the extremities.
syn_en: Distal amyotrophy, especially of the hands and feet
Distal muscle atrophy, upper and lower limbs

terms.def_en: Lack of strength of the proximal musculature occurring late in the clinical course.

terms.en: Absent epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
terms.def_en: Absence of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger.
lay_en: Absent end part of the outermost bone of the little finger
Absent end part of the outermost bone of the pinkie finger
Absent end part of the outermost bone of the pinky finger

terms.def_en: Muscular atrophy in the distribution of shoulder girdle and peroneal muscles.
Generalized (diffuse, unlocalized) amyotrophy (muscle atrophy) affecting multiple muscles.
A lack of strength of the proximal muscles.
lay_en: Weakness in muscles of upper arms and upper legs

terms.def_en: Enlargement of the muscles of the calf due to their replacement by connective tissue or fat.
Sudden and involuntary contractions of one or more muscles brought on by physical exertion.
Abnormal increase in muscle size and mass not due to training.
Abnormal cell death involving muscle fibers usually associated with break in, or absence of, muscle surface fiber membrane and resulting in irreversible damage to muscle fibers.
Myofibrillar structural changes characterized by abnormal intracellular accumulation of the intermediate filament desmin and other proteins.
Percussion-induced, local prolonged contractions (mounding) in muscle persisting for several seconds.
Hypertrophy (increase in size) of muscle tissue in a generalized (not localized) distribution.
lay_en: Generalized increase in muscle cell size
syn_en: Generalised increase in muscle cell size

terms.def_en: Weakness of the muscles involved in neck flexion (sternocleidomastoid, longus capitus, longus colli, and scalenus anterior).

terms.it: Atrofia dei muscoli del cingolo scapolare
terms.def_en: Amyotrophy affecting the muscles of the shoulder girdle.

A state of increased firmness (i.e., a reduced tendency to yield to pressure) of skeletal muscle tissue. This finding is ascertained by palpation and is to be distinguished from increased muscle tone (abnormal elevation in the resting tension of a muscle, leading to stiffness and resistance to movement).
Spontaneous, repetitive electrical activity demonstrated by electromyography (EMG).
Weakness of the quadriceps muscle (that is, of the muscle fasciculus of quadriceps femoris).
Muscle hypertrophy affecting the thighs.

The lysosomal-vacuolar pathway has a role in the controlled intracellular digestion of macromolecules such as protein complexes and organelles. This feature refers to the presence of an abnormally increased number of autophagic vacuoles in muscle tissue.
A type of myopathy associated with mitochondrial disease and characterized by findings on biopsy such as ragged red muscle fibers.
The occurrence of an unusually high amount of muscle pain following exercise.
Myotonia that occurs after a period of rest and decreases with continuing exercise.

terms.it: Debolezza dei muscoli del cingolo pelvico
terms.def_en: Weakness of the muscles of the pelvic girdle (also known as the hip girdle), that is, lack of strength of the muscles around the pelvis.
An abnormal, increased fatiguability of the musculature.
Recurrent episodes of muscle flaccidity, a type of paralysis in which a muscle becomes soft and yields to passive stretching.

terms.en: Type 1 fibers relatively smaller than type 2 fibers
terms.def_en: The presence of abnormal muscle fiber size such that type 1 fibers are smaller than type 2 fibers.
syn_en: Type 1 fibres relatively smaller than type 2 fibres

terms.def_en: A reduced amount of fat tissue in the lowest layer of the integument. This feature can be appreciated by a reduced skinfold thickness.
lay_en: Reduced fat tissue below the skin

terms.def_en: Congenital underdevelopment of lymph vessels.

terms.it: Contrazioni muscolari rapide da rotolamento indotte da percussione
terms.def_en: Mechanical percussion (i.e., striking a muscle with a reflex hammer) leads to spreading waves of muscle contractions that begin proximally and spread laterally across the muscle.
Formation of calcium deposits in any soft tissue.
lay_en: Calcium buildup in soft tissues of body

terms.def_en: A malformation of the uterus in which the uterus is present as a paired organ as a result of the failure of fusion of the mullerian ducts during embryogenesis.
Bruxism is characterized by the grinding of the teeth including the clenching of the jaw and typically occur during sleep.
A nevus is a type of hamartoma that is a circumscribed stable malformation of the skin.
A skin abnormality characterized by redness and irritation, with thick, red skin that displays flaky, silver-white patches (scales).
Episodes of muscle weakness.

Pulp calcifications may appear as punctate calcifications, irregular, roughly spherical mineralized masses in any part of the pulp. It may occur isolated or associated to calcifications elsewhere such as the carotid arteries and kidneys. The diagnosis pulp calcifications can be established using radiological studies.

A degree of kidney failure severe enough to require dialysis or kidney transplantation for survival characterized by a severe reduction in glomerular filtration rate (less than 15 ml/min/1.73 m2) and other manifestations including increased serum creatinine.
Pili (from Latin pilus, hair) torti (from Latin tortus, twisted) refers to short and brittle hairs that appear flattened and twisted when viewed through a microscope.

syn_en: Short body and ramus of mandible

terms.def_en: Excessive production of saliva.
A body habitus that is tall, slim and underweight, with long legs and long arms (i.e., arm span exceeds height by 5 cm or more).

terms.it: Diminuzione della concentrazione di acido omovanillico nel liquor
terms.def_en: Decreased concentration of homovanillic acid (HVA) in the cerebrospinal fluid. HVA is a metabolite of dopamine.

terms.en: Type 1 and type 2 muscle fiber minicore regions
terms.def_en: Multiple small zones of sarcomeric disorganization and lack of oxidative activity (known as minicores) in type 1 and type 2 muscle fibers.
syn_en: Type 1 and type 2 muscle fibre minicore regions

terms.def_en: Multiple small zones of sarcomeric disorganization and lack of oxidative activity (known as minicores) in muscle fibers.
Developmental hypoplasia (shortening) of middle phalanx of toe.
Irregularity of the iliac crest, which is the superior border of the wing of the ilium.
Muscular atrophy affecting the muscles of the limb girdle.

Nemaline rods are abnormal bodies that can occur in skeletal muscle fibers. The rods can be observed on histological analysis of muscle biopsy tissue or upon electron microscopy, where they appear either as extensions of sarcomeric Z-lines, in random array without obvious attachment to Z-lines (often in areas devoid of sarcomeres) or in large clusters localized at the sarcolemma or intermyofibrillar spaces.

terms.en: Muscle abnormality related to mitochondrial dysfunction

terms.it: Predominanza di fibre muscolari di tipo 1
terms.def_en: An abnormal predominance of type I muscle fibers (in general, this feature can only be observed on muscle biopsy).

Presence of abnormal vacuoles (membrane-bound organelles) in the sarcolemma. On histological staining with hematoxylin and eosin, rimmed vacuoles are popcorn-like clear vacuoles with a densely blue rim. The vacuoles are often associated with cytoplasmic and occasionally intranuclear eosinophilic inclusions.
An abnormally reduced amount of adipose tissue in the thoracic cavity.
A displacement or misalignment of the humerus with respect to the other bones of the should joint. Note that a subluxation is a partial dislocation.
A partial dislocation of the shoulder joint.
Formation of calcified tissue in the soft tissues surrounding the shoulder.
lay_en: Calcification of the soft-tissue around the shoulders
Abnormal shape of end part of upper limb long bones
syn_en: Abnormality involving the epiphyses of the upper limbs
Abnormality of upper limb epiphysis morphology
Epihyseal plate abnormality of the upper limbs

terms.def_en: A delay in the process of formation and maturation of the epiphysis of one or more long bones of the upper limbs.
lay_en: Delayed maturation of the end part of the upper limb bone
Fragmented end part of upper limb bones
syn_en: Fragmented epiphyses of the upper limbs

terms.en: Irregular epiphyses of the upper limbs
lay_en: Irregular end part of upper limb bones

terms.en: Round epiphyses of the upper limbs
lay_en: Round end part of upper limb bones

terms.en: Small epiphyses of the upper limbs
lay_en: Small end part of upper limb bones

terms.en: Wide epiphyseal plates of the upper limbs
lay_en: Broad growth plates of upper limbs
syn_en: Broad epiphyseal plates of the upper limbs

terms.en: Cupped metaphyses of the upper limbs
lay_en: Cupped wide portion of the upper limb bone

terms.def_en: The presence of a splayed (i.e.,flared) metaphyseal segment of one or more long bones of the arm.
lay_en: Flared wide portion of the upper limb bone
syn_en: Flared metaphyses of the upper limbs

lay_en: Irregular wide portion of upper limb bones
syn_en: Irregular metaphyses of the upper limbs

terms.en: Lytic defects in metaphyses of the upper limbs
Normal density transverse bands in metaphyses of the upper limbs
Sclerosis with transverse striations in metaphyses of the upper limbs
Sclerosis of metaphyses of the upper limbs
lay_en: Increased bone density in wide portion of the upper limb bones

terms.en: Spurred metaphyses of the upper limbs
lay_en: Spurred wide portion of upper limb bone

terms.def_en: Increased width (breadth) of metaphyses of the arms.
lay_en: Broad wide portion of upper limb bone
syn_en: Wide/broad metaphyses of the upper limbs

terms.en: Cortical diaphyseal irregularity of the upper limbs
Cortical diaphyseal thickening of the upper limbs
Diaphyseal sclerosis of the upper limbs
terms.def_en: An elevation in bone density in one or more diaphyses of the arms. Sclerosis is normally detected on a radiograph as an area of increased opacity.
lay_en: Increased bone density in central part of long bone of upper limbs

terms.en: Broad diaphyses of the upper limbs
lay_en: Broad shaft of long bone of the upper limbs
Wide shaft of long bone of the upper limbs
syn_en: Wide diaphyses of the upper limbs

terms.def_en: Missing humerus bone associated with congenital failure of development.
lay_en: Absent long bone in upper arm
Angulated long bone in upper arm

terms.def_en: Clefting affecting the humerus.
lay_en: Notched long bone in upper arm

terms.def_en: A bending or abnormal curvature of the humerus.
lay_en: Bowed long bone in upper arm
Crumpled long bone in upper arm
Deformed long bone in upper arm

terms.def_en: Presence of more than one exostosis originating in one or both humerus bones. An exostosis is a benign growth the projects outward from the bone surface. It is capped by cartilage, and arises from a bone that develops from cartilage.
Destruction of an area of humerus bone due to a disease process, such as cancer.

lay_en: False joint (long bone in upper arm)
Increased bone density in long bone of upper arm

terms.def_en: Reduction in diameter of the humerus.
lay_en: Slender long bone of upper arm
Tapered long bone of upper arm
Triangular long bone of upper arm
Wide long bone of upper arm
Abnormal head of long bone in upper arm
Flattended head of long bone in upper arm

terms.def_en: An anomaly of the humeral epiphysis.
lay_en: Abnormality of end part of the long bone of the upper arm

terms.def_en: Lack of formation of bone in the epiphysis of the humerus.
lay_en: Absent maturation of end part of long bone in upper arm
syn_en: Absent ossification of the humeral epiphyses

terms.en: Advanced ossification of the humeral epiphysis
terms.def_en: Ossification of the humeral epiphysis at an earlier age than normal.
lay_en: Accelerated maturation of end part of long bone in upper arm

terms.def_en: A delay in the process of formation and maturation of the humeral epiphysis.
lay_en: Delayed maturation of the end part of the long bone in upper arm
syn_en: Delayed maturation/delayed ossification of the humeral epiphyses

lay_en: Flattened end part of long bone in upper arm
Irregular end part of long bone in upper arm

terms.en: Irregular ossification of the humeral epiphyses
lay_en: Irregular maturation of the end part of the long bone in upper arm
Large end part of long bone in upper arm
Round end part of long bone in upper arm
Small end part of long bone in upper arm

terms.en: Stippled calcification of the humeral epiphyses

terms.def_en: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in the humeral epiphysis.
syn_en: Stippled ossification of the humeral epiphyses

terms.def_en: Increased width of the humeral epiphysis.
lay_en: Wide end part of long bone in upper arm

terms.en: Wide epiphyses of the upper limbs
lay_en: Wide end part of upper limb bones
syn_en: Broad epiphyses of the upper limbs

terms.en: Abnormality of the humeral epiphyseal plate
lay_en: Abnormality of arm long bone growth plate

terms.def_en: Increased width of the humeral epiphyseal growth plate.
lay_en: Wide long bone of arm growth plate
Abnormality of the wide portion of the long bone in upper arm

terms.def_en: Fracture or fragmentation at the lateral portion of the metaphysis of a long bone. The radiographic appearance is that of a small corner of metaphysis separated from the metaphyseal edge by thin linear radiolucency. This feature can be observed in child abuse but fragmented appearance of the metaphysis or facture-like lesions can also be detected in the setting of certain skeletal dysplasias.

terms.en: Cortical subperiosteal resorption of humeral metaphyses

lay_en: Enlarged wide portion of long bone of upper arm

terms.def_en: Flaring (increase of width with a splayed appearance) of the humeral metaphysis.
lay_en: Flared wide portion of long bone of upper arm
Irregular wide portion of long bone in upper arm
Irregular bone maturation of the wide portion of the long bone in upper arm

terms.en: Lytic defects of the humeral metaphysis

lay_en: Pointed wide portion of long bone of upper arm
Hardening of wide portion of long bone of upper arm
Stiffening of wide portion of long bone of upper arm

terms.en: Sclerotic humeral metaphysis with longitudinal striations

lay_en: Sloping metaphysis of long bone of upper arm
Laterally sloping metaphysis of long bone of upper arm
Spurred metaphysis of long bone of upper arm
Square metaphysis of long bone of upper arm
Speckled calcification in metaphysis of long bone of upper arm

terms.def_en: An anomaly of the humeral diaphysis.
lay_en: Abnormality of shaft of long bone in upper arm

terms.def_en: An abnormal irregularity of the cortical surface of the diaphysis (shaft) of the humerus.

terms.en: Ground glass opacity of humeral diaphysis
Periosteal new bone of humeral diaphysis

lay_en: Increased bone density in shaft of long bone in upper arm
Slender shaft of long bone in upper arm

terms.def_en: Increased width of the humeral diaphysis.
lay_en: Broad shaft of long bone in upper arm
Wide shaft of long bone in upper arm

terms.def_en: An abnormal osseous union (fusion) between the ulna and the humerus.

terms.en: Abnormality of the joint spaces of the elbow
lay_en: Abnormality of the joint spaces of the elbow

terms.en: Narrow joint spaces of the elbow
lay_en: Narrow joint spaces of the elbow

terms.en: Irregular articular surfaces of the elbow joints

lay_en: Abnormality of end part of the elbow bone

Increase in width (breadth) of the ulnar metaphysis.
The total absence of the hand, with no bony elements distal to the radius or ulna.

A hand in which the fingers are of nearly equal length and deflected at the first interphalangeal joint, so as to give a forklike shape consisting of separation of the first and second as well as the third and fourth digits.

Deviated fingers is a term that should be used if one or more fingers of the hand are deviated from their normal position, either to the radial or ulnar side. A deviation of a finger can be caused by an abnormal form of one or more of the phalanges of the affected finger, or by a deviation or displacement of one or more phalanges.

An anomaly of the second finger, also known as the index finger.
An abnormal groove on the midline of the nose that may extend to the nasal tip.
This term groups together three conditions that presumably represent different degrees of severity of a midline defect of the nose or nasal tip.

terms.def_en: Congenital absence of a carpal bone.
The presence of more than the normal number of carpal bones.
Ossification of carpal bones at an abnormally early age.

The bone-in-bone sign is a radiographic finding produced by increased sclerosis (abnormally dense bone) occurring intermittently with zones of relatively normal bone density. This term should be used to describe such a finding in the carpal bones.
Carpal bones with irregular or fragmented margins.
Increased size of carpal bones.
Point-shaped (punctate) calcifications affecting the carpal bones.
Any structural anomaly of the scaphoid. The scaphoid is the largest bone of the proximal row of carpal bones. It is located on the same side as the thumb.

Variations in the development of carpal bones are uncommon, with the scaphoid bone typically forming from the fusion of the os centrale carpi and the radial chondrification center during embryogenesis. A bipartite scaphoid is a rare congenital disorder that occurs when these ossification centers fail to fuse.
Formation of bone tissue of scaphoid is less than expected for age.
Underdevelopment of the scaphoid.
Any structural anomaly of the lunate bone, which is located in the proximal row of carpal bones.
Osseous fusion of the lunate and triquetrum.
An anomaly of the trapezium, which is the carpal bone located at the base of the thumb.
Formation of bone tissue of trapezium is less than expected for age.
Underdevelopment of the trapezium.
A structural anomaly of the trapezoid bone, which is the smallest bone in the distal row of carpal bones.

terms.en: Delayed ossification of the trapezoid bone
terms.def_en: Formation of bone tissue of trapezoid is less than expected for age.

terms.def_en: Underdevelopment of the trapezoid.
A structural anomaly of the hamate bone, which is the ulnar-most bone located within the distal row of carpal bones, neighboured by the capitate bone radially.
A structural anomaly of the capitate bone, which is the largest of the carpal bones in the human hand.

Cupped wide portion of hand bones

For children from birth to 4 years of age, the palm width is more than 2 SD below the mean; for children from 4 to 16 years of age the palm width is below the 5th centile; or, the width of the palm appears disproportionately narrow for its length.

Any abnormality of the skeletal muscle cell. Muscle fibers are subdivided into two types. Type I fibers are fatigue-resistant and rich in oxidative enzymes (they stain light with the myosin ATPase reaction), and type II fibers are fast-contracting, fatigue-prone, and rich in glycolytic enzymes (these fibers stain darkly). Normal muscle tissue has a random distribution of type I and type II fibers.
Involuntary contractions of muscle leading to involuntary movements of extremities, neck, trunk, or face.
An abnormality of the endocardium.

terms.en: Abnormal anatomic location of the heart

An abnormality in which the cardiac ventricles depolarize too early as a result of an abnormality of cardiac conduction pathways such as an accessory pathway.
An abnormality of macrophages.
A reticulocyte abnormality.

terms.it: Diminuzione del livello di anticorpi circolanti

terms.it: Diminuzione del livello di IgG circolanti
terms.def_en: An abnormally decreased level of immunoglobulin G (IgG) in blood.
Abnormally reduced levels of aldosterone.
The presence of a fistula of the vagina.
The presence of a fistula connecting the urinary bladder to another organ or the skin. The fistula can involve the bowel, the vagina, or rarely, the skin.

A height below that which is expected according to age and gender norms. Although there is no universally accepted definition of short stature, many refer to "short stature" as height more than 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender (or below the 3rd percentile for age and gender dependent norms).
An abnormal increase or decrease of weight or an abnormal distribution of mass in the body.
Abnormally increased body weight.
Abnormally low body weight.
Severe weight loss, wasting of muscle, loss of appetite, and general debility related to a chronic disease.
Any structural anomaly of the vitreous body.
An abnormality of the anterior segment of the eyeball (which comprises the structures in front of the vitreous humor: the cornea, iris, ciliary body, and lens).

Abnormality of the anterior segment of the eyeball

A reduction in the magnitude or amount of ossification of the skull.
An abnormality of lymphocytes.

syn_en: Large vacuolated foam cells ('NP cells') on bone marrow biopsy
Large vacuolated foam cells on bone marrow biopsy

The presence of excessive redundant myelin in the peripheral nerve sheath.

The concentration of vitamin B12 (or one of its metabolites) in the blood circulation is outside the limits of normal.

terms.def_en: Abnormality of galactoside metabolism. A galactoside is a glycoside (a sugar moiety bound to some other moiety) containing galactose.
An abnormality of glycosphingolipid metabolism.

Defects in the lysosomal glycosidases or specific co-activators, result in accumulation of the substrates, such as glycosphingolipids, including gangliosides in GM1 gangliosidosis (Tay-Sachs disease) and GM2 gangliosidosis (Sandhoff disease).

Reduced function of the muscles required to generate subatmospheric pressure in the thoracic cavity during breathing: the diaphragm, the external intercostal and the interchondral part of the internal intercostal muscles.

This term applies to all changes in bone mineral density which (depending on severity) can be seen on x-rays as a change in density and or structure of the bone. Changes may affect all bones of the organism, just certain bones or only parts of bones and include decreased mineralisation as may be seen in osteoporosis or increased mineralisation and or ossification as in osteopetrosis, exostoses or any kind of atopic calicfications of different origin and distribution. The overall amount of mineralization of the bone-organ can be measured as the amount of matter per cubic centimeter of bones, usually measured by densitometry of the lumbar spine or hip. The measurements are usually reported as g/cm3 or as a Z-score (the number of standard deviations above or below the mean for the patient's age and sex). Note that measurement with this method does not reflect local changes in other bones, and as such might not be correct with regard the hole bone-organ.
syn_en: Abnormality of bone mineralisation and ossification

terms.def_en: A reduction of bone mineral density, that is, of the amount of matter per cubic centimeter of bones.
lay_en: Low solidness and mass of the bones
syn_en: Decreased bone mineral density Z score

Any deviation from the normal concentration of carboxylic acid in the blood circulation.

Any deviation from the normal concentration of fatty acid in the blood circulation.
An abnormality of the balance or maintenance of the balance of acids and bases in bodily fluids, resulting in an abnormal pH.
An abnormal concentration of leptin in the blood.

An abnormality of the enteric nervous system, which comprises two types of ganglia, the myenteric (Auerbach's) and submucosal (Meissner's) plexuses. The enteric nervous system functions to control gut movement, fluid exchange between the gut and its lumen, and local blood flow.

Any deviation from the normal concentration of nitrogen compound in the blood circulation.

The concentration of purines in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
An abnormality of temperature homeostasis.
Abnormality of glycosaminoglycan metabolism.
Abnormally diminished level of attention, responsiveness, or wakefulness.
A type of dystonia that is localized to a specific part of the body.

Loss of strength in the arm, leg, and sometimes face on one side of the body. Hemiplegia refers to a severe or complete loss of strength, whereas hemiparesis refers to a relatively mild loss of strength.
lay_en: Paralysis or weakness of one side of body

terms.def_en: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the nervous system.
A family of tumors arising in the embryonal remnants of the sympathetic nervous system, which includes neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroblastoma, and ganglioneuroma.
Neoplasms located in the blood and blood-forming tissue (the bone marrow and lymphatic tissue).
Abnormality of the anal canal.

terms.it: Anomalia del livello di fosfatasi alcalina
terms.def_en: An abnormality of alkaline phosphatase level.
Deposition of calcium salts in the aortic valve.
A pathological narrowing in the region above the aortic valve associated with restricted left ventricular outflow.
Abnormal calcification of the mitral valve.
A severe congenital heart defect characterized by underdevelopment of the left ventricle.

Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) with a short pulmonary trunk arises from the truncus arteriosus, giving rise to both pulmonary arteries.
Inflammation of the alimentary part of the gastrointestinal system.
An inflammation of the colon and small intestine. However, most conditions are either categorized as Enteritis (inflammation of the small intestine) or Colitis (inflammation of the large intestine).
A colon of abnormally small caliber.

A functional rather than mechanical obstruction of the intestines, associated with manifestations that resemble those caused by an intestinal obstruction, including distension, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, constipation or diarrhea, in an individual in whom a mechanical blockage has been excluded.

Polyp-like protrusions which are histologically hamartomas. These can occur throughout the gastrointestinal tract. Hamartomatous polyps are composed of the normal cellular elements of the gastrointestinal tract, but have a markedly distorted architecture.
A kind of congenital defect of the anterior abdominal wall in which the intestines are evident through the thin, lax, and protruding abdominal wall in affected infants.
A deficiency in the intake of energy and nutrients.
A reduced desire to eat.
Abnormal displacement or malposition of the anus.

The term peptic ulcer refers to acid peptic injury of the digestive tract, resulting in mucosal break reaching the submucosa. Peptic ulcers are usually located in the stomach or proximal duodenum, but they can also be found in the esophagus or Meckel's diverticulum. Infection with Helicobacter pylori and the use of non steroidal antiinflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or aspirin are the main risk factors of both gastric and duodenal peptic ulcers.
lay_en: Sore in the lining of gastrointestinal tract

terms.def_en: Congenital atresia of the pylorus.
An abnormality of the pylorus.
Obstruction of the intestine due to abnormally thick meconium.
An abnormality of the nipple.

terms.def_en: An anomaly in the ability to perceive and distinguish scents (odors).
lay_en: Abnormality of the sense of smell

terms.def_en: A decreased sensitivity to odorants (that is, a decreased ability to perceive odors).
Positioning of the nasal septum to the right or left in contrast to the normal midline position of the nasal septum.
An abnormality of the pulmonary artery.
An abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.

Intermittent claudication is a symptom of peripheral arterial occlusive disease. After having walked over a distance which is individually characteristic, the patients experience pain or cramps in the calves, feet or thighs which typically subsides on standing still.
Inflammation of a vein associated with venous thrombosis (blood clot formation within the vein).
Repeated episodes of inflammation of a vein associated with venous thrombosis (blood clot formation within the vein).
The formation of a blood clot inside an artery.
Abnormal increase in systolic blood pressure.
A narrowing of the biparietal diameter (i.e., of the transverse distance between the protuberances of the two parietal bones of the skull).

Cranium bifidum occultum, also known as Catlin mark, is a congenital midline skull defect presenting as an enlarged posterior fontanelle in the upper posterior angle of the parietal bone close to the intersection of the sagittal and lambdoid sutures. Cranium bifidum occultum occurs due to a defect in intramembranous ossification, a process through which skull bones (frontal, parietal, squamous temporal and occipital bones superior to the mendosal suture) ossify under a vascularized membrane toward the midline to cover the brain. Unlike cranium bifidum cysticum, cranium bifidum occultum does not have herniation of intracranial contents. As the skull grows, the midline cranium bifidum occultum defect is separated into bilateral enlarged parietal foramina (EPF) by a midline osseous bridge.
A forehead with abnormal flatness.

An abnormality of the cheek- one of two bilateral soft tissue facial structures in the region of the face inferior to the eyes and between the nose and the ear. "Buccal" means relating to the cheek. The cheek is part of the midface

This is a description previously used to describe a facial form characterized by a short, upturned nose, wide mouth, widely spaced eyes, and full cheeks. Because of the imprecision in this definition it is preferable to describe these features precisely. This term is retained because it was often used in the past, but it should not be used for new annotations.
Increased susceptibility to viral infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of viral infection.
A type of primary immune deficiency that is characterized by a more severe defect in both the T- and B-lymphocyte systems.
An immunodeficiency defined by the absent or suboptimal functioning of one of the complement system proteins.
A lasting absence of total IgG and total IgA and total IgM in the blood circulation, whereby at most trace quantities can be measured.

Deficiency of secretory IgA (polymers of 2-4 IgA monomers are linked by two additional chains) and is the primary antibody response at the mucosal level, where it forms immune complexes with pathogens and allergens.
Concentration of the complement component C8 in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
Excessive growth of the bones of cranium, i.e., of the skull.
Bony overgrowth of the internal (endosteal) surface of the frontal bone.
lay_en: Thick inner surface of the frontal bone
syn_en: Excessive growth of inner surface of the frontal bone
Hyperostosis of the internal surface of the frontal bone
Overgrowth of the inner surface of the frontal bone

Premature closure of the coronal suture of skull.
A kind of craniosynostosis affecting the sagittal suture.
lay_en: Early closure of midline skull joint

terms.def_en: A kind of craniosynostosis affecting the lambdoidal suture.
The presence of erythrocytes that are sphere-shaped.
The presence of elliptical, cigar-shaped erythrocytes on peripheral blood smear.
The presence of erythrocytes with a mouth-shaped (stoma) area of central pallor on peripheral blood smear.
The presence of abnormally shaped erythrocytes.

Hepatic failure refers to the inability of the liver to perform its normal synthetic and metabolic functions, which can result in coagulopathy and alteration in the mental status of a previously healthy individual. Hepatic failure is defined as fulminant if there is onset of encephalopathy within 4 weeks of the onset of symptoms in a patient with a previously healthy liver.
A groove of the skin immediately in front of the ear.
lay_en: Skin groove in front of the ear
syn_en: Skin sulcus in front of the ear

terms.def_en: A rudimentary tag of ear tissue often containing a core of cartilage and located just in back of the auricle (outer part of the ear).

terms.en: Abnormality of the middle ear ossicles
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the middle-ear ossicles (three small bones called malleus, incus, and stapes) that are contained within the middle ear and serve to transmit sounds from the air to the fluid-filled labyrinth (cochlea).
A condition in which the superior portion of the helix is folded over to a greater degree than normal.
The presence of a dilated inner part of external acoustic meatus.

terms.en: Exostosis of the external auditory canal
terms.def_en: A benign bony growth projecting outward from a bone surface within the external auditory canal.
Pits in the earlobes at the location where ears are typically pierced for earrings.
Lack of measurable response to stimulation of auditory evoked potentials.
Benign congenital lesion of the postauricular soft tissue consisting of a blind-ending narrow tube or pit.

terms.en: Delayed brainstem auditory evoked response conduction time

Small indentation anterior to the insertion of the ear.
lay_en: Pit in front of the ear

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the C-shaped rings of hyaline cartilage, normally 16 to 20 in number, that occupy the anterior two-thirds of the circumference of the trachea (the posterior portion of the ring is completed by fibrous and smooth muscle tissue).
Chronic inflammation of the bronchi.
A congenital defect in the occipital region of the skull, covered by skin of the scalp and containing meninges or remnants of glial or neural tissues.

terms.en: Aplasia cutis congenita over the scalp vertex
terms.def_en: A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin on the scalp vertex, often just lateral to the midline.
Hyperostosis (bony overgrowth) of the mandible.
The anterior fontanelle generally ossifies by around the 18th month of life. A persistent open anterior fontanelle is diagnosed if closure is delayed beyond this age.

terms.en: Aplasia cutis congenita over parietal area
terms.def_en: A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin on the scalp in the parietal area.
syn_en: Absent cutis congenita over parietal area

terms.def_en: The progressive development of an abnormally large skull.

A relatively mild degree of macrocephaly in which the head circumference is not above two standard deviations from the mean, but appears dysproportionately large when other factors such as body stature are taken into account.
Asymmetry of the bones of the skull and the face.
Stagnation of head growth seen as flattening of the head circumference curve.

A type of atrial arrhythmia characterized by atrial rates of between 240 and 400 beats per minute and some degree of atrioventricular node conduction block. Episodes of ventricular tachycardia that have a sudden onset and ending.
A form of atrioventricular (AV) dissociation (i.e., the atria and the ventricles are under the control of two separate pacemakers) with congenital onset.

Atrial fibrillation (AF) that cannot be successfully terminated by cardioversion, and longstanding (more than 1 year) AF, where cardioversion is not indicated or has not been attempted, is termed permanent.
Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) is an abnormally increased heart rate (over 100 beats per minute at rest) with origin above the level of the ventricles.

Episodes of atrial fibrillation that typically last for several hours up to one day and terminate spontaneously.

An acute leukemia characterized by the proliferation of both neutrophil and monocyte precursors.
An excessive division of the lobes of the nucleus of a neutrophil.

An abnormal increase in the binding affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen.

Repeated episodes of obstruction of blood flow due to an embolus, i.e., blood clot that has traveled from its point of origin within the blood stream.
The presence of erythrocytes that are sphere-shaped and reduced in size.
A type of acute myeloid leukemia in which abnormal promyelocytes predominate.
A form of severe hemolytic anemia characterized by erythrocyte morphology reminiscent of that seen in patients after a thermal burn.
A type of anemia characterized by an abnormally low concentration of hemoglobin in the erythrocytes and lower than normal size of the erythrocytes.

Decreased activity of coagulation factor XII. Factor XII (fXII) is part of the intrinsic coagulation pathway and binds to exposed collagen at site of vessel wall injury, activated by high-MW kininogen and kallikrein, thereby initiating the coagulation cascade.
A type of hemolytic anemia in which the Coombs test is positive.
The accumulation of transformed primitive hematopoietic blast cells, which lose their ability of normal differentiation and proliferation.
Bleeding that persists longer than the normal time following a surgical procedure.

A subset of acute lymphoblastic leukemia that results from a reciprocal translocation between the ABL-1 oncogene and a breakpoint cluster region (BCR), resulting in a fusion gene, BCR-ABL, that encodes an oncogenic protein with constitutively active tyrosine kinase activity.
Repeated episodes of the formation of a blot clot in a deep vein.
A type of megaloblastic anemia (i.e., anemia characterized by the presence of erythroblasts that are larger than normal) that improves upon the administration of folate.
Decreased alkaline phosphatase measured within leukocytes.
Reduced platelet count that occurs sporadically, i.e., it comes and goes.
An abnormality of coagulation related to a decreased concentration of vitamin K-dependent protein S. Protein S is a cofactor of protein C.
A type of anemia characterized by an normal concentration of hemoglobin in the erythrocytes and lower than normal size of the erythrocytes.
A type of anemia characterized by abnormally large erythrocytes with abnormally high amounts of hemoglobin.
Thrombocytopenia related to lack of or severe reduction in the count of megakaryocytes.
A type of megaloblastic anemia (i.e., anemia characterized by the presence of erythroblasts that are larger than normal) that improves upon the administration of thiamine.

terms.en: Elevated bone marrow ring sideroblast count
terms.def_en: Count of ring sideroblasts in the bone marrow above the upper limit of normal. Ring sideroblasts are nucleated erythroblasts with a pathologic accumulation of iron granules in the mitochondrial matrix. They can be detected by Prussian blue staining as blue perinuclear aggregates in bone marrow aspirate erythroblasts.

The presence of a fistula between the bowel and the perineum.
An abdominal hernia that occurs at a site of weakness in the abdominal wall resulting from an incompletely-healed surgical wound.
Pneumothorax occurring neonatally without traumatic injury to the chest or lung.
Lack of strength of the intercostal muscles, i.e., of the muscle groups running along the ribs that create and move the chest wall.
Episodic hyperventilation.
Increased susceptibility to respiratory infections in early life, as manifested by recurrent episodes of respiratory infections.

The term Maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY) was initially used for patients diagnosed with fasting hyperglycemia that could be treated without insulin for more than two years, where the initial diagnosis was made at a young age (under 25 years). Thus, MODY combines characteristics of type 1 diabetes (young age at diagnosis) and type 2 diabetes (less insulin dependence than type 1 diabetes). The term MODY is now most often used to refer to a group of monogenic diseases with these characteristics. Here, the term is used to describe hyperglycemia diagnosed at a young age with no or minor insulin dependency, no evidence of insulin resistance, and lack of evidence of autoimmune destruction of the beta cells.
syn_en: Maturity onset diabetes of the young

Increased pressure in the pre-hepatic portal vein.

Aortic dilatation refers to a dimension that is greater than the 95th percentile for the normal person age, sex and body size. In contrast, an aneurysm is defined as a localized dilation of the aorta that is more than 150 percent of predicted (ratio of observed to expected diameter 1.5 or more). Aneurysm should be distinguished from ectasia, which represents a diffuse dilation of the aorta less than 50 percent of normal aorta diameter.

A separation (dissection) of the layers of the extracranial portion of the internal carotid artery wall.
An abnormal connection between an artery and vein.
Abnormal twisting of arteries or veins.

Narrowing of peripheral arteries with reduction of blood flow to the limbs. This feature may be quantified as an ankle-brachial index of less than 0.9, and may be manifested clinically as claudication.

Underdeveloped, small left heart atrium
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with an symmetrical and concentric pattern of hypertrophy.

A congenital malformation of the aortic valve characterized by leaflet deformation.
Arteriosclerosis occurring at an age that is younger than usual.
