Reduction of the diameter of the coronary arteries as the result of an accumulation of atheromatous plaques within the walls of the coronary arteries before age of 45.
The presence of a bicuspid pulmonary valve.
An abnormal dilatation of lymph vessels in the pericardium.

A longer than normal interval (corrected for heart rate) between the Q and T waves in the heart's cycle. Prolonged QTc can cause premature action potentials during late phase depolarizations thereby leading to ventricular arrhythmias and ventricular fibrillations.

A reduced ejection fraction and an enlarged left ventricle chamber, the latter by an increased resistance to filling with increased filling pressures. Systolic dysfunction is clinically associated with left ventricular failure in the presence of marked cardiomegaly.
Synovial hyperplasia involves proliferation of mesenchymal stromal/stem cells and leads to synovial thickening, which can be observed radiographically.

terms.it: Limitazione del movimento delle grandi articolazioni

terms.def_en: Abnormally flat shape of the heads of the metatarsal bones.
lay_en: Flattened head of long bone of foot

terms.def_en: A sensation of stiffness in the joints that occurs following waking up in the morning.
Interphalangeal joint stiffness is a perceived sensation of tightness in the interphalangeal joints when attempting to move them after a period of inactivity.

terms.en: Aplasia of the abdominal wall musculature
terms.def_en: Absence of the abdominal musculature.
A recurrent infection of the GI tract with helicobacter pylori, a gram-negative, microaerophilic bacterium usually found in the stomach.
The occurrence of the full-thickness tear (perforation) of the wall of the esophagus.
Cyst-like space not lined by epithelium and contained within the pancreas. Pancreatic pseudocysts are often associated with pancreatitis.
Hypertrophy of the stomach.
Watery voluminous diarrhea resulting from an imbalance between ion and water secretion and absorption.
The presence of cyst of the intrahepatic bile duct.
Underdevelopment of the colon.

Leukoplakia is a precancerous dermatosis of mucous membranes analogous Leukoplakia is basically a chronic inflammatory hypertrophy in which anaplasia and malignant dyskeratosis may develop and subsequently advance to an invasive squamous cell cancer. The clinical diagnosis of primary anal leukoplakia is indicated by single or multiple slightly raised,irregular, marginated, grayish-white keratinized' patches in the anal canal. Tissue biopsy is necessary for confirmation.
The presence of abnormal calcium deposition lesions in the pancreas.
Blockage or impairment of the normal flow of the contents of the intestine towards the anal canal.
Increased susceptibility to Giardia lamblia infection of the intestine, as manifested by a medical history of multiple episodes of Giardia lamblia intestinal infection.
An abnormal reduction in the ability to masticate (chew), i.e., in the ability to crush and ground food in preparation for swallowing.
A congenital malformation characterized by the development of an additional organ or organ-like structure, i.e., an extra copy of the organ normally located in the abdomen.
The presence of a fistula (abnormal tunnel) between the anal canal and the perineum.
Absence of gastric intrinsic factor, which is normally produced by the parietal cells of the stomach, and is required for the absorption of vitamin B12.
syn_en: Intrinsic factor absent from gastric juice

terms.def_en: The presence of multiple diverticula of the intestine.
A collection of pus in the area of the rectum.
Accumulation of cell free, noninflammatony fluid within the wall of the intestinal tract producing uniform thickening of the mucosal folds.
Presence of multiple adenomatous polyps in the colon.
Obstruction affecting the biliary tree.
A chronic form of gastritis.
The presence of developmental dysplasia of the pancreas.
The presence of a hypoplastic gallbladder.
A developmental defect resulting in abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the jejunum.
A form of chronic pancreatitis that is characterized by calcification.
The presence of degenerative changes of the liver.
A congenital defect characterized by the lack of ganglion cells in the entire intestine, i.e., the aganglionic segment comprises the entire large and small bowel.
Atresia in the extrahepatic bile duct.
Failure to form of portions of the abdominal musculature.

lay_en: Death of digestive organ tissue due to poor blood supply

terms.def_en: Developmental hypoplasia of the intestine.
A type of gastritis characterized by excessive proliferation of the gastric mucosa and diffuse thickening of the gastric mucosal folds.

terms.en: Hypoplasia of the abdominal wall musculature
terms.def_en: Underdevelopment of the abdominal musculature.
Atresia in the intrahepatic bile duct.
Aplasia (congenital absence) of the pectoralis minor.

terms.en: Unilateral absence of pectoralis major muscle
terms.def_en: Aplasia (congenital absence) of the pectoralis minor on only one side of the chest.
syn_en: Unilateral aplasia of pectoralis major muscle

terms.en: Abnormal facility in opposing the shoulders
terms.def_en: Increased range of shoulder movement related to aplasia or hypoplasia of the clavicles that results in the ability to approximate the shoulders in front of the chest.
Hemorrhage occurring within a joint.

Any structural anomaly of the synovium, which is a membrane that lines the cavity of synovial joints and consists of a lining layer of macrophage-like synoviocytes and fibroblast-like synoviocytes, as well as a sublining of connective tissue. Synovial cells are thought to contribute to joint homeostasis by secreting various factors such as hyaluronic acid and lubricin important for joint lubrication and function, as well as disposing of the waste products.
The presence of inflammation of the gastric mucous membrane.
An abnormality of the gallbladder.
An abnormality of the jejunum, i.e., of the middle section of the small intestine.
A discrete abnormal tissue mass that protrudes into the lumen of the intestine and is attached to the intestinal wall either by a stalk, pedunculus, or a broad base.

terms.en: Premature delivery because of cervical insufficiency or membrane fragility

terms.def_en: Exaggerated bulkiness of the crease or fold of skin running from the lateral margin of the nose, where nasal base meets the skin of the face, to a point just lateral to the corner of the mouth (cheilion, or commissure).
Lack of the cartilage of the nasal septum.
lay_en: Failure of development of nasal septal cartilage
Decreased size of tip of nose

terms.def_en: Posterior positioning of the nasal root in relation to the overall facial profile for age.

syn_en: Decreased size of bridge of nose

terms.def_en: Abnormality of the nostril.

lay_en: Decreased size of internal carotid artery

terms.en: Intimal thickening in the coronary arteries

terms.def_en: A separation (dissection) of the layers of an artery.

Pseudocoarctation is a congenital anomaly of kinking, or buckling, of the aorta without a pressure gradient across the lesion. It is characterized by elongation and kinking of the aorta at the level of the ligamentum arteriosum.
Peripheral arterial stenosis with onset before the age of 50 years.
A rare congenital vascular anomaly that results when the left superior cardinal vein caudal to the innominate vein fails to regress.
Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of the carotid arteries.
Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the arch of aorta.
Formation of a blood clot (thrombus) inside a cerebral vein, causing the obstruction of blood flow.
The presence of a capillary hemangioma, which are hemangiomas with small endothelial spaces.
A type of vasculitis (inflammation of blood vessel walls) affecting large arteries such as the aorta and branches of the aorta.
A developmental defect characterized by the lack of formation of the pulmonary blood vessels.
Formation of excess fibrous connective tissue in the tunica intima (innermost layer) of arteries in the pulmonary circulation.

An arterial lesion that is characterized by either intimal fibroplasia, with neointimal lesions of cells and matrix deposition, or medial fibroplasia, in which there is loss of smooth muscle cells and increased deposition of collagen and proteoglycans in the medial layer.

terms.en: Anomalous branches of internal carotid artery

terms.def_en: Pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) more than 3 wood units, as defined by the current definition of pulmonary hypertension. 95% of individuals have a PVR of less than 2.4 wood units.
Inflammation of the blood vessels within the brain.

lay_en: Lack of facial fat below the skin

terms.def_en: A type of craniofacial dysostosis associated with abnormalities of the external ears, mirognathia, macrostomia, coloboma of the lower eyelid, and cleft palate. This is a bundled term that is left in the HPO now for convenience with legacy annotations but should not be used for new annotations.
Unilateral overgrowth of facial tissues, including muscles, bones and skin.
lay_en: Increase in size of half of face

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the gestures or movements executed with the facial muscles with which emotions such as fear, joy, sadness, surprise, and disgust can be expressed.

terms.en: Extension of hair growth on temples to lateral eyebrow
terms.def_en: A pattern of hair growth in which there is hair extending from the temples to the lateral eyebrows.
syn_en: Unusual hairline with hair growth on temples extending to lateral eyebrow

terms.def_en: Underdevelopment of the philtrum.
A degree of wrinkling of the facial skin that is more than expected for the age of the individual, leading to a prematurely aged appearance.
Recurrent partial dislocations of the mandible.
Decreased density/number and/or decreased diameter of lateral eyebrow hairs.
lay_en: Limited hair on end of eyebrow

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the complement system.
Abnormal bladder function (increased urge or frequency of urination or urge incontinence) resulting from abnormal functioning of the autonomic nervous system.
Underdevelopment of the urinary bladder.
Any structural abnormality of the carotid arteries, including the common carotid artery and its' arterial branches.
An abnormality of the structure of the veins that return deoxygenated blood from the body into the heart, i.e., the superior vena cava and the inferior vena cava.

Tracheal cartilaginous sleeve (TCS) is a rare congenital airway malformation in which distinct tracheal rings are replaced by a continuous cartilaginous segment. Vertically fused C- or O-shaped cartilaginous rings can extend from the subglottis to the carina or bronchus with little to no pars membranacea posteriorly. Comment:Tracheal cartilaginous sleeve has been associated with various craniosynostosis syndromes.
Inspiratory stridor is a high pitched sound upon inspiration that is generally related to laryngeal abnormalities.
Hypoplasia of the epiglottis.
A primary immune deficiency that is characterized by defects or deficiencies of T-lymphocytes that causes specific susceptibility to intracellular micro-organisms.
Increased susceptibility to herpesvirus, as manifested by recurrent episodes of herpesvirus.

terms.en: Decreased circulating complement factor I concentration
terms.def_en: Concentration of the complement component factor I in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Reduced functionality of the process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of a B cell. A B cell is a lymphocyte of B lineage with the phenotype CD19-positive and capable of B cell mediated immunity.
Absence of the thymus. This feature may be appreciated by the lack of a thymic shadow upon radiographic examination.
Increased susceptibility to chicken pox, as manifested by recurrent episodes of chicken pox.
A general term referring to a defect in immunity resulting from impaired antibody production.
Increased susceptibility to streptococcus pneumoniae infections as manifested by a history of recurrent infections by streptococcus pneumoniae.
An abnormality of the humoral immune system, which comprises antibodies produced by B cells as well as the complement system.

terms.en: Decreased circulating complement factor H concentration
terms.def_en: Concentration of the complement component factor H in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
An abnormality of the physiological functioning of B cells.
An immunodeficiency characterized by defective cell-mediated immunity or humoral immunity.
Increased susceptibility to Haemophilus influenzae infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Haemophilus influenzae infection.
Increased susceptibility to Neisseria meningitidis infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Neisseria meningitidis infection.
lay_en: Increased susceptibility to neisseria meningitidis infections

terms.def_en: A reduced ability of a B cell to become activated, i.e., the change in morphology and behavior of
Increased susceptibility to protozoan infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of protozoan infection.

A group of phenotypically heterogeneous genetic disorders characterized by profound deficiencies of T- and B-cell function, which predispose the patients to both infectious and noninfectious complications.

terms.en: Depletion of components of the alternative complement pathway
terms.def_en: An abnormal reduction in the components of the alternative complement pathway, such as the C3 protein or its cleavage products.

Increased susceptibility to opportunistic infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection by opportunistic agents, i.e., by microorganisms that do not usually cause disease in a healthy host, but are able to infect a host with a compromised immune system.
Increased susceptibility to coronavirus 229e, as manifested by recurrent episodes of coronavirus 229e.
An abnormal reduction of the cell motility of neutrophils.
Increased susceptibility to Candida infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Candida infection.

Abnormal decrease in the absolute number of T cells, commonly characterized as CD3+ lymphocytes, per microliter of blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These may include both TCR alpha/beta and gamma/delta T cells.
syn_en: Decreased absolute count of circulating T cells

terms.it: Aumento della conta delle cellule B
terms.def_en: The absolute number of B cells in the blood, per microlitre is above the upper limit of normal of the reference range for the appropriate sex and age-group.
Increased susceptibility to bacterial infections of the skin, as manifested by recurrent episodes of infectious dermatitis.
Persistent overgrowth of Candida albicans in the gastrointestinal tract.
The concentration of alpha-globulin in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.en: Decreased total CD8+ T cell proportion
terms.it: Diminuzione della percentuale di cellule T CD8-positive
terms.def_en: Abnormal decrease of cytotoxic CD3+CD8+ T cells, measured as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.
syn_en: Decreased proportion of CD8+ T cells
Decreased proportion of CD8-positive T cells
Decreased proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells

terms.en: Decreased circulating complement factor B concentration
terms.def_en: Concentration of the complement component factor B in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
Decreased or impaired activation of T cells in response to a mitogen, cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or an antigen for which it is specific.
Increased susceptibility to infection by gram-negative bacteria, as manifested by a medical history of repeated or frequent infections by these agents.
Concentration of the complement component C3 in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
Lack of detectible CD8-positive T cells
An abnormality of the functioning of any aspect of the alternative complement pathway.

Inability of the immune system to produce targeted, protective antibodies (immunoglobulins) against specific pathogens or vaccines in the setting of normal or near-normal serum levels of total IgG, IgA, and IgM and normal absolute counts of B cells and T cells.
An increased susceptibility to infections involving both the paranasal sinuses and the lungs, as manifested by a history of recurrent sinopulmonary infections.
Increased susceptibility to systemic pyogenic infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of systemic pyogenic infections.
Recurrent infections by bacteria of the genus Neisseria, including N. meningitidis (one of the most common causes of bacterial meningitis).

At birth, newborns are endowed with maternal antibodies. IgG production normally begins at the age of two months. A delay in recovery from this physiological hypogammaglobulinemia between the 3rd and the 6th month of life, and of recovery period between 18 and 36 months defines transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy.

terms.en: Recurrent infections in infancy and early childhood
terms.def_en: Recurrent infections at an early age with improvement in later childhood.
Hypoplasia of the maxillozygomatic complex.
syn_en: Decreased size of zygomaticomaxillary bone complex

terms.def_en: An increased density in the cranial sutures following obliteration.
The presence of a coronal suture (the cranial suture that separates the frontal and parietal bones) that is not ossified but rather wide open at an age when it is normally closed.
Abnormal increased size of the posterior cranial fossa.

Abnormally flat (obtuse) angle of the mandible. The angle of the mandibular, located at the junction between the body and the ramus of the mandible, is normally close to being a right angle. This terms describes an abnormal increase of this angle such that the mandible appears flatter than normal.
An increase in bone density affecting the calvaria (roof of the skull).
Aplasia or hypoplasia of the paranasal sinuses.
Lack (aplasia) of the ethmoidal sinus.
syn_en: Failure of development of ethmoid sinuses

terms.def_en: Normally, the posterior and lateral fontanelles are obliterated by about six months after birth, the anterior fontanelle closes by about the middle of the second year. This term refers to the situation in which the fontanelles close at an inappropriately early time point.
The presence of calcium deposition in the falx cerebri.
Abnormally increased density of craniofacial bone tissue.
Excessive growth (overgrowth) of the facial bones, that is of the facial skeleton.
lay_en: Increase in size of the facial bones

terms.def_en: Underdevelopment of the frontal bone.
lay_en: Decreased size of bone of forehead

terms.def_en: Reduced convexity of the occiput (posterior part of skull).
Bony fusion of malleus, incus, and stapes.
Abnormal reduction in ossification of the calvaria (roof of the skull consisting of the frontal bone, parietal bones, temporal bones, and occipital bone).
The presence of a sagittal suture (the cranial suture that separates the left and right parietal bones) that is not ossified but rather wide open at an age when it is normally closed.
Progressively increasing bone density of the skull base without significant changes in bony contour.
An abnormally decreased level of immunoglobulin E (IgE) in blood.

terms.en: Abnormality of the alternative complement pathway
terms.def_en: A deviation in any aspect of the alternative complement pathway.
An abnormality of the epiglottis.
Head circumference which falls below 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender because of insufficient head growth after birth.
lay_en: Development of small head that was not present at birth

terms.def_en: A fontanelle that is small for age.
Vertical bony ridge positioned in the midline of the forehead.
The postnatal development of an abnormally large skull (macrocephaly).

terms.en: Metopic suture patent to nasal root
terms.def_en: The frontal suture divides the two halves of the frontal bone in infants and usually fuses by the age of six years. The suture runs from the bregma (the point on the skull at which the coronal suture is intersected perpendicularly by the sagittal suture) to the nasion or nasal root. This term applies if the suture is widely patent from bregma to nasal root.

terms.en: Midline skin dimples over anterior/posterior fontanelles

terms.it: Aumento della fragilità osmotica dei globuli rossi

terms.def_en: A myeloproliferative disorder characterized by increased proliferation of the granulocytic cell line without the loss of their capacity to differentiate.

Normal adult hemoglobin is composed of two chains each of alpha and beta globin. Hb Barts (Hemoglobin Barts) is a tetramer with four gamma globin chains, and is essentially pathognomonic for one or another form of alpha thalassemia. Hb Barts has an extremely high affinity for oxygen, resulting in almost no oxygen delivery to the tissues.

terms.en: Monoclonal elevation of circulating IgM concentration
terms.def_en: Presence of a monoclonal immunoglobulin M protein in the serum.
A transient reduction in the number of erythroblasts in the circulation.
syn_en: Transient decrease in blood erythrocyte number

terms.def_en: Anemia characterized by abnormal intracellular inclusions, composed of denatured hemoglobin, found on the membrane of red blood cells.
Increased megakaryocyte number, i.e., of platelet precursor cells, present in the bone marrow.
A type of T-cell lymphoma in which cancerous T-cells may present in the blood (leukemia), lymph nodes (lymphoma), skin or in multiple areas.
Larger than normal size of erythrocytes.

A chronic form of disseminated intravascular coagulation in which a persistent weak or intermittent activating stimulus is present and destruction and production of coagulation factors and platelets are balanced.

Disseminated intravascular coagulation is characterized by the widespread activation of coagulation, which results in the intravascular formation of fibrin and ultimately thrombotic occlusion of small and midsize vessels.
A type of sideroblastic anemia that is alleviated by pyridoxine (vitamin B-6) treatment.

A malignant lymphocytic neoplasm of B-cell or T-cell lineage involving primarily the bone marrow and the peripheral blood. This category includes precursor or acute lymphoblastic leukemias and chronic leukemias.
Amount or activity of kininogen is below the lower limit of normal. Kininogen functions as a cofactor in the contact phase of the intrinsic blood coagulation cascade.
A reduced number of hematopoietic cells present in the bone marrow relative to marrow fat.

A type of actue leukemia with features characteristic of both the myeloid and lymphoid lineages. These leukemias are for this reason are designated mixed-lineage, hybrid or biphenotypic acute leukemias.

A unique clonal neoplastic disorder that is linked to trisomy 21, is restricted to neonatal period, and spontaneously regresses. It often has characteristics of megakaryocytic lineage and is associated with GATA1 mutations in myeloblasts.
A form of hemolytic anemia that can be triggered by exertion.

terms.it: Diminuzione del volume medio delle piastrine
terms.def_en: Average platelet volume below the lower limit of the normal reference interval.

A form of lymphoid leukemia or lymphoma in which too many T-cell lymphoblasts are found in the blood, bone marrow, and tissues. Leukemia or lymphoma classification depends on which feature is more prominent.
Persistent absence of detectable circulating granulocytes in the blood with no detected secondary cause. Usually a value of less than 50 granulocytes per microliter is considered to be an absence.
An abnormal prolongation (delay) in the time required by whole blood to produce a visible clot.

An abnormality of coagulation related to a decreased concentration of vitamin K-dependent protein C. Protein C is activated to protein Ca by thrombin bound to thrombomodulin. Activated protein C degrades factors VIIIa and Va.
Proliferation (excess production) of hemopoietically active tissue or of tissue which has embryonic hemopoietic potential.
A reduced count of megakaryocytes.

A chronic lymphocytic/lymphatic/lymphoblastic leukemia (CLL) is a neoplastic disease characterized by proliferation and accumulation (blood, marrow and lymphoid organs) of morphologically mature but immunologically dysfunctional lymphocytes. A CLL is always a B-cell lymphocytic leukemia as there are no reports of cases of T-cell lymphocytic leukemias.

The frontal suture divides the two halves of the frontal bone of the skull in infants and children and generally undergoes fusion by the age of six. A persistent frontal suture is referred to as a "metopic suture".
An abnormality of the zygomatic arch, also known as the cheek bone.

A slowly progressing leukemia characterized by a clonal (malignant) proliferation of maturing and mature myeloid cells or mature lymphocytes. When the clonal cellular population is composed of myeloid cells, the process is called chronic myelogenous leukemia. When the clonal cellular population is composed of lymphocytes, it is classified as chronic lymphocytic leukemia, hairy cell leukemia, or T-cell large granular lymphocyte leukemia.
The activity or concentration of a component of the kinin-kallikrein system is outside the limits of normal.

Normal hemoglobin synthesis is characterized by production of equal amounts of alpha and beta globins. This term refers to a deviation from this pattern and is the main characteristic of the various forms of thalassemia.
An anomaly of the form or number of cells in the bone marrow.
syn_en: Abnormality of bone marrow cell morphology
Anomaly of the bone marrow cells

terms.def_en: The presence of many cysts in the kidney.
A reduction in the count of nephrons per kidney.
A lack of differentiation between renal cortex and medulla on diagnostic imaging.
Reduced differentiation between renal cortex and medulla on diagnostic imaging.
syn_en: Loss of definition of corticomedullary differentiation

terms.def_en: High urine magnesium in the presence of hypomagnesemia.

syn_en: Increased percent tubular reabsorption of phosphorus

terms.def_en: A type of proximal renal tubulopathy characterized by resorption defects leading to glycosuria, aminoaciduria, tubular proteinuria, renal hypophosphatemia, and urate tubular hyporeabsorption without bicarbonate loss.

A thrombotic microangiopathy with presence of non-immune, intravascular hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia and acute kidney injury. A vicious cycle of complement activation, endothelial cell damage, platelet activation, and thrombosis is the hallmark of the disease.

A progressive detrimental connective tissue deposition (fibrosis) on the kidney parenchyma involving the tubules and interstitial tissue of the kidney. Tubulointerstitial injury in the kidney is complex, involving a number of independent and overlapping cellular and molecular pathways, with renal interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (IF/TA) as the final common pathway. However, IF and TA are separable, as shown by the profound TA in renal artery stenosis, which characteristically has little or no fibrosis (or inflammation). For new annotations it is preferable to annotate to the specific HPO terms for Renal interstitial fibrosis and/or Renal tubular atrophy.

terms.en: Impaired renal tubular reabsorption of chloride
terms.def_en: Any impairment of reabsorption of chloride by the kidney.
A duplication of the renal pelvis.
DIsruption and breaking up of the basement membrane of the tubules of the kidney.
syn_en: Disintegration of the tubular basement membrane

terms.def_en: A type of carcinoma of the kidney with origin in the epithelium of the proximal convoluted renal tubule.
lay_en: Cancer starting in small tubes in kidneys

terms.def_en: A focal type of palmoplantar keratoderma in which only certain areas of the palms and soles are affected.
The presence of large spherical melanosomes (1 to 6 micrometer in diameter) in the cytoplasm of melanocytes.

terms.en: Macular hypopigmented whorls, streaks, and patches

terms.def_en: Loss of all scalp hair with congenital onset.

terms.en: Facial telangiectasia in butterfly midface distribution
terms.def_en: Telangiectases (small dilated blood vessels) located near the surface of the skin in a butterfly midface distribution.
The giant congenital nevus is greater than 8 cm in size, pigmented and often hairy. A giant congenital nevus is smaller in infants and children, but it usually continues to grow with the child.

terms.en: Large cafe-au-lait macules with irregular margins
terms.def_en: Large hypermelanotic macules with jagged borders.
The presence of a bilobed gallbladder, related to a duplication of the gallbladder primordium.
Absence or underdevelopment of the femur.

An abnormally increased rate of skeletal maturation. Accelerated skeletal maturation can be diagnosed on the basis of an estimation of the bone age from radiographs of specific bones in the human body.
syn_en: Premature fusion of the epiphyseal growth plate

terms.def_en: Hyperconvexity of the thoracolumbar spine producing a rounded or humped appearance.
The ability of the interphalangeal joints to move beyond their normal range of motion.

An anomalous trapezoidal appearance of a vertebral body. A trapezoid is a four-sided shape that has two sides that are parallel and two sides that are not parallel. In this case, the two lateral sides of the vertebra are parallel, and the top and the bottom are slanted with respect to each other such that the vertebra is shorter in the front or back than on the other side.
Increased cross-section (diameter) of the long bones. Note that widening may primarily affect specific regions of long bones (e.g., diaphysis or metaphysis), but this should be coded separately.

Acalvaria is an extremely rare congenital malformation characterized by an absence of flat bones of skull, dura mater, and associated muscles in the presence of normal cranial contents and facial bones.
Osteoporosis affecting predominantly the vertebrae.
Bony fusion of the posterior part of the L5 vertebral body with the sacrum.
This type of brachydactyly is characterized by short and broad terminal phalanges of the thumbs and big toes.

terms.en: Decreased anterioposterior diameter of lumbar vertebral bodies

terms.def_en: The ability of the joints of the hand to move beyond their normal range of motion.
Underdevelopment (hypoplasia) of the third toe.
The presence of abnormal calcium deposition of the intervertebral disk.
Underdevelopment of the ulna on both sides.
A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the second to the fifth fingers that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.
Sclerosis (abnormal hardening) of cortical bone, characterized by increased radiodensity.
Moderate osteoporosis.
Multiple exostoses originating in the fingers and toes.
A foot deformity resulting due to an abnormality affecting the muscle and soft tissue. In contrast if the bones of the foot are affected the term structural foot deformity applies.
Osteomyelitis caused by infection with the bacteria, salmonella.
Extreme thickening of the cortex of long bones.
Separation of the odontoid process from the body of the axis.
Deposition of calcium salts on both sides of the cerebrum.
An abnormality of the hand resulting from contracture of the palmar fascia with a fixed flexion deformity of the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints and the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints.
A tongue-like protusion from the anterior aspect of lumbar vertebral bodies.

Juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) is comprised of a heterogeneous group of several disease subtypes that are characterized by the onset of arthritis before the age of 16 years and has symptoms lasting at least 6 weeks.

An inherited primary limb malformation disorder characterized by congenital contractures of two or more different body areas and without primary neurologic and/or muscle disease that affects limb function.
Patchy (irregular) increase in bone density. This can take on many forms depending on severity and distribution as can be seen on x-rays.
syn_en: Patchy increase of bone mineral density

lay_en: Deformed head of long bone in upper arm

terms.en: Dysplastic distal thumb phalanges with a central hole
Partial fusion of proximal row of carpal bones
lay_en: Partial fusion of innermost row of wrist bones

terms.def_en: Supernumerary digits located at the ulnar side of the hand with a complete extra finger and extra metacarpal.

terms.en: Increased bone density with cystic changes

terms.def_en: A bilateral form of triphalangeal thumb.

terms.it: Sindattilia cutanea del 2-3 dito del piede
syn_en: Complete cutaneous syndactyly of second and third toes
Cutaneous syndactyly of second and third toes

lay_en: Flattened end part of knee bone

terms.def_en: Abnormal reduction in length of all metacarpal bones.
The ability of the thumb joints to move beyond their normal range of motion.
A form of triphalangeal thumb that cannot be placed opposite the fingers of the same hand.
An abnormal irregularity of cortical bone.

terms.en: Spinal stenosis with reduced interpedicular distance
terms.def_en: An abnormal narrowing of the spinal canal related to a reduction in the interpedicular distance (i.e., the distance measured between the pedicles on frontal [coronal] imaging).
syn_en: Spinal stenosis due to short pedicles

terms.def_en: Underdevelopment (reduced size) of the tibia.
Partial dislocation of the head of the radius in the posterior direction.

terms.en: Avascular necrosis of the capital femoral epiphysis
terms.def_en: Avascular necrosis of the proximal epiphysis of the femur occurring in growing children and caused by an interruption of the blood supply to the head of the femur close to the hip joint. The necrosis is characteristically associated with flattening of the femoral head, for which reason the term coxa plana has been used to refer to this feature in the medical literature.

terms.en: Osteosclerosis of the base of the skull
terms.def_en: An increase in bone density affecting the basicranium (base of the skull).

A limitation in the passive range of motion of a joint of the lower limb resulting from loss of elasticity in the periarticular tissues owing to structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules or skin.
syn_en: Contractures of the joints of the lower limbs

terms.def_en: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in one or more epiphyses during the neonatal period.
lay_en: Speckled calcifications in bone end parts in neonates

terms.def_en: Abnormal elevation of the floor of the posterior fossa including occipital condyles and foramen magnum.
An abnormally small and flat configuration of the posterior cranial fossa.
syn_en: Small and flat posterior fossa of skull
Small and flat posterior skull bones

terms.def_en: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the toes 2, 3, and 4.

terms.def_en: A swan neck deformity describes a finger with a hyperextended PIP joint and a flexed DIP joint. The most common cause for a swan neck-like deformity is a disruption of the end of the extensor tendon. Conditions that loosen the PIP joint and allow it to hyperextend, for example conditions that weaken the volar plate, can produce a swan neck deformity of the finger. One example is rheumatoid arthritis. Another cause are conditions that tighten up the small (intrinsic) muscles of the hand and fingers, for example hand trauma or nerve disorders, such as cerebral palsy, Parkinson's disease, or stroke.

lay_en: Small innermost upper end of calf bone
Underdeveloped innermost upper end of calf bone

terms.def_en: Absence of the patella.

terms.en: Multicentric ossification of proximal femoral epiphyses
Lateral displacement of the femoral head
terms.def_en: A developmental anomaly with lateral displacement of the femoral head.
Formation of bone in the patella later than normal.
lay_en: Delayed bone maturation of the knee cap

terms.def_en: Anomaly of the contour of the proximal epiphysis of the tibia such that its normally smooth appearance is irregular.
Partial dislocation of the ulna in the dorsal direction.
The ankle joint can move, passively and/or actively, beyond normal limits along its physiological axes.

Slipped capital femoral epiphysis is defined as a posterior and inferior slippage of the proximal epiphysis of the femur onto the metaphysis (femoral neck), occurring through the physeal plate during the early adolescent growth spurt.
lay_en: Slipped end part of innermost thighbone

terms.def_en: A generalized decrease in bone mineral density.

terms.en: Periosteal thickening of long tubular bones
terms.def_en: Thickening of the periosteum of long bone.
A limitation of the range of movement of the shoulder joint.
Decreased width of the diaphysis of long bones.
An abnormal anterior curvature of a long bone.

terms.en: Abnormality of the pancreatic islet cells
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the islet of Langerhans, i.e., of the regions of the pancreas that contain its endocrine cells. These are the alpha cells, which produce glucagon, the beta cells, which produce insulin and amylin, the delta cells, which produce somatostatin, the PP cells, which produce pancreatic polypeptide, and the epsilon cells, which produce ghrelin.
Any abnormality of the alveolar ridges (on the upper or lower jaws). The alveolar ridges contain the sockets (alveoli) of the teeth.
An abnormality of the dental pulp.
Exfoliation of a tooth more than 2 SD earlier than the normal age for the deciduous teeth and not related to traume or neglect. Exfoliation of a permanent tooth is per se abnormal.
Any abnormality of the primary tooth.
An abnormality of the morphology of the tooth.
The presence of an altered number of of teeth.
Agenesis of incisor.
An abnormality of the dental root.
A bending or abnormal curvature of a long bone.
A bending or abnormal curvature affecting a long bone of the arm.
An anomaly of the femoral metaphysis.
lay_en: Abnormality of the wide portion of the femoral bone
Abnormality of the wide portion of the lower-limb bone
Abnormality of the wide portion of shankbone
Abnormality of the wide portion of shinbone

terms.def_en: Absence or underdevelopment of the fibula.

terms.en: Aplasia/hypoplasia involving bones of the lower limbs
terms.def_en: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of the bones of the lower limbs.

terms.en: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving bones of the feet

terms.def_en: Absence or underdevelopment of the ulna.
syn_en: Hypoplasia or unilateral/bilateral absence of ulna

terms.en: Aplasia/hypoplasia involving bones of the upper limbs
terms.def_en: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of the bones of the upper limbs.
lay_en: Absent/small bones of the upper limbs
Absent/underdeveloped bones of the upper limbs

terms.def_en: Absence or underdevelopment of the patella.
An anomaly of a growth plate of a femur.
An anomaly of one or more epiphyses of one or both legs.
lay_en: Abnormal shape of end part of lower limb end bone
syn_en: Abnormality involving the epiphyses of the lower limbs
Abnormality of lower limb epiphysis morphology

terms.def_en: A small/hypoplastic or absent/aplastic radius.
syn_en: Absence or underdevelopment of the radius bone of the arm

terms.def_en: Absence or underdevelopment of the carpal bones.
Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of one or more forearm bones.
An anomaly of one or more epiphyses of a limb.
lay_en: Abnormal shape of end part of limb bones
syn_en: Abnormality involving the epiphyses of the limbs

terms.def_en: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of the humerus.
lay_en: Absent/small long bone in upper arm
Absent/underdeveloped long bone in upper arm
Abnormality of end part of shinbone

terms.def_en: Tracheal diverticula are blind-ended outpouchings arising from the trachea. They are usually an incidental finding. Occasionally they can mimic pneumomediastinum. Tracheal diverticula are either congenital or acquired, in the latter case the most common causes are prolonged increased intraluminal pressure, e.g. chronic cough, COPD, tracheomalacia, and iatrogenic (e.g. post-surgical).
An anomaly that is characterized progressive airflow obstruction that is only partly reversible, inflammation in the airways, and systemic effects or comorbities.
An abnormal high-pitched noisy sound, occurring during inhalation or exhalation caused by the incomplete obstruction in the throat.

Hypersensitivity pneumonitis involves inhalation of an antigen. This leads to an exaggerated immune response and a following inflammation of the alveoli within the lungs. The main feature of chronic hypersensitivity pneumonitis on lung biopsies is expansion of the interstitium by lymphocytes accompanied by an occasional multinucleated giant cell or loose granuloma. After exposure to the provoking antigen, following symptoms can be seen: fever, chills, malaise, cough, hemoptysis, chest tightness, dyspnea, rash, swelling and headache and can be completely reversible, based on the duration of the illness, categorized as acute (HP:0011009), subacute (HP:0011011), and chronic (HP:0011010).
Accumulation of amorphous PAS-positive material in the space between alveolar macrophages, sometimes as condensed form (oval bodies) are typically found in alveolar proteinosis.
syn_en: Detection of PAS-positive extracellular material in broncho-alveolar lavage

terms.def_en: Substantial narrowing or blockage of small pulmonary veins as a result of disorganized smooth muscle hypertrophy and collagen matrix deposition.
Adenocarcinoma of the Bronchus.

Abnormal dilatation of the pulmonary lymphatic vessels. Lymphatic fluid in the lung is derived from normal leakage of fluid out of the blood capillaries in the lung. In pulmonary lymphangiectasia, the pulmonary lymphatics are not properly connected and become dilated with fluid.

Lymphocytic interstitial pneumonitis is a benign lymphoproliferative disorder of the lung that is characterized by the presence of a dense, predominantly lymphocytic interstitial infiltrate (lymphocytes, plasma cells, other elements of the lymphoreticular system) that expands the alveolar septa.

According to the definitions of the American and British Thoracic Societies, including pulmonary functional tests, X-rays, and CT scans for items such as fibrosis, bronchiectasis, bullae, emphysema, nodular or lymphomatous abnormalities.
An abnormality of the pulmonary lymphatic chain.
Abnormality of the lung parenchyma extending to the pulmonary interstitium and leading to diffuse pulmonary fibrosis.
lay_en: Abnormality in area between air sacs in lung

terms.def_en: An increased susceptibility to pneumonia as manifested by a history of recurrent episodes of pneumonia.
A recurrent hemorrhage occurring within the lung.
Obstruction of conducting airways of the lung.
An increased susceptibility to bronchopulmonary infections as manifested by a history of recurrent bronchopulmonary infections.
lay_en: Recurrent infections in bronchi and lungs

terms.def_en: A type of pulmonary sequestration that is completely enclosed in its own pleural sac, occurring above, within, or below the diaphragm, and without communication with the tracheobronchial tree.

Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation, a condition most commonly associated with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, is an abnormal communication between the pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein without an intervening capillary communication. HRCT images usually show a coarse spidery appearance of the peripheral vascular markings in the lungs. More specific findings are obtained in the pulmonary angiogram where the normally invisible capillary phase is replaced by irregular vascular channels bridging the peripheral branches of pulmonary arteries and veins.

Hepatic failure refers to the inability of the liver to perform its normal synthetic and metabolic functions, which can result in coagulopathy and alteration in the mental status of a previously healthy individual. Hepatic failure is defined as acute if there is onset of encephalopathy within 8 weeks of the onset of symptoms in a patient with a previously healthy liver.
A diffuse form of hepatic steatosis.

terms.en: Decreased mitochondrial complex III activity in liver tissue
terms.def_en: Decreased activity of complex III of the mitochondrion in the liver.
The presence of abnormal calcium deposition in the liver.
Hyperplasia of the biliary tree, as manifested by increased size of bile ducts, dilated lumen, and histologically by an increased number of epithelial cells or hyperplasia.
Inflammation of the liver due to infection with a virus.

terms.en: Malformation of the hepatic ductal plate

terms.def_en: Intermittently increased size of the liver.
An abnormal increase in the amount of intracellular lipid droplets in hepatocytes.
An increase in the amount of glycogen stored in hepatocytes compared to normal.

terms.en: Reduced number of intrahepatic bile ducts
terms.def_en: The presence of reduced numbers of intrahepatic bile duct than normal.
An acute form of hepatic steatosis.
A type of cirrhosis characterized by the presence of large regenerative nodules.

Neonatal jaundice refers to a yellowing of the skin and other tissues of a newborn infant as a result of increased concentrations of bilirubin in the blood. Neonatal jaundice affects over half of all newborns to some extent in the first week of life. Prolonged neonatal jaundice is said to be present if the jaundice persists for longer than 14 days in term infants and 21 days in preterm infants.
lay_en: Prolonged yellowing of skin in newborn

terms.def_en: Fibroblast proliferation and fiber expansion from the portal areas to the lobule.

terms.en: Depletion of mitochondrial DNA in liver
terms.def_en: An abnormal reduction in the number of mitochondria in hepatocytes.
Repeated occurrences of acute noninflammatory encephalopathy and fatty degenerative liver failure.

The two portions of the clavicle (corresponding to the two primary ossification centers of the clavicle) are connected by a fibrous bridge that is contiguous with the periosteum, and a synovial membrane develops, resulting in a clavicle with a bipartite appearance radiographically. Congenital pseudarthrosis of the clavicle generally presents as a painless mass or swelling over the clavicle.
An abnormally straight configuration of the clavicle, a tubular bone which normally is doubly curved .
Prematurely closed sternal sutures.
Lack of development of the glenoid fossa, also known as the glenoid cavity, which is the articular surface of the scapula that articulates with the head of the humerus.
Bony fusion between the humerus and scapula, leading to an impairment in mobility of the affected shoulder joint.
lay_en: Fusion of shoulder blade to long bone in upper arm

terms.def_en: The presence of a paralyzed diaphragm.

terms.en: Irregular ossification at anterior rib ends

terms.def_en: Irregular surface of the normally relatively smooth border between the distal part of the ribs and the costal cartilages, which are bars of hyaline cartilage that connect the ribs to the sternum.
Early ossification of the costochondral junction, which is the joint between the ribs and costal cartilage in the front of the rib cage.
Underdevelopment of the middle portion of the clavicle.
lay_en: Underdeveloped middle portion of the collarbone

terms.def_en: A larger than usual distance between the left and right nipple.

terms.en: Decreased number of sternal ossification centers
terms.def_en: A less than normal number of sternal ossification centers. The sternum is initially formed from bilateral sternal plates that chondrify and begin to fuse with ribs at 10 weeks gestational age. Ossification starts in the manubrium and upper part of the sternal body at the 6th month, in the middle of the sternal body at the 7th month, in the lower part of the body during the 1st postnatal year and in the xiphoid process between years 5 and 18. The number of ossification centers vary up to six, and it is the ossification centers that are visualized by prenatal ultrasound. This term describes a reduction in the number of ossification centers compared with age-related norms.
syn_en: Decreased number of sternal ossification centres

terms.def_en: Lack of formation and mineralization of the ribs in utero.
Deposition of calcium salts in point-like foci within the anterior portion of one or more ribs.
Abnormal increase in density of the tissue at the costochondral junctions.
Breast carcinoma that is bilateral or otherwise multifocal.
Lack of formation of mineralized bony tissue of the sternum.

lay_en: Small distal segments of the shoulder blade
Underdeveloped outermost segments of shoulder blade

terms.def_en: Underdevelopment of the glenoid fossa, which is the cavity in the lateral part of the scapula which articulates with the head of the humerus.
Osteosclerosis of ribs (increased density related to increased bone mass).
Developmental defect resulting in congenital absence of the middle portion of the clavicle.

More than one fracture of the ribs. Callus formation around multiple rib fractures can produce a row of multiple rounded expansions (beadlike prominences) giving the appearance of beaded ribs. Note that rachitic rosary would have one bead per rib (a swelling at the costochondral junction), while beaded ribs in the context of multiple rib fractures have multiple beads (fractures) along the same rib.
Abnormally reduced diameter (cross section) of the clavicles.

Calcification of the costal cartilages, which are bars of hyaline cartilage found at the anterior ends of the ribs which serve to prolong the ribs forward and contribute to the elasticity of the walls of the thorax.
Chest wall pain in the area of the costochondral junctions.

terms.en: Thickening of the lateral border of the scapula
lay_en: Thickening of the lateral border of the shoulder blade

terms.def_en: Absence of the clavicles as a developmental defect.
An abnormal morphology of the ribs consisting of shorted, abnormally curved ribs. On posteroanterior chest radiography, the ribs show a curvature resembling that of a coat hanger (clothes hanger).
Increased time for the complex comprised of the Q wave, R wave, and S wave as measured by the electrocardiogram (EKG).. In adults, normal values are 0.06 - 0.10 sec.

Inflammation of the coronary arteries involving a granulomatous response, i.e., a non-specific inflammatory response involving granulomas, defined as a compact organized collection of mature mononuclear phagocytes including epithelioid and giant cells.

Premature ventricular contractions (PVC) or ventricular extrasystoles are premature contractions of the heart that arise in response to an impulse in the ventricles rather than the normal impulse from the sinoatrial (SA) node.
An abnormality of filling of a ventricle with blood during diastole.

terms.en: Ventricular preexcitation with multiple accessory pathways
terms.def_en: A form of ventricular preexcitation due to the presence of multiple accessory pathways for cardiac conduction.
The presence of excessive connective tissue in the endocardium.
Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of the aorta.
A bacterial infection of the endocardium, the inner layer of the heart, which usually involves the heart valves.
Calcium deposition in the myocardium.
A benign tumor of connective tissue containing mucous or gelatinous material (myxoma) localized in the pumonic valve.

terms.en: Short chordae tendineae of the tricuspid valve
terms.def_en: Abnormally short chordae tendineae of the tricuspid valve.
Steatosis in the myocardium.

terms.en: Early progressive calcific cardiac valvular disease

terms.def_en: A defect of the atrioventricular septum of the heart.
A localized outpouching of ventricular cavity that is generally associated with dyskinesia and paradoxical expansion during systole.
A type of cardiac arrhythmia with premature atrial contractions or beats caused by signals originating from ectopic atrial sites.
Acute occurrence of a dissection (tear within the tunica intima and entry of blood into the tunica media) of a coronary artery.
Any structural abnormality of the coronary arteries.
An abnormality of an atrioventricular valve.
An abnormality of the hepatic vasculature.
Absence or underdevelopment of the clavicles (collar bones).

terms.en: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving bones of the thorax

terms.def_en: A form of acute leukemia characterized by excess lympoblasts.
The presence of an adenocarcinoma of the pancreas.
Acute lymphoblastic leukemia of T-cell origin. It comprises about 15% of childhood cases and 25% of adult cases. It is more common in males than females.

A paraganglioma (previously referred to as chemodectoma) located in the retroperitoneal space. Paragangliomas (also known as extra-adrenal pheochromocytomas) are rare tumors that arise from extra-adrenal chromaffin cells. Paragangliomas are characterized by secretions of excessive catecholamines, including epinephrine, norepinephrine and dopamine, which may lead to clinical symptoms, including episodic hypertension, tachycardia and diaphoresis. However, between 40 and 50% of paragangliomas are non-functional.
The presence of an follicular adenocarcinoma of the thyroid gland.
A type of papillary renal cell carcinoma in which the papillae are covered by large eosinophilic cells with pleomorphic nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and nuclear pseudostratification.
A rare subtype of acute myeloid leukemia evolving from primitive megakaryoblasts.
The presence of an adenoma in the cortex of the kidney.
Pheochromocytoma not originating from the adrenal medulla but from another source such as from chromaffin cells in or about sympathetic ganglia.

terms.en: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin
terms.def_en: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin is a malignant tumor of squamous epithelium.

terms.en: Transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder
terms.def_en: The presence of a carcinoma of the urinary bladder with origin in a transitional epithelial cell.
A malignant neoplasm of the adrenal cortex that may produce hormones such as cortisol, aldosterone, estrogen, or testosterone.
Pheochromocytoma originating from the adrenal medulla.
A neurofibroma (benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor) localized adjacent to the spine.
A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the stomach.
The presence of leiomyosarcoma of the skin.
The presence of a malignant neoplasm of the genital system.
The presence of a carcinoma in the renal pelvis.
A slowly growing malignant neoplasm derived from cartilage cells.
The presence of renal cell carcinoma in the renal papilla.

A type of pituitary adenoma originating in prolactin secreting cells. This kind of adenoma is characterized by overproduction of prolactin, and may cause loss of menstrual periods and breast milk production in women.
A subtype of renal cell carcinoma thought to originate from mature renal tubular cells in the proximal tubule of the nehpron.
A malignant epithelial tumor with a glandular organization that originates in the duodenum.
A benign renal neoplasm composed of fat, vascular, and smooth muscle elements.
The presence of a papillary adenocarcinoma of the ovary.
A malignant plasma cell tumor growing within soft tissue or within the skeleton.
A non-malignant neoplasm of the genitourinary system.
A malignancy of the parathyroid glands. Parathyroid carcinoma usually secretes parathyroid hormone, leading to hyperparathyroidism.
A kind of thyroid adenoma characterized by the presence of oxyphil cells.
Underdevelopment of the paranasal sinuses.
Muscular dystrophy affecting the muscles of the limb girdle (the hips and shoulders).

terms.en: Loss of ability to walk in first decade
terms.it: Perdita della capacità di camminare nella prima decade di vita
lay_en: Loss of ability to walk in first decade

syn_en: Cystic lesions in the basal ganglia

terms.def_en: Any anomaly of the anterior horn cell.
syn_en: Abnormality of the anterior horn cells
Anomaly of the anterior horn cells

terms.def_en: Perceptual experiences that are vivid, intense, and sensory in nature occur in the absence of corresponding stimuli from the external environment.
Reduced amount of myelin in the nervous system resulting from defective myelinogenesis in the white matter of the central nervous system.

terms.en: Abnormal posterior periventricular white matter morphology
terms.def_en: An anomaly of the white matter of the brain localized in the region posterior to the cerebral ventricles.
syn_en: White matter abnormalities in the posterior periventricular region

terms.def_en: A type of focal clonic seizure characterized by sustained rhythmic jerking rapidly involves one side of the body at seizure onset.
Absence or underdevelopment of the vermis of cerebellum.

A form of lissencephaly in which the cortex is thickened and has four more or less disorganized layers rather than six normal layers resulting from incomplete neuronal migration during brain development. At neuropathological examination, a 4-layered cortex consists of an upper molecular layer, a second thin cellular layer containing pyramidal neurons usually observed in layer V, a third pale poorly cellular layer and a fourth thick deep layer made up of neurons which had failed to migrate. Radiologocally would manifest as agyria or pachygyria with cortical thickness greater than 10 mm.
A type of polymicrogyria with a gradient of severity (anterior more severe than posterior) extending from frontal poles posteriorly to precentral gyrus and inferiorly to frontal operculum.

terms.en: Pallor of dorsal columns of the spinal cord
terms.def_en: An abnormally pale appearance of the dorsal portion of the gray substance of the spinal cord. This finding can be observed by histological examination.
A severe degree of muscular hypotonia characterized by markedly reduced muscle tone.

terms.en: Developmental stagnation at onset of seizures
terms.it: Stagnazione dello sviluppo all'inizio delle crisi epilettiche
terms.def_en: A cessation of the development of a child in the areas of motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and/or emotional skills, following the onset of epilepsy.
A type of Horner syndrome with congenital onset.
Absence of the knee jerk reflex, which can normally be elicited by tapping the patellar tendon with a reflex hammer just below the patella.
Developmental defect characterized by a small and malformed corpus callosum.
Underdevelopment of the ventral portion of the pons.
Multiple neurofibromas of the spinal nerve roots with a symmetric distribution.
syn_en: Spinal nerve root neurofibromas, symmetric, multiple

terms.def_en: The occurrence of repeated episodes of generalized muscular hypotonia.
Wasting (atrophy) of the vermis of cerebellum.
A loss or impairment of the sensation of the relative position of parts of the body and joint position occurring at distal joints.
A severe delay in the acquisition of the ability to use language to communicate needs, wishes, or thoughts.

terms.en: Sensorimotor polyneuropathy affecting arms more than legs

terms.def_en: A type of holoprosencephaly in which most of the right and left cerebral hemispheres and lateral ventricles are separated but the most rostral aspect of the telencephalon, the frontal lobes, are fused, especially ventrally.
Underdevelopment of the cerebrum.
A symmetric and progressive loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers of the peripheral nervous system.
Atrophy affecting the pons and the cerebellum.
A hemangioblastoma of the cerebellum.
A diffuse loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers of the peripheral nervous system.

terms.it: Riduzione della sensazione di vibrazione distale
terms.def_en: A decrease in the ability to perceive vibration in the distal portions of the limbs.
Borderline intellectual disability is defined as an intelligence quotient (IQ) in the range of 70-85.
Atrophy (wasting, decrease in size of cells or tissue) affecting the frontotemporal cerebrum.
Hallucinations occurring during the transition from sleep to wakefulness.

Malfunction of the abducens nerve as manifested by impairment of the ability of the affected eye to be moved outward. Patients who develop abducens nerve palsy often present with binocular horizontal diplopia, which is a double vision when looking at objects side by side. There will be a notable weakness of the ipsilateral lateral rectus muscle leading to a deficit in of eye abduction on the affected side. Some patients may present with a constant head turning movement to maintain binocular fusion and to lessen the degree of diplopia.
The presence of calcium deposition within brain structures that is present already at the time of birth.
Atrophy of the frontal cortex.

terms.en: Intraaxonal accumulation of curvilinear autofluorescent lipopigment storage material
terms.def_en: Curvilinear intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material within axons.
Stiffness (a condition in which muscles cannot be moved quickly without accompanying pain or spasm) of the axial musculature.
Excessive number of small gyri (convolutions) on the surface of one side of the brain.

Brain damage related to a lowering of blood glucose below a critical level (around 30 mg/dl), which may lead to confusion, lethargy and delirium followed by seizures and coma. Prolonged hypoglycemia may lead to irreversible brain damage.
The presence of developmental dysplasia of the cortex of frontal lobe and the cortex of parietal lobe.
Pericallosal lipomas are congenital soft masses of adipose cells encapsulated by a thin layer of fibrous tissue, appearing adjacent to the corpus callosum of the brain.

Relatively short-lived periods of psychosis are characterized by the sudden onset of severe disturbances in perception, thinking, and behavior. These episodes typically last for a brief duration, generally ranging from a few days to a few weeks, and are often triggered by a significant stressor or traumatic event.
Nystagmus dating from or present at birth.

A reduced sense of touch (tactile sensation) on the skin of the distal limbs. This is usually tested with a wisp of cotton or a fine camel's hair brush, by asking patients to say 'now' each time they feel the stimulus.
A decrease in the ability to perceive vibration at the ankles. Clinically, this is usually tested with a tuning fork which vibrates at 128 Hz and is applied to the malleoli of the ankles.
A complete loss of the ability to perceive vibration.
An increased susceptibility to meningitis as manifested by a medical history of recurrent episodes of meningitis.
Hypoplasia of the cerebellum, pontine nuclei, and inferior olivary nucleus.

An abnormality of the auditory evoked potentials, which are used to trace the signal generated by a sound, from the cochlear nerve, through the lateral lemniscus, to the medial geniculate nucleus, and to the cortex.
Proximal spinal muscular atrophy, i.e., muscular weakness and atrophy related to loss of the motor neurons of the spinal cord and brainstem.
The presence of calcium deposition in the choroid plexus.

terms.en: Gait instability, worse in the dark
lay_en: Unstable walking, worse in the dark

terms.def_en: Periventricular leukomalacia is characterized by diffuse injury of deep cerebral white matter, accompanied in its most severe form by focal necrosis. The neuropathologic hallmarks of PVL are microglial activation and focal and diffuse periventricular depletion of premyelinating oligodendroglia.
A type of encephalopathy (brain disease, damage, or malfunction accompanied by an altered mental state) that is characterized by evidence of necrosis of brain tissue.
Deficit in grammar, including syntax and morphology.
Any abnormality of an individual's circadian rhythm that affects the timing of sleeping and being awake is referred to as a sleep-wake disorder.
Leukoencephalopathy that gets more severe with time.
A type of holoprosencephaly characterized by the presence of a single ventricle and no separation of the cerebral hemisphere. The single midline ventricle is often greatly enlarged.

Dysplasia and dysgenesis of the corpus callosum are nonspecific descriptions that imply defective development of the corpus callosum. The term dysplasia is applied when the morphology of the corpus callosum is altered as a congenital trait. For instance, the corpus callosum may be hump-shaped, kinked, or a striped corpus callosum that lacks an anatomically distinct genu and splenium.
A type of gliosis that occurs in the vicinity of injured neurons.
Focal proliferation of glial cells in the basal ganglia.

terms.en: Loss of Purkinje cells in the cerebellar vermis

terms.def_en: Progressive impairment of function of motor axons with muscle weakness, atrophy, and cramps. The deficits are length-dependent, meaning that muscles innervated by the longest nerves are affected first, so that for instance the arms are affected at a later age than the onset of deficits involving the lower leg.
The formation of small cavities in the tissue of the basal ganglia.

An abnormality of the ability (skills) to perform a precise movement of small muscles with the intent to perform a specific act. Fine motor skills are required to mediate movements of the wrists, hands, fingers, feet, and toes.

Paralysis of the fourth cranial (trochlear) nerve manifested as weakness of the superior oblique muscle which causes vertical diplopia that is maximal when the affected eye is adducted and directed inferiorly.

An abnormality of the ability (skills) to perform a precise movement of large muscles with the intent to perform a specific act. Gross motor skills are required to mediate movements of the arms, legs, and other large body parts.

terms.it: Disturbo da deficit di attenzione e iperattività
terms.def_en: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) manifests at age 2-3 years or by first grade at the latest. The main symptoms are distractibility, impulsivity, hyperactivity, and often trouble organizing tasks and projects, difficulty going to sleep, and social problems from being aggressive, loud, or impatient.
Inability to perceive painful stimuli.
Cerebral hemorrhage that occurs before birth.

Bilateral impairment of the function of the cranial nerves 9-12, which control musculature involved in eating, swallowing, and speech. Pseudobulbar paralysis is characterized clinically by dysarthria, dysphonia, and dysphagia with bifacial paralysis, and may be accompanied by Pseudobulbar behavioral symptoms such as enforced crying and laughing.
A morphological abnormality of the metencephalon.
A small, sac-like aneurysm (outpouching) of a cerebral blood vessel.

Cerebellar dysplasia (abnormal growth or development) is defined by abnormal cerebellar foliation, white matter arborization, and gray-white matter junction. Cerebellar dysplasia is a neuroimaging finding that describes abnormalities of both the cerebellar cortex and white matter and is associated with variable neurodevelopmental outcome. Dysplasia may globally involve the cerebellum or affect only one cerebellar hemisphere. In addition, cerebellar dysplasia may be associated with cortical/subcortical cysts.
A type of congenital malformation in which brain tissue protrudes through a defect in the anterior (front) part of the skull.

terms.en: Symmetric T2-signal increase with T1-signal decrease in the putamen
terms.def_en: A symmetric magnetic resonance imaing (MRI) abnormality of the basal ganglia characterized by an increase of signal intensity in T2-weighted images and a corresponding signal decrease on T1-weighted images.
Meningitis that persists for more than 4 weeks, and lymphocytes are present in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).
Partial or complete wasting (loss) of dentate nucleus.
Increased size of the basal ganglia.

terms.it: Anomalie multifocali della sostanza bianca cerebrale

terms.def_en: Hyperactive stretch reflexes of muscles that move proximal joints (elbow, knee).
Generalized atrophy or hypoplasia of the cerebrum.

terms.en: Aplasia of the inferior half of the cerebellar vermis
syn_en: Absent inferior half of the cerebellar vermis

terms.def_en: Progressive loss of previously present language abilities.

terms.en: Disorganization of the anterior cerebellar vermis
syn_en: Disorganisation of the anterior cerebellar vermis

terms.def_en: Stiffness of the limbs (a condition in which muscles cannot be moved quickly without accompanying pain or spasm) occurring in the proximal limb muscle.
Peripheral sensory neuropathy affecting primarily distal sensation.
Underdevelopment of the inferior portion of the vermis of cerebellum.
Increased vertical dimension of the corpus callosum. This feature can be visualized by sagittal sections on magnetic resonance tomography imaging of the brain.
Muscular rigidity (continuous contraction of muscles with constant resistance to passive movement).

terms.en: Decreased amplitude of sensory action potentials
terms.it: Diminuzione dell'ampiezza dei potenziali d'azione sensoriali
terms.def_en: A reduction in the amplitude of sensory nerve action potential. This feature is measured by nerve conduction studies.
An increase in size of the third ventricle.
Fasciculations affecting the tongue muscle and the musculature of the face.
Episodes of choreoathetosis that can occur following triggers such as quick voluntary movements.

terms.it: Malformazione di Chiari di tipo I
terms.def_en: Arnold-Chiari type I malformation refers to a relatively mild degree of herniation of the posteroinferior region of the cerebellum (the cerebellar tonsils) into the cervical canal with little or no displacement of the fourth ventricle. It is characterized by one or both pointed (not rounded) cerebellar tonsils that project 5 mm below the foramen magnum, measured by a line drawn from the basion to the opisthion (McRae Line)

terms.en: Hypointensity of cerebral white matter on MRI
terms.def_en: A darker than expected signal on magnetic resonance imaging emanating from the cerebral white matter.
Encephalopathy with onset in the infantile period.
A loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers from segments of the peripheral nervous system.
Demyelinating neuropathy is characterized by slow nerve conduction velocities with reduced amplitudes of sensory/motor nerve conduction and prolonged distal latencies.
Atrophy of the temporal cortex.
A type of encephalocele that occurs along the medial orbit wall at the level of the frontal process of the maxilla and the ethmoid-lacrimal bone junction.
A particular type of dementia characterized by a pattern of mental defects consisting prominently of forgetfulness, slowness of thought processes, and personality or mood change.
Amyotrophy (muscular atrophy) affecting the proximal musculature.
lay_en: Wasting of muscles near the body

terms.def_en: Acute progressive areflexic weakness and mild sensory changes resulting from myelin breakdown and axonal degeneration.
Neurodegeneration involving the globus pallidus,a part of the basal ganglia that is involved in the regulation of voluntary movement.

lay_en: Nerve damage causing decreased feeling and movement

terms.def_en: Muscular atrophy of distal arm muscles.
Stiffness of the limbs (a condition in which muscles cannot be moved quickly without accompanying pain or spasm) occurring in an asymmetric pattern.
A progressive degree of muscular rigidity (continuous contraction of muscles with constant resistance to passive movement).
Changes in one's level of awareness and responsiveness to their environment.

terms.en: Diffuse demyelination of the cerebral white matter
terms.def_en: A diffuse loss of myelin from nerve fibers in the central nervous system.

A form of gray matter heterotopia were the mislocalized gray matter is typically located periventricularly, also sometimes called subependymal heterotopia. Periventricular means beside the ventricles. This is by far the most common location for heterotopia. Subependymal heterotopia present in a wide array of variations. There can be a small single node or a large number of nodes, can exist on either or both sides of the brain at any point along the higher ventricle margins, can be small or large, single or multiple, and can form a small node or a large wavy or curved mass.
Episodic bouts of involuntary movements with dystonic, choreic, ballistic movements, or a combination thereof. There is no loss of consciousness during the attacks.
A complete lack of the ability to track objects with the ocular smooth pursuit system, a class of rather slow eye movements that minimizes retinal target motion.

Atrophy of the interosseus muscles (including the palmar interossei that lie on the anterior aspect of the metacarpals, the dorsal interosseus muscles of the hand, which lie between the intercarpals, the plantar interosseus muscles, which lie underneath the metatarsal bones, and the dorsal interossei, which are located between the metatarsal bones.
Reduced amount of myelin in the nervous system resulting from defective myelinogenesis in the peripheral nervous system.

terms.en: Focal T2 hyperintense basal ganglia lesion
terms.it: Lesione focale T2 iperintensa dei gangli della base
terms.def_en: A lighter than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the basal ganglia. This term refers to a localized hyperintensity affecting a particular region of the basal ganglia.

Loss of awareness of oneself or one's surroundings, involving (i) a loss of normal motor control is evident as flaccidity or stiffness, either of which can be accompanied by jerking movements, and postural control is lost so that patients fall if they are in an upright position; (ii) normal responsiveness is lost; and (iii) the patient experiences amnesia for the event. Loss of consciousness my be transitory (e.g., syncope) or prolonged.
A congenital absence of the convolutions of the cerebral cortex and a poorly formed sylvian fissure that affects a particular part of the cortex.
Facial diplegia (that is, bilateral facial palsy) with congenital onset.

terms.en: Neuronal loss in the cerebral cortex
terms.it: Perdita di neuroni nella corteccia cerebrale

terms.def_en: Bilateral tonic-clonic seizure of either generalized or focal onset occurring on or soon after wakening (typically within 90 minutes of waking, regardless of the time of day).
Recurrent episodes of hypersomnia (sleeping 16 or more hours a day) over a period of days or weeks.
The formation of the formation of fibrofatty lesions in the wall of an artery located in the brain.
Enlargement of all or parts of one cerebral hemisphere.
Generalized-onset tonic-clonic seizures that are provoked by flashing or flickering light.
Presence of irregular redundant loops of focally folded myelin in a peripheral nerve.
Complete loss of ability to move facial muscles innervated by the facial nerve (i.e., the seventh cranial nerve).
Muscular atrophy affecting the lower limb.
Episodes of muscle weakness associated with elevated levels of potassium in the blood.
Demyelination of peripheral motor nerves.
The presence of calcium deposition in the cerebral white matter surrounding the cerebral ventricles.

terms.en: Decreased distal sensory nerve action potential
terms.it: Ridotto potenziale d'azione del nervo sensitivo distale
terms.def_en: A reduction in the amplitude of sensory nerve action potential in distal nerve segments. This feature is measured by nerve conduction studies.

terms.en: Spinocerebellar tract disease in lower limbs

terms.def_en: Groups of small caliber axons in peripheral nerve biospies indicative of axonal regeneration.
A type of gait ataxia displaying progression of clinical severity.

terms.en: Decreased number of small peripheral myelinated nerve fibers
syn_en: Decreased number of small peripheral myelinated nerve fibres

terms.def_en: Alternating and recurrent weakness of the external ocular muscles.
Functional neurological abnormalities related to dysfunction of the pyramidal tract.

terms.en: Severe demyelination of the white matter
terms.def_en: A severe loss of myelin from nerve fibers in the central nervous system.
A form of lissencephaly characterized by an uneven cortical surface with a so called 'cobblestone' appearace. There are no distinguishable cortical layers.
A symmetric loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers of the peripheral nervous system.
Atrophy affecting the cerebellum and the spinocerebellar tracts of the spinal cord.
Agenesis of the midbrain.
Defective structure and function of myelin sheaths of the white matter of the brain.
An abnormality characterized by chronic impairment of the normal functioning of the axons.
Muscular weakness and atrophy related to loss of the motor neurons of the spinal cord and brainstem.

An atypical absence seizure is a type of generalized non-motor (absence) seizure characterized by interruption of ongoing activities and reduced responsiveness. In comparison to a typical absence seizure, changes in tone may be more pronounced, onset and/or cessation may be less abrupt, and the duration of the ictus and post-ictal recovery may be longer. Although not always available, an EEG often demonstrates slow (<3 Hz), irregular, generalized spike-wave activity.
An increased susceptibility to bacterial meningitis as manifested by a medical history of recurrent episodes of bacterial meningitis.

terms.en: Paucity of anterior horn motor neurons

terms.def_en: A cessation of the development of a child in the areas of motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and/or emotional skills.

terms.en: Facial palsy secondary to cranial hyperostosis
terms.def_en: Paralysis of the facial nerves on the basis of overgrowth of the cranial bones causing impingement upon the seventh cranial nerve.
syn_en: Facial palsy caused by enlargement of cranial bones
Facial palsy caused by excessive growth of facial bones
Facial palsy caused by overgrowth of cranial bones
Facial palsy secondary to hypertrophy of cranial bones

terms.def_en: Nystagmus consisting of horizontal to-and-fro eye movements, in which the movement in one direction is faster than in the other.
Fasciculations affecting the musculature of the arms and legs.
A discrete posterior fossa cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) collection that does not communicate directly with the fourth ventricle.

Oral-motor apraxia is the inability to volitionally sequence oral movements of the speech structure for nonspeech tasks in the absence of neuromuscular deficits such as paralysis or muscle weakness. Oral-motor apraxia is diagnosed when, despite intact sensory motor function an individual is unable to use these effector systems under voluntary control.
Bipolar disorder is an illness of mood characterized by alternating episodes of elevated and depressed moods, which are interspersed with euthymic periods.
A loss of myelin from nerve fibers in the central nervous system.

Loss of neurological function in a time frame that is considered relatively quick, for instance, loss of a develomental milestone or substantial exacerbation of neurological complications such as seizures or feeding difficulties within a few months.
