terms.it: Andatura a passi corti e scalcinati

terms.def_en: Multiple areas of darker than expected signal on magnetic resonance imaging emanating from the deep cerebral white matter.
A type of dystonia that affects all or most of the body.
Reduced ability to perceive painful stimuli.

A type of anterior encephalocele in which there is a protrusion of the contents of the skull through a breach at the point where the frontal and ethmoidal bones meet. Frontoethmoidal encephalocele can be divided further into three distinct categories: nasofrontal, nasoethmoidal, and nasoorbital.
Focal seizure characterized at onset by clonic movements affecting half of the face.
Underdevelopment of the frontal lobe of the cerebrum.

terms.en: Bilateral tonic-clonic seizure with focal onset
terms.it: Crisi tonico-clonica bilaterale con esordio focale
terms.def_en: A bilateral tonic-clonic seizure with focal onset is a focal-onset seizure which progresses into a bilateral tonic-clonic phase.
syn_en: Generalised tonic-clonic seizure with focal onset
Generalised tonic-clonic seizure with partial onset
Generalised tonic-clonic seizures with focal onset
Generalized tonic-clonic seizure with focal onset
Generalized tonic-clonic seizure with partial onset
Generalized tonic-clonic seizures with focal onset

terms.def_en: Recurrent episodes of brain dysfunction that may be triggered by factors such as metabolic disturbances or infections.
A saccade that overshoots the target with the dynamic saccade.
Weakness of the muscles of the legs.

terms.en: Diffuse swelling of cerebral white matter
Abnormal morphology of the limbic system
terms.def_en: Any structural anomaly of the limbic system, a set of midline structures surrounding the brainstem of the mammalian brain, originally described anatomically, e.g., hippocampal formation, amygdala, hypothalamus, cingulate cortex. Although the original designation was anatomical, the limbic system has come to be associated with the system in the brain subserving emotional functions. As such, it is very poorly defined and doesn't correspond closely to the anatomical meaning any longer. [BirnLex].

syn_en: Atrophic and degenerative changes in the spinal cord

terms.def_en: Increased intensity of the a reflex in the arm.
A type of tremors that is triggered by holding an arm in a fixed position.

A focal-onset seizure is a type of seizure originating within networks limited to one hemisphere. They may be discretely localized or more widely distributed, and may originate in subcortical structures.
lay_en: Seizure affecting one half of brain

terms.def_en: A structural abnormality of the pons.

terms.en: Atrophy/Degeneration affecting the central nervous system

terms.def_en: The presence of atrophy (wasting) of the cerebrum, also known as the telencephalon, the largest and most highly developed part of the human brain.
Absence or underdevelopment of the corpus callosum.
syn_en: Complete or partial absence of the corpus callosum
Hypoplasia or absence of the corpus callosum

terms.def_en: The presence of atrophy (wasting) of the corpus callosum.
Wasting involving the motor neuron.
An abnormality of the septum pellucidum, which is a thin, triangular, vertical membrane separating the lateral ventricles of the brain.
An abnormality of the choroid plexus, which is the area in the cerebral ventricles in which cerebrospinal fluid is produced by modified ependymal cells.

An abnormality of somatosensory evoked potentials (SSEP), i.e., of the electrical signals of sensation going from the body to the brain in response to a defined stimulus. Recording electrodes are placed over the scalp, spine, and peripheral nerves proximal to the stimulation site. Clinical studies generally use electrical stimulation of peripheral nerves to elicit potentials. SSEP testing determines whether peripheral sensory nerves are able to transmit sensory information like pain, temperature, and touch to the brain. Abnormal SSEPs can result from dysfunction at the level of the peripheral nerve, plexus, spinal root, spinal cord, brain stem, thalamocortical projections, or primary somatosensory cortex.
A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the gastrointestinal tract.
A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the genitourinary system.
Telangiectases (small dilated blood vessels) located near the surface of the skin of the face.

terms.it: Aplasia cutis congenita del cuoio capelluto
terms.def_en: A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin on the scalp.
Underdevelopment of the sweat glands.
A type of ichthyosiform erythroderma with postnatal onset.
Photosensitivity of the skin occurring early in life.
lay_en: Sun sensitivity occurring early in life

terms.def_en: Developmental hypoplasia of the apocrine sweat glands in the region of the axilla.
A nonspecific term denoting wasting, especially as a result of degeneration, of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and neurosensory retinal cells in the macula.

terms.en: Areas of hypopigmentation and hyperpigmentation that do not follow Blaschko lines

terms.def_en: Abnormal thickening of the skin on the palms and soles charactersized by hyperkeratosis of the stratum corneum with no evidence of epidermolysis characteristic of epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.

terms.en: Excessive skin wrinkling on dorsum of hands and fingers
lay_en: Excessive skin wrinkling on back of hands and fingers

terms.def_en: Increased susceptibility to infection by the protozan parasite of the genus Leishmania.
An abnormally increased perspiration on palms and soles.
lay_en: Excessive sweating of palms and soles

terms.def_en: Naevus flammeus localized in the skin of the forehead.

terms.en: Neonatal wrinkled skin of hands and feet
lay_en: Wrinkled skin of hands and feet in newborn

terms.def_en: Cutaneous lesion that develops as a dry, scaly, red patch that evolves to an indurated and hyperpigmented plaque with adherent scale. Scarring may result in central white patches (loss of pigmentation) and skin atrophy.
Loss of all scalp hair.
Spontaneous development of hematomas (hematoma) or bruises without significant trauma.
Telangiectases (small dilated blood vessels) located near the surface of the skin of the cheeks.
Telangiectasia (that is, the presence of small dilated superficial blood vessels) of the oral mucosa.
lay_en: Spider veins of the oral mucosa
syn_en: Angioectasia of the oral mucous membrane
Telangiectasia of the oral mucous membrane

terms.def_en: The presence of two to five cafe-au-lait macules.
Generalized abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin, or in one or more cavities of the body.
An ichthyosiform abnormality of the skin with congenital onset.
Hemangioma is a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells. This term refers to facial hemangiomas that have a plaque-like morphology.
The presence of multiple leiomyomas of the skin.

terms.en: Mottled pigmentation of the trunk and proximal extremities

terms.def_en: Absence of melanin pigment in various areas, which is found at birth and is permanent. The lesions are known as leucoderma and are often found on the face, trunk, or limbs.
syn_en: Congenital partial albinism on face, trunk, or limbs

terms.def_en: A type of blistering that affects the skin of the palms of the hands and the soles of the feet.
Diffuse abnormal thickening of the skin on the palms and soles.

terms.en: Increased groin pigmentation with raindrop depigmentation

terms.def_en: Inability to sweat on the same side of the face that is affected by ptosis and miosis. This is a feature of Horner syndrome.
Lichenification affecting primarily flexural areas of the skin.
Prominent thoracic and abdominal veins.
The spontaneous detachment of a digit (finger or toe) from the body due to long standing pathology.
Keratinization of the bulbar conjunctiva near the limbus (corneoscleral junction), resulting in a raised spot.
Reduced number or density of facial hair.
Abnormal thickening of the skin on the palms and soles with an honeycomb pattern.
Increased amount of keratin (visible as white scales) surrounding hair follicles.
Cutis gyrata of palms and soles.
syn_en: Cutis gyrata of palms and soles

terms.def_en: Subcutaneous nodules that are located in the vicinity of joints.

terms.en: Axillary and groin hyperpigmentation and hypopigmentation

terms.def_en: An ichthyosiform abnormality of the skin that presents at birth or shortly thereafter with generalized erythema, blistering, erosions, and peeling. In the subsequent months, erythema and blistering improves but patients go on to develop hyperkeratotic scaling that is especially prominent along the joint flexures, neck, hands and feet.
An abnormality of dermatoglyphs (fingerprints), which are present on fingers, palms, toes, and soles.

The term collodion baby applies to newborns who appear to have an extra layer of skin (known as a collodion membrane) that has a collodion-like quality. It is a descriptive term, not a specific diagnosis or disorder (as such, it is a syndrome). Affected babies are born in a collodion membrane, a shiny waxy outer layer to the skin. This is shed 10-14 days after birth, revealing the main symptom of the disease, extensive scaling of the skin caused by hyperkeratosis. With increasing age, the scaling tends to be concentrated around joints in areas such as the groin, the armpits, the inside of the elbow and the neck. The scales often tile the skin and may resemble fish scales.

terms.en: Decreased sweating due to autonomic dysfunction

terms.def_en: Lack of subcutaneous adipose tissue.
lay_en: Lack of fatty tissue below the skin

terms.def_en: Telangiectases (small dilated blood vessels) with a diffuse localization.

terms.en: Linear arrays of macular hyperkeratoses in flexural areas
Discrete 2 to 5-mm hyper- and hypopigmented macules

terms.def_en: Hyperkeratosis affecting the palm of the hand and the sole of the foot in areas exposed to friction.
Increased susceptibility to staphylococcal infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of staphylococcal infections.
The presence of fewer than normal sweat glands.

terms.en: Streaks of hyperkeratosis along each finger onto the palm

terms.def_en: A skin condition characterized by excessive development of keratin in hair follicles, resulting in rough, cone-shaped, elevated papules resulting from closure of hair follicles with a white plug of sebum.

terms.en: Congenital absence of skin of limbs
lay_en: Missing skin on limbs since birth

terms.def_en: Tiny bumps of thickened skin (hyperkeratosis) on the palms of the hands.

terms.en: Edema of the dorsum of hands
terms.def_en: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin on the back of the hands.
syn_en: Oedema of the dorsum of hands

terms.def_en: Loose and sagging skin of the fingers.
Loose, wrinkled skin of hands and feet.
lay_en: Excessive wrinkled skin of palms and soles
Increased wrinkles of palms and soles
Wrinkled skin of hands and feet

terms.en: Yellow subcutaneous tissue covered by thin, scaly skin

lay_en: Patchy loss of skin color on arms
syn_en: Patchy loss of skin colour on arms

terms.def_en: Loss of hair in the occipital region of the scalp with congenital onset.

terms.en: Aplasia cutis congenita of midline scalp vertex

terms.def_en: A severe degree of photosensitivity of the skin.
Presence of a cutaneous lipoma on the forehead.

terms.en: Absent pigmentation of the ventral chest
terms.def_en: Lack of skin pigmentation (coloring) of the anterior chest.

Congenital large depigmented (white) macule of irergular rhomboid shape. Piebald skin depigmentation generally presents with multiple such macules in the affected individual. There may be smaller (5-15mm), discrete, skin-colored and hyperpigmented macules interspersed within the depigmented macules.
Abnormal thickening of the skin on the palms and soles that is present at birth.

terms.en: Desquamation of skin soon after birth

lay_en: Lack of sweating or excessive sweating
Abnormal fat tissue distribution below the skin

terms.en: Confetti hypopigmentation pattern of lower leg skin
lay_en: Confetti hypopigmentation pattern of lower leg skin

terms.def_en: Hyperkeratosis affecting the sole of the foot.
The presence of six or more cafe-au-lait spots.
lay_en: Multiple flat light-brown marks on skin

terms.def_en: Seborrheic dermatitis that is not localized to any one particular region.

Hyperkeratosis lenticularis perstans (HLP), also known as Flegel disease, is a keratinization abnormality characterized by small, asymptomatic erythematous papules that leave characteristic punctate bleeding when they become detached. The lesions generally occur symmetrically along the top of the foot and on the legs, appearing more rarely on the arms, forearms, palms, and soles, and even on the oral mucosa.
A form of atopic dermatitis with onset in adulthood characterized by atopic red face, chronic lichenified eczema on the trunk, subacute or psoriasiform dermatitis.
A neurofibroma (benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor) localized in the palm of the hand.
Increased pigmentation of the skin with a netlike (reticular) pattern.

terms.en: Aplasia cutis congenita on trunk or limbs
terms.def_en: A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin on the trunk or the limbs.

terms.en: Aplasia cutis congenita over posterior parietal area
Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the eccrine sweat glands
terms.def_en: Absence or developmental hypoplasia of the eccrine sweat glands.
The presence of multiple subcutaneous lipoma that cause pain.
lay_en: Painful noncancerous fat tissue tumor under the skin
syn_en: Painful noncancerous fat tissue tumour under the skin

terms.def_en: The distal and proximal transverse palmar creases are merged into a single transverse palmar crease on both hands.
An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin, or in one or more cavities of the body because of decreased osmotic pressure of plasma (hypoproteinemia).

terms.en: Spinous keratoses of palms and soles

terms.def_en: Naevus flammeus localized in the skin of the neck. This is one of the most common birthmarks and present in approximately 25% of all newborns.
Deposition of calcium salts in subcutaneous tissue (i.e., the the lowermost layer of the integument).
The presence of leiomyoma of the skin.
Osteomyelitis of the lower jaw.

syn_en: Underdevelopment of condylar process of mandible
Decreased size of condylar process of mandible
Hypoplasia of condylar process of mandible
Hypoplasia of subcondylar region of mandible

terms.def_en: A developmental anomaly characterized by abnormal smallness of both eyes.
lay_en: Abnormally small eyeball on both sides

terms.def_en: An acute condition characterized by sudden visual loss (usually discovered in the morning), optic disc edema at onset, optic disc-related visual field defects. Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy can be associated with flame hemorrhages on the swollen disk or nearby neuroretinal layer, and sometimes with nearby cotton-wool exudates.
A form of colorblindness in which only two of the three fundamental colors can be distinguished due to a lack of one of the retinal cone pigments.
A usually nonprogressive (i.e., stationary) form of night blindness with early (presumed to be congenital) onset.
Tractional retinal detachment at the periphery of the retina.
syn_en: Tractional retinal detachment at the periphery of the retina

terms.def_en: Lack of eyelashes on the lower lid.
lay_en: Failure of development of lower eyelashes

terms.def_en: Congenital abnormality of the extraocular muscles.
A type of cataract with punctate opacities of the lens.

terms.en: Congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
terms.def_en: Sharply demarcated, congenital hyperpigmentation of the retinal pigment epithelium. It can be solitary, clustered or multifocal, uni- or bilateral.

terms.en: Eversion of lateral third of lower eyelids
terms.it: Eversione del terzo laterale delle palpebre inferiori

terms.def_en: A congenital defect of development characterized by absence of the lacrimal gland.
Opacity of the entire lens nucleus.
Abnormally curly or curved eyelashes.

Degenerative changes of the peripheral retina consisting of close-packed tiny cystic spaces at the outer plexiform/inner nuclear retinal level. The degeneration is common in adult eyes and starts adjacent to the ora serrata and extends circumferentially and posteriorly.

An abnormality of the vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR). The VOR attempts to keep the image stable on the retina. Ideally passive or active head movements in one direction are compensated for by eye movements of equal magnitude.
Congenital underdevelopment of the iris.

Egg yolk-like (vitelliform) maculopathy is a lesion caused by the accumulation of material, often lipofuscin, in the subretinal space underlying the macula. Lesions may be singular or multiple, and may be either sharply or poorly demarcated.
Narrowing of a tear duct (lacrimal duct).
Incomplete peripheral vascular development.
A functional abnormality of the pupil.
A unilateral form of ptosis.
Absence of the combined rod-and-cone response on electroretinogram.
syn_en: Absent cone and rod functions by electroretinogram
Absent rod-and cone-mediated responses on ERG

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the reflex that controls the diameter of the pupil, in response to the intensity of light that falls on the retina of the eye.
Underdevelopment of the lower eyelid.
Abnormal development (dysgenesis) of the anterior segment of the eye globe. These structures are mainly of mesenchymal origin.
Any deviation from the normal pigmentation of the retina.
Sudden-onset episode of abnormal, involuntary eye movements.
Absence of the crystalline lens of the eye as a result of a developmental defect.
A type of genetically determined disease of the cornea with corneal lesions with a band-like shape.
A malignant melanoma originating within the eye. The tumor originates from the melanocytes in the uvea (which comprises the iris, ciliary body, and choroid).
A chronic irritative conjunctivitis, which commonly presents with general irritation and redness of the eyes, with a burning, dry, or foreign-body sensation of the eyes.

Cornea plana is an abnormally flat shape of the cornea such that the normal protrusion of the cornea from the sclera is missing. The reduced corneal curvature can lead to hyperopia, and a hazy corneal limbus and arcus lipoides may develop at an early age.
Presence of multiple dilatations (sac-like outpouchings) in the blood vessels of the conjunctiva.
A nonspecific term denoting wasting, especially as a result of degeneration, of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE).
Lack of transparency of the corneal epithelium.
Abnormal (non-physiological) constriction of the pupil of congenital onset.
An abnormal reduction in the amount of pigmentation of the iris.
Abnormal development of the choroid and retina.
Underdevelopment of the lacrimal gland.
Abnormally big lacrimal glands.

terms.it: Pigmentazione a spicole ossee della retina
terms.def_en: Pigment migration into the retina in a bone-spicule configuration (resembling the nucleated cells within the lacuna of bone).
syn_en: Bone spicule pigmentation of the retina

terms.def_en: Underdevelopment of the fovea centralis.
Macular dystrophy is a nonspecific term for retinal degeneration, generally confined to the macula, usually presumed of genetic origin.
Reduced transparency of the stroma of cornea.
A scotoma (area of diminished vision within the visual field) that surrounds the central fixation point.
Localized, irregular dilatation of small tortuous intraretinal blood vessels.
Increased depth of the anterior chamber, i.e., the anteroposterior distance between the cornea and the iris is increased.
Underdevelopment of the optic disc, that is of the optic nerve head, where ganglion cell axons exit the eye to form the optic nerve.
The presence of an increased number of twists and turns of retinal blood vessels (arteries, arterioles, veins, venules).
Progressive loss of peripheral retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and/or neurosensory retinal cells.
An impairment of the ability to track objects with the ocular smooth pursuit system, a class of rather slow eye movements that minimizes retinal target motion.
Ocular abnormality characterized by premature degeneration of the vitreous and the retina that may be associated with increased risk of retinal detachment.
Underdevelopment of the ciliary body.
Fibrous connective tissue resulting from incomplete healing of a wound (i.e., a scar) located in the choroid and retina or the eye.
A type of retinal neovascularization that affects the posterior pole of the retina.
syn_en: Neovascularization of peripheral and posterior retina

terms.def_en: A type of cataract characterized by punctate, dust-like opacities within the cortical region of the lens.
A type of cataract affecting the posterior pole of lens immediately adjacent to ('beneath') the Lens capsule.
syn_en: Posterior subcapsular opacities of the lens

terms.en: Patchy atrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium
terms.def_en: A nonspecific term denoting wasting, especially as a result of degeneration, of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) that occurs in small, isolated areas.
Mottled (spotted or blotched with different shades) pigmentary abnormality of the macula.
A cataract that affects the anterior part of the cortex of the lens.
A group of development abnormalities of retinal blood vessels.
The presence of whitish deposits in the conjunctiva resembling salt. May be related to calcinosis.

terms.en: Increased axial length of the globe
terms.it: Aumentata lunghezza assiale del bulbo oculare
terms.def_en: Abnormal largeness of the eye with an axial length > 2.5 standard deviations from population mean.
lay_en: Increased front to back length of eyeball

terms.def_en: The presence of central, fine, whitish granular lesions in the stroma of the cornea. This type of corneal dystrophy is usually asymptomatic and begins in childhood and shows a slow progression. Later in the course, the corneal epithelium and Bowman's layer may be affected. Histologically, the cornea shows a uniform deposition of hyaline material.
Complete color blindness, a complete inability to distinguish colors. Affected persons cannot perceive colors, but only shades of gray.
Nystagmus consisting of horizontal to-and-fro eye movements of equal velocity.

The presence of one or more dendritic corneal epithelial ulcers characterized by a treelike branching linear pattern with feathery edges and terminal bulbs. Herpetiform corneal ulcers can be identified by fluorescein staining.
A form of uveitis that is not associated with the formation of granulomas.

Mottling (spots or blotches of different shades) of the retinal pigment epithelium, i.e., localized or generalized fundus pigment granularity associated with processes at the level of the retinal pigment epithelium.
syn_en: Focal hypopigmentation of the retinal pigment epithelium

terms.def_en: A supranuclear gaze palsy is an inability to look in a horizontal direction as a result of cerebral impairment. There is a loss of the voluntary aspect of eye movements, but, as the brainstem is still intact, all the reflex conjugate eye movements are normal.
The presence of distinct colors in the central (pupillary) zone of the iris than in the mid-peripheral (ciliary) zone.
Presenile cataract is a kind of cataract that occurs in early adulthood, that is, at an age that is younger than usual.
Congenital absence or closure of the opening of the lacrimal punctum.
Paralysis of both the extrinsic and intrinsic ocular muscles.
Inability to see well at night or in poor light with onset in adulthood.

Nonprogressive restriction of movement of the external ocular muscles such that the eyes of affected individuals are partially or completely fixed in a strabismic position. Residual eye movements are significantly limited.

lay_en: Pigmentation of the outer white part of the eyeball

terms.def_en: A kind of cataract that progresses with age.
A progressive form of ptosis.
Increased length of the upper eyelashes.

terms.en: Amyloid deposition in the vitreous humor
terms.def_en: Deposition of hyaline extracellular material (amyloid) into the vitreous humor, which can manifest as vitreous opacities and reduced visual acuity.
syn_en: Amyloid deposition in the vitreous humour

terms.def_en: Narrowing of the retinal blood vessels, both arterioles and venules.
lay_en: Narrowing of blood vessels in back of eye

terms.def_en: Punctate opacification (reduced transparency) of the corneal stroma.
Punched out lesions in the pigmented layer of the retina.
Horizontal nystagmus dating from or present at birth.
Deposition of calcium salts in the retina.
Fibrosis of only some of the external ocular muscles such that the eyes of affected individuals are partially or completely fixed in a strabismic position.
Benign choroidal tumour, seen in the fundus as a reddish or orange choroidal lesion and usually associated with cystoid edema, and less commonly with Subretinal fluid.

A shape created by an acute downward arching of the upper eyelid and upward arching of the lower eyelid, toward the medial canthus, which gives the outline of the palpebral fissures the configuration of an almond. Thus, the maximum distance between the fissures is offset from, and medial to, the center point.
Blindness with onset at birth.
Allergic Conjunctivitis is an allergic inflammation of the conjunctiva.
An abnormally slow velocity of horizontal saccadic eye movements.
Congenital absence of the extraocular muscles.
A type of posterior subcapsular cataract characterized by an iridescent color.
Underdevelopment of the lacrimal puncta.
Generalized or focal reduced pigmentation of the fundus, evaluated in the context of skin and hair color. Fundoscopy may reveal a low level pigment.

Retinal nonattachment is a developmental (congenital) condition in which persistent fetal blood vessels appear to proliferate more dramatically during infancy, causing complete perinatal detachment of the retina. This may occur during or shortly after neurogenesis, since the pathology is apparent at birth, and it may have a tractional basis, involving fibrovascular strands between the retina, posterior lens and hyaloid vessels.
Bleeding within the vitreous compartment of the eye.
Chorioretinal atrophy along the retinal veins.
Intraocular pressure that is 2 standard deviations above the population mean.

lay_en: Congenital drooping of both upper eyelids

terms.def_en: A type of of patterned retinal dystrophy that shows a reticular pattern of pigmentation.

This corneal dystrophy affects the posterior limiting membrane of the cornea and is characterized by polymorphous plaques of calcium deposits in the deep stromal layers of the cornea, and occasionally by vesicular lesions of the endothelium and edema of the deep corneal stroma.
A type of retinal detachment arising due to a combination of contracting retinal membranes, abnormal vitreoretinal adhesions, and vitreous changes, in the absence of a full-thickness retinal defect.
Myelinated retinal nerve fiber (MRNF) layer is a rare and mostly benign congenital anomaly in which the retinal nerve fibers anterior to the lamina cribrosa have a myelin sheath.

lay_en: Slow decrease in sharpness of vision

terms.def_en: A congenital defect resulting in absence of the lacrimal duct.

terms.it: Potenziali evocati visivi da flash anomali
terms.def_en: Anomaly of the visual evoked potentials elicited by a flash stimulus, generally a flash of light subtending an angle of at least 20 degrees of the visual field and presented in a dimly lit room.
Separation of the inner layers of the retina (neural retina) from the pigment epithelium occurring near the outer limit (periphery) of the retina.
Congenital abnormal dilation of the pupil on both sides.
Regional increase in the width (height) of the lateral eyebrow.
Fibrosis of the external ocular muscles such that the eyes of affected individuals are partially or completely fixed in a strabismic position. Residual eye movements are significantly limited.
A pattern of peripheral netlike retinal pigmentation that forms a polygonal arrangement of hyperpigmented lines forming geometric patterns in the fundus.
A form of monochromacy in which vision is derived from the remaining preserved blue (S) cones and rod photoreceptors.
Limited mobility of the eye within its socket.
Paralysis of the iris and ciliary apparatus.
A form of stapes ankylosis with congenital onset.
A fixed reduction in the vertical distance between the upper and lower eyelids with short palpebral fissures on one side only.
lay_en: Unequal size of opening between the eyelids

terms.def_en: A subtype of retinitis pigmentosa in which, instead of the pathology starting in the mid-periphery like typical retinitis pigmentosa, the disease starts in the near periphery closer to the vascular arcades and tends to spare the far periphery.
A type of posterior cortical cataract characterized by dense lenticular opacities.
Chorioretinal atrophy concentrated around the optic papilla (i.e., the optic nerve head).
A reduction of corneal clarity.
syn_en: Scarring or clouding of the cornea of the eye

terms.en: Optic atrophy from cranial nerve compression

terms.def_en: A spectrum of fundoscopic appearances characterized by the development of a variety of patterns of deposits predominantly in the macular area. The deposits are typically bilateral, relatively symmetrical, yellow/white and associated with changes at the level of the retinal pigment epithelium. With time, retinal atrophy may occur. A number of pattern dystrophy subtypes have been described including butterfly-shaped dystrophy, reticular dystrophy (net-like pattern) and fundus pulverulentus (granular, mottled pigmentation).

terms.en: Remnants of the hyaloid vascular system
terms.def_en: Persistence of the hyaloid artery, which is the embryonic artery that runs from the optic disc to the posterior lens capsule may persist; the site of attachment may form an opacity. The hyaloid artery is a branch of the ophthalmic artery, and usually regresses completely before birth. This features results from a failure of regression of the hyaloid vessel, which supplies the primary vitreous during embryogenesis and normally regresses in the third trimester of pregnancy, leading to a particular form of posterior cataract.
syn_en: Persistent posterior fetal fibrovascular sheath of the lens
Persistent posterior foetal fibrovascular sheath of the lens

terms.def_en: A congenital cataract in which opacity is limited to layers of the lens external to the nucleus (i.e., the perinuclear region), i.e., between the nuclear and cortical layers of the lens.
Abnormal growth and differentiation, structure and appearance of the retina present from birth.
Saccadic undershoot of horizontal saccadic eye movements, i.e., a horizontal saccadic eye movement that has less than the magnitude that would be required to gain fixation of the object.

Cerulean cataracts are a kind of congenital cataract having peripheral bluish and white opacifications in concentric layers with occasional central lesions arranged radially. Although the opacities may be observed during fetal development and childhood, usually visual acuity is only mildly reduced until adulthood, when lens extraction is generally necessary.
Horizontal nystagmus made apparent by looking to the right or to the left.
Discrete areas of pallor in which the pigment epithelium, choriocapillaris and choroidal pigment are absent.
A dark-adapted bright flash electroretinogram in which the b-wave that is of markedly lower amplitude than the associated a-wave.
syn_en: Reduced amplitude of dark-adapted bright flash electroretinogram b-wave

terms.def_en: Blockage of retinal arteriole, generally associated with interruption of blood flow and oxygen delivery to affected regions of the retina. This can affect the inner or mid-retinal structures.
Decreased amount of pigmentation in the macula.
Retinal exudate within the retinal tissue itself.
Underdevelopment of the stroma of iris.
A pattern of white lines and dots in the far periphery of the retina.
Congenital malformation of the lacrimal duct associated with incomplete development of the bony nasolacrimal canal or craniofacial anomalies.
Loss of peripheral vision with retention of central vision, resulting in a constricted circular tunnel-like field of vision.

An abnormally reduced response to stimulation of the cornea (by touch, foreign body, blowing air). The corneal reflex (also known as the blink reflex, normally results in an involuntary blinking of the eyelids.
Increased amount of pigmentation in the fovea.
Any deviation from the normal, uniform distribution or appearance of pigment within the macular region of the retina.
Reduced transparency of the peripheral region of the cornea.
Partial dislocation of the lens in a superior direction.
Inherited progressive cone degeneration.
A form of macular degeneration characterized by the presence of multiple cystoid spaces in the macula.
A type of sutural cataract in which the opacity follows the posterior Y suture.
Abnormal pigmentation of the iris.

terms.en: Absent anterior chamber of the eye
terms.def_en: Absence of the anterior chamber of the eye owing to a developmental defect.
Absence or underdevelopment of the lacrimal gland.
Focal decreased retinal arteriolar diameters, which may decrease blood flow and slow oxygen delivery to regions of the retina.
A structural abnormality of retinal vasculature.

terms.en: Abnormality of the vasculature of the eye

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the line of Schwalbe.
syn_en: Abnormality of the line of Schwalbe

terms.def_en: An abnormality of an extraocular muscle.
An anomaly of the space between the medial and lateral canthi of the two open eyelids.
lay_en: Abnormality of the opening between the eyelids

terms.def_en: A wrinkle of retinal tissue projecting outward from the surface of the retina and visible as a line on fundoscopy.
Absence or underdevelopment of the iris.

terms.en: Abnormal morphology of the conjunctival vasculature
terms.def_en: Any abnormality of the blood vessels of the conjunctiva.
syn_en: Abnormal morphology of the conjunctiva vasculature
Abnormal vasculature of the conjunctiva morphology
Abnormality of the vasculature of the conjunctiva

terms.def_en: Absence or underdevelopment of the uvea, the pigmented middle layer of the eye consisting of the iris and ciliary body together with the choroid.
A developmental defect characterized by lack of development or underdevelopment of the fundus/fovea.
Congenital absence or underdevelopment of the fovea.

terms.en: Aplasia/Hypoplasia affecting the anterior segment of the eye
terms.def_en: Absence or underdevelopment of the anterior segment of the eye.
Absence or underdevelopment of the lens.
An abnormality of the skin characterized the presence of excessive amounts of dry surface scales on the skin resulting from an abnormality of keratinization.
The presence of one or more bullae on the skin, defined as fluid-filled blisters more than 5 mm in diameter with thin walls.
A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the skin.
Reduced density of hairs.
Reduction in bone mineral density affecting any or all of the tarsal bones, seven bones of the foot comprising the calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, and the cuneiform bones.
A developmental abnormality characterized by the absence of the fifth metatarsal bone.
syn_en: Aplasia of the fifth metatarsal bone

terms.def_en: Medial deviation of the great toe owing to a deformity of the great toe joint causing the hallux to deviate medially.
An outward (valgus) deviation of the calcaneus relative to the longitudinal axis of the lower leg at the talocalcaneal (subtalar) joint, such that the heel is everted.
The presence of a fifth metatarsal bone that has not undergone ossification at an age when ossification is usually visible.

terms.en: Abnormality of the fifth metatarsal bone
terms.def_en: An anomaly of the fifth metatarsal bone.
lay_en: Abnormality of the 5th long bone of foot

terms.def_en: Underdevelopment (hypoplasia) of the fourth toe.
An overall widening of the spaces between the digits.
Osteolysis affecting the talus.
Medial deviation of the second toe.

terms.en: Expanded metatarsals with widened medullary cavities

terms.def_en: Delayed maturation and calcification of any of the tarsal bones, seven bones of the foot comprising the calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, and the cuneiform bones.

terms.en: Plantar crease between first and second toes
terms.def_en: The presence of unusually deep creases (ridges/wrinkles) on the skin of sole of foot located between the first and second toe.
Precocious (accelerated) maturation and calcification of any of the tarsal bones, seven bones of the foot comprising the calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, and the cuneiform bones.
A type of contracture in which the plantar flexion muscles are contracted.
Osteosclerosis of the endosteal surface of the diaphyses (shafts) of the metatarsal bones.
Bending or curvature of a third toe in the tibial direction (i.e., towards the big toe).
Limitation of the ability to bend the toes.
Synostosis of the calcaneus with the navicular bone.
A congenital deformity characterized by a dorsiflexed, inverted, and adducted foot, i.e., a combination of talipes calcaneus and talipes varus.
A two-part calcaneus, a finding that probably results from delayed coalescence of two primary calcaneal centers of ossification.
syn_en: Delayed coalescence of calcaneal ossification centers
Delayed coalescence of calcaneal ossification centres

terms.def_en: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in one or more tarsal bones.

terms.en: Medial rotation of the medial malleolus
terms.def_en: Hindfoot valgus (posterior part of the foot turns outward) in combination with forefoot abduction (front part of the foot (the forefoot) is angled outwards away from the midline of the body, relative to the hindfoot) and lowering of the midfoot.
Defective ossification in an irregular pattern of the seven bones of the foot comprising the calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, and the cuneiform bones.

Abnormal plantar flexion of the calcaneus relative to the longitudinal axis of the tibia. This results in the angle between the long axis of the tibia and the long axis of the heel bone (calcaneus) being greater than 90 degrees.
Delayed maturation and calcification of the calcaneus.
Abnormal response to epinephrine as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of epinephrine.
Elevations of the levels of SGOT (serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase) and SGPT (serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase) that occur during infections.

Increased time to coagulation in the prothrombin time test, which is a measure of the extrinsic pathway of coagulation. The results of the prothrombin time test are often expressed in terms of the International normalized ratio (INR), which is calculated as a ratio of the patient's prothrombin time (PT) to a control PT standardized for the potency of the thromboplastin reagent developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) using the formula: INR is equal to Patient PT divided by Control PT.
Episodes of muscle weakness associated with reduced levels of potassium in the blood.
Excessive amounts of mucopolysaccharide in the urine.
Hyperapobetalipoproteinemia is defined as the combination of a normal low density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol in the face of an increased LDL apolipoprotein B (apoB) protein.
The concentration of 2-hydroxydicarboxylic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
Alkaline phosphatase levels measured within leukocytes is below detectable levels.
An increased concentration of ammonia in the blood not associated with symptoms such as encephalopathy.

terms.it: Diminuzione del livello di cortisolo circolante
terms.def_en: Abnormally reduced concentration of cortisol in the blood.
Abnormally decreased rate of beta-galactosidase activity. Beta-galactosidase activity can be measured in leukocyte, fibroblast, or plasma.
syn_en: Beta-galactosidase deficiency in fibroblasts and white blood cells

terms.en: Very long chain fatty acid accumulation

terms.def_en: Reduced activity of coagulation factor VII. Factor VII is part of the extrinsic coagulation pathway, which is initiated at the site of injury in response to the release of tissue factor (fIII). Tissue factor and activated factor VII catalyze the activation of factor X.
An abnormal reduction in the Arden ratio, which is the ratio between the light peak and the dark trough of the smoothed (physiologic) EOG record.
An absence of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.
The onset of puberty before the age of 9 years in boys.
lay_en: Early onset of puberty in males

terms.def_en: The presence of large polyhedral cells with eosinophilic granular cytoplasm and enlarged nuclei in the adrenal cortex.
No secondary sexual characteristics are present at puberty.
syn_en: No secondary sexual characteristics at puberty

terms.def_en: Thyroid dysgenesis is a descriptive term that should be avoided if more precise information is available. However, the HPO keeps retains this term because it is commonly used in the medical literature. In humans, the process of thyroid morphogenesis occurs from the 3rd to 16th week of gestation. Alterations occurring during this period may result in a thyroid gland that is absent (thyroid agenesis or athyreosis), hypoplastic (thyroid hypoplasia), or located in an unusual position (thyroid ectopy). All these entities are grouped under the term thyroid dysgenesis.
Decreased sensitivity toward insulin.
The congenital absence of the thyroid gland.
The presence of multiple pancreatic islet cell adenomas.
Deficiency of parathyroid hormone with congenital onset.
A type of hyperparathyroidism caused by a primary abnormality of the parathyroid glands (e.g., adenoma, carcinoma, hyperplasia). Primary hyperparathyroidism is associated with hyercalcemia.

A reduced level of prolactin in the blood circulation. Prolactin is a protein hormone that is secreted by lactotrophs in the anterior pituitary and that stimulates mammary gland development and milk production.

terms.en: Precocious puberty with Sertoli cell tumor
syn_en: Precocious puberty with Sertoli cell tumour

terms.def_en: Ketosis-resistant diabetes is a synonym for type II diabetes. This term thus refers to a form of type II diabetes in which patients are dependent on insulin.
Insufficient production of steroid hormones (primarily cortisol) by the adrenal glands as a result of a primary defect in the glands themselves.
Hyperplasia of the parathyroid gland.

Amenorrhea due to loss of ovarian function before the age of 40. Primary ovarian insuficiency (POI) is a state of female hypergonadotropic hypogonadism. It can manifest as primary amenorrhea with onset before menarche or secondary amenorrhea.
Aplasia of the parathyroid gland.

A reduced ability to secrete gonadotropins, which are protein hormones secreted by gonadotrope cells of the anterior pituitary gland, including the hormones follitropin (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH).
A reduction below normal concentration of estradiol in the circulation.
Abnormal development of the adrenal gland.
Enlargement of the adrenal gland.
Condition associated with a raised serum concentration of thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) but a normal serum free thyroxine (FT4).
Insufficient amount of androgenic activity.

A condition in which the pituitary gland is partially resistant to thyroid hormone, so that it continues to secrete thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) until the blood level of thyroid hormone rises higher than normal.
The presence of lymphangiectasis of the thyroid gland.

terms.en: Elevated circulating follicle stimulating hormone level
terms.it: Elevati livelli di ormone follicolo-stimolante circolante
terms.def_en: An elevated concentration of follicle-stimulating hormone in the blood.
syn_en: Increased circulating follicle stimulating hormone level

terms.def_en: An reduced concentration of progesterone in the blood.
A type of hypothyroidism that results from a defect in thyrotropin-releasing hormone activity.
Developmental hypoplasia of the adrenal medulla.
A state of renal tubular unresponsiveness or resistance to the action of aldosterone.
A type of adrenal hypoplasia with congenital onset.
A type of hypothyroidism that results from a defect in thyroid-stimulating hormone secretion.
lay_en: Low thyroid gland function due to abnormal pituitary gland

terms.def_en: Increased levels of thyroxine without evidence of clinical thyroid disease.
Hyperplasia of the thyroid gland.
An enlargement of the thyroid gland with congenital onset.
Adrenocortical adenomas are benign tumors of the adrenal cortex.
A type of adrenal hyperplasia with congenital onset.
Adrenal insufficiency secondary to a defect in the ACTH receptor.
The presence of an adenoma of the pancreas with origin in a pancreatic B cell.

terms.en: Thyroid defect in oxidation and organification of iodide

terms.def_en: The presence of intracellular inclusion bodies (aggregates of stainable substances, usually proteins) in neutrophils. Cytoplasmic neutrophil inclusions (oval, basophilic) are also known as Doehle bodies.

terms.en: Increased red cell hemolysis by shear stress

terms.def_en: Abnormal morphology of collagen fibers in cartilage. In cartilage, collagen II, actually a collagen II:IX:XI heterofibril, is by far the most important type of collagen. A number of abnormalities may be appreciated by electron micrography or biochemical investigations, including sparse collagen fibers in the cartilage matrix.
Any deviation from the normal concentration of zinc in the blood circulation.
Atrophy (wasting) of the cerebellar cortex.
An increased concentration of ammonia in the blood with sudden onset.
An increased amount of unconjugated (indirect) bilurubin in the blood.
An increased concentration of insulin in the blood in the fasting state, i.e., not as the response to food intake.
lay_en: High blood insulin levels while fasting

terms.def_en: A partial reduction in level of the complement component Factor H in circulation.
A type of pituitary adenoma that produces adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH).
An increase in the level of long-chain dicarboxylic acid in the urine.

A condition of not having consistently high levels of phenylalanine in the blood but of experiencing temporary hyperphenylalaninemia following ingestion of large quantities of phenylalanine (for instance, following an oral loading test with phenylalanine).
An increased concentration of dermatan sulfate in the urine.
Degeneration of the olivary bodies, prominent oval structures in the medulla oblongata.
Presence of myoglobin in the urine following exercise.
An increase in the level of medium chain dicarboxylic acid in the urine.
Lower than normal amount of myelin in the dorsal (posterior) tract of the spinal cord white matter.
syn_en: Spinal cord posterior columns myelin loss

terms.en: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex II
terms.it: Diminuzione dell'attività del complesso mitocondriale II
terms.def_en: A reduction in the activity of the mitochondrial respiratory chain complex II, which is part of the electron transport chain in mitochondria.
A decreased concentration of free (unbound) carnitine in the blood.
An abnormality of the mitochondria in muscle tissue.
Increased alkaline phosphatase measured within leukocytes.
Abnormal response to collagen or collagen-mimetics as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition collagen or collagen-mimetics.

Reduced activity of coagulation factor X. The extrinsic and intrinsic pathways converge at factor X (fX). The extrinsic pathway activates fX by means of d factor VII with its cofactor, tissue factor. The intrinsic pathway activates fX by means of the tenase complex (Ca2+ and factors VIIIa, IXa and X) on the surface of activated platelets. Factor Xa in turn activates prothrombin (factor II) to thrombin (factor IIa).
Any structural anomaly of the mitochondria.
An abnormality of the combined rod-and-cone response on electroretinogram.
An abnormally decreased concentration of vitamin B6 in the blood circulation.
The presence of microscopic crystalline calcium precipitates in the form of oxalate and/or phosphate in the renal parenchyma.

terms.it: Ridotta attività del fattore von Willebrand
terms.def_en: Decreased activity of von Willebrand factor. Von Willebrand factor mediates the adhesion of platelets to the collagen exposed on endothelial cell surfaces.

terms.en: Partial functional complement factor D deficiency
terms.def_en: A partial reduction in level of the complement component Factor D in circulation.
An increased urine level of any amino acid carrying two amino groups (Asparagine, glutamine and lysine, cystine, ornithine).

A type of renal tubular acidosis characterized by a failure of acid secretion by the alpha intercalated cells of the cortical collecting duct of the distal nephron. The urine cannot be acidified below a pH of 5.3, associated with acidemia and hypokalemia.

terms.en: Elevated circulating branched-chain amino acid concentration
terms.def_en: The concentration of branched-chain amino acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
syn_en: Elevated branched-chain amino acid level in blood
Increased branched-chain amino acid level in blood

terms.en: Hypoplasia of the iris dilator muscle
terms.def_en: Underdevelopment of the dilatator pupillae.
syn_en: Hypoplasia of the pupil dilator muscle

terms.en: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex IV
terms.it: Diminuzione dell'attività del complesso mitocondriale IV
terms.def_en: A reduction in the activity of the mitochondrial respiratory chain complex IV, which is part of the electron transport chain in mitochondria.
A reduction in immunoglobulin levels of the IgG2 subclass in the blood circulation.

An abnormality of adhesion of thrombocytes. Normally, platelets adhere to collagen in the vascular subendothelium within seconds of injury via a receptor made up of glycoprotein Ia and IIa and GPVI and to vWF via receptor GPIb/IX/V. The adherent platelets then release granules that lead to platelet activation and aggregation.

The presence of an abnormally increased concentration of neutral amino acids in the urine. The neutral amino acids are tryptophan, alanine, asparagine, glutamine, histidine, isoleucine, leucine, phenylalanine, serine, threonine, tyrosine and valine.
Reduced ability to transform factor X into its activated form factor Xa.
Decreased activity of coagulation factor XIII (also known as fibrin stabilizing factor). Activated Factor XIII cross-links fibrin polymers solidifying the clot.
The concentration of proline in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
A neonatal decreased concentration of proteins in the blood.
Absence or underdevelopment of the big toe.
Absence or underdevelopment of the tarsal bones.
An abnormality of the calcaneus, also known as the heel bone, one of the or heel bone, one of the components of the tarsus of the foot which make up the heel.
An abnormality of the talus.
Contractures of one or more joints of the feet meaning chronic loss of joint motion due to structural changes in non-bony tissue.
syn_en: Contractures involving the joints of the feet
Joint contractures involving the joints of the feet

terms.def_en: Synostosis (bony fusion) involving one or more bones of the tarsus (calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, cuneiiform bones).
An abnormality of the formation and mineralization of any of the tarsal bones, seven bones of the foot comprising the calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, and the cuneiform bones.

Any abnormal process of ossification of the metatarsal bones, which normally are each ossified from two centers: one for the body, and one for the head (metatarsal II,III,IV, and V) and one for the body and one for the base (metatarsal I). The ossification process begins in the center of the body about the ninth week, and extends toward either extremity. The center for the base of the first metatarsal appears about the third year, and the centers for the heads of the other bones between the fifth and eighth years. They join the bodies between the eighteenth and twentieth years.
lay_en: Abnormal maturation of long bone of foot

terms.def_en: Concentration of vitamin A in the blood circulation outside limits of normal.
Nails whose growth is slower than normal.
Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the nail.
An anomaly of the toenail.

terms.en: Recurrent loss of toenails and fingernails
terms.def_en: Repeated loss, or shedding, of the nails of the fingers and toes.
lay_en: Recurrent loss of toenails and fingernails
Recurrent shedding of toenails and fingernails

terms.def_en: The presence of misshapen or partially destroyed nail plates, often with accumulation of soft, yellow keratin between the dystrophic nail plate and nail bed, resulting in elevation of the nail plate.
A thickening of the stratum corneum in the region beneath the nails.

terms.en: Congenital curved nail of fourth toe

terms.def_en: Chronic infection of the nails by Candida species.
A nail of the fifth finger that is diminished in length and width, i.e., underdeveloped nail of little finger.
A thickening of the stratum corneum, the outer layer of the skin, in the region surrounding the nails.
Detachment of the distal fingernails from the nail bed.
Thickened toenails.
Longitudinal, linear prominences in the fingernail plate.

Onychodystrophy (nail dystrophy) refers to nail changes apart from changes of the color (nail dyschromia) and involves partial or complete disruption of the various keratinous layers of the nail plate.
Small, underdeveloped vertebral bodies.
The presence of degenerative changes of intervertebral disk.
The presence of punctiform calcification of the bone of the vertebral bodies.
An abnormal shape of the vertebral bodies whereby the vertebral bodies are thick on one side and taper to a thin edge at the other.
The presence of developmental dysplasia of the vertebral column.
Schisis (cleft or cleavage) of vertebral bodies.
Anterior tongue-like protrusions of the vertebral bodies of the lumbar spine.
syn_en: Anterior tongue-like protrusion of lumbar vertebral bodies

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the shape of the lumbar vertebra L1 such that it is wedge-shaped (narrow towards the front).

terms.en: Absent in utero ossification of vertebral bodies

terms.def_en: A morphological abnormality of the vertebral arch, i.e., of the posterior part of a vertebra.
Absence of one half of the vertebral body in the lumbar spine.
Any abnormality of the atlas and the axis.
The presence of one or more herniated nucleus pulposus of intervertebral disk.
Excessive growth of the bones of the vertebral bodies.

A progressive disorder of vertebral joint degeneration that occurs in the setting of any condition characterized by decreased afferent innervation, involving loss of deep pain and proprioceptive sensation in the vertebral column. Patients most commonly present with symptoms of lower back pain, sitting imbalance, progressive spinal deformity (usually kyphosis), and an audible clicking sound on changing postures.
An abnormality of the shape of vertebrae, such that they are wedge-shaped (narrow towards the back).
An abnormal narrowing of the cervical spinal canal.

A reduction of the distance between vertebral pedicles, which are the two short, thick processes, which project backward, one on either side, from the upper part of the vertebral body, at the junction of its posterior and lateral surfaces.
Over curvature of the lumbar region.

A developmental defect of the sacrum characterized by partial or disordered development of the sacrum in which portions of the sacrum, which normally is formed by fusion of five sacral vertebrae S1-S5, fail to form or fail to form normally.
lay_en: Absence of some of the sacral and coccygeal bones

terms.def_en: A partial dislocation of the intervertebral joint between the second and third cervical vertebrae.

Narrowing (becoming gradually narrower) of the distance between vertebral pedicles that gets progressively more severe towards to caudal (lower) end of the vertebral column. Note that normally, the interpedicular distances get progressively wider as one proceeds down the spine.
A progressive form of scoliosis with congenital onset.
Agenesis of one or more vertebrae of the cervical vertebral column.

terms.en: Absent spinous processes of lower thoracic and lumbar vertebrae

terms.def_en: A developmental defect characterized by agenesis of one or more vertebral bodies.
Absence of one half of the vertebral body in the thoracic spine.
An abnormality related to a defect of vertebral separation of sacral vertebrae during development.
Dysplasia of the cervical vertebral column.
A reduction of the distance between the lower thoracic vertebral pedicles.
syn_en: Narrowness of interpediculate distances in lower thoracic regions

terms.def_en: An abnormal reduction of the anterioposterior diameter of the vertebral body.
syn_en: Reduced anterior-posterior diameter of vertebral bodies

terms.def_en: Decreased ossification of the cervical vertebral bodies, i.e., of the Cervical vertebrae set.
Arthrosis, i.e., of degenerative joint disease, affecting the cervical vertebral column.

terms.en: Cervical vertebral bodies with decreased anteroposterior diameter

terms.def_en: A reduction of the distance between thoracolumbar vertebral pedicles.
Narrowing (becoming gradually narrower) of the distance between lumbar vertebral pedicles that gets progressively more severe towards to caudal (lower) end of the vertebral column.
Complete bilateral fractures of the pars interarticularis resulting in the anterior slippage of the fifth lumbar vertebral body (L5) onto the sacrum (level S1).
Early closure (ossification) of the anterior fontanelle, which generally undergoes closure around the 18th month of life.
Partial displacement of the lens in the inferior direction.
A severe form of hypermetropia with over +5.00 diopters.
The presence of a moderate form of sensorineural hearing impairment.
Reduced transparency of the central posterior portion of the corneal stroma.
A bilateral type of conductive hearing impairment.

terms.en: Abnormality of the vertebral spinous processes

terms.def_en: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the sacral bone.

Congenital absence of the lumen of the larynx. Laryngeal atresia is a rare condition. If the laryngeal opening fails to develop, fluid secreted by the lungs cannot be expelled. In a fetus with laryngeal atresia, the lungs are either normal or hyperplastic, not hypoplastic. Mortality is reported as 100%. At obstetric US examination, views of the fetal neck demonstrate a dilated trachea filled with trapped fluid. Views of the fetal chest show enlarged, hyperechoic lungs, with dilated fluid-filled bronchi. Fetal ascites is usually present.

syn_en: Triangular epiphysis of the outermost bone of the thumb

terms.def_en: Absence of one or more epiphyses of the thumb.
An abnormality of the thumb in which the epiphysis surrounds a phalangeal bone, having a bracket-like form and reaching from the proximal side of a phalanx to the distal side.
lay_en: Bracket shaped end part of the thumb bone

terms.def_en: A cone-shaped appearance of the epiphyses of the thumb, producing a 'ball-in-a-socket' appearance. The related entity 'angel-shaped' epiphysis refers to a pronounced cone-shaped epiphysis in combination with a pseudoepiphysis at the distal end of a phalanx.
lay_en: Cone-shaped end part of thumb long bone

terms.def_en: Abnormally large size of the epiphyses of the thumb with respect to age-dependent norms.
lay_en: Enlarged end part of thumb long bone

terms.def_en: Epiphysis of the thumb having multiple bony fragments.
lay_en: Fragmentation of end part of long bone of thumb
syn_en: Fragmentation of the epiphyses of the thumb

terms.def_en: Uneven radiographic opacity of the one or more epiphyses of the thumb.
lay_en: Irregular end part of thumb long bone

terms.def_en: Sclerosis of one or more of the epiphyses of the thumb, leading to an increased degree of radiopacity (white or ivory appearance) in X-rays.
lay_en: Increased bone density of end part of the thumb

terms.def_en: A pseudoepiphysis (which is a secondary ossification center distinct from the normal epiphysis) of one or more phalanges of the thumb.
Abnormally small size of one or more of the epiphyses of the thumb with respect to age-dependent norms.
lay_en: Small end part of thumb long bone

terms.def_en: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in one or more of the epiphyses of the thumb.
lay_en: Speckled calcifications in end part of thumb bone
syn_en: Stippling of the epiphyses of the thumb

lay_en: Triangular end part of the thumb bone

terms.en: Contracture of the distal interphalangeal joint of the fingers
terms.def_en: Chronic loss of joint motion in one or more distal interphalangeal joints of the fingers.

terms.en: Osteolytic defects of the hand bones

terms.def_en: An abnormal union between bones or parts of bones of the fingers. The synonymous term "symphalangism of the hand" may be translated as fusions of bones of varying digree, that involve at least one phalangeal bone of the hand. If bony fusions are referred to as "Symphalangism" the fusion occurs in a proximo-distal axis. Fusions of bones of the fingers in a radio-ulnar axis are referred to as "bony" Syndactyly.
syn_en: Synostosis involving bones of the fingers

terms.def_en: Fusion involving two or more metacarpal bones (A synostosis of the first metacarpal and the proximal phalanx of the thumb can also be observed, note that the first metacarpal bone corresponds to a proximal phalanx).
Synostosis (bony fusion) involving one or more bones of the carpus (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate, pisiform).

Fusion of the 1st metacarpal with another bone. In contrast to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2 to 5, the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.
lay_en: Fusion involving 1st long bone of hand

terms.def_en: Chronic cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) lymphocytosis is defined as the finding, in at least two serial CSF examinations, of more than 5 cells per cubic millimeter.

lay_en: Fusion involving the 2nd long bone of hand
Fusion involving the 3rd long bone of hand
Fusion involving the 4th long bone of hand
Fusion involving the 5th long bone of hand

terms.def_en: Increased concentration of interferon alpha in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

Chilblains, also called perniosis, are an inflammatory skin condition related to an abnormal vascular response to the cold. We are unaware of a reliable estimate of incidence. It typically presents as tender, pruritic red or bluish lesions located symmetrically on the dorsal aspect of the fingers, toes, ears and nose. Less commonly, reports describe involvement of the thighs and buttocks. The lesions present hours after exposure to cold and usually resolve spontaneously in one to three weeks.
A benign vascular tumor of the retina without any neoplastic characteristics.
A hemangioblastoma of the spinal cord.
An abnormality of the epididymis.
A cystadenoma, an epithelial tumor, that originates within the head of the epididymis.
Small nodular masses which originate in the subependymal region of the lateral ventricles and protrude into the ventricular cavity. They may represent subependymal hamartomas of tuberous sclerosis.

Cortical tubers in the brain are hamartomatous lesions typically located at the gray-white matter interface, commonly in the frontal and parietal lobes. Cortical tubers are composed of abnormal glial and neural cells, and the size, number, and location vary among patients.

A demarcated, largely intraventricular tumor in the region of the foramen of Monro composed of spindle to large plump or ganglion-like cells with eosinophilic to amphophilic cytoplasm and somewhat pleomorphic nuclei with occasional prominent nucleoli. These tumors are almost always associated with tuberous sclerosis.

Hypomelanotic macules ("ash leaf spots") are white or lighter patches of skin that may appear anywhere on the body and are caused by a lack of melanin. White ash leaf-shaped macules are considered to be characteristic of tuberous sclerosis.
The presence of a sebaceous adenoma with origin in the sebum secreting cells of the skin.

A plaque representing a connective-tissue nevus. Connective tissue naevi are uncommon skin lesions that occur when the deeper layers of the skin do not develop correctly or the components of these layers occur in the wrong proportion. Shagreen patches are oval-shaped and nevoid, skin-colored or occasionally pigmented, smooth or crinkled. The word shagreen refers to a type of roughened untanned leather.
The presence of small depressions in the dental enamel.
A lesion located beneath a fingernail or toenail.
The presence of fibromata beneath finger or toenails.
The presence of a neoplasm of the urinary bladder.
The presence of a neoplasm of the kidney.
Areas of the retina lacking pigmentation. Punched out areas of chorioretinal hypopigmentation less than 1 disk diameter in size and tending to be located in the midperiphery of the retina.
syn_en: Punched out areas of chorioretinal hypopigmentation

terms.def_en: A benign or malignant neoplasm (tumor) originating in striated muscle, either skeletal muscle or cardiac muscle.
A benign tumor of cardiac striated muscle.
A benign tumor of striated muscle.
The presence of a hamartoma of the cerebrum.
A neurofibroma in which Schwann cells proliferate inside the nerve sheath, producing an irregularly thickened, distorted, tortuous structure.
The presence of a glioma, which is a neoplasm of the central nervous system originating from a glial cell (astrocytes or oligodendrocytes).
A glioma originating in the optic nerve or optic chiasm.
A neurofibroma (benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor) localized in the spine.

Pseudarthrosis, or "false joint" of the tibia is the result of a developmental failure in the tibia progressing to spontaneous fracture and subsequent fibrous nonunion. The fracture is rarely present at birth but commonly develops during the first 18 months of life.
The presence of pigmented, oval and dome-shaped raised hamartomatous nevi of the iris..
An abnormality of the antihelix.
Developmental hypoplasia of the antihelix.
Absence of the parotid gland.
Nephrosclerosis refers to thickening or scarring ("sclerosis") resulting from damage to the renal arterioles, also referred to as arteriosclerosis of the kidney arteries.
Shoulder joint stiffness is a perceived sensation of tightness in shoulders when attempting to move them after a period of inactivity.
Double rows of eyelashes.
An abnormality of the spinal dura mater, which is the outermost of the three layers of the meninges surrounding the spinal cord.
syn_en: Abnormality of the spinal dura mater

terms.def_en: Presence of arachnoid cysts of the spinal canal extradurally in the epidural space.
syn_en: Epidural arachnoid cysts of the spinal canal

terms.def_en: Abnormally increased thickness of the nasal septum.
Abnormally increased hair growth in the lumbosacral region.
Increased volume of the earlobe, that is, abnormally prominent ear lobules.

terms.en: Aplasia of the pectoralis major muscle
terms.def_en: Absence of the pectoralis major muscle.
A bony defect in the skull base.
Complete or nearly complete soft tissue fusion of the alveolar ridges.
Partial fusion of the upper and lower eyelid margins by single or multiple bands of tissue.
A pterygium (or pterygia) occurring in the popliteal region (the back of the knee).
A pterygium (or pterygia) in the intercrural (groin) region.

terms.en: Pyramidal skinfold extending from the base to the top of the nails
terms.def_en: Pyramidal skinfold extending from the base to the top of the nails is a rare and distinctive anomaly seen in popliteal pterygia syndrome.
Pterygia affecting the neck.
Pterygium affecting the elbow. This is a cutaneous web that can lead to severe flexion contracture of the elbow joint. Antecubital pterygium can be unilateral, bilateral, symmetric, or asysmmetric.
Anterior schisis (cleft or cleavage) of vertebral bodies.
Excessive wrinkling of the skin of the face.
Chronic pain in the limbs with no clear focal etiology.
Columella extending inferior to the level of the nasal base, when viewed from the side.
syn_en: Extension of the columella below the ala nasi

terms.en: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the phalanges of the hand
terms.def_en: Small or missing phalangeal bones of the fingers of the hand.
Increased width of the phalanges of the hand.
syn_en: Widening of phalanges of the hand

terms.def_en: The presence of short and wide phalanges which taper distally ("bullet shaped").
syn_en: Conical bullet-shaped distal ends of phalanges

terms.en: Osteolytic defects of the phalanges of the hand
terms.it: Difetti osteolitici delle falangi della mano
terms.def_en: Dissolution or degeneration of bone tissue of the phalanges of the hand.
lay_en: Breakdown of small bones of fingers

terms.def_en: Uneven (irregular) increase in bone density of one or more of the phalanges of the hand.
lay_en: Uneven increase in bone density in finger bone
syn_en: Patchy sclerosis of the phalanges of the hand

terms.en: Triangular shaped phalanges of the hand
terms.it: Falangi della mano a forma triangolare

terms.def_en: Annular constrictions around the digits, limbs, or trunk, occurring congenitally (sometimes causing intrauterine autoamputation) and also associated with a wide variety of disorders. Constrictive amniotic bands are the result of primary amniotic rupture, which can lead to entanglement of fetal tissue (especially limbs) in fibrous amniotic strands.
The absence of all phalanges of all the digits of a limb and the associated soft tissues.
Absent thumb, i.e., the absence of both phalanges of a thumb and the associated soft tissues.
Hypoplasia (congenital reduction in size) of the thumb.
Syndactyly with fusion of toes three and four.

Horn-like malformations of the iliac crests with symmetrical bilateral central posterior iliac processes. A characteristic finding in the Nail-Patella syndrome. Iliac horns are visible on X-ray and may be palpable, but are asymptomatic.
A zone of darker pigmentation around the central part of the iris with a roughly cloverleaf or flower shape.
Absence or underdevelopment of the biceps muscle.
Absence of the biceps muscle.
Absence or underdevelopment of the triceps muscle.
Absence of the triceps muscle.

terms.en: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the musculature of the thigh
terms.def_en: Absence or underdevelopment involving the musculature of the thigh.
Absence or underdevelopment of the quadriceps muscle.
Absence of the quadriceps muscle.
The presence of an abscess located around the anus.
A hemisacral defect involving the sacral vertebrae S2 to S5. In hemisacrum, the first sacral vertebra is intact and there is agenesis involving only S2-S5.
Presence of a bifid sacral bone.
The presence of a teratoma.
A type of sacrococcygeal teratoma located anterior to the sacrum and entirely inside the body (Altman type IV).
Congenital developmental defect arising from the primitive branchial apparatus.
A congenital fistula in the neck resulting from incomplete closure of a branchial cleft.

A branchial cyst is a remnant of embryonic development resulting from a failure of obliteration of a branchial cleft and consists of a subcutaneous cystic mass. Cysts are located anterior or posterior to the ear or in the submandibular region.

Cholesteatoma is a benign but potentially destructive growth consisting of keratinizing epithelium located in the middle ear and/or mastoid process. In cholesteatoma, a skin cyst grows into the middle ear and mastoid. The cyst is not cancerous but can erode tissue and cause destruction of the ear.
A goiter that is not associated with functional thyroid abnormalities.
The presence of two or more accessory spleens.

terms.en: Aplasia of the phalanges of the hand
terms.def_en: Absence of one or more of the phalanges of the hand.
lay_en: Absent finger bone of the hand

terms.def_en: Short (hypoplastic) phalanx of finger, affecting one or more phalanges.
The absence of one or more teeth from the normal series by a failure to develop
syn_en: Failure of development of some teeth

terms.def_en: A form of heart failure characterized by reduced cardiac output. This may be seen in patients with heart failure owing to ischemic heart disease, hypertension, cardiomyopathy, and other causes.
A form of diabetes insipidus caused by failure of the kidneys to respond to vasopressin (AVP).

terms.en: Anomaly of the upper limb diaphyses
terms.def_en: A structural abnormality of a diaphysis of the arm.
lay_en: Abnormality of shaft of long bone of the upper limbs
syn_en: Abnormality involving the diaphyses of the upper limbs
Diaphyseal abnormality of the upper limbs

terms.def_en: An anomaly of one or more metaphyses of the arms.
lay_en: Abnormality of the wide portion of upper limb bone
syn_en: Metaphyseal abnormality of the upper limbs

lay_en: Abnormality of the joints of the upper limbs

terms.def_en: An anomaly of the joint that connects the upper and the lower arm.

terms.it: Amelia che coinvolge gli arti superiori
terms.def_en: Amelia of one or both upper limbs.

Missing or malformed long bones of the upper limbs with the distal parts (the hands) connected to the variably shortened or even absent upper extremity, leading to a flipper-like appearance, as opposed to other forms of limb malformations were either the whole limb is missing (such as amelia), or the distal part of a limb is absent (peromelia).
Peromelia affecting only the upper limbs. That is, the distal parts of the arm are missing leading to stump formation.
Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of the extremities.
Leg shortening because of underdevelopment of one or more bones of the lower extremity.
syn_en: Hypoplasia involving bones of the lower limbs

terms.en: Aplasia involving bones of the lower limbs
lay_en: Absent bones of the lower limbs

terms.def_en: Complete or near-complete absence of a leg.
Phocomelia affecting only the lower limbs.
Peromelia affecting only the lower limbs. That is, the distal parts of the leg are missing leading to stump formation.
Forearm shortening because of underdevelopment of one or more bones of the forearm.

terms.en: Aplasia involving bones of the upper limbs
lay_en: Absent bones of the upper limbs

terms.def_en: Arm shortening because of underdevelopment of one or more bones of the upper extremity.
syn_en: Hypoplasia involving bones of the upper limbs

terms.en: Aplasia involving bones of the extremities

terms.def_en: Limb shortening because of underdevelopment of one or more bones of the extremities.
syn_en: Hypoplasia involving bones of the extremities

terms.def_en: Congenital absence (aplasia) of one or more limbs.
The distal parts of the limbs are missing leading to a stump formation.

Missing or malformed long bones of the extremities with the distal parts (such as hands and/or feet) connected to the variably shortened or even absent extremity, leading to a flipper-like appearance, as opposed to other forms of limb malformations were either the entire limb is missing (such as amelia), or the distal part of a limb is absent (peromelia).

Peripheral neuropathy is a general term for any disorder of the peripheral nervous system. The main clinical features used to classify peripheral neuropathy are distribution, type (mainly demyelinating versus mainly axonal), duration, and course.
A focal lesion of a single peripheral nerve. Damage to a sensory nerve is accompanied by sensory impairment of all modalities in the affected anatomic distribution.

terms.en: Abnormal distal phalanx morphology of finger
terms.def_en: Any anomaly of distal phalanx of finger.
lay_en: Abnormality of the outermost finger bone
syn_en: Abnormal terminal phalanges of the hand
Abnormality of the distal phalanges of the hand
Abnormality of the distal phalanx of finger

lay_en: Abnormality of the middle finger bones of the hand
syn_en: Abnormality of the middle phalanges of the hand

lay_en: Abnormality of the innermost finger bones of the hand
syn_en: Abnormality of the proximal phalanges of the hand

lay_en: Absent/small outermost finger bone of the hand
Absent/underdeveloped outermost finger bone of the hand

syn_en: Broad distal phalanges of the hand
Broad, square ends of distal phalanges

lay_en: Curved outermost finger bone of the hand

Absent/underdeveloped middle finger bone of the hand

terms.en: Bullet-shaped middle phalanges of the hand
terms.def_en: Any of the middle phalanges with short and wide phalanx that tapers distally. Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction.

terms.en: Triangular shaped middle phalanges of the hand

Absent/underdeveloped innermost finger bones of the hand

terms.en: Broad proximal phalanges of the hand
terms.def_en: Increased width of the proximal phalanges of the finger.
lay_en: Broad innermost finger bones of the hand
Wide innermost finger bones of the hand

terms.en: Curved proximal phalanges of the hand
lay_en: Curved innermost finger bones of the hand

Patchy sclerosis of proximal phalanx of finger

Triangular shaped distal phalanges of the hand
