terms.en: Cerebellar ataxia associated with quadrupedal gait
terms.it: Atassia cerebellare associata ad andatura quadrupedica
terms.def_en: The presence of cerebellar signs and symptoms such as lack of balance associated with quadrupedal gait (locomotion on all four extremities with a 'bear-like' gait with the legs held straight).
An abnormality of the cerebral cortex with fewer gyri but with normal cortical thickness. This pattern is usually often associated with congenital microcephaly.

terms.en: Broad distal phalanges of all fingers
terms.def_en: Abnormally wide (broad) distal phalanx of finger of all fingers.

syn_en: Absent distal phalanges of the hand
Aplasia of the distal phalanges of the hand

terms.def_en: Short distance from the end of the finger to the most distal interphalangeal crease or the distal interphalangeal joint flexion point. That is, hypoplasia of one or more of the distal phalanx of finger.
syn_en: Hypoplasia of the distal phalanges of the hand

terms.en: Duplication of the distal phalanx of hand
terms.def_en: This term applies if one or more of the distal phalanges of the hand are either partially duplicated, depending on severity leading to a broad or bifid appearance of the phalanges, or completely duplicated.
lay_en: Duplication of the outermost bone of hand
syn_en: Partial/complete duplication of the distal phalanges of the hand

terms.def_en: A reduction in diameter of the distal phalanx of finger towards the distal end.
syn_en: Tapered distal phalanges of the hand

terms.def_en: Trichorrhexis nodosa is the formation of nodes along the hair shaft through which breakage readily occurs. It is thus a focal defect in the hair fiber that is characterized by thickening or weak points (nodes) that cause the hair to break off easily. The result is defective, abnormally fragile hair.
An abnormality of hair pigmentation (color).

Abnormality of the growth of secondary sexual hair, which normally ensues during puberty. In males, secondary sexual hair usually comprises body hair, including underarm, abdominal, chest, and pubic hair. In females, secondary sexual hair usually comprises a lesser degree of body hair, most prominently underarm and pubic hair.
Abnormally increased hair growth with a localized distribution.

Distance between the hairline (trichion) and the glabella (the most prominent point on the frontal bone above the root of the nose), in the midline, more than two SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased distance between the hairline and the glabella.
Flatness of the supraorbital portion of the frontal bones.
Complete absence of any auricular structures.
The presence of telangiectasia of the ear.
Increased thickness of the external ear.

terms.en: Abnormality of the crus of the helix
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the crus of the helix, which is the horizontal piece of cartilage located outside the ear canal that divides the upper and lower parts of the ear.
syn_en: Abnormality of the crus of the ear

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the antitragus, which is a small tubercle opposite to the tragus of the ear. The antitragus and the tragus are separated by the intertragic notch.

An abnormal horizontal axis orientation of the crus of the helix. That is, the main axis of the crus of the helix is perpendicular to the medial longitudinal axis of the ear, instead of sloping inferoposteriorly.
syn_en: Horizontal orientation of the crus of helix
Horizontal orientation of the ear crus

terms.def_en: Developmental hypoplasia of the crus of the helix. That is, flatter and/or shorter crus helix than average.
syn_en: Hypoplasia of the crus of the ear

terms.def_en: The presence of an abnormally prominent of the crus of the helix. That is, development of the crus helix to the same degree as an average antihelix stem or helix.
syn_en: Abnormal prominence of the crus of the ear

terms.def_en: A unilateral absence of sensory perception of sound.
Distortion of the course of the normal folds of the ear and the appearance of supernumerary crura and folds.
A notched form of the helix of the ear. That is, a defect in the continuity of the helix, which may occur at any point along its length.
Presence of nodules in the conjunctiva of the eye.
Abnormally prominent ear helix.
Decreased thickness of the helix of the ear.
Absence or underdevelopment of the ear lobes.
Attachment of the lobe to the side of the face at the lowest point of the lobe without curving upward.
Sharply demarcated, typically linear and approximately horizontal, indentations in the outer surface of the ear lobe.
An abnormal orientation of the earlobes such that they point out- and upward. That is, the lateral surface of ear lobe faces superiorly.

terms.en: Aplasia of the middle ear ossicles
terms.def_en: Absence of the middle ear ossicles, malleus, incus, and stapes.
Abnormality of the temporal bone of the skull, which is situated at the sides and base of the skull roughly underlying the region of the face known as the temple.
An abnormality of the tragus.
Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the tragus.
Cyclopia is a congenital abnormality in which there is only one eye. That eye is centrally placed in the area normally occupied by the root of the nose.
The presence of a size difference between the left and right cornea.
Anisocoria, or unequal pupil size, may represent a benign physiologic variant or a manifestation of disease.
The presence of remnants of a fetal membrane that persist as strands of tissue crossing the pupil.
A malposition of the pupil owing to a developmental defect of the iris.
A tumor of the eye originating from cells of the retina.
A dermal melanocytic hamartoma that presents as bluish hyperpigmentation on the face along the first or second branches of the trigeminal nerve. Nevus of Ota may involve the sclera.
A condition associated with a limitation of the horizontal ocular movement with retraction of the globe and narrowing of the palpebral fissure on adduction
syn_en: Limited eye motility from Duane anomaly
Limited eye movement from Duane anomaly

terms.en: Vascular remnant arising from the disk
terms.def_en: Persistence of the hyaloid artery, which is the embryonic artery that runs from the optic disc to the posterior lens capsule may persist; the site of attachment may form an opacity. The hyaloid artery is a branch of the ophthalmic artery, and usually regresses completely before birth.
Underdevelopment or absence of the nose or parts thereof.
Abnormally increased lacrimation, that is, excessive tearing (watering eye).
Complete absence of all nasal structures.
Increase in bulk of the ala nasi.
A structural abnormality of the columella.
Asymmetry or size difference between the left and right nostril.
syn_en: Asymmetry in the implantation of nares

terms.def_en: Increased aperture of the nostril.
The presence of only a single nostril.
Slender, slit-like aperture of the nostril.
The presence of more than two nostrils.
Absence or underdevelopment of the nasal septum.
lay_en: Failure of development of nasal septum

terms.def_en: Abnormally narrow nasal septum.
Excess facial hair.
Lack or loss of the soft tissues between the zygomata and mandible.
Absence of the mandible.
lay_en: Failure of development of lower jaw
syn_en: Aplasia of the lower jaw bone

terms.def_en: Lack of symmetry between the left and right mandible.
lay_en: Lower jaw shifted to one side

terms.def_en: The presence of an asymmetric mouth.

Complete or partial duplication of the phalanges of the thumb. Depending on the severity, the appearance on x-ray can vary from a notched phalanx (the duplicated bone is almost completely fused with the phalanx), a partially fused appearance of the two bones (bifid), two separate bones appearing side to side, or completely duplicated phalanges (proximal and distal phalanx of the thumb and/or 1st metacarpal). In contrast to the phalanges of the digits 2-5 (proximal, middle and distal), the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits.
syn_en: Complete/partial duplication of phalanges of the thumb

terms.def_en: A complete duplication affecting one or more of the phalanges of the thumb. As opposed to a partial duplication were there is still a variable degree of fusion between the duplicated bones, a complete duplication leads to two separate bones appearing side to side (radio-ulnar axis) as seen on x-rays. A duplication leading to an accessory bone appearing in the proximo-distal axis on x-rays, this is actually a different entity called a Pseudoepiphyses (see according terms) sometimes also referred to as Hyperphalangism.
syn_en: Complete duplication of the phalanges of the thumb

terms.it: Duplicazione parziale della falange del pollice
terms.def_en: A partial duplication, depending on severity leading to a broad or bifid appearance, affecting one or more of the phalanges of the thumb. As opposed to a complete duplication there is still a variable degree of fusion between the duplicated bones.
lay_en: Partial duplication of the thumb bones
syn_en: Partial duplication of the phalanges of the thumb

terms.def_en: This term applies if one or more of the phalanges of the 2nd finger are either partially duplicated, depending on severity leading to a broad or bifid appearance of the phalanges, or completely duplicated.
lay_en: Duplication of the bones of index finger
syn_en: Partial/complete duplication of phalanges of the 2nd finger

terms.en: Duplication of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger

terms.def_en: A structural abnormality of the interventricular septum.

In contrast to forms of polydactyly where the supernumerary digit (this can either be a rudimentary or a completely 'normal' digit) is either located postaxial (on the fibular side of the foot, next top the little toe), preaxial (on the tibial side of the foot, next to the big toe) or mesoaxial (somewhere central, between big and little toe), a supernumerary digit may also be placed ectopically, meaning anywhere else except post-,meso- or preaxial. In the literature this is sometimes referred to as Disorganisation-like Syndrome (OMIM223200).

In contrast to forms of polydactyly where the supernumerary digit (this can either be a rudimentary or a completely 'normal' digit) is either located postaxial (on the ulnar side of the hand, next to the little finger), preaxial (on the radial side of the hand, next to the thumb) or mesoaxial (somewhere central, between thumb and little finger), a supernumerary digit may also be placed ectopically, meaning anywhere else except post-,meso- or preaxial. In the literature this is sometimes referred to as Disorganisation-like Syndrome (OMIM223200).
A congenital anomaly characterized by the presence of supernumerary fingers or toes.
lay_en: More than five fingers or toes on hands or feet

terms.def_en: A bifid or bifurcated appearance of the femur as seen on x-rays, possible appearing as a more or less severe bowing of the upper leg. Might be associated with hip dysplasia on the affected side.
The retrograde (backwards) flow of blood through the pulmonary valve into the right ventricle during diastole.

An ostium primum atrial septal defect is located in the most anterior and inferior aspect of the atrial septum. The ostium primum refers to an anterior and inferior opening (ostium) within the septum primum, which divides the rudimentary atrium during fetal development. The ostium primum is normally sealed by fusion of the superior and inferior endocardial cushions around 5 weeks' gestation. Ostium primum defects result from a failure of the fusion of the embryologic endocardial cushion and septum primum.
A narrowing of the orifice of the tricuspid valve of the heart.
An abnormal connection between the epithelialised surface of the anal canal and the perianal skin.
A developmental defect resulting in complete obliteration of the lumen of the colon. That is, there is an abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the colon.
An abnormal narrowing of the lumen of the esophagus.
Absence or underdevelopment of the spleen.
An abnormal (non-anatomic) location of the spleen.
Pelvic asymmetry refers to asymmetric positioning of landmarks on the two sides of the pelvis and may have a structural or functional etiology.
The presence of osteophytes (bone spurs), i.e., of bony projections originating from the acetabulum.
An exaggeration of the normal arched form of the acetabular roof such that it takes on a steep appearance.
An abnormality of the sacrosciatic notch, i.e., the deep indentation in the posterior border of the hip bone at the point of union of the ilium and ischium.
syn_en: Abnormality of the greater sacrosciatic notch

terms.def_en: Hermaphroditism refers to a discrepancy between the morphology of the gonads and that of the external genitalia. In female pseudohermaphroditism, the genotype is female (XX) and the gonads are ovaries, but the external genitalia are virilized.
The presence of both ovarian and testicular tissues either in the same or in opposite gonads. Affected persons have ambiguous genitalia and may have 46,XX or 46,XY karyotypes or 46,XX/XY mosaicism.
Abnormality of the female genital system.
Abnormality of the male genital system.
Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the ovary.
Aplasia, that is failure to develop, of the ovary.

A developmental disorder characterized by the progressive loss of primordial germ cells in the developing ovaries of an embryo, leading to hypoplastic ovaries composed of wavy connective tissue with occasional clumps of granulosa cells, and frequently mesonephric or hilar cells.
The onset of puberty before the age of 8 years in girls.
Absence or underdevelopment of the testes.
Testis not palpable in the scrotum or inguinal canal.
The presence of more than two testes.
Increased urinary excretion of oligosaccharides (low molecular weight carbohydrate chains composed of at least three monosaccharide subunits), derived from a partial degradation of glycoproteins.
Any deviation from the normal concentration of porphyrins in the blood circulation.
Abnormally increased excretion of porphyrins in the urine.
Buildups of minerals that form in the urinary bladder.
Cloacal exstrophy is a severe anterior abdominal wall defect in which the two hemibladders are visible and are separated by a midline intestinal plate, an omphalocele, and an imperforate anus.
Absence or underdevelopment of the urinary bladder.
Aplasia (absence) of the urinary bladder.
Abnormality of the urachus.
Persistence of the urachal canal resulting in a canal between the bladder and the umbilicus.
The presence of an abnormal connection between the urethra and another organ or the skin.
The presence of an abnormal membrane obstructing the urethra.
Shortening of the arms predominantly affecting terminal parts of the arm in relation to the upper and middle limb segments.
Amniotic constriction rings affecting the arms.
Abnormal increase in size of the upper limbs (due to an increase of the size of cells).
The ability of the elbow joint to move beyond its normal range of motion.
An abnormality of the hypothenar eminence, i.e., of the muscles on the ulnar side of the palm of the hand (i.e., on the side of the little finger).
Reduced muscle mass on the ulnar side of the palm, that is, reduction in size of the hypothenar eminence.
Absence or underdevelopment of the palmar creases.
The absence of the major creases of the palm (distal transverse crease, proximal transverse crease, or thenar crease).
An abnormality of the creases of the skin of palm of hand.
A narrow segment of significantly reduced circumference of a digit.
Webbing or fusion of the fingers, involving soft parts and including fusion of individual finger bones.
An abnormally increased length of the metacarpal bones.
Shortening of the legs predominantly affecting terminal parts of the leg in relation to the upper and middle arm segments.
Amniotic constriction rings affecting the legs.
Abnormal increase in size of the lower limbs (due to an increase of the size of cells).
A developmental defect in which the legs are fused together.
A developmental defect that occurs if the two halves of the patella fail to fuse in early childhood.

The kneecap normally is located within the groove termed trochlea on the distal femur and can slide up and down in it. Patellar subluxation refers to an unstable kneecap that does not slide centrally within its groove, i.e., a partial dislocation of the patella.
The ability of the knee joint to extend beyond its normal range of motion (the lower leg is moved beyond a straight position with respect to the thigh).
An abnormal limitation of knee joint mobility.
A bending or abnormal curvature of the fibula.
Duplication of the fibula. This may occur as a part of diplopodia (accessory tarsal or metatarsal bone). Diplopodia with double fibula is an extremely rare condition.
An abnormal increase in the length of the tibia.
An abnormal limitation of the mobility of the ankle joint.
An abnormality of dermatoglyphs on the toes and soles, i.e., an abnormality of the patterns of ridges of the skin of sole of foot.
A difference in size or shape between the left and right foot.
A condition in which the anterior part of the foot rotates outward away from the midline of the body and the heel remains straight.
Absence of the tarsal bones.
An ability of the toe joints to move beyond their normal range of motion.
Toes that appear disproportionately long compared to the foot.
Calcification within the adrenal glands.
Deposition of calcium salts in the pituitary gland.

Hypersecretion of one or more pituitary hormones. This can occur in conditions in which deficiency in the target organ leads to decreased hormonal feedback, or as a primary condition most usually in connection with a pituitary adenoma.
Absence or underdevelopment of the thymus.
Enlargement of the thymus.

The presence of ectopic thymus tissue. Normally, cells of the ventral bud of the third pharyngeal pouch detach and migrate in the eighth gestational week caudally and medially towards the location of the mature thyroid. They migrate further retrosternally into the superior mediastinum. There are two main ways ectopic thymus tissue can develop. Either cells detach along the descensus path and proliferate, thereby forming accessory thymus tissue, or the entire gland fails to descend.
An abnormality of the thyroid gland owing to the presence of a fibrous cyst resulting from the persistence of the thyroglossal duct.
An abnormal increase in quantity or strength of fetal movements.
Gait apraxia affecting the ability to make walking movements with the legs.

A learning disorder characterized primarily by difficulties in learning to read and spell. Dyslectic children also exhibit a tendency to read words from right to left and to confuse letters such as b and d whose orientation is important for their identification. Children with dyslexia appear to be impaired in phonemic skills (the ability to associate visual symbols with the sounds they represent).
An acquired type of sensory aphasia where damage to the brain leads to the loss of the ability to read.
Alteration or impairment in the processing or interpretation of sensory information can lead to abnormal perceptions or experiences.
The examiner identified the inability to name, move, or touch specific fingers.

A writing disability in the absence of motor or sensory deficits of the upper extremities, resulting in an impairment in the ability to write regardless of the ability to read and not due to intellectual impairment.
Tactile agnosia refers to the inability to recognize objects by touch, while the inability to discriminate shape and size by touch is also a related condition.
Inability to recognize faces of familiar persons.

Echolalia is the automatic imitative repetition of sounds, words, or phrases in the absence of explicit awareness. The repeated words or phrases are typically odd or used in a non-social manner. These can be words or phrases that the affected individual has heard or invented.
Palatal tremor (PT) is an involuntary, rhythmic and oscillatory movement of the soft palate. PT is a rare type of tremor involving the soft palate. It can be unilateral or bilateral.

Spinal myoclonus is generally due to a tumor, infection, injury, or degenerative process of the spinal cord, and is characterized by involuntary rhythmic muscle contractions, usually at a rate of more than one per second. Myoclonus occurs synchronously in several muscles and can be increased in severity and frequency by fatigue or stress, but is usually unaffected by sensory stimuli. Spinal myoclonus ceases during sleep or anesthesia.
Paroxysmal episodes of vertigo.
The combination of pendular nystagmus, head nodding, and torticollis.
A paroxysmal, transient loss of memory function with preservation of immediate recall and remote memory but with a severe impairment of memory for recent events and ability to retain new information.

An intermittent cessation of airflow at the mouth and nose during sleep is known as sleep apnea. Apneas that last at least 10 seconds are considered significant, but individuals with sleep apnea may experience apneas lasting from 20 seconds up to 2 or 3 minutes. Patients may have up to 15 events per hour of sleep.
Sleep apnea results from a temporary loss of the central drive to the muscles responsible for breathing.
An abnormally increased width of the cranial sutures for age-related norms (generally resulting from delayed closure).
An abnormally small sella turcica.
The presence of an abnormally thin calvarium.
A degree of pneumatization that is increased compared to age-related norms.

The presence of convoluted folds and furrows formed from thickened skin of the scalp, resembling cerebriform pattern. The scalp has convoluted and elevated folds, 1 to 2 cm in thickness. The convolutions generally cannot be flattened by traction.
lay_en: Furrows in thickened skin on top of scalp
Thickened folds on top of scalp

terms.def_en: Nystagmus due to disturbance of the vestibular system; eye movements are rhythmic, with slow and fast components.
Bursts of large-amplitude multidirectional saccades without intersaccadic interval

Vertical nystagmus may present with either up-beating or down-beating eye movements or both. When present in the straight-ahead position of gaze it is referred to as upbeat nystagmus or downbeat nystagmus.
Downbeat nystagmus is a type of fixation nystagmus with the fast phase beating in a downward direction. It generally increases when looking to the side and down and when lying prone.

Fine, rapid twitching of individual muscle fibers with little or no movement of the muscle as a whole as ascertained by electromyography (EMG). If a motor neuron or its axon is destroyed, the muscle fibers it innervates undergo denervation atrophy. This leads to hypersensitivity of individual muscle fibers to acetyl choline so that they may contract spontaneously. Isolated activity of individual muscle fibers is generally so fine it cannot be seen through the intact skin, although it can be recorded as a short-duration spike in the EMG.

A type of paralysis in which a muscle becomes soft and yields to passive stretching, which results from loss of all or practically all peripheral motor nerves that innervated the muscle. Muscle tone is reduced and the affected muscles undergo extreme atrophy within months of the loss of innervation.
A localized myotonic contraction in a muscle in reaction to percussion (tapping with the examiner's finger, a rubber percussion hammer, or a similar object).
syn_en: Transient swelling of muscle induced by percussion

terms.en: Weakness due to upper motor neuron dysfunction
terms.def_en: Paralysis of voluntary muscles means loss of contraction due to interruption of one or more motor pathways from the brain to the muscle fibers. Although the word paralysis is often used interchangeably to mean either complete or partial loss of muscle strength, it is preferable to use paralysis or plegia for complete or severe loss of muscle strength, and paresis for partial or slight loss. Paralysis due to lesions of the principle motor tracts is related to a lesion in the corticospinal, corticobulbar or brainstem descending (subcorticospinal) neurons.
syn_en: Paralysis due to lesions of the principle motor tracts

terms.def_en: Severe or complete weakness of both lower extremities with sparing of the upper extremities.
Weakness of both lower extremities with sparing of the upper extremities. Paraplegia refers to a severe or complete loss of strength, whereas paraparesis refers to a relatively mild loss of strength.

An acute dystonic reaction with blepharospasm, periorbital twitches, and protracted fixed staring episodes. There may be a maximal upward deviation of the eyes in the sustained fashion. Oculogyric crisis can be triggered by a number of factors including neuroleptic medications.

A soft tissue continuity in the A/P axis between two fingers that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints, or a soft tissue continuity in the A/P axis between two fingers that lies significantly distal to the flexion crease that overlies the metacarpophalangeal joint of the adjacent fingers.
A finger resting on the dorsal surface of an adjacent digit when the hand is at rest.
An abnormality of the clivus, which is the inclined bony region of the posterior cranial fossa located between the sella turcica and the foramen magnum.
An abnormal vertical orientation of the clivus (which normally forms a kind of slope from the sella turcica down to the region of the foramen magnum).
An abnormally wavy surface or edge of the clavicles.
An abnormally wavy surface or edge of the ribs.

A midline anterior-posterior cleft of the epiglottis that involves at least two-thirds of the epiglottic leaf. It is a useful feature for clinical diagnosis because it appears to be very rare in syndromes other than Pallister-Hall-Syndrome and is also rare as an isolated malformation.
This term applies if the Epiglottis is absent or hypoplastic.

A disordered proliferation of mature tissues that is native to the site of origin, e.g., exostoses, nevi and soft tissue hamartomas. Although most hamartomas are benign, some histologic subtypes, e.g., neuromuscular hamartoma, may proliferate aggressively such as mesenchymal cystic hamartoma, Sclerosing epithelial hamartoma, Sclerosing metanephric hamartoma.

Y-shaped metatarsals are the result of a partial fusion of two metatarsal bones, with the two arms of the Y pointing in the distal direction. Y-shaped metatarsals may be seen in combination with polydactyly.
A hamartoma (disordered proliferation of mature tissues) which can originate from any tissue of the eye.
The concentration of 7-dehydrocholesterol in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
An abnormal elevation of phytanic acid.

terms.en: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the femoral head
terms.def_en: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
lay_en: Abnormality of the end part of the innermost thighbone
syn_en: Abnormality of the proximal femoral epiphysis

terms.def_en: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the femoral head.
A cystic lesion originating within the brain.

lay_en: Bracket shaped end part of long bone

terms.def_en: Cone-shaped epiphyses (also known as coned epiphyses) are epiphyses that invaginate into cupped metaphyses. That is, the epiphysis has a cone-shaped distal extension resulting from increased growth of the central portion of the epiphysis relative to its periphery.
Increased size of epiphyses.
An alteration of the normally smooth contour of the epiphysis leading to an irregular appearance.
lay_en: Irregular end part of long bone

terms.def_en: Sclerosis of the epiphyses, leading to an increased degree of radiopacity (white or ivory appearance) in X-rays.
lay_en: Increased bone density in end part of bone

terms.def_en: Reduction in the size or volume of epiphyses.

Longitudinal epiphyseal bracket or bracket epiphysis is an uncommon disorder of growth. Alternatively known as a delta phalanx, it is due to an anomalous secondary ossification center that extends longitudinally along the diaphysis. Although rare, longitudinal epiphyseal bracket most commonly manifests in the hands as clinodactyly and in the feet as hallux varus.

Stop of growth at the epiphyseal plate the hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at each end of a long bone, at an earlier than normal age, resulting in growth arrest and shortening of the involved bone.

terms.en: Abnormality of the distal femoral epiphysis
terms.def_en: Any abnormality of the distal epiphysis of the femur.
lay_en: Abnormality of the end part of the outermost thighbone

terms.en: Abnormality of the proximal tibial epiphysis
terms.def_en: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the tibia.
lay_en: Abnormality of the end part of innermost shankbone
Abnormality of the end part of innermost shinbone

terms.en: Abnormality of the distal tibial epiphysis
lay_en: Abnormality of the end part of outermost shankbone
Abnormality of the end part of outermost shinbone
Abnormality of the end part of the calf bone

terms.en: Abnormality of the proximal fibular epiphysis
terms.def_en: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the fibula.
lay_en: Abnormality of the innermost end part of calf bone

terms.en: Abnormality of the distal fibular epiphysis
terms.def_en: Any abnormality of the distal epiphysis of the fibula.
lay_en: Abnormality of the outermost end part of calf bone

terms.def_en: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the radius.
syn_en: Abnormality of the proximal radial epiphysis

terms.en: Abnormality of the distal radial epiphysis
terms.def_en: Any abnormality of the distal epiphysis of the radius.

terms.en: Abnormality of the proximal humeral epiphysis
terms.def_en: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the humerus.
lay_en: Abnormality of the end part of the innermost long bone in upper arm

terms.def_en: Any abnormality of the distal epiphysis of the humerus.
lay_en: Abnormality of the end part of the outermost long bone in upper arm
syn_en: Abnormality of the distal humeral epiphysis

terms.def_en: Any abnormality of the distal epiphysis of the ulna.
syn_en: Abnormality of the distal ulnar epiphysis

terms.def_en: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the ulna.
syn_en: Abnormality of the proximal ulnar epiphysis

terms.it: Prevalenza di fibre muscolari di tipo 2
terms.def_en: An abnormal predominance of type II muscle fibers (in general, this feature can only be observed on muscle biopsy).

A benign uni- or multicystic, intraosseous tumor of odontogenic origin, with a characteristic lining of parakeratinized stratified squamous epithelium and potential for aggressive, infiltrative behavior.

A chronic epithelioid cell granulomatous inflammation of the meibomian gland caused by inflammation of a blocked meibomian gland. A chalazion or meibomian cyst appears as a painless tuberous swelling in the upper lid without loss of eyelashes.

An acute purulent infection of the sebaceous glands of Zeis at the base of the eyelashes, of the apocrine sweat glands of Moll or the meibomian sebacious glands often caused by staphylococcus infections. Hordeola can either occur as Hordeola externa affecting the sebaceous glands of Zeis or the apocrine sweat glands of Moll or as Hordeola interna affecting the meibomian sebacious glands. In contrast to chalazia, hordeola are extremely painful and can cause extreme local swelling.

Hordeola externa are acute purulent infections affecting the sebaceous glands of Zeis or the apocrine sweat glands of Moll, often caused by staphylococcus infections. In contrast to chalazia, hordeola are extremely painfull and can cause extreme local swelling.

Hordeola interna are acute purulent infections affecting the meibomian sebacious glands, often caused by staphylococcus infections. In contrast to chalazia (chronic epithelioid cell granulomatous inflammation of the meibomian gland caused by inflammation of a blocked meibomian gland), hordeola are extremely painfull and can cause extreme local swelling.

Cutaneous skin tags also known as acrochorda or fibroepithelial polyps are small benign tumors that may either form secondarily over time primarily in areas where the skin forms creases, such as the neck, armpit or groin or may also be present at birth, in which case they usually occur in the periauricular region.
The presence of multiple pits (small, pinpoint-large indentations on the surface of the skin) located on the skin of sole of foot.

Benign tumors that are composed of fibrous or connective tissue. They can grow in all organs, arising from mesenchyme tissue. The term "fibroblastic" or "fibromatous" is used to describe tumors of the fibrous connective tissue. When the term fibroma is used without modifier, it is usually considered benign, with the term fibrosarcoma reserved for malignant tumors.
Angiofibroma consist of many often dilated vessels.
The presence of a lung fibroma, a benign neoplasm that can present as a mass causing airway obstruction, cough, and hemoptysis, or present without symptoms as a solitary pulmonary nodule.
A fibroma of the heart.
The presence of a fibroma of the ovary.
A benign biphasic tumor of the breast with epithelial and stromal components.
Prominence of the malar process of the maxilla and infraorbital area appreciated in profile and from in front of the face.

terms.it: Sindattilia cutanea delle dita dei piedi
terms.def_en: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between adjacent foot digits that involves at least half of the proximodistal length of one of the two involved digits; or, a soft tissue continuity in the A/P axis between two digits of the foot that does not meet the prior objective criteria.
A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the skeleton.
Absence or underdevelopment of the toenail.
Absence or underdevelopment of the anterior pituitary gland, also known as the adenohypophysis.
Absence of the anterior pituitary gland resulting from a developmental defect.
Underdevelopment of the anterior pituitary gland.

Facial nerve palsy is a dysfunction of cranial nerve VII (the facial nerve) that results in inability to control facial muscles on the affected side with weakness of the muscles of facial expression and eye closure. This can either be present in unilateral or bilateral form.

terms.en: Abnormal morphology of the cortex of the humerus
terms.def_en: Any abnormality affecting the cortex of the humerus.
Any abnormality of a metatarsal bone epiphysis.
lay_en: Abnormality of end part of long bone of foot
syn_en: Abnormality of the epiphyses of the metatarsals

terms.en: Abnormality of the epiphyses of the feet
terms.def_en: Any abnormality of the epiphyses of the feet.
lay_en: Abnormality of the end part of the foot bone

terms.def_en: Inability to detect any qualitative olfactory sensation.
Inability to perceive certain odorants (implies that the sense of smell is maintained for other classes of odorants).
Reduced ability to detect any qualitative olfactory sensation.
Reduced ability to perceive certain odorants (implies that the sense of smell is maintained for other classes of odorants).
The presence of a cleft in the cerebral cortex unilaterally or bilaterally, usually located in the frontal area.
A form of amyloidosis that affects the conjunctiva.

terms.en: Elevated alkaline phosphatase of hepatic origin
terms.def_en: An abnormally increased level of liver isoforms of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.

terms.en: Elevated alkaline phosphatase of bone origin
terms.it: Fosfatasi alcalina elevata di origine ossea
terms.def_en: An abnormally increased level of bone isoforms of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.
lay_en: Elevated alkaline phosphatase of bone origin

terms.def_en: Abnormality of the nasal cavity (the cavity includes and starts at the nares and reaches all the way through to the and includes the choanae, the posterior nasal apertures).
Abnormality of the midnasal cavity which includes the cavity between the nares and the choanae.
Absence or abnormal closure of the midnasal cavity.
Abnormal narrowing (stenosis) of the midnasal cavity, i.e., of the middle nasal meatus, which in neonates can cause respiratory distress.

terms.en: Aplasia of the distal phalanges of the toes
terms.def_en: Absence of the distal phalanges of the toes.
lay_en: Absent outermost bone of the toes

terms.def_en: An abnormal lack of stability of the cervical spine.
Any abnormal increase or reduction in skin elasticity.
An abnormally increased ability of the skin to permit light to pass through (translucency) such that subcutaneous structures such as veins display an increased degree of visibility.

An abnormal degree of flatness of the Ala of nose, which can be defined as a reduced nasal elevation index (lateral depth of the nose from the tip of the nose to the insertion of the nasal ala in the cheek x 100 divided by the side-to-side breadth of the nasal alae).

An abnormality of the premaxilla (the embryonic structure that forms the anterior part of the maxilla) causing it to appear relatively small in size compared to the other parts of the maxilla or other facial structures.
lay_en: Hypoplasia of the primary palate bone
Underdevelopment of the primary palate bone
syn_en: Decreased size of the primary palate bone

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the Meninges, including any abnormality of the Dura mater, the Arachnoid mater, and the Pia mater.
An abnormality of the Dura mater.
An abnormality of the Falx cerebri.
A developmental defect characterized by aplasia of the Falx cerebri.
The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in one or more epiphyses.
lay_en: Speckled calcifications in end part of bone

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the formation and mineralization of an epiphysis.
lay_en: Abnormal maturation of the end part of a bone
syn_en: Abnormality of the mineralisation or ossification of the epiphyses

terms.en: Patchy reduction of bone mineral density
terms.def_en: Patchy (irregular) reduction in bone density. This can take on many forms depending on severity and distribution as can be seen on x-rays.

terms.en: Patchy changes of bone mineral density
terms.def_en: Patchy (irregular) changes in bone mineral density. These changes can either be patchy reduction or increase of mineral density as seen on x-rays. Depending on the pathomechanism and the underlying disease, these changes can either appear solely as reduction or increase or as a combination of both (patches of bone showing an increased density while others are affected by reduction of mineral density).

terms.en: Patchy variation in bone mineral density
terms.def_en: Patchy (irregular) changes in bone mineral density with patches of bone showing an increased density side to side with patches that are affected by reduction of mineral density. This is sometimes referred to as a moth-eaten appearance on x-rays.
lay_en: Patchy increased and decreased bone mineral density

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the formation and mineralization of any bone of the skeleton of hand.
lay_en: Abnormal maturation of the hand bones
syn_en: Abnormality of the mineralisation and ossification of bones of the hand

terms.en: Absence of the third cerebral ventricle
terms.def_en: A developmental defect characterized by the absence of the third ventricle.
An abnormality of the Diencephalon, which together with the cerebrum (telencephalon) makes up the forebrain.
An abnormality of the thalamus.

terms.en: Fusion of the left and right thalami
terms.def_en: A developmental defect characterized by fusion of the left and right halves of the thalamus.
The presence of bilateral coxa valga.

terms.en: Hypoplasia of the anterior nasal spine
terms.def_en: Underdevelopment of the anterior nasal spine of maxilla.
syn_en: Decreased projection of anterior nasal spine
Decreased size of anterior nasal spine

terms.def_en: A congenital defect characterized by absence of the Maxilla.
lay_en: Failure of development of upper jaw bones
syn_en: Aplasia of the upper jaw bones

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the zygomatic bone.
Underdevelopment of the zygomatic bone. That is, a reduction in size of the zygomatic bone, including the zygomatic process of the temporal bone of the skull, which forms part of the zygomatic arch.

terms.en: Abnormality of the third metatarsal bone
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the third metatarsal bone.
lay_en: Abnormality of the 3rd long bone of foot

terms.en: Abnormal curvature of the vertebral column
terms.def_en: The presence of an abnormal curvature of the vertebral column.
syn_en: Abnormality of the curvature of the vertebral column

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the formation and mineralization of any bone of the skeleton of foot.
syn_en: Abnormality of the mineralisation and ossification of bones of the feet

terms.def_en: Enuresis occurring during sleeping hours.
Enuresis occurring during waking hours of the day.
An abnormally increased level of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.

terms.en: Elevated alkaline phosphatase of renal origin
terms.def_en: An abnormally increased level of kidney isoforms of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.
An abnormally increased level of alkaline phosphatase, intestinal type in the blood.
An abnormally increased level of alkaline phosphatase, placental type in the blood.
An abnormally reduced level of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.

terms.en: Low alkaline phosphatase of bone origin
terms.def_en: An abnormally reduced level of bone isoforms of alkaline phosphatase in the blood.

terms.en: Low alkaline phosphatase of renal origin
terms.def_en: An abnormally reduced level of kidney isoforms of alkaline phosphatase in the blood.

terms.en: Low alkaline phosphatase of hepatic origin
terms.def_en: An abnormally reduced level of liver isoforms of alkaline phosphatase in the blood.
An abnormally reduced level of alkaline phosphatase, intestinal type in the blood.
An abnormally reduced level of alkaline phosphatase, placental type in the blood.

A hand or foot with more than five digits that has a recognizable A/P axis of symmetry. The axis can lie within a normally formed or partially duplicated digit resembling a middle finger, index finger, thumb, toe, or hallux. Alternatively, the axis can be in an interdigital space with a flanking pair of digits that resemble a middle finger, index finger, thumb, toe or hallux. The most lateral digits on each side of the hand/foot typically resemble fifth fingers/toes.
Mirror image duplication of digits affecting the hands only.
Mirror image duplication of digits affecting the feet.
A kind of congenital cataract that is characterized by a hollow sphere of punctate opacities involving the fetal nucleus and that usually occurs bilaterally.
A Lamellar cataract with a pulverulent (punctate, "dust-like" opacities) appearance.
A type of congenital cataract in which the opacity follows the anterior or posterior Y suture.
A type of Congenital cataract in which the opacities occupy the subcapsular cortex at the anterior or posterior pole of the lens.
A type of anterior polar cataract which projects as a conical opacity into the anterior chamber.
A type of nuclear cataract involving congenital dust-like (pulverulent) opacity of the embryonal and fetal nucleus.
A nuclear cataract with a triangular form.
An abnormal deviation from normal levels of immunoglobulins in blood.

terms.it: Aumento del livello di anticorpi circolanti
terms.def_en: An increased level of gamma globulin (immunoglobulin) in the blood.
A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the thumb to the index finger that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.
A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the fourth (ring) to the fifth (little) finger that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.
A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the thumb to the middle finger that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.
A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the thumb to the ring finger that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.

A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the thumb to the little finger that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints (complete syndactyly of all fingers of the hand).
A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the second (index) to the fourth (ring) finger that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.
syn_en: Syndactyly of second to fourth fingers

terms.def_en: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the middle to little fingers that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.
lay_en: Webbed third, fourth and fifth toes

terms.def_en: Syndactyly with fusion of toes one and two.
Syndactyly with fusion of toes one to four.
Syndactyly with fusion of toes one to five (complete syndactyly of all toes of the foot).
Syndactyly with fusion of toes two to four.
Syndactyly with fusion of toes two to five.
Syndactyly with fusion of toes three to five.

Webbing or fusion of the toes, involving soft parts and including fusion of individual bones of the toes. Bony fusions are referred to as "bony" Syndactyly if the fusion occurs in a tibial-fibular axis. Fusions of bones of the toes in a proximo-distal axis are referred to as "Symphalangism".
An abnormality of the texture of the hair.
An abnormality of the distribution of hair growth.
An abnormal hair whorl (that is, a patch of hair growing in the opposite direction of the rest of the hair).
An asymmetriy, i.e., difference in size, shape or position between the left and right ear.

terms.en: Advanced pneumatization of the mastoid process
terms.def_en: An abnormally advanced degree of pneumatization (i.e., formation of air cells) in the mastoid process with respect to age-dependent norms.
Abnormal prominence of the corneal nerve fibers.
Rupture of the eyeball not due to trauma.
A developmental defect characterized by absence of the retina.

terms.en: Cherry red spot of the macula
terms.def_en: Pallor of the perifoveal macula of the retina with appearance of a small circular reddish choroid shape as seen through the fovea centralis due to relative transparency of the macula.
This may present as a partial or complete duplication of the eyebrows.

terms.en: Extension of eyebrows towards upper eyelid
terms.def_en: The eyebrows extend towards - or even all the way down to - the margin of the upper eyelid.
lay_en: Extension of eyebrows towards upper eyelid

terms.def_en: Nodular changes affecting the eyelids may have many different causes such as cystic lesions (chalaziae, hordeolae), lipogranulomas, melanomas, infectious diseases (Molluscum contagiosum) and many more.
Naevus flammeus localized in the skin of the eyelid.

replacement of normal bone with abnormal, structurally unsound fibro-osseous tissue, with concomitant obliteration of the hematopoietic bone marrow. The fibrous tissue is rich in fibroblast-like cells that express markers of early stages of osteogenic maturation
Fibrous dysplasia of the bones were lesions are localized in many bones throughout of the body. Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia is a cardinal feature of McCune-Albright syndrome.
Fibrous dysplasia of the bones were lesions are localized in only one bone.

Osteopoikilosis is a benign, asymptomatic sclerotic dysplasia of the bones. It affects both male and female and may be seen at any age. Radiographically sclerotic circular or ovoid lesions are usually symmetrically distributed in a periarticular location. Lesions can increase or decrease in size and number in serial radiographs or even disappear and do not have increased bone radiotracer uptake.

A lamellar pattern visible on radiographs and mainly localized at the metaphyses of the long tubular bones. Pathologic-anatomical studies revealed that these benign signs on x-rays are the result of a juvenile metaphyseal bone necrosis. Calcifications in the necrotic marrow lead to this lamellar or lattice-like appearance.
An abnormal accumulation of excess fluid in the lower extremity resulting in swelling of the feet and extending upward to the lower leg.
An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin of the arms.
Diminished length of a metatarsal bone, with resultant proximal displacement of the associated toe.
A developmental abnormality characterized by the absence (aplasia) of a metatarsal bone.

terms.en: Aplasia of the phalanges of the toes
terms.def_en: Absence of a digit or of one or more phalanges of a toe.

terms.en: Hypoplasia of the phalanges of the toes

terms.def_en: An abnormal distribution of eyebrow hair growth in the medial direction.
Positioning of a lacrimal punctum other than at the medial margins of the eyelid.
syn_en: Abnormal position of the lacrimal punctum

terms.def_en: Blepharochalasis is characterized by recurrent, non-painful, nonerythematous episodes of eyelid edema. It has been divided into hypertrophic and atrophic forms. In the hypertrophic form recurrent edema results in orbital fat herniation through a weakened orbital septum. Most patients who have blepharochalasis present in an atrophic condition with atrophy of redundant eyelid skin and superior nasal fat pads.
Loss of elasticity of the upper and lower eyelids causing the skin to sag and bulge.
A persistent midline depression of the skin over the fat pad of the chin.
Midline deficiency of the mandible and some or all overlying tissues.
An anomaly of the temporomandibular joint.
Asymmetry between the left and right sides of the maxilla.
syn_en: Asymmetry of right and left side of the maxilla

terms.def_en: Absence or underdevelopment of the premaxilla.
syn_en: Aplasia/hypoplasia of the primary palate bone

terms.def_en: Absence of the premaxilla, which is the embryonic structure that forms the anterior part of the maxilla.
lay_en: Absence of the primary palate bone
syn_en: Aplasia of the primary palate bone
Failure of development of the primary palate bone

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the premaxilla, the most anterior part of the maxilla that usually bears the central and lateral incisors and includes the anterior nasal spine and inferior aspect of the piriform rim. The premaxilla contains the bone and teeth of the primary palate.
lay_en: Abnormality of the primary palate bone
syn_en: Abnormality of the intermaxillary segment of the maxilla

terms.def_en: Prominent positioning of the premaxilla in relation to the rest of the maxilla, the facial skeleton, or mandible. Not necessarily caused by an increase in size (hypertrophy of) the premaxilla.
lay_en: Anterior position of the primary palate bone
Prominence of the primary palate bone

terms.def_en: Aplasia of a toe. That is, absence of all phalanges of a non-hallux digit of the foot and the associated soft tissues.
Increased width of the columella.

A chordoma is a tumor that arises from embryonic remnants of the notochord along the length of the neuraxis. Chordomas generally occur in the sacrum, intracranially at the clivus, or along the spinal axis.
Insertion of the posterior columella below the nasal base.
Decreased length of the eyelashes (subjective).
Abnormal thickening of the skin localized to the palm of the hand.
Deposition of calcium salts in a tissue or location in which calcification does not normally occur.
The presence of a cyst, fistula, or abscess in the sacrococcygeal region (gluteal crease) characteristically accompanied by hair and skin folds.
A sinus in the coccygeal region (the region of the intergluteal cleft). A pilonidal sinus often contains hair and skin debris.
A hair-containing cyst or sinus usually in the coccygeal region.

A developmental defect characterized by abnormal connection of one or more pulmonary veins to the superior or inferior vena cava, the right atrium, or the coronary sinus, resulting in a left-to-right shunt of oxygenated blood.
A form of anomalous pulmonary venous return in which not all pulmonary veins drain abnormally. Partial anomalous pulmonary venous return frequently involves one or both of the veins from one lung.
The presence of an additional membrane in the left or right cardiac atrium which results in the subdivision of the affected atrium (and thus in total three atria, whence the name).

A developmental defect of the aortic arch system in which the trachea and esophagus are completely encircled by connected segments of the aortic arch and its branches. This occurs if the normal process of regression and persistence of the bilateral embryonic aortic arches fails.
Marked widening of the trachea and major bronchi that may be predispose to chronic respiratory tract infection.
Marked widening of the major bronchi that may be predispose to chronic respiratory tract infection.
Marked widening of the trachea.
The presence of an abnormally large pelvis.
Over-sensitivity to certain frequency ranges of sound.
Skin dimples are cutaneous indentations that are the result of tethering of the skin to underlying structures (bone) causing an indentation.
A subtype of skin dimples occurring in the shoulder region.
Redness of the skin, caused by hyperemia of the capillaries in the lower layers of the skin.
lay_en: Redness of skin or mucous membrane

terms.def_en: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the uterus.
A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of a gonad.
The presence of a neoplasm of the urinary system.
A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the genital system.
The presence of a neoplasm of the testis.
Underdevelopment of the interstitial (Leydig) cells of the testis. These cells produce testosterone.
Hypertrophy or overdevelopment of the interstitial (Leydig) cells of the testis. These cells produce testosterone.
A digit with two nails, with at least some soft tissue between them.

Reduced ability affecting mainly visuospatial cognition which may be tested using pattern construction (for example by Differential Ability Scales, which test a person's strengths and weaknesses across a range of intellectual abilities).
A glioma affecting the cerebellum.
A glioma affecting the brainstem.

A hemangioblastoma is a benign vascular neoplasm that arises almost exclusively in the central nervous system. Hemangioblastomas consist of a tightly packed cluster of small blood vessels forming a mass of up to 1 or 2 cm in diameter.
Increased focal pigmentation of the vermilion of the lips.
A neoplasm of the pineal gland.
Lack of paramedian peaks and median notch of the upper lip vermilion.
syn_en: Failure of development of cupid's bow

terms.def_en: Reduced bulkiness of the crease or fold of skin running from the lateral margin of the nose, where nasal base meets the skin of the face, to a point just lateral to the corner of the mouth (cheilion or commissure).
Increased pigmentation, either focal or generalized, of the skin surrounding the vermilion of the lips.
lay_en: Darkening of skin around the mouth

terms.def_en: Inner aspect of the upper lip vermilion (normally apposing the teeth) visible in a frontal view, i.e., the presence of an everted upper lip.
Triangular appearance of the oral aperture with the apex in the midpoint of the upper vermilion and the lower vermilion forming the base.
Oral commissures positioned superior to the midline labial fissure.

terms.it: Vermiglio del labbro superiore a forma di U
terms.def_en: Gentle upward curve of the upper lip vermilion such that the center is placed well superior to the commissures.
Visible space between the dental arches in occlusion.
lay_en: Absence of overlap of upper and lower teeth
Open bite between upper and lower teeth

terms.def_en: Tongue extending beyond the alveolar ridges or teeth at rest.
Increased width of the uvula (subjective finding).
Increased length of the uvula.
Decreased width of the uvula.
Decreased length of the uvula.
More than two clockwise hair whorls.
Hair growth from a single point on the scalp in any location other than lateral to the midline and close to the vertex of the skull.

A congenital, hairless plaque consisting of overgrown epidermis, sebaceous glands, hair follicles, apocrine glands and connective tissue. They are a variant of epidermal naevi. Sebaceous naevi most often appear on the scalp, but they may also arise on the face, neck or forehead. At birth, a sevaceous nevus typically appears as a solitary, smooth, yellow-orange hairless patch. Sebaceous naevi become more pronounced around adolescence, often appearing bumpy, warty or scaly.
Epidermal naevi are due to an overgrowth of the epidermis and may be present at birth (50%) or develop during childhood.
A type of nevus sebaceous with a linear form, raised borders and yellowish color.

A generalized tonic seizure is a type of generalized motor seizure characterized by bilateral limb stiffening or elevation, often with neck stiffening without a subsequent clonic phase. The tonic activity can be a sustained abnormal posture, either in extension or flexion, sometimes accompanied by tremor of the extremities.

Atonic seizure is a type of motor seizure characterized by a sudden loss or diminution of muscle tone without apparent preceding myoclonic or tonic event lasting about 1 to 2 seconds, involving head, trunk, jaw, or limb musculature.

Focal emotional seizure with crying (dacrystic) is characterized by the presence of stereotyped crying, this may be accompanied by lacrimation, sad facial expression and sobbing. The subjective emotion of sadness may or may not be present.
Focal emotional seizure with laughing (gelastic) is characterized by bursts of laughter or giggling, usually without appropriate related emotion of happiness, and described as 'mirthless'.

A scintillating scotoma is a common visual aura that can precede a migraine, whereby a spot of flickering light near the center of the visual fields occurs. The spot prevents vision, and is thus termed scotoma. The scotoma can extend into one or more shimmering arcs of white or colored flashing lights.
An overlap of the bony plates of the skull in an infant, with or without early closure.
Any structural abnormality of the fifth cranial nerve.
syn_en: Abnormality of the fifth cranial nerve

terms.en: Abnormality of the eleventh cranial nerve
terms.def_en: Abnormality of the eleventh cranial nerve.

terms.en: Abnormality of the twelfth cranial nerve
terms.def_en: Abnormality of the twelfth cranial nerve.
Abnormality of the seventh cranial nerve sometimes also referred to as the facial nerve.
Intermittent clonic or tonic contraction of muscles supplied by facial nerve. Muscles are relaxed in between contractions.
lay_en: Spasms on one side of the face

terms.def_en: A reduced ability to discriminate between different temperatures.
A reduced sense of touch (tactile sensation). This is usually tested with a wisp of cotton or a fine camel's hair brush, by asking patients to say 'now' each time they feel the stimulus.
A loss or impairment of the sensation of the relative position of parts of the body and joint position.

Pain is an unpleasant sensation that can range from mild, localized discomfort to agony, whereby the physical part of pain results from nerve stimulation and is often accompanied by an emotional component. This term groups abnormalities in pain sensation presumed to result from abnormalities related to the specific nerve fibers that carry the pain impulses to the brain.
Spontaneous pain is a kind of neuropathic pain which occurs without an identifiable trigger.

Trophic changes is a term used to describe abnormalities in the area of pain that include primarily wasting away of the skin, tissues, or muscle, thinning of the bones, and changes in how the hair or nails grow, including thickening or thinning of hair or brittle nails.
A pattern of sensory loss with selective loss of touch sensation and proprioception without loss of pain and temperature, or vice-versa.

terms.it: Concentrazione anormale di rame in circolo
terms.def_en: Any deviation from the normal concentration of copper cation in the blood circulation.

terms.it: Diminuzione della concentrazione di ceruloplasmina in circolo
terms.def_en: The concentration of ceruloplasmin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
An increased concentration of non ceruloplasmin bound copper in the blood.
An increased concentration of copper in the urine.
An abnormality in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG) and being identified at multiple locations (foci).
Focal (localized) slow activity reflects focal dysfunction, not diffuse dysfunction (i.e., encephalopathy).
Multifocal slowing of cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).
Diffuse slowing of cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).

terms.en: EEG with persistent abnormal rhythmic activity

terms.it: EEG con complessi di onde di punta (<2,5 Hz)
terms.def_en: The presence of complexes of slow spikes and slow waves (<2.5 Hz) in electroencephalography (EEG).

terms.it: EEG con complessi di onde spike (2,5-3,5 Hz)
terms.def_en: The presence of complexes of spikes and waves (2.5-3.5 Hz) in electroencephalography (EEG).
The presence of complexes of spikes and waves (>3.5 Hz) in electroencephalography (EEG).

terms.it: EEG con complessi di onde di punta
terms.def_en: Complexes of spikes (<70 ms) and sharp waves (70-200 ms), which are sharp transient waves that have a strong association with epilepsy, in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).

The burst suppression pattern in electroencephalography refers to a characteristic periodic pattern of low voltage (<10 microvolts) suppressed background and a relatively shorter pattern of higher amplitude slow, sharp, and spiking complexes.
EEG abnormalities (epileptiform discharges) evoked by flashing lights or black and white striped patterns.

terms.en: EEG with periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges
terms.def_en: Periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges (PLEDs)are periodic, lateralized, and epileptiform. PLEDs show a relatively constant interval between discharges (0.5 to 3 seconds).

terms.en: EEG with generalized low amplitude activity
terms.def_en: An abnormal generalized reduction in amplitude of the cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).
syn_en: EEG with generalised low amplitude activity

terms.en: EEG with localized low amplitude activity
terms.def_en: An abnormal localized reduction in amplitude of the cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).
syn_en: EEG with localised low amplitude activity

terms.def_en: Periodically occurring generalized periodic complexes.
Periodically recurring abnormalities in the EEG.
Epileptiform discharges induced by hyperventilation (overbreathing) in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).
A kind of breech presentation in which the hips are flexed and the knees are extended.
A kind of breech presentation in which the hips are flexed and the knees are flexed.
A kind of breech presentation in which one or both hips are extended and one or both of the fetus' feet are pointing down and entering the birth canal.

terms.it: Ritardo nello sviluppo della motricità fine
terms.def_en: A type of motor delay characterized by a delay in acquiring the ability to control the fingers and hands.
A delay in the acquisition of the ability to understand the speech of others.

Severe intellectual disability (ID) is defined as a type of ID characterized by severely sub-average adaptive functioning and intellectual functioning, with an intelligence quotient (IQ) the range of 20-34.

A pervasive and characteristic pattern of arguing, defiance, and hostility toward others, particularly authority figures, that goes beyond the occasional oppositionality seen as a normal behavior in individuals at a certain age, e.g., during child and adolescent development.
An incomplete closure of the abdominal wall.

A type of ataxia characterized by the impairment of the ability to smoothly perform the elements of a voluntary movement in the appropriate order and speed. With dyssynergia, a voluntary movement appears broken down into its component parts.
A type of dyssynergia affecting eye movements and characterized by the inability to smoothly follow a visual target across the visual field.
A type of dyssynergy characterized by the lack of the ability to smoothly perform the elements of a voluntary movement in the appropriate order and speed.

Incoordination of movement caused by a deficit in the sensory nervous system. Sensory ataxia can be distinguished from cerebellar ataxia by asking the patient to close his or her eyes. Persons with cerebellar ataxia show only a minimal worsening of symptoms, whereas persons with sensory ataxia show a marked worsening of symptoms.
An inversion of the T-wave (which is normally positive).
Atrophy of the cervical segment of the spinal cord.
The presence of xanthomas (intra-and extra-cellular accumulations of cholesterol) extensor tendons (typically over knuckles, Achilles tendon, knee, and elbows).

A diagnostic reflex elicited by stimulation of the skin over the surface of the lateral malleolus of the foot. The Chaddock refelx is present if there is extension of one or more or all of the toes with or without fanning of them when the external inframalleolar skin is stimulated. The Chaddock sign, similar to the Babinski sign, is taken to be an indication of disease of the spinocortical (pyramidal) tract.
An abnormal level of a circulating protein in the blood.

A type of strabismus in which the fixating eye is always the same one, while the other eye is constantly deviated. Monocular strabismus is to be distinguished from alternating strabismus, in which either of the eyes 'squints' at different times.

The presence during the prenatal period of a cystic mass with multiple septa with multiple, asymmetric, thin-walled cysts near the posterior aspect of the neck. Fetal cystic hygroma can be defined as nuchal translucency with or without septations measuring greater than 3.0 mm. Increased NT refers to a measurement above the 95th centile, and the term is used irrespective of whether the collection of fluid is septated or not, and whether it is confined to the neck or envelopes the whole fetus. After 14 weeks, increased NT usually resolves, but in some cases it evolves into nuchal edema or cystic hygromas.
Nuchal translucency is the sonographic appearance of subcutaneous accumulation of liquid in the back of the fetal neck in the first trimester of pregnancy (11-14 gestational weeks of pregnancy).
An abnormality of the umbilical cord, which is the cord connecting the developing embryo or fetus to the placenta.
A congenital disorder of the pulmonary valve in which the orifice of the valve fails to develop.
A congenital disorder of the aortic valve in which the orifice of the valve fails to develop.
Shortening of the extremities affecting primarily the distal parts of the limbs (hands and feet) in relation to the other segments of the limbs.
A disease where there is cellular death (necrosis) of bone components due to interruption of the blood supply.
lay_en: Death of bone due to decreased blood supply

terms.def_en: A joint disorder caused by blood deprivation in the subchondral bone causing the subchondral bone to die in a process called avascular necrosis. The bone is then reabsorbed by the body, leaving the articular cartilage it supported prone to damage. The result is fragmentation (dissection) of both cartilage and bone, and the free movement of these osteochondral fragments within the joint space, causing pain and further damage.
Morbus Koehler is a Juvenile aseptic necrosis affecting the Os naviculare pedis.
Morbus Kienboeck is a Juvenile aseptic necrosis affecting the Os lunatum.
Morbus Osgood-Schlatter is a Juvenile aseptic necrosis affecting the Tuberositas tibiae.

A developmental growth retardation of the vertebral end plates that may lead to secondary destruction of the vertebral end plates and protrusion of the nucleus pulposus into the vertebral body (so called Schmorl's nodes as seen on x-rays).

Any deviation from the normal concentration of tyrosine in the blood circulation.
An abnormality of a cysteine metabolic process.
Any deviation from the normal concentration of homocysteine in the blood circulation.
Zonular cataracts are defined to be cataracts that affect specific regions of the lens.
A 'coral-like' pattern of opacity in the lens of the eye. That is, a cataract with an irregular, stellate form.
A form of cataract in which the lens substance has shrunk, leaving a collapsed, flattened capsule with little or no cortex or epithelium on the lens.
A type of cataract affecting the anterior pole of lens immediately adjacent to ('beneath') the lens capsule.
A cataract that affects the posterior part of the cortex of the lens.
A kind of nuclear cataract characterized by fiberglasslike or needlelike crystals projecting in different directions, through or close to the axial region of the lens.

terms.en: Abnormal circulating inorganic divalent cation concentration
terms.def_en: An abnormality of divalent inorganic cation homeostasis.
syn_en: Abnormality of divalent inorganic cation homeostasis

terms.def_en: Any deviation from the normal concentration of inorganic cation in the blood circulation.

terms.def_en: Any deviation from the normal concentration of monovalent inorganic cation in the blood circulation.
syn_en: Abnormal blood monovalent inorganic cation concentration
Abnormality of monovalent inorganic cation homeostasis

terms.it: Concentrazione anormale di sodio nel sangue
terms.def_en: Any deviation from the normal concentration of sodium in the blood circulation.
Any deviation from the normal concentration of nucleobase in the blood circulation.
An increased level of xanthine in the blood circulation.
An increased concentration of xanthine in the urine.

terms.en: Abnormality of the upper urinary tract
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the upper urinary tract.
lay_en: Abnormality of the upper urinary tract

terms.en: Abnormality of the lower urinary tract
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the lower urinary tract.
An abnormality of the nasal skeleton.
lay_en: Deformity of the bones of the nose
Distortion of the bones of the nose
Malformation of the bones of the nose

terms.it: Anomalia della morfologia del naso esterno
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the external nose.
An abnormality of the nasal bone, comprising the left nasal bone and the right nasal bone.
Absence or underdevelopment of the nasal bone.
Absence of the nasal bone.
lay_en: Failure of development of the nasal bone
Lack of development of the nasal bone

terms.def_en: A finding of a focus of increased echogenicity upon prenatal ultrasound examination of the fetus. The foci may be present in one or both ventricles. Echogenic intracardiac focus (EICF) is defined as a focus of echogenicity comparable to bone, in the region of the papillary muscle in either or both ventricles of the fetal heart.
Echogenic bowel is defined as fetal bowel with homogenous areas of echogenicity that are equal to or greater than that of surrounding bone.
An abnormality of the renal pelvis.

Mild pyelectasis is defined as a hypoechoic spherical or elliptical space within the renal pelvis that measures at least 5mm and not more than 10 mm. The measurement is taken on a transverse section through the fetal renal pelvis using the maximum anterior-to-posterior measurement.
The presence of dilatation of the renal pelvis.

terms.en: Abnormality of ductus venosus blood flow
terms.def_en: A first-trimester prenatal ultrasound finding of abnormal blood flow in the ductus venosus.

A structural abnormality of the fetal circulation system. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other HPO terms can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.
syn_en: Abnormality of the fetal cardiovascular system
Abnormality of the fetal circulation system
Abnormality of the foetal cardiovascular system
Abnormality of the foetal circulation system

terms.en: Abnormality of umbilical vein blood flow
terms.def_en: A first-trimester prenatal ultrasound finding of abnormal blood flow in the umbilical vein.
An abnormality of the fourth ventricle.
An abnormality of the third ventricle.

A kind of ventriculomegaly occurring in the fetal period and usually diagnosed by prenatal ultrasound. Cerebral ventriculomegaly is defined by atrial measurements 10 mm or more. Mild ventriculomegaly (MVM) is defined as measurements between 10 and 15 mm. Measurements are obtained from an axial plane at the level of the thalamic nuclei just below the standard image to measure the BPD (PMID:16100637).
A form of hydrocephalus in which the flow of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) within the cerebral ventricular system or in the outlets of the CSF to the arachnoid space is obstructed.
Underdevelopment of the right ventricle.
The presence of a dilated urinary bladder.
Fetal megacystis is an abnormally enlarged bladder identified at any gestational age.
A developmental defect resulting in an obstructing membrane in the posterior male urethra.
A bilateral form of agenesis of the kidney.

Congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM) - previously known as congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation (CCAM) - is a relatively rare developmental malformation of the lower respiratory tract. It is a hamartomatous, dysplastic developmental abnormality of the lung characterized by abnormal airway patterning during lung branching morphogenesis and is formed by abnormal branching of the immature bronchioles.
syn_en: Congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation of the lung
Congenital cystic disease of the lung

terms.en: Absence of stomach bubble on fetal sonography
terms.def_en: By the 14th week of gestation it is nearly always possible to visualized the fluid-filled fetal stomach bubble on prenatal sonography. This term refers to the absence of a normal fetal stomach bubble on fetal ultrasonography performed at around 16 to 20 weeks' gestation.
syn_en: Absence of stomach bubble on foetal sonography

terms.def_en: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a long-chain fatty acid in the blood circulation.
Any deviation from the normal concentration of phytanic acid in the blood circulation.

terms.def_en: Any deviation from the normal concentration of fatty acid anion in the blood circulation.
Any deviation from the normal concentration of carnitine in the blood circulation.
An abnormality of liposaccharide metabolism.
An abnormality of glycolipid metabolism.
An abnormality of an erythrocyte cell surface molecule.

terms.en: Absence of Lutheran antigen on erythrocytes
terms.def_en: Absence of the Lutheran antigen (a type I integral membrane glycoprotein) from the surface of red blood cells.
A kind of anemia characterized by inadequate production of erythrocytes.
An abnormality of myeloid leukocytes.
The absolute number of B cells in the blood, per microlitre is outside the limits of normal of the reference range for the appropriate sex and age-group.
The absolute number of B cells in the blood, per microlitre is below the lower limit of normal of the reference range for the appropriate sex and age-group.

An abnormal functioning of phagocytosis. Phagocytosis is an elegant but complex process for the ingestion and elimination of pathogens, but it is also important for the elimination of apoptotic cells and hence fundamental for tissue homeostasis. Phagocytosis can be divided into four main steps: (i) recognition of the target particle, (ii) signaling to activate the internalization machinery, (iii) phagosome formation, and (iv) phagolysosome maturation.
A functional abnormality of the immune system.
Any deviation from the normal concentration of lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood circulation.
syn_en: Abnormality of the level of lipoprotein cholesterol

terms.def_en: An abnormal increase in the level of lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.
An abnormal decrease in the level of lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.
An abnormality of the morphology or counts of the cells that make up the immune system.
An abnormality of the extrinsic pathway (also known as the tissue factor pathway) of the coagulation cascade.
An abnormality of the intrinsic pathway (also known as the contact activation pathway) of the coagulation cascade.

terms.en: Abnormality of the common coagulation pathway
terms.def_en: An abnormality of blood coagulation, common pathway.

terms.en: Abnormal morphology of the abdominal musculature
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the abdominal musculature.
Involuntary urine leakage synchronous with exertion, or actions such as sneezing, or coughing.
An abnormality of the cerebral subcortex.
Abnormality of the striatum, which is the largest nucleus of the basal ganglia, comprising the caudate, putamen and ventral striatum, including the nucleus accumbens.
Any deviation from the normal concentration of dicarboxylic acid in the blood circulation.
Any deviation from the normal concentration of monocarboxylic acid in the blood circulation.

terms.en: Chromosomal breakage induced by ionizing radiation
terms.def_en: Increased amount of chromosomal breaks in cultured blood lymphocytes or other cells induced by treatment with ionizing radiation.
syn_en: Chromosomal breakage induced by ionising radiation

terms.en: Increased susceptibility to spontaneous sister chromatid exchange
terms.def_en: An increase in the number of spontaneous sister chromatid exchanges observed in cell culture of lymphocytes or other cells.

An abnormal increase of bone mineral density, that is, of the amount of matter per cubic centimeter of bones which is often referred to as osteosclerosis. Osteosclerosis can be detected on radiological examination as an increased whiteness (density) of affected bones.
Abnormally increased formation of dense trabecular bone tissue. Despite the increased density of bone tissue, osteopetrotic bones tend to be more fracture-prone than normal.
A severe form of myopia with greater than -6.00 diopters.
An abnormality of the systemic arterial tree, which consists of the aorta and other systemic arteries.
syn_en: Abnormality of the systemic arterial tree

terms.def_en: A type of cirrhosis characterized by the presence of regenerative nodules of a variety of sizes.

A deviation from the normal concentration of a carbohydrate in the blood circulation.
Abnormality of glucose homeostasis.

An abnormality of chromosome condensation.
An abnormality of the metabolism of mucopolysaccharide.

An abnormality of the gastrointestinal tract.
Abnormal functionality of the cardiovascular system.
Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the vagina.
An abnormality of the fallopian tube.
An abnormality of blood circulation.
The presence of hemorrhage within the body.
