Abnormality of transition element cation homeostasis

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the homeostasis (concentration) of iron cation.
An abnormality of the regulation of body fluids.
An impairment of a fructose metabolic process.
Pathologic deposits of specific fibrillar protein aggregates with distinct microscopic properties, particularly affinity for the dye Congo red with typical birefringence.
An abnormality of the cortex of the kidney.
An altered ability of the kidneys to void urine and/or specific substances.
A decreased rate of urine production.
An abnormality of renal absorption.
An abnormality of the helix. The helix is the outer rim of the ear that extends from the insertion of the ear on the scalp (root) to the termination of the cartilage at the earlobe.
An abnormality of the intrahepatic bile duct.
syn_en: Abnormality of the intrahepatic bile duct

terms.def_en: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the cervical vertebral column.

terms.it: Concentrazione anormale di potassio nel sangue

An abnormal concentration of corticotropin in the blood.
The presence of an altered number of of permanent teeth.

syn_en: Dentinogenesis imperfecta of adult and baby teeth
Dentinogenesis imperfecta of both sets of teeth

terms.def_en: Talon cusp is an accessory cusp located near the cingulum (the portion of the lingual or palatal aspect of the tooth that forms a convex protuberance at the cervical third of the anatomic crown).
lay_en: Extra cusp on inside of front tooth

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the incisor characterized by invagination of the enamel, giving a radiographic appearance that suggests a tooth within a tooth.
Fusion of two adjacent teeth.
The union of two separately developing tooth germs typically leading to one less tooth than normal in the affected dental arch.
The development of two teeth from a single tooth bud, leading to a larger fused tooth.
Mulberry molars are irregular teeth generally affecting the first molars and are characterized by a grossly deformed crown imitating, as the name implies, the surface of a mulberry.
Increased size and molar morphology of premolar tooth.
Maxillary teeth cover the mandibular teeth when biting to an increased degree. The feature is defined as a vertical overlap of the maxillary incisors over the mandibular incisors that exceeds 2 mm.
syn_en: Increased overlap of upper and lower incisors

terms.def_en: An abnormal anteroposterior extension of the maxillary teeth beyond the plane of the mandibular teeth upon jaw closure.
lay_en: Protrusion of upper teeth in front of lower teeth

terms.def_en: A loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers of the peripheral nervous system.

A sudden flexion, extension, or mixed extension-flexion of predominantly proximal and truncal muscles that is usually more sustained than a myoclonic movement but not as sustained as a tonic seizure. Limited forms may occur: Grimacing, head nodding, or subtle eye movements. Epileptic spasms frequently occur in clusters. Infantile spasms are the best known form, but spasms can occur at all ages

A type of apraxia that is characterized by difficulty or inability to execute speech movements because of problems with coordination and motor problems, leading to incorrect articulation. An increase of errors with increasing word and phrase length may occur.
Unilateral paresis (weakness) with spasticity of the affected muscles and increased tendon reflexes.
An abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the intestine.
An abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the ileum.

terms.en: Abnormal left ventricular outflow tract morphology
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the outflow tract of the left ventricle.
syn_en: Abnormality of the left ventricular outflow tract

terms.def_en: An abnormality in the amount of volume occupied by intravascular blood.
An increase in the amount of intravascular fluid, particularly in the volume of the circulating blood.
An decrease in the amount of intravascular fluid, particularly in the volume of the circulating blood.
Recurrent episodes of ulceration of the oral mucosa, typically presenting as painful, sharply circumscribed fibrin-covered mucosal defects with a hyperemic border.
A recurrent form of sinusitis.
A chronic form of sinusitis.

Inflammation of the tonsils that has occurred repeatedly. The definition of recurrent may vary somewhat, but the criteria used recently as a measure of severity were five or more episodes of true tonsillitis per year, symptoms recurring for at least a year, and episodes that are disabling and that prevent normal functioning. In some cases recurrent tonsillitis may be related to immunosusceptibility. Evidence exists for a genetic predisposition for recurrent tonsillitis.
An abnormality of the concentration or function of circulating immune proteins.
syn_en: Abnormality of immune serum protein physiology

terms.def_en: Abnormality of the cytokine levels in the blood, i.e., an abnormality of any of the non-antibody proteins made by inflammatory leukocytes and some non-leukocytic cells that affect the behavior of other cells.

An abnormality in the production or cellular release of a cytokine (i.e., any of the non-antibody proteins made by inflammatory leukocytes and some non-leukocytic cells that affect the behavior of other cells).
An impairment in the production by leukocytes of NFKB1-dependent cytokines such as tumor necrosis factor-alpha and interferon-alpha.
An abnormality in the production or cellular release of a chemokine (a class of cytokines).
The concentration of an interferon is outside the limits of normal.
The concentration of an interleukin (a class of cytokines) is outside the limits of normal.

terms.en: Abnormality of tumor necrosis factor secretion
terms.def_en: An abnormality in the production or cellular release of tumor necrosis factor.
syn_en: Abnormality of tumour necrosis factor secretion

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the nasal dorsum, also known as the nasal ridge.
lay_en: Malformation of the dorsum of nose
syn_en: Abnormality of the dorsum of nose

terms.def_en: Nasal ridge curving posteriorly to an imaginary line that connects the nasal root and tip.
Any morphological abnormality of the skin.
Any abnormality of the physiological function of the skin.
The presence of inflammation of the skin. That is, an abnormality of the skin resulting from the local accumulation of fluid, plasma proteins, and leukocytes.
syn_en: Abnormal tendency to infections of the skin

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the morphology of the epidermis.
An abnormality of the melanosomes, i.e., of the cellular organelles in which melanin pigments are synthesized and stored within melanocytes (the cells that produce pigment in the dermis).
A significant descent of the kidney as the patient moves from the supine to the erect position.
A type of eczema that occurs in the lips and perioral area.

A condition characterized by necrosis of the mucosal and submucosal layers of the esophagus not related to ingestion of caustic or other injurious agents. Endoscopically, there is a dark lesion ('black esophagus') distributed in a circumferential manner in the distal one-third of the esophagus with or without exudates. There is involvement of the distal esophagus ending sharply at the gastroesophageal junction.
A bilateral form of fetal pyelectasis.
Any abnormality of the morphology of the major calices or minor calices of the kidney.
The presence of a rash (change of color and texture) of the perianal skin.

A furuncle (boil) is a skin infection involving an entire hair follicle and nearby skin tissue. Chronic furunculosis refers to recurrent episodes of furuncles, often caused by recurrent staphylococcus infection.
An abnormally increased sensitivity to the effects of ionizing radiation.
Mild fever that does not exceed 38.5 degrees centigrade.
Absence or developmental hypoplasia of the sweat glands.
Absence of the sweat glands.
Pale reddish slightly elevated papules and plaques of 0.5-3 cm in diameter and not accompanied by pruritus.

An abnormality of the skin adnexa (skin appendages), which are specialized skin structures located within the dermis and focally within the subcutaneous fatty tissue, comprising three histologically distinct structures: (1) the pilosebaceous unit (hair follicle and sebaceous glands); (2) the eccrine sweat glands; and (3) the apocrine glands.
Gastric duplication is a usually cystic malformation of gastrointestinal tract, usually attached to the greater curvature of the stomach and has no communication with the stomach.
A spherical hollow structure with a smooth muscle coat, lined by a mucous membrane, and attached to any part of the gastrointestinal tract, from the base of the tongue to the anus.
A type of cataract (opacification of the lens) that forms during the course of aging.
lay_en: Clouding of the lens of the eye with age

terms.def_en: A type of age-related cataract that primarily affects the nucleus of the lens.
A type of age-related cataract that primarily affects the cortex of the lens.
A type of age-related cataract consisting of granular opacities occurring mainly in the central posterior cortex just under the posterior capsule.
A seizure that occurs in the context of a brain insult (systemic, toxic, or metabolic) and may not recur when the underlying cause has been removed or the acute phase has elapsed.
A dialeptic seizure is a type of seizure characterized predominantly by reduced responsiveness or awareness and with subsequent at least partial amnesia of the event.
syn_en: Behavioral arrest seizure with impairment of awareness irrespective of onset
Behavioural arrest seizure with impairment of awareness irrespective of onset
Unknown onset behavioral arrest seizure with impairment of awareness
Unknown onset behavioural arrest seizure with impairment of awareness

terms.def_en: A typical absence seizure is a type of generalized non-motor (absence) seizure characterized by its sudden onset, interruption of ongoing activities, a blank stare, possibly a brief upward deviation of the eyes. Usually the patient will be unresponsive when spoken to. Duration is a few seconds to half a minute with very rapid recovery. Although not always available, an EEG would usually show 3 Hz generalized epileptiform discharges during the event.
An absence with eyelid myoclonia seizure is a type of generalized non-motor (absence) seizure characterized by forced upward jerking of the eyelids during an absence seizure.

Myoclonic absence seizure is a type of generalized non-motor (absence) seizure characterized by an interruption of ongoing activities, a blank stare and rhythmic three-per-second myoclonic movements, causing ratcheting abduction of the upper limbs leading to progressive arm elevation, and associated with 3 Hz generalized spike-wave discharges on the electroencephalogram. Duration is typically 10-60 s. Whilst impairment of consciousness may not be obvious the ILAE classified this seizure as a generalized non-motor seizure in 2017.
Atypical absence status epilepticus is a type of generalized non-convulsive status epilepticus without coma that is semiologically a prolonged atypical absence seizure.
Typical absence seizures starting before the age of 4 years.
A type of focal-onset seizure characterized by a motor sign as its initial semiological manifestation.
An autonomic seizure is a type of focal non-motor seizure characterized by alteration of autonomic nervous system function as the initial semiological feature.
A focal sensory seizure is a type seizure beginning with a subjective sensation.

terms.en: Focal sensory seizure with auditory features
terms.def_en: A seizure characterized by elementary auditory phenomena including buzzing, ringing, drumming or single tones as its first clinical manifestation.

terms.en: Focal autonomic seizure with epigastric sensation/nausea/vomiting/other gastrointestinal phenomena
terms.def_en: A type of focal autonomic seizure characterized by symptoms or signs pertaining to the gastrointestinal system as the initial semiological feature.

terms.en: Focal sensory seizure with gustatory features
terms.def_en: A seizure characterized by taste phenomena including acidic, bitter, salty, sweet, or metallic tastes as its first clinical manifestation.

terms.en: Focal sensory seizure with olfactory features
terms.def_en: Seizures characterized by olfactory phenomena as its first clinical manifestation.

terms.en: Focal sensory seizure with somatosensory features
terms.def_en: A seizure characterized by sensory phenomena including tingling, numbness, electric-shock like sensation, pain, sense of movement, or desire to move as its first clinical manifestation.

terms.en: Focal sensory seizure with visual features
terms.def_en: A seizure characterized by elementary visual hallucinations such as flashing or flickering lights/colors, or other shapes, simple patterns, scotomata, or amaurosis as its first clinical manifestation.

A type of focal motor seizure characterized by sudden, brief (<100 ms) involuntary single or multiple contraction(s) of muscles(s) or muscle groups of variable topography (axial, proximal limb, distal). Myoclonus is less regularly repetitive and less sustained than is clonus.
A type of focal motor seizure characterized by sustained increase in muscle contraction, lasting a few seconds to minutes.
Focal seizure with eyelid myoclonia, not eyelid myoclonias in the context of absence seizures.

Generalized clonic seizure is a type of generalized motor seizure characterized by sustained bilateral jerking, either symmetric or asymmetric, that is regularly repetitive and involves the same muscle groups.
A generalized myoclonic-atonic seizure is a type of generalized motor seizure characterized by a myoclonic jerk followed by an atonic motor component.

A short generalized seizure, of a duration of <15 min, not recurring within 24 h, occurring during a febrile episode not caused by an acute disease of the nervous system intracranial infection or severe metabolic disturbance.

A febrile seizure that has any of the following features: focal semiology (or associated with post-ictal neurologic abnormalities beyond drowsiness, such as a Todd's paresis), prolonged seizure beyond 15 minutes, or recurring (occurring more than once) in a 24 hour period.

terms.it: Crisi di arresto del comportamento focale
terms.def_en: A type of focal non-motor seizure characterized by an arrest or pause of activities, freezing, or immobilization as the predominant semiological feature throughout the seizure.

A focal seizure characterized at onset by predominantly proximal limb or axial muscles producing irregular sequential ballistic movements, such as pedaling, pelvic thrusting, thrashing, rocking movements.
A type of focal motor seizure characterized by sustained, forced conjugate ocular, cephalic, and/or truncal rotation or lateral deviation from the midline as the initial semiological manifestation.
An EEG with constitutional variants contains waves that are rare or unusual but not generally pathologic.
EEG background activity at 4-5/second.
EEG dominated by diffuse alpha-waves (8-13Hz).
EEG dominated by diffuse beta-waves (>13 Hz).
EEG dominated by diffuse beta waves (>13 Hz) with occipitally localized alpha waves (8-13 Hz).
EEG with an amplitude less than 30 microvolts without observable occipital alpha rhythm (8-13 Hz).

Epileptiform activity refers to distinctive EEG waves or complexes distinguished from background activity found in in a proportion of human subjects with epilepsy, but which can also be found in subjects without seizures. Interictal epileptiform activity refers to such activity that occurs in the absence of a clinical or subclinical seizure.

terms.en: EEG with hyperventilation-induced focal epileptiform discharges
terms.def_en: Focal epileptiform discharges induced by hyperventilation (overbreathing) in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).

terms.en: EEG with hyperventilation-induced generalized epileptiform discharges
terms.def_en: Generalized epileptiform discharges induced by hyperventilation (overbreathing) in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).
syn_en: EEG with hyperventilation-induced generalised epileptiform discharges

terms.def_en: EEG discharges recorded in particular areas of a localized (focal) abnormality in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).

terms.en: Focal epileptiform discharges with limited propagation to contralateral hemisphere
terms.def_en: Focal epileptiform discharges with spreading to contralateral hemisphere but without secondary generalization.

terms.en: Focal EEG discharges with propagation to ipsilateral hemisphere
terms.def_en: Focal epileptiform discharges with spreading to the hemisphere on the same side of the brain.

terms.en: Focal EEG discharges with secondary generalization
terms.it: Scariche EEG focali con generalizzazione secondaria
terms.def_en: Focal EEG discharges that secondarily spread to both hemispheres and can then be recorded over the entire scalp.
syn_en: Focal EEG discharges with secondary generalisation

terms.def_en: Epileptiform discharges being identified at multiple locations in both hemispheres.

terms.en: Uni- and bilateral multifocal epileptiform discharges
terms.def_en: Epileptiform discharges identified at multiple locations temporarily in both hemispheres and temporarily in one hemisphere.
Epileptiform discharges being identified at multiple locations in one hemisphere.
Focal epileptiform discharges of different shapes and frequencies.
EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration less than 80 msec.

terms.en: EEG with series of focal spikes
terms.def_en: Focal spikes occurring for several seconds.

terms.en: EEG with focal sharp slow waves
terms.it: EEG con onde lente acute focali
terms.def_en: EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.
EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.

terms.it: EEG con onde di picco focali
terms.def_en: EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration less than 80 msec followed by a slow wave.
EEG discharges recorded on the entire scalp typically seen in persons with epilepsy.

terms.en: EEG with generalized sharp slow waves
terms.it: EEG con onde lente acute generalizzate
terms.def_en: EEG with generalized sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.
syn_en: EEG with generalised sharp slow waves

terms.en: EEG with generalized polymorphic epileptiform discharges
terms.def_en: Generalized epileptiform discharges of different shapes and frequencies.
syn_en: EEG with generalised polymorphic epileptiform discharges

terms.def_en: EEG with abnormal amplitude.
EEG frequency is abnormally increased.
EEG with abnormally slow frequencies.
EEG showing diffuse slowing without interruption.
Non-continuous diffuse slowing of electroencephalographic patterns.

terms.en: EEG with generalized slow activity grade 1
terms.it: EEG con attività lenta generalizzata di grado 1
terms.def_en: Slowing at frequencies between 7.5 and 8.5 Hz.
syn_en: EEG with generalised slow activity grade 1

terms.en: EEG with generalized slow activity grade 2
terms.def_en: Generalized slowing of EEG activity at frequencies between 4-7 Hz.
syn_en: EEG with generalised slow activity grade 2

terms.en: EEG with generalized slow activity grade 3
terms.def_en: Generalized slowing of EEG activity at frequencies between 0.5-3 Hz.
syn_en: EEG with generalised slow activity grade 3

terms.en: EEG with generalized slow activity grade 4
terms.def_en: EEG without electrical activity.
syn_en: EEG with generalised slow activity grade 4

terms.def_en: Slowing in occipital areas of the scalp EEG.

terms.en: EEG with photoparoxysmal response grade I
terms.def_en: Occurrence of epileptiform discharges in occipital regions during photic stimulation.

terms.en: EEG with photoparoxysmal response grade II
terms.def_en: Occurrence of epileptiform discharges in occipital and central regions during photic stimulation.

terms.en: EEG with photoparoxysmal response grade III
terms.def_en: Occurrence of epileptiform discharges in occipital, central, temporal and parietal regions during photic stimulation.

terms.en: EEG with photoparoxysmal response grade IV
terms.def_en: Occurrence of generalized epileptiform discharges during photic stimulation.
Hypsarrhythmia occurring in one hemisphere.
An abnormal shape of occiput.
lay_en: Abnormal shape of the back of the head
Abnormal shape of the back of the skull

terms.en: Abnormal shape of the frontal region
terms.def_en: An abnormal shape of the frontal part of the head.
syn_en: Abnormal morphology of the frontal region

terms.def_en: Facial height (length) is more than two standard deviations below the mean (objective); or an apparent decrease in the height (length) of the face (subjective).
Forward prominence of the entire forehead, due to protrusion of the frontal bone.
Vertical soft tissue creases in the midline of the forehead, often extending from the hairline to the brow, and seen with facial expression or when the face is at rest.
Posterior positioning of the glabella, i.e., of the midline forehead between the supraorbital ridges.
Linear vertical groove in the midline of the forehead, extending from hairline to glabella.
Absent eyelids.
Redundant eyelid skin pressing the eyelashes against the cornea and/or conjunctiva.
Absence or underdevelopment of the eyelid.

terms.it: Elevata concentrazione di proteina C-reattiva circolante
terms.def_en: The concentration of C-reactive protein in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
syn_en: Elevated C-reactive protein level in blood
Increased C-reactive protein level in blood

terms.def_en: An eyebrow that extends straight across the brow, without curve.
Regional increase in the width (height) of the eyebrow.
An eyebrow that extends laterally beyond the orbital rim rather than turning gently downward at that location.
Eyelashes that draw the attention of the viewer due to increased density and/or length and/or curl without meeting the criteria of trichomegaly.
Elevated ridge(s) of skin starting well below the medial aspect of the lower lid that curves gradually upward toward and/or across the nasal bridge.
Antihelix protrusion directed more anteriorly than laterally, forming a shelf overlying the posterior concha.
No discernible ridge between concha and triangular fossa and helix.
Supernumerary ridge or crus of the ear arising from the antihelix.
Antihelical ridge that forms an acute angle between the antitragus and its bifurcation (stem) instead of a gently curving arc.
Increased width of the inferred cross-section of the inferior crus.
Increased protrusion of the inferior crus relative to the prominence of the antihelix stem.
Decreased protrusion of the inferior crus relative to the prominence of the antihelix stem.
Increased protrusion of the antihelical ridge, proximal to its bifurcation, relative to the prominence of the helix.
Posterior curving of the antihelix from its origin at the antitragus, traveling initially almost perpendicular to the descending helix and obscuring some of the concha.
Decreased protrusion of the antihelical ridge, proximal to its bifurcation, relative to the prominence of a normal helix.

terms.en: Abnormality of inferior crus of antihelix
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the inferior crus of the antihelix is the lower cartilaginous ridge arising at the bifurcation of the antihelix that ends beneath the fold of the ascending helix, and separates the concha from the triangular fossa.
syn_en: Abnormality of anterior crus of antihelix

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the stem of the antihelix, which is the part below the bifurcation of the antihelix into the inferior and superior crura.

terms.en: Abnormality of superior crus of antihelix
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the superior crus of the antihelix is the upper cartilaginous ridge arising at the bifurcation of the antihelix that ends beneath the fold of the ascending helix, and separates the concha from the triangular fossa.
syn_en: Abnormality of posterior crus of antihelix

terms.def_en: Decreased protrusion of the superior crus relative to the prominence of a normal antihelix stem.
Increased protrusion of the superior crus relative to the prominence of a normal antihelix stem.
Positioning of the antitragus at an angle perpendicular to the plane of the ear (oriented away from the plane of the ear).
Absence of the anterosuperior prominence of the area between the bottom of the incisura and the inner margin of the antihelix.
Double rather than single peak of the antitragus.
Reduction in the anterosuperior prominence of the area between the bottom of the incisura and the inner margin of the antihelix.
Invagination of the superior part of the auricle under a fold of temporal skin.
A type of cryptotia associated with reduction in size of the antihelix and superior crus.
A type of cryptotia associated with reduction in size of the antihelix and inferior crus that are affected.
Continuum between the tragus and ascending helix, without any evidence of a posterior extension (crus) towards the concha.

terms.en: Crus of helix connected to antihelix
terms.def_en: Extension of the ridge of the crus helix across the ear and connection of the crus to the antihelix.
Curving course of the crus of the helix, approaching or joining the antitragus.

terms.en: Tragal bridge of crus of helix
terms.def_en: The anterior origin of the crus encompasses the superior margin of the tragus, the crus overrides the upper portion of the conchal cavum and ends at the antihelix.

terms.en: Expanded terminal portion of crus of helix
terms.def_en: Widening, rather than tapering, of the crus at its posterior border near the antihelix.
Small defect of the helical fold that lies at the junction of the superior and descending portions of the helix.
Small expansion of the helical fold at the junction of the superior and descending portions of the helix.
Linear, circumferential indentation in the convexity of the outer surface of the helix.
Positioning of the anterior surface of the ear lobe in a more coronal plane than the remainder of the ear.
Interruption between the ascending helix and the crus helix, allowing the ascending helix to be attached directly to the mastoid.
Discontinuity in the convexity of the inferior margin of the lobe.
Presence of all the normal ear components and the median longitudinal length more than two standard deviations below the mean.
Presence of some auricular structures, but none of these structures conform to recognized ear components.
Lack of convexity or prominence of the contour of the ridge between the bottom of the incisura and the confluence of the ascending helix and crus helix.
Increased height of the tragal ridge with a shallow indentation at the apex, giving the appearance of a double peak.
A complete or partial duplication of the tragus; expected to lie anterior to the normal tragus.
Increase posterolateral protrusion of the tragus.
Decreased posterolateral protrusion of the tragus.
Abnormally increased variability in the size of erythrocytes.
lay_en: Unequal size of red blood cells

terms.def_en: Increased susceptibility to mycobacterial infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of mycobacterial infection.
Increased susceptibility to mycobacterial avium complex infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of mycobacterial infection.

terms.en: Abnormality of the urinary system physiology

terms.def_en: A type of pulmonary sequestration that occurs within the visceral pleura of normal lung tissue, usually without communication with the tracheobronchial tree.
An abnormal amount of hydrogencarbonate in the urine.

terms.it: Anomalia della concentrazione di calcio nelle urine
terms.def_en: An abnormality of calcium concentration in the urine.
An abnormal amount of urinary catecholamine concentration.
An abnormality of the hindbrain, also known as the rhombencephalon.
An abnormality of the metencephalon. The metencephalon is the part of the hindbrain that consists of the pons and the cerebellum.
A type of aganglionic megacolon in which the aganglionic segment does not extend beyond the upper sigmoid.
A type of aganglionic megacolon in which the aganglionic segment extends proximal to the sigmoid.
A type of aganglionic megacolon in which the aganglionic segment comprises the entire colon.

terms.en: EEG with occipital sharp slow waves
terms.def_en: EEG with sharp slow waves in the occipital region. Sharp slow waves are focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.

terms.en: EEG with parietal sharp slow waves
terms.it: EEG con onde lente acute parietali
terms.def_en: EEG with sharp slow waves in the parietal region. Sharp slow waves are focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.

terms.en: EEG with temporal sharp slow waves
terms.it: EEG con onde lente acute temporali
terms.def_en: EEG with sharp slow waves in the temporal region. Sharp slow waves are focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.

terms.en: EEG with frontal sharp slow waves
terms.it: EEG con onde lente frontali acute
terms.def_en: EEG with sharp slow waves in the frontal region. Sharp slow waves are focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.

terms.en: EEG with central sharp slow waves
terms.it: EEG con onde lente acute centrali
terms.def_en: EEG with sharp slow waves in the central region. Sharp slow waves are focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.
EEG with sharp waves in the occipital region, i.e., sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.
EEG with sharp waves in the central region, i.e., sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.
EEG with sharp waves in the frontal region, i.e., sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.
EEG with sharp waves in the parietal region, i.e., sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.
EEG with sharp waves in the temporal region, i.e., sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.
A morphological abnormality of a digit, i.e., of a finger or toe.
A soft tissue prominence of the ventral aspects of the fingertips or toe tips.
The absence of a phalangeal segment of a finger.
Increased width of the distal segment of a finger.
The total absence of the foot, with no bony elements distal to the tibia or fibula.
For children from birth to 16 years of age the length of the palm is more than the 97th centile; or, the length of the palm appears relatively long compared to the finger length or the limb length.
The contour of the foot in lateral profile has a convex shape.
Increased thumb width without increased dorso-ventral dimension.
The absence of a phalangeal segment of a toe or hallux.
Divergence of digits along the anteroposterior axis (in the plane of the sole).
Toes that are disproportionately narrow (reduced girth) for the hand/foot size or build of the individual.
The gradual reduction in girth of the toe from proximal to distal.
A crease that connects the proximal and distal transverse palmar creases.
Extension of the proximal transverse crease (five finger crease) to the ulnar edge of the palm.
A nail plate that has a longitudinal separation with partially separated nails, each with a separate lateral radius of curvature.
Decreased width of nail.
An abnormality of size or shape of the long bones.
Synostosis affecting only one of the coronal sutures.
Synostosis affecting only the left coronal suture.
Unicoronal synostosis affecting only the right coronal suture.
Synostosis affecting the right and the left coronal suture.
Premature synostosis of both lambdoid sutures.
Premature synostosis of only one lambdoid suture.
Premature synostosis of only the left lambdoid suture.
Premature synostosis of only the right lambdoid suture.
Incomplete fusion of the chin, resulting from a developmental defect and manifesting as a midline cleft or fissure of the chin.
Craniosynostosis involving at least 2 cranial sutures, where the exact pattern of sutures fused has not been precisely specified.
Craniosynostosis of all calvarial sutures.
Asymmetry of the anterior part of the skull.
Asymmetry of the posterior part of the skull.
An abnormality of the fontanelle.
Any anomaly of a cranial suture, that is one of the six membrane-covered openings in the incompletely ossified skull of the fetus or newborn infant.
Premature fusion of the metopic suture.
Unilateral atrophy of facial tissues, including muscles, bones and skin.
syn_en: Atrophy of one side of the face

terms.def_en: Unilateral underdevelopment of the facial tissues, including muscles and bones.
lay_en: Decreased size of half of the face
Decreased size of one side of the face
syn_en: Decrease in size of half of face
Decrease in size of one side of the face
Shrinking of one side of the face

terms.def_en: Asymmetry observed in the face of a neonate or infant whose face appears symmetric at rest and asymmetric during crying as the mouth is pulled downward on one side while not moving on the other side.
Excessive amount of hair growth on forehead.
Bilateral temporal scarlike defects, which are said to resemble forceps marks.
syn_en: Congenital ectodermal dysplasia of the face

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the outline, configuration, or contour of the mouth.
An abnormality of the vermilion border, the sharp demarcation between the lip (red colored) and the adjacent normal skin.
lay_en: Abnormality of the red part of the upper lip

terms.en: Incomplete cleft of the upper lip
terms.def_en: Cleft of the upper lip that does not go all the way from the bottom of the upper lip until the nasal cavity.
lay_en: Incomplete cleft of the upper lip
Notched cleft of the upper lip
Partial cleft of the upper lip

terms.def_en: Increased width of the upper lip.
lay_en: Increased vertical length of upper lip

terms.def_en: A mild delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child.
A moderate delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child.
A severe delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child.
A moderate delay in the acquisition of the ability to use language to communicate needs, wishes, or thoughts.
A mild delay in the acquisition of the ability to use language to communicate needs, wishes, or thoughts.
An abnormality involving the movement of the eye outwards.
Any structural abnormality of the abducens nerve.
syn_en: Abnormality of the sixth cranial nerve

terms.def_en: A mild delay in the acquisition of the ability to understand the speech of others.
A moderate delay in the acquisition of the ability to understand the speech of others.
A severe delay in the acquisition of the ability to understand the speech of others.
Formation of excess fibrous connective tissue in the tunica intima (innermost layer) of arteries.
An abnormality of the skin that is not localized to any one particular region.
A lesion of the skin that is located in a specific region rather than being generalized.
An abnormality of the skin that is restricted to a particular body region.
Reduced pigmentation of hair diffusely.
Hair that lacks the luster (shine or gleam) of normal hair.
An abnormality of the distribution of hair growth that is acquired during the course of life.
A congenital abnormality of the distribution of hair growth.
An abnormal amount of hair.
Hair whose growth rate deviates from the norm.
lay_en: Abnormality of pace of hair growth
Abnormality of speed of hair growth

terms.def_en: Hypopigmented hair that appears white.
Reduced pigmentation of hair in patches.
Yellowish discoloration of the nails.
Thickening of the epidermal layer of the skin.
Congenital deep dermal melanosis in the sacral area.
Increased susceptibility to cutaneous fungal infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of cutaneous fungal infections.
Increased susceptibility to viral skin infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of viral skin infections.
Absence of the inner ear due to a developmental defect.

Incomplete formation of the cochlear partition. The scala vestibuli and scala tympani separated by the cochlear partition, except in the apical turn where the two scalae are in continuity via the helicotrema.

terms.en: Incomplete partition of the cochlea type I
terms.def_en: Incomplete partition I is also known as cystic cochleovestibular malformation, where the cochlea has no bony modiolus, resulting in an empty cystic cochlea. This is accompanied by a dilated cystic vestibule with developmental arrest at the fifth week of gestation.
Absence of the cochlea, a spiral shaped cavity in the inner ear, owing to a developmental defect.

terms.en: Abnormal morphology of the vestibule of the inner ear
terms.def_en: A morphological abnormality of the vestibule, the central part of the osseous labyrinth that is situated medial to the tympanic cavity, behind the cochlea, and in front of the semicircular canals.
syn_en: Morphological abnormality of the vestibule of the inner ear

terms.def_en: Complete absence of the vestibule of the inner ear.

terms.en: Hypoplasia of the vestibule of the inner ear
terms.def_en: Underdevelopment of the vestibule of the inner ear.

terms.en: Dilated vestibule of the inner ear
terms.def_en: Dilatation of the vestibule of the inner ear.
An abnormality of the morphology of the semicircular canal.
syn_en: Morphological abnormality of the semicircular canal

terms.def_en: Absence of the semicircular canal.
Underdevelopment of the semicircular canal.
Increased size of the semicircular canal.

terms.en: Abnormality of the internal auditory canal
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the Internal acoustic meatus, i.e., of the canal in the petrous part of the temporal bone through which the cranial nerve VII and cranial nerve VIII traverse.
syn_en: Abnormality of the internal acoustic meatus

terms.def_en: Aplasia of the internal auditory canal.
Reduction in diameter of the internal auditory canal.
Increased size of the vestibular aqueduct.
Increased size of the cochlear duct, i.e., of a duct that communicates between the perilymphatic space and the subarachnoid space, and transmits a vein from the cochlea to join the internal jugular.

terms.en: Functional abnormality of the inner ear
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the function of the inner ear.
lay_en: Functional abnormality of the inner ear

terms.def_en: A structural anomaly of the internal part of the ear.
syn_en: Morphological abnormality of the inner ear
Morphological abnormality of the nerves of the inner ear

terms.def_en: Absence of the vestibular nerve
syn_en: Aplasia of the eighth cranial nerve

terms.def_en: Underdevelopment of the vestibular nerve.
syn_en: Hypoplasia of the eighth cranial nerve

terms.def_en: Absence or underdevelopment of the cochlea, a spiral shaped cavity in the inner ear, owing to a developmental defect.

Any anomaly of the cohclear nerve, which is the part of the vestibulocochlear nerve that is responsible for transmitting auditory signals from the inner ear to the cochlear nuclei within the brainstem and ultimately to the primary auditory cortex within the temporal lobe.

terms.en: Abnormal spinal cord dorsal column morphology
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the dorsal columns, i.e., of the dorsal portion of the gray substance of the spinal cord. The dorsal column consists of the fasciculus gracilis and fasciculus cuneatus and itself is part of the dorsal funiculus.
syn_en: Abnormality of the dorsal column of the spinal cord

terms.def_en: Wasting of the tibialis anterior muscle.
An abnormality of myelination of nerves in the central nervous system.
Delayed myelination in the peripheral nervous system.
Demyelination of peripheral sensory nerves.

terms.en: Abnormal umbilical cord blood vessel morphology

terms.def_en: A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short trunk but a average-sized limbs that is lethal at birth.
A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short trunk but a average-sized limbs with onset in infancy.
Intrauterine growth retardation that is at least 3 standard deviations (SD) below average, but not as low as 4 SD, corrected for sex and gestational age.

Structural anomaly of the fetal membranes (also known as the amniochorionic or placental membranes), which comprise a vital intrauterine compartment, where they perform mechanical, immune, and endocrine functions to promote growth of the fetus and protection from environmental adversity. Amniochorionic membranes anatomically consist of a single layer of cuboidal amnion epithelial cells, chorionic trophoblasts, and scattered fibroblasts connected by a layer of type IV collagen-rich extracellular matrix.
Delivery of a fetus through surgical incisions made through the abdominal wall (laparotomy) and the uterine wall (hysterotomy).
Delivery of newborn by means of a ventouse, a vacuum device used to assist the delivery of a baby when the second stage of labor has not progressed adequately.
Shoulder dystocia occurs when the fetal anterior shoulder impacts against the maternal symphysis following delivery of the vertex.
An abnormality of the placenta in which there are numerous cystic spaces within the placenta as well as placental enlargement.
Increased length of the umbilical cord.
Anomalous location of the insertion of umbilical cord in the placenta. Normally, the insertion is at least two centimers distant from the edge of the placenta.
Separation of the placenta from the uterus wall before delivery.

terms.it: Concentrazione anormale di cloruro nel sangue
terms.def_en: Any deviation from the normal concentration of chloride in the blood circulation.
The concentration of chloride in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
An increased concentration of zinc in the blood.

An finding upon obstetric ultrasound examination performed at around 16 to 20 weeks of gestation that is abnormal but not clearly identifiable as a fetal anatomic malformation or growth restriction. Such findings are known as soft markers since they are associated with increased risk for fetal aneuploidy or other disorders.

Fetal choroid plexus cysts (CPCs) are sonographically discrete, small cysts found in the choroid plexus within the lateral cerebral ventricles of the developing fetus at 14 to 24 weeks gestation. Imaging of the choroid plexus is performed in the transverse plane of the fetal head at the same level that the lateral cerebral ventricle is evaluated. The choroid plexus should be inspected bilaterally for the presence of cysts. The size of CPCs is not of clinical relevance (PMID:16100637).

The cisterna magna is measured on a transaxial view of the fetal head angled 15 degrees caudal to the canthomeatal line. The anterior/posterior diameter is taken between the inferior/posterior surface of the vermis of the cerebellum to the inner surface of the cranium. An enlarged cisternal magna is defined by an anterior/posterior diameter of 10 mm or more (PMID:16100637).

A short femur length is defined as either a measurement below the 2.5th percentile for gestational age or a measurement that is less than 0.9 of that predicted by the measured biparietal diameter. The femur should be measured with the bone perpendicular to the ultrasound beam and with epiphyseal cartilages visible but not included in the measurement (PMID:16100637).

A short humerus length is defined as a length below the 2.5th percentile for gestational age or as a measurement less than 0.9 of that predicted by the measured biparietal diameter. The humerus should be measured with the bone perpendicular to the ultrasound beam and with epiphyseal cartilages visible but not included in the measurement (PMID:16100637).
lay_en: Short fetal long bone in upper arm length
syn_en: Short foetal long bone in upper arm length

terms.def_en: On prenatal ultrasound, the nasal bone is a thin echogenic line within the bridge of the fetal nose. The fetus is imaged facing the transducer with the fetal face strictly in the midline. The angle of insonation is 90 degrees, with the longitudinal axis of the nasal bone as the reference line. Calibres are placed at each end of the nasal bone. Absence of the nasal bone or measurements below 2.5th percentile are considered significant (PMID:16100637).

Fifth finger clinodactyly is defined by a hypoplastic or absent mid-phalanx of the fifth digit. Ultrasound identification of the fetal hand must first be undertaken and then appropriate magnification accomplished. The evaluation requires stretching of the 5 fingers. The diagnosis is established when the middle phalanx of the fifth finger is markedly smaller than normal or absent, which often causes the finger to be curved inward (PMID:16100637).
Rhabdomyolysis induced by anesthesia.
Rhabdomyolysis induced by intake of alcohol.
An abnormality of the medulla oblongata, the lower half of the brainstem.
An anomaly of the control or production of movement in the central nervous system.
A type of rigidity in which the arms are in flexion and adduction and the legs are extended. This signifies a lesion in the cerebral white matter, internal capsules, or thalamus.
A type of cerebral palsy characterized by slow, involuntary muscle movement and mixed muscle tone.
Cognitive, psychiatric, or memory anomaly.
Hyposegmented (hypolobulated) or bilobed neutrophil nuclei.
syn_en: Hyposegmentation of neutrophil nuclei in peripheral blood

terms.def_en: Clonus is an involuntary tendon reflex that causes repeated flexion and extension of the foot. Ankle clonus is tested by rapidly flexing the foot upward.
Clonus is an involuntary tendon reflex that causes repeated flexion and extension of the foot. Knee clonus can be tested by rapidly pushing the patella towards the toes.

Increased susceptibility to infections of the central nervous system, as manifested by recurrent, severe, or invasive infections involving the brain, meninges, or spinal cord. This can include infections caused by opportunistic or atypical pathogens, or common pathogens presenting with unusual severity or in anatomical locations.
Head circumference below 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender at birth.
syn_en: Decreased head circumference present at birth

terms.en: Functional abnormality of the middle ear
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the function of the middle ear.
lay_en: Functional abnormality of the middle ear

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the incus, an ossicle in the middle ear.
An abnormality of the malleus, an ossicle in the middle ear.
Aplasia of the malleus.
Aplasia of the stapes.
This term refers to the loss of eyelashes that were previously present.
A subjective manifestation of disease localized to the abdomen.
The presence of a carcinoma of the esophagus.
A lack of intestinal ganglion cells (i.e., an aganglionic section of bowel) affecting the small intestine.
A lack of intestinal ganglion cells (i.e., an aganglionic section of bowel) affecting the duodenum.
Absence or underdevelopment of the gallbladder.
A developmental defect in which the gallbladder fails to form.
Sudden, repetitive, nonrhythmic motor movements (spasms), involving the eyes and muscles of the face.
Regurgitation of milk through the nose.

terms.it: Alimentazione con sondino nasogastrico nella prima infanzia
terms.def_en: Feeding problem necessitating nasogastric tube feeding.
Feeding problem necessitating gastrostomy tube feeding.

syn_en: Abnormal shape of small intestinal villus
Abnormality of small intestinal villus morphology

terms.def_en: The enteric villi are atrophic or absent.
Sensorineural hearing impairment with childhood onset.
Persistence of the stapedial artery, which normally regresses during embryonic life.
Complete loss of hearing related to a sensorineural defect.

In primary position, the eyes drift slowly downward and then spontaneously beat upward. Upward gaze accentuates the nystagmus. The associated oscillopsias are often very irritating, but the symptoms are usually transient.
Absence of globe, optic nerve, chiasm and optic tracts. No evidence of ocular tissue on MRI scan or examination.
An abnormality of the lacrimal punctum, an opening on the eyelid close to the medial canthus that drains tears from the conjunctival sac into the lacrimal duct in the same eyelid.
A developmental anomaly characterized by abnormal smallness of one eye.
lay_en: Abnormally small eyeball on one side

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the lacrimal duct, a duct that drain tears from the conjunctiva, via the lacrimal puncta, into the lacrimal sac.
Abnormality of the lacrimal gland, i.e., of the almond-shaped gland that secretes the aqueous layer of the tear film for each eye.

terms.en: Anterior synechiae of the anterior chamber
terms.def_en: Adhesions between the iris and the cornea.

terms.en: Posterior synechiae of the anterior chamber
terms.def_en: Adhesions between the iris and the lens.
Developmental abnormality in which the lens and cornea are not separated.
An abnormal anteroposterior thickness of the cornea.
A increased anteroposterior thickness of the cornea.
Abnormality of the corneal endothelium, that is, the single layer of cells on the inner surface of the cornea.
Abnormal migration of corneal endothelium.
Abnormality of Descemet's membrane, which is the basement membrane of the corneal endothelium.

terms.en: Reduced number of corneal endothelial cells
terms.def_en: A reduction in the number of corneal endothelial cells.
An abnormality of the stroma of cornea, also known as the substantia propria of cornea.
Reduced transparency of the central portion of the corneal stroma.
Generalized reduced transparency of the stroma of the cornea.
Abnormality of the corneal epithelium, that is of the epithelial tissue that covers the front of the cornea.
Ingrowth of new blood vessels into the cornea.
lay_en: New blood vessel formation in cornea

terms.def_en: Formation of new blood vessels on the iris. The new vessels do not display the typical radially symmertic growth pattern of normal iris blood vessels, but rather appear disorganized. Rubeosis usually starts from the pupillary border with tiny tufts of dilated capillaries or red spots that can only be appreciated with high magnification.
lay_en: New blood vessel formation in iris

terms.def_en: Abnormal dilatation of the iris.
Multiple pupils.
A conical projection of the anterior surface of the lens, occurring as a developmental anomaly.
A conical projection of the posterior surface of the lens, occurring as a developmental anomaly.
Congenital absence of the fovea.
Progressive maculopathy characterized by concentric regions of hyper- and hypopigmentation, with an initial foveal sparing and whose appearance is said to resemble the central target of a dart board.

Cystoid thickening of the retina that takes place due to accumulation of extracellular fluid in the macula as a nonspecific response to blood-retinal barrier breakdown. Histological studies show that radially orientated cystoid spaces consisting of ophthalmoscopically clear fluid are often clinically detectable in the macula area.

Choroidal neovascularization (CNV) is the inward growth of new blood vessels arising from the choriocapillaris. Depending on the stage of development, they can be external (type 1 NV) or internal (type 2 NV) to the retinal pigment epithelium.
Pale, often indistinct, multiple lesions of the macula, of variable shape that is not round. The lesions can be notched, angular, or pisciform (said to resemble a fish).
A macular hole is a full thickness gap in the macula, located in the center of the retina.
Increased amount of pigmentation in the macula.
Drusen (singular, 'druse') are tiny yellow or white accumulations of extracellular material (lipofuscin) that build up in the Bruch membrane of the eye.
Splitting of the retina in the macular region.
Increased pigmentation of the fundus

A benign tumor of the retina that appears as a grouping of blood-filled saccules within the inner retinal layers or on the surface of the optic disc. Retinal cavernous hemangioma are described as having a 'cluster of grapes' appearance.
An abnormality of binocular vision, that is of the ability to synthesize the visual inputs from both eyes to a single image with perception of depth.
Inability to make fine depth discriminations from parallax provided by the two eyes' different positions on the head.
A condition where the retina contains no functional cone cells, so that in addition to the absence of color discrimination, vision in lights of normal intensity is difficult.
The condition of having both rods and cones, but only a single kind of cone. Affected individuals have good pattern vision in daylight, but cannot distinguish between colors.
Individuals affected by dichromacy possess only two types of cones, instead of three.
Individuals with anomalous trichromacy possess three types of cones, but one of the three types of cones has an abnormal spectral sensitivity compared to normal cones.

A type of anomalous trichromacy associated with abnormal M photopigment, such that the absorption spectrum is shifted toward L wavelengths. Affected individuals have difficulties distinguishing between red and green.
Complete lack of the M photopigment, which is replaced with the L photopigment. Affected individuals tend to confuse red and green.
Blue and green cones only; no functional red cones.
An iris cyst is composed of a single cell layer of epithelium and is filled with fluid.
Malignant tumor of melanocytes affecting the iris.
A benign brown pigmented area over the iris representing proliferation of melanocyte cells in the stromal layer of the iris. An iris nevus can be flat or occasionally slightly elevated.
An abnormal shape of the lens.
Exaggerated curvature of the lens of the eye, producing an anterior or posterior spherical bulging.

terms.en: Solitary congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
terms.def_en: Sharply demarcated hyperpigmentation of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) that is congenital and of no functional significance.
syn_en: Single isolated congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium

terms.en: Multiple congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
terms.def_en: Unilateral or bilateral small, well-demarcated pigmented lesions localized in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). Lesions are dark in the center, with a pale circumference and are mostly located in the periphery.
syn_en: Multiple bilateral congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium

terms.def_en: A full-thickness defect in the retina.
Inflammation of the vitreous body, characterized by the presence of inflammatory cells and protein exudate in the vitreous cavity.
A type of retinal exudate located in the subretinal space between the sensory retina and the retinal pigment epithelium.
The appearance of yellow/white crystalline-like (hence the name) spots in the retina and thickening of the peripheral part of the vitreous.

terms.en: Abnormal spatial orientation of the cardiac segments
terms.def_en: Abnormality of the spatial relationship of the cardiac segments to other components of the heart.
Abnormality of the spatial relationship of the atria to other components of the heart.
Right atrial isomerism is characterized by bilateral triangular, morphologically right atrial, appendages, both joining the atrial chamber along a broad front with internal terminal crest.
In left atrial isomerism there is a bilateral small finger-shaped morphologically left atrial appendage joining the atrial chamber along a narrow front without an internal terminal crest.
Mirror image atrial arrangement, with morphologic right atrium on the left hand side and morphologic left atrium on the right hand side.
Common atrium without defining morphologic features.

Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (ccTGA) is a discordance of atrioventricular (AV) and ventriculoarterial connections. The anatomy of ccTGA involves systemic venous drainage to the morphologic right atrium (mRA), which is connected via the mitral valve to the morphologic left ventricle (mLV) whose outflow is the pulmonary arterial system. The pulmonary venous drainage arrives at the morphologic left atrium (mLA), which crosses the tricuspid valve into the morphologic right ventricle (mRV) with outflow into the systemic arterial system. In isolation, ccTGA has an in-series circulation without mixing; therefore, the presence or absence of associated defects dictates the patient's clinical presentation.
syn_en: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries
Physiologically corrected transposition of the great vessels

terms.def_en: Crossing of the inflow streams of the two ventricles, due to an apparent twisting of the heart about its long axis.

terms.en: Criss-cross atrioventricular valves with superior-inferior ventricles
terms.def_en: Criss-cross atrioventricular valves with a rare cardiac malformation characterized by the two ventricles lying one above the other instead of side by side.

terms.en: Superior-inferior ventricles without criss-cross atrioventricular valves
Abnormal connection of the cardiac segments
terms.def_en: A deviance in the normal connections between two cardiac segments.
syn_en: Abnormal connexion of the cardiac segments
Discordant connection of the cardiac segments

terms.def_en: An abnormality of the circulatory connection between atria and ventricles.
A defect where there is no connection between the left atrium and left ventricle.
A defect where there is no connection between the right atrium and right ventricle.

terms.en: Univentricular heart with absent left sided atrioventricular connection
syn_en: Univentricular heart with absent left sided atrioventricular connexion

terms.en: Biventricular heart with straddling right sided atrioventricular valve and absent left sided atrioventricular connection
Right sided atrium to left ventricle and absent left sided atrioventricular connection
syn_en: Right sided atrium to left ventricle and absent left sided atrioventricular connexion

terms.def_en: With left or right cardiac isomerism in a biventricular, the atrioventricular connections are perforce ambiguous, in that one of the connections is concordant (e.g., right-sided morphologic right atrium connected to a morphologic right ventricle) and one of the connections is discordant (e.g., left-sided morphologic right atrium connected to a morphologic left ventricle).
Connection of the right atrium to the left ventricle and of the left atrium to the right ventricle in a biventricular heart.
The condition in which both atria are joined to a single ventricle each by its own atrioventricular valve.

The condition in which both atria are joined to the left ventricle each by its own atrioventricular valve. Usually there is a hypoplastic right ventricle, which may be on the opposite side of the heart as usual.
The condition in which both atria are joined to the right ventricle each by its own atrioventricular valve. Usually, the left ventricle is hypoplastic.

terms.en: Double inlet to single ventricle of indeterminate morphology
terms.def_en: The condition in which both atria are joined to a single ventricle each by its own atrioventricular valve. The morphology of this ventricle does not allow one to determine if it corresponds to the left or right ventricle.

terms.en: Double inlet to single ventricle with common atrioventricular orifice
Double inlet to single ventricle with two atrioventricular valves

terms.def_en: A congenital defect with failure to open of the mitral valve orifice.
An atrioventricular valve that empties into both ventricles. The valve overrides the interventricular septum above a ventricular septum defect.
Anomalous insertion of the chordae tendinae or papillary muscles into the contralateral ventricle in the presence of a ventricular septum defect.
An abnormality of the circulatory connection between the ventricles and the pulmonary artery and aorta.

Anomalous mitral valve arcade is diagnosed based on the following features (1) An adequately sized mitral valve orifice; (2) short, thick, and poorly differentiated chordae with direct union of the papillary muscles to the anterior leaflet; (3) narrow or nearly nonexistent spaces between the abnormal chordae; and (4) greater differentiation of the chordae attached to the posterior papillary muscle.
Complete absence of the interatrial septum with common atrioventricular valve and two atrioventricular connections.

A congenital anomaly with partitioning of the right atrium to form a triatrial heart caused by persistence of the right valve of the sinus venosus. Typically, the right atrial partition is due to exaggerated fetal eustachian and thebesian valves, which together form an incomplete septum across the lower part of the atrium. This septum may range from a reticulum to a substantial sheet of tissue.

terms.it: Difetto del setto atriale del seno venoso
terms.def_en: An interatrial communication caused by a deficiency of the common wall between the superior vena cava (SVC) and the right-sided pulmonary veins. SVASD is commonly associated with anomalous pulmonary venous connection (APVC) of some or all of the pulmonary veins, which produces additional left-to-right shunting.
The left atrio-ventricular connection consists of two anatomically distinct orifices separated by accessory fibrous tissue.

terms.it: Mancanza del lembo anteriore della valvola mitrale
terms.def_en: Cleft in the anterior mitral valve leaflet not associated with an atrioventricular canal defect.
Mitral stenosis with congenital onset.
Abnormality of the mitral valve apparatus, whereby chordae attach to a single papillary muscle or hypoplastic papillary muscles.
A congenital stenotic mitral valvular anomaly with a ring of tissue above the mitral valve.
Congenital defect characterized by underdevelopment of the tricuspid valve.
An atrioventricular valve that has failed to open (atretic).
A tricuspid valve that has failed to open.
A specific combination of heart defects with a primum atrial septal defect, cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet, and inlet ventricular defect. There is one valve annulus and two valve orifices.

A specific combination of heart defects including a primum atrial septal defect and cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet. There is not an inlet ventricular septal defect present. There are two valve annuluses and two valve orifices.

A specific combination of heart defects with a primum atrial septal defect, cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet, and an inlet ventricular septal defect. There are two valve annuli and two valve orifices.

Anatomic features of unbalanced atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD) include varying amounts of ventricular hypoplasia, as well as malalignment of the atrioventricular junction. In complete AVSD, the common AV valve can be situated either equally over the right and left ventricles (balanced) or unequally over the ventricles (unbalanced).

terms.en: Short chordae tendineae of the mitral valve
terms.def_en: Abnormally short chordae tendineae of the mitral valve.
A congenital defect of heart development characterized by origin of both pulmonary artery and aorta from the morphological left ventricle.
Displacement of the heart outside the thoracic cavity and into the abdomen.
A type of ectopia cordis with the heart partially in the cervical region and without a defect of the sternum.
A type of ectopia cordis with the heart partially in the cervical region with a defect of the superior portion of the sternum.
Congenital malformation of the thoracic wall with partial or total displacement of the heart outside the thoracic cavity. This feature is associated with sternal cleft or absence of the sternum.
Congenital malformation of the ventral wall with partial or total evisceration of the heart outside the thoracic cavity and displacement partially into the abdominal cavity.

terms.en: Abnormal branching pattern of the aortic arch
terms.def_en: A deviance from the norm of the origin or course of the right brachiocephalic artery, the left common carotid artery, the left subclavian artery or the proximal vertebral arteries.
The aortic arch extends into the soft tissues of the neck before turning down into to become the descending aorta.

terms.en: Common origin of the right brachiocephalic artery and left common carotid artery
terms.def_en: The left common carotid artery has a common origin with the innominate artery.

A conenital abnormality of the aortic arch in which the two embryonic aortc arches form a vascular ring that surrounds the trachea or esophagus and then join to form the descending aorta. Double aortic arch can cause symptoms because of compression of the esophagus (dysphagia, cyanosis while eating) or trachea (stridor).

terms.en: Left aortic arch with cervical origin of the right subclavian artery
Left aortic arch with isolated subclavian artery
terms.def_en: The subclavian artery arises from ductus arteriosus. While the ductus arteriosus is patent its blood supply comes from the ductus, hence from the pulmonary artery. After it closes, the blood supply is retrogradely from the vertebral artery via the circle of Willis.

terms.en: Left aortic arch with retroesophageal diverticulum of Kommerell
terms.def_en: A patent ductus arteriosus or ductal ligament completes the ring.

terms.en: Right aortic arch with retroesophageal diverticulum of Kommerell
terms.def_en: Aortic arch crosses the right mainstem bronchus. The left carotid artery is the first branch, right carotid artery the second branch and right subclavian artery as the third branch.

terms.en: Left aortic arch with retroesophageal right subclavian artery
terms.def_en: Aortic arch crosses the left mainstem bronchus. The first branch is the right carotid artery, the second branch is the left carotid artery, the third branch is the subclavian artery, the fourth branch is the right subclavian artery arising from the posteromedial aspect of the distal aortic arch and continuing posterior to the esophagus to the right hand side of the body.

terms.en: Left aortic arch with right descending aorta and right ductus arteriosus
terms.def_en: The ring may be completed by the ductal ligament.

terms.en: Right aortic arch with left descending aorta and left ductus arteriosus
Right aortic arch with retroesophageal left subclavian artery
syn_en: Right aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery
Right aortic arch with anomalous left subclavian artery

terms.def_en: Mesocardia is an abnormal location of the heart in which the heart is in a midline position and the longitudinal axis of the heart lies in the mid-sagittal plane.
Abnormal plane of direction of the heart from the base to the apex. Left sided is normal.
Abnormal plane of direction of the heart from the base to the apex towards the right. Left sided is normal.
Abnormal plane of direction of the heart from the base to the apex in the midline. Left sided is normal.

terms.en: Congenital malformation of the great arteries
terms.def_en: Defect or defects of the morphogenesis of the aorta and pulmonary arteries.
A congenital anomaly with an abnormal connection between the aorta and the main pulmonary artery resulting in an aortopulmonary shunt.

Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) with each pulmonary artery arising separate from each other on the posterior or lateral aspect of the truncus.

Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) whereby one of the two pulmonary artery branched does not arise from the common pulmonary trunk, but instead from the ductus arteriosus or directly from the aorta.

Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) whereby the aortic arch is hypoplastic or interrupted, and a large patent ductus arteriosus is present.
Non-continuity of the arch of aorta with an atretic point or absent segment.
Non-continuity of the aortic arch with an atretic point or absent segment at the level of the isthmus.

terms.it: Arco aortico interrotto di tipo B
terms.def_en: Non-continuity of the aortic arch with an atretic point or absent segment between the left carotid and subclavian arteries.
Non-continuity of the aortic arch with an atretic point or absent segment between the innominate and left carotid arteries.

An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, which is defined by characteristics such as the number of lobes per lung and the relationship of the pulmonary arteries to their bronchi.
Mirror image arrangement of the mainstem bronchi with the right pulmonary artery posterior to the right upper lobe bronchus and the left pulmonary artery anterior to the left upper lobe bronchus.
An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, in which the morphology of both left and right lungs is the same.

terms.en: Pulmonary situs ambiguus with bilateral morphologic right lungs
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, in which both lungs have the morphology of a right lung.

terms.en: Pulmonary situs ambiguus with bilateral morphologic left lungs
terms.def_en: An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, in which both lungs have the morphology of a left lung.
An abnormality of the abdominal situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the abdomen and its organs.

A type of ventricular septal defect communicating directly between the left ventricle and right atrium. This is anatomically possible because the normal tricuspid valve is more apically displaced than the mitral valve.
A ventricular septal defect that involves the inlet of the right ventricular septum immediately inferior to the AV valve apparatus.
syn_en: Atrioventricular canal type ventricular septal defect

terms.def_en: The trabecular septum is the largest part of the interventricular septum. It extends from the membranous septum to the apex and superiorly to the infundibular septum. A defect in the trabecular septum is called muscular VSD if the defect is completely rimmed by muscle.
A muscular ventricular septal defect located at the apex of the heart.
A type of muscular ventricular septal defect characterized by the presence of multiple small defects in the ventricular septum.
Right pulmonary venous return to the inferior vena cava.
Aorto-ventricular tunnel is a congenital, extracardiac channel which connects the ascending aorta above the sinotubular junction to the cavity of the left, or (less commonly) right ventricle.
A developmental defect of the pericardium with congenital onset.
No pericardium around the heart, occurring as a congenital defect, not the result of a surgical pericardectomy.
No pericardium over the diaphragmatic surface of the heart. It is a congenital defect, not the result of a pericardectomy. Pericardium is present on other parts of the heart.

terms.en: Complete right sided absence of pericardium
terms.def_en: No pericardium is present on the righthand side of the heart. It is a congenital absence of pericardium rather than the result of a pericardectomy.

terms.en: Partial right sided absence of pericardium
terms.def_en: A congenital anomaly with lack of part of the pericardium on the righthand side of the heart.

terms.en: Complete left sided absence of pericardium
terms.def_en: A congenital anomaly with complete lack of the pericardium on the lefthand side of the heart.
lay_en: Absent lining around of left side of heart

terms.en: Partial left sided absence of pericardium
terms.def_en: A congenital anomaly with lack of part of the pericardium on the lefthand side of the heart.
Lack of a part of the pericardium over the diaphragmatic surface of the heart. It is a congenital defect, not the result of a pericardectomy. Pericardium is present on other parts of the heart.

Isolated abnormalities of the coronary artery origins. This may be in associated with other structural heart malformations but not the patterns of complex structural heart malformations which result in abnormal course of the coronary arteries.

terms.en: Anomalous origin of coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
terms.def_en: A coronary artery begins (branches off from) the pulmonary artery rather than as normal from the root of the aorta.

terms.en: Anomalous origin of left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
terms.def_en: Left main coronary artery begins (branches off from) the pulmonary artery rather than as normal from the root of the aorta, above the left cusp of the aortic valve.
syn_en: Anomalous left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery

terms.en: Anomalous origin of right coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
terms.it: Origine anomala dell'arteria coronaria destra dall'arteria polmonare
terms.def_en: Right coronary artery begins (branches off from) the pulmonary artery rather than as normal from the root of the aorta, above the right cusp of the aortic valve.
The presence of a single coronary artery ostium from which both coronary arteries arise.
A congenital malformation with abnormal connection between one of the coronary arteries and a heart chamber or another blood vessel.

An abnormality of the coronary sinus, which is formed by the union of the great cardiac vein and the left marginal vein and terminates in the right atrium. The coronary sinus functions to o collect deoxygenated blood from the myocardium of the heart and drain it into the right atrium.

An atrial septal defect characterized by a deficiency in the tissue separating the coronary sinus from the left atrium (LA). This results in partial or complete unroofing of the coronary sinus leading to a predominantly left-to-right shunt through the coronary sinus (LA to coronary sinus to right atrium [RA]). The orifice of the ostium is frequently large because of the increased flow. From the RA side, the defect is located at the level of the coronary sinus ostium and may also include some deficiency in atrial tissue around the ostium. From the LA side, the size can be variable depending on the degree of unroofing of the coronary sinus. There is partial (either focal or fenestrated) or complete absence of the roof of the CS, which results in a communication between the CS and the LA. Unroofed CS is the rarest type of atrial septal defect. It is often associated with persistent left superior vena cava (LSVC) and other forms of complex congenital heart disease, usually heterotaxia syndromes.
A venous pouch within the left ventricular wall, with a neck opening into the coronary sinus.

terms.en: Dilatation of the sinus of Valsalva
terms.def_en: Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation of one of the anatomic dilations of the ascending aorta, which occurs just above the aortic valve.
Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized at the insertion of the ductus arteriosus, i.e., to the juxtaductal region of aortic arch.
Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized distal to the ductus arteriosus, i.e., to the postductal region of aortic arch.

terms.en: Patent ductus arteriosus after birth at term
terms.it: Brevetto del dotto arterioso dopo la nascita a termine
terms.def_en: Abnormal persistent patency of the ductus arteriosus in postnatal life when birth was at 37 completed weeks of gestation or greater.

terms.en: Patent ductus arteriosus after premature birth
terms.def_en: Abnormal persistent patency of the ductus arteriosus when birth was at less than 37 weeks completed gestation.
The presence of both a left and a right ductus arteriosus.

terms.en: Double outlet right ventricle with doubly committed ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
terms.def_en: A double outlet right ventricle with a subaortic ventricular septal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that extends anterosuperiorly and are closely related to the pulmonary artery as well, are considered to be doubly committed. There is associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
syn_en: DORV with doubly committed VSD and pulmonary stenosis

terms.en: Double outlet right ventricle with doubly committed ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
terms.def_en: A double outlet right ventricle with a subaortic ventritricular septal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that extends anterosuperiorly and are closely related to the pulmonary artery as well, are considered to be doubly committed. There is not associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
syn_en: Double outlet right ventricle, doubly committed ventricular septal defect

terms.en: Double outlet right ventricle with non-committed ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
terms.def_en: A double outlet right ventricle with a non-committed ventricular septal defect (VSD), which is a VSD that is anatomically related to, or close to, neither great vessel, being separated from both by considerable muscle, and also has a pulmonary stenosis; abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
syn_en: DORV with non-committed VSD and pulmonary stenosis

terms.en: Double outlet right ventricle with non-committed ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
terms.def_en: A double outlet right ventricle with a non-committed ventricular septal defect (VSD), which is a VSD that is anatomically related to, or close to, neither great vessel, being separated from both by considerable muscle, but there is not accompanying pulmonary stenosis; the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
syn_en: DORV with non-committed VSD without pulmonary stenosis
Double outlet right ventricle, noncommitted ventricular septal defect

terms.en: Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
terms.def_en: A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the aortic origin. There is associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
syn_en: DORV with subaortic VSD and pulmonary stenosis

terms.en: Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
