Absence of the outer dynein arms of respiratory motile cilia, which normally are situated outside of the peripheral microtubules of motile cilia. This feature is usually appreciated by electron microscopy.

Absence of the inner dynein arms of respiratory motile cilia, which normally are situated within the peripheral microtubules of motile cilia. This feature is usually appreciated by electron microscopy.

terms.en: Abnormal axonemal organization of respiratory motile cilia
terms.def_en: Abnormal arrangement of the structures of the axoneme, which is the cytoskeletal structure that forms the inner core of the motile cilium and displays a canonical 9+2 microtubular pattern of motile cilia studded with dynein arms.
syn_en: Abnormal axonemal organisation of respiratory motile cilia

terms.en: Absent inner and outer dynein arms
terms.def_en: Complete absence of the dynein arms of respiratory motile cilia, that is, absence of the inner and the outer dynein arms, which normally are situated inside and outside of the peripheral microtubules of motile cilia. This feature is usually appreciated by electron microscopy.

terms.en: Abnormal central microtubular pair morphology of respiratory motile cilia
terms.def_en: A structural anomaly of the two central microtubules of motile cilia with a 9+2 microtubuluar configuration.
Any functional anomaly of the respiratory motile cilia.

Any anomaly of the normal motility of motile cilia. Evaluation of ciliary beat frequency and ciliary beat pattern requires high-speed videomicroscopy of freshly obtained ciliary biopsies that are maintained in culture media under controlled conditions.

terms.en: Absent central microtubular pair morphology of respiratory motile cilia
terms.def_en: Absence of the two central microtubules of motile cilia with a 9+2 microtubuluar configuration.
A deviation from the normally well coordinated pattern of intracellular and intercellular synchrony of motile cilia. Dyskinetic cilia usually beat out of synchrony relative to neighboring cilia.
syn_en: Lack of coordinated beating of respiratory cilia

terms.def_en: A periodic beat-to-beat variation in the amplitude or shape of the T wave in an EKG.

terms.en: Absent respiratory ciliary axoneme radial spokes
terms.def_en: Absence of the radial spokes of the axoneme of the respiratory cilium.
A liposarcoma that contains myxomatous tissue.
Any anomaly in the amount of glycogen in muscle tissue.
A decreased amount of glycogen in muscle tissue.
Intermittent episodes of increased resistance to the passage of air in the upper airway.
The J wave is a positive convex deflection that occurs at the junction of the QRS complex and ST segment, the J-point.

terms.en: Increased carotid artery intimal medial thickness
terms.def_en: An increase in the combined thickness of the intima and media of the carotid artery.

Inflammation of the flexor digitorum tendon, often associated with the Kanavel signs: (i) finger held in slight flexion, (ii) fusiform swelling, (iii) tenderness along the flexor tendon sheath, and (iv) pain with passive extension of the digit.
An abnormally reduced concentration of glycine in the blood.
Any deviation from the normal concentration of serine in the blood circulation.
The concentration of serine in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
A form of amyloidosis that affects the liver.
Extravasation of chyle into the peritoneal cavity.

An exanthema consisting of widespread pink-to-red macules (flat spots of 2-10 mm in diameter) or papules (red bumps) that blanch with pressure. The macules and papules may cluster and merge to form sheets over several days.
Reduced size of the Distal epiphysis of femur.
lay_en: Small end part of outermost thighbone

terms.def_en: Reduced size of the proximal epiphysis of the tibia.
lay_en: Small end part of innermost shankbone
Small end part of innermost shinbone

terms.def_en: An abnormal functionality of the hypothalamus.
Any structural anomaly of the hypothalamus.
Decreased secretion of luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone by the hypothalamus.
A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the head and neck region with origin in the lip, oral cavity, nasal cavity, paranasal sinuses, pharynx, or larynx.
A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the face.
A congenital defect with an abnormal joining of the gums of the upper and lower jaw.
lay_en: Upper and lower gums fused together

terms.def_en: An abnormal pigmentation pattern of the external genitalia.
Abnormality of the occipital bone of the skull.
Reduced diameter of the middle phalanx of finger.
Reduced diameter of the distal phalanx of finger.
Reduced diameter of the proximal phalanx of finger.
Increased length of the middle phalanx of finger.
Increased length of the distal phalanx of finger.
Failure of the ureter to undergo development.

terms.it: Profilo dell'isoforma della transferrina di tipo II
terms.def_en: Abnormal transferrin isoform profile consistent with a type II congenital disorder of glycosylation.
syn_en: Abnormal isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin, type II pattern
Isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin consistent with CDG type II

terms.def_en: Infection of the brain parenchyma with herpes simplex virus, resulting in inflammation of the brain parenchyma with neurologic dysfunction.
An anomaly of the arch of aorta.
Underdevelopment of the arch of aorta.

terms.en: Coarctation of the descending aortic arch
terms.def_en: Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized to the region of the descending trunk of arch of aorta.
An anomaly of the process of rib bone formation.
Ribs that are increased in width and taper to the posterior ends.
Concentration of the complement component C9 in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
The presence of amyloid deposition in the superficial dermis.
Abnormal increase or decrease of total monocytes, or their phenotype, in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group, measured ex vivo.
Abnormal increase of absolute number of monocytes in the blood, per microlitre, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.
Abnormal decrease of absolute number of monocytes in the blood, per microlitre, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.
Bony swelling of the distal interphalangeal joint (DIP) associated with the formation of osteophytes (calcific spurs) of the articular (joint) cartilage that are visible radiographically.
Bony swelling of the proximal interphalangeal joint (PIP) associated with the formation of osteophytes (calcific spurs) of the articular (joint) cartilage that are visible radiographically.
A neoplasm containing histiocytes.
Any neoplasm composed of fibrous tissue.
Inflammation of the sacroiliac joint, generally accompanied by lower back pain.
A distinct type of headache characterized by piercing, throbbing, or electric-shock-like chronic pain in the upper neck, back of the head, and behind the ears, usually on one side.
Lack of skin pigmentation (coloring) of the abdomen.
Lack of skin pigmentation (coloring) of the arms and legs.
An increased concentration of 2-hydroxyglutaric acid in the urine.
Inflammation surrounding hair follicles.
Myoclonus that occurs during the initial phases of sleep.
A leukemia that originates from a myeloid cell, that is the blood forming cells of the bone marrow.

A myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm which is characterized by persistent monocytosis, absence of a Philadelphia chromosome and BCR/ABL fusion gene, fewer than 20 percent blasts in the bone marrow and blood, myelodysplasia, and absence of PDGFRA or PDGFRB rearrangement.
An anomaly of the celiac artery.
Compression of the celiac artery.
An odontogenic tumor of the cementum of tooth.
A vascular tumor of the skin and subcutaneous tissues and characterized by slow angiomatous proliferation.
An inflammation of the kidney involving the parenchyma of kidney, the renal pelvis and the kidney calices.
A structural abnormality of the autonomic nervous system.

terms.it: Fisiologia anomala del sistema nervoso autonomo
terms.def_en: A functional abnormality of the autonomic nervous system.
An abnormal regulation of the sweat glands by the sympathetic nervous system associated with abnormal perspiration.
Impairment of bile flow due to obstruction in large bile ducts outside the liver.
An anomaly in the processes involved in the maintenance of an internal equilibrium.
Any anomaly in the utilization of energy (calories).
An increase in the number of calories used per unit time.
A reduction in the number of calories used per unit time.
A pituitary prolactin cell adenoma of less than 10 mm diameter.
A pituitary prolactin cell adenoma of more than 10 mm diameter.

terms.it: Diminuzione della concentrazione di ferritina in circolo
terms.def_en: Abnormally reduced concentration of ferritin, a ubiquitous intracellular protein that stores iron, in the blood.
Isolated patches of hardened skin (scleroderma).
An anomaly of a glycosylation process, i.e., a process involved in the covalent attachment of a glycosyl residue to a substrate molecule.

An anomaly of a protein glycosylation process, i.e., of a protein modification process that results in the addition of a carbohydrate or carbohydrate derivative unit to a protein amino acid, e.g. the addition of glycan chains to proteins.

terms.it: Anomalia della glicosilazione N-linked delle proteine
terms.def_en: An anomaly of protein N-linked glycosylation, i.e., an abnormality of the protein glycosylation process in which a carbohydrate or carbohydrate derivative unit is added to a protein via a nitrogen atom in an amino acid residue in a protein.

terms.en: Decreased galactosylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
terms.def_en: A reduction in the amount of galactose residues of N-glycans.

terms.en: Abnormal sialylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
terms.def_en: An anomaly of the addition of sialic acids to N-linked glycans.

terms.en: Decreased sialylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
terms.def_en: Decreased addition of sialic acids to N-linked glycans.

terms.en: Increased sialylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
terms.def_en: Increased addition of sialic acids to N-linked glycans.

terms.en: Abnormal fucosylation of protein N-linked glycosylation
terms.def_en: An anomaly of the addition of fucose sugar units to N-linked glycans.

terms.en: Decreased fucosylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
terms.def_en: Decreased addition of fucose sugar units to N-linked glycans.

terms.en: Increased fucosylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
terms.def_en: Increased addition of fucose sugar units to N-linked glycans.

terms.en: Abnormal mannosylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
terms.def_en: An anomaly of the addition of mannose to N-linked glycans.

terms.en: Decreased mannosylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
terms.def_en: Reduced addition of mannose to N-linked glycans.

terms.en: Increased mannosylation of N-linked protein glycosylation
terms.def_en: Increased addition of mannose to N-linked glycans.

terms.it: Anomalie della glicosilazione O-linkata delle proteine
terms.def_en: An anomaly of protein O-linked glycosylation, i.e., of the process in which a carbohydrate or carbohydrate derivative unit is added to a protein via the hydroxyl group of a serine or threonine residue.

terms.en: Abnormal fucosylation of O-linked protein glycosylation
terms.def_en: An anomaly of the addition of fucose sugar units to O-linked glycans.

terms.en: Decreased fucosylation of O-linked protein glycosylation
terms.def_en: A reduction of the addition of fucose sugar units to O-linked glycans.

terms.en: Increased fucosylation of O-linked protein glycosylation
terms.def_en: Increased addition of fucose sugar units to O-linked glycans.

terms.en: Abnormal sialylation of O-linked protein glycosylation
terms.def_en: An anomaly of the addition of sialic acids to O-linked glycans.

terms.en: Decreased sialylation of O-linked protein glycosylation
terms.def_en: An reduced addition of sialic acids to O-linked glycans.
A decreased concentration of potassium(1+) in the urine.
An abnormally decreased phosphate concentration in the urine.

Projection of the tip of the dens more than 5 mm above a line joining the hard palate to the posterior lip of the foramen magnum (Chamberlain's line) or the tip of the dens is greater than 7 mm above McGregor's line (the back of the hard palate to the lowest point of the occipital squama).
An extra soft spot (fontanelle) on an infant's skull beyond the standard six normal fontanelles.
Absence of concavity or convexity of the face when viewed in profile.
Large or prominent malar surface of the zygomatic bone of the skull, which is convex and forms the prominence of the 'cheek bones'.

Abnormally anterior positioning of the infraorbital and perialar regions, or increased convexity of the face, or increased nasolabial angle. The midface includes the maxilla, the cheeks, the zygomas, and the infraorbital and perialar regions of the face
A structural anomaly of the globe of the eye, or bulbus oculi.
A functional anomaly of the eye.
Edema (swelling) of the bulbar conjunctiva.
Abnormal smallness of the lens.
Partial or complete loss of vision in one half of the visual field of one or both eyes.
A subjective feeling of tiredness characterized by a lack of energy and motivation.

terms.en: Abnormal circulating enzyme concentration or activity
terms.def_en: Concentration or activity of an enzyme is above or below the limits of normal in the blood circulation.

Reduced carnitine O-palmitoyltransferase (CPT II; EC 2.3.1.21) activity or level, leading to a reduced activity of the reaction: palmitoyl-CoA + L-carnitine = CoA + L-palmitoylcarnitine. (CPT II activity can be measured in tissues including fibroblasts, lymphoblasts, and skeletal muscle.
A delay in the development of skills required to feed oneself in the toddler period (between one and three years of age).
Pattern of blood flow in the heart that deviates from the normal circuit of the circulatory system from the left side of the heart to the right.
Pattern of blood flow in the heart that deviates from the normal circuit of the circulatory system from both right side of the heart to the left and vice versa.
Inflammation of the nasal mucosa with nasal congestion.
The distal interphalangeal joint and/or the proximal interphalangeal joint of the fingers or toes cannot be extended to 180 degrees by either active or passive extension.
lay_en: Permanent flexion of the finger or toe

terms.def_en: Aplasia of the hallux, that is, a development defect such that the big toe does not develop.
Inflammation of the large airways in the lung including any part of the bronchi from the primary bronchi to the tertiary bronchi.
Inflammation of the large airways of the lung with rapid onset and short course usually associated with cough, mucus production, shortness of breath, wheezing, and chest tightness.
Muscular hypotonia of one or more limbs.
A small tear in the thin, moist tissue (mucosa) that lines the anus. It appears as a crack or slit in the mucous membrane of the anus.
Reduced intensity of muscle tendon reflexes in the upper limbs. Reflexes are elicited by stretching the tendon of a muscle, e.g., by tapping.
Reduced intensity of muscle tendon reflexes in jaw.
An allergy is an immune response or reaction to substances that are usually not harmful.
Allergy to iodine contrast media used in radiological studies.
An allergy experienced at a particular time of year when trees or grasses pollinate and elicit an allergic reaction.
A motility disorder characterized by biliary colic in the absence of gallstones with a reduced gallbladder ejection fraction.
The presence of atheromas or atherosclerotic plaques in the aorta.
An abnormal accumulation of interstitial fluid in the soft tissues of the limbs.

A type of ulcer that is caused when an area of skin is subject to pressure over a prolonged period of time, ranging in range in severity from patches of discolored skin to open wounds that expose the underlying bone or muscle. The most common sites are the sacrum, coccyx, heels and the hips.

An abnormal concentration of aldolase in the serum. Aldolase is an enzyme responsible for converting fructose 1,6-bisphosphate into the triose phosphates dihydroxyacetone phosphate and glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate.
A deviation from normal of the concentration of 2-oxoglutaric acid in the urine.
syn_en: Abnormality of urine alpha ketoglutarate concentration

terms.def_en: A greater than normal concentration of 2-oxoglutaric acid in the urine.
A lower than normal concentration of 2-oxoglutaric acid in the urine.
A deviation from normal of the concentration of citrate(3-) in the urine.
A lower than normal concentration of citrate(3-) in the urine.
A greater than normal concentration of citrate(3-) in the urine.

A type of spastic paraparetic gait in which the muscle tone in the adductors is marked. It is characterized by hypertonia and flexion in the legs, hips and pelvis accompanied by extreme adduction leading to the knees and thighs hitting, or sometimes even crossing, in a scissors-like movement. The opposing muscles (abductors) become comparatively weak from lack of use.
The deposition of calcium salts in the parenchyma of the renal medulla (innermost part of the kidney).
The deposition of calcium salts in the parenchyma of the renal cortex (the outer portion of the kidney between the renal capsule and the renal medulla).

A type of anemia resulting from suppression of erythropoiesis with little or no abnormality of leukocyte or platelet production. Erythroblasts are virtually absent in bone marrow; however, leukocyte and platelet production show little or no reduction.
The onset of growth of pubic hair at an earlier age than normal.
Onset of adrenarche at an earlier age than usual.
The presence of a V-shaped indentation (notch) in the primary central incisor.
Wasting or decrease in size of all or part of the duodenum.
An abnormality of the partial pressure of oxygen or carbon dioxide in the arterial blood.
Abnormally elevated blood carbon dioxide (CO2) level.
Abnormally reduced blood carbon dioxide (CO2) level.
lay_en: Reduced carbon dioxide in the blood

terms.def_en: An abnormally low level of blood oxygen.
An abnormally high level of blood oxygen.
Amniotic fluid containing the earliest stools of a mammalian infant.
Congenital lack of the skin of prepuce of penis, that is, of the double-layered fold of skin and mucous membrane that covers the glans penis.
Overgrowth of the choroid plexus.
The inability of the colon to modify stool to an acceptable consistency and move the stool from the cecum to the rectosigmoid area at least once every three days.
An inflammation of the choroid and retina.
An ulcer of the colon due to pressure and irritation from retained fecal masses.

Optic disc drusen are acellular, calcified deposits within the optic nerve head. Optic disc drusen are congenital and developmental anomalies of the optic nerve head, representing hyaline-containing bodies that, over time, appear as elevated, lumpy irregularities on the anterior portion of the optic nerve.

An increased degree of femoral version, which is defined as the angular difference between axis of femoral neck and transcondylar axis of the knee. Thus, femoral anteversion is an inward twisting of the femur that causes the knees and feet to turn inward.
Protruding heel bone, or calcaneus.

terms.en: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the cerebral white matter
terms.def_en: Absence or underdevelopment of the cerebral white matter.
Underdevelopment of the cerebral white matter.
Intermittent and recurrent bouts of a subjective feeling of tiredness characterized by a lack of energy and motivation.
Subjective feeling of tiredness characterized by a lack of energy and motivation that persists for six months or longer.
An abnormality of actions or reactions of a person exhibited during social interactions with other individuals.

terms.it: Ritardo nello sviluppo delle tappe sociali nella prima infanzia
terms.def_en: A failure to meet one or more age-related milestones of social behavior.
Reduction in length of the ventral (lower) skin of prepuce of penis.
Coronary disease that has not progressed to the point of causing significant occlusion (blockage) of the coronary arteries.
A structural anomaly of the gallbladder.
A functional anomaly of the gallbladder.
A functional abnormality of the biliary tree.
A structural abnormality of the biliary tree.
Reduced motility through the sphincter of Oddi, resulting in impedance of bile and pancreatic juice flow from the common bile duct into the duodenum.
Reduced motility of the gallbladder with reduced emptying fraction.
A structural abnormality of the brain, which has as its parts the forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain.
Partial or complete wasting (loss) of brain tissue that was once present.
A reduced concentration of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate(2-) in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). 5-methyltetrahydrofolate is the active folate metabolite.
Any anomaly in the process by which myelin sheaths are formed and maintained around neurons.
Delayed myelination.
Inflammation of the synovial membrane of the sacroiliac joint.
Constipation for longer than three months with fewer than 3 bowel movements per week, straining, lumpy or hard stools, and a sensation of anorectal obstruction or incomplete defecation.
Constipation of sudden onset and lasting for less than three months.

An irresistible urge to move the legs, usually accompanied by unpleasant sensations deep within the limbs. Symptoms typically begin or worsen during periods of rest or inactivity, are most pronounced in the evening or at night, and are temporarily relieved by movement such as walking or stretching. The disturbance often interferes with the initiation or maintenance of sleep.

terms.it: Contrattura bilaterale della flessione del polso
terms.def_en: A chronic loss of wrist joint motion on the right and left sides.
A chronic loss of wrist joint motion on one side only.
Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the tunica media of arteries.
Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the tunica media of medium-sized (muscular or distributive) arteries.
Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the tunica media of small arteries.
A headache disorder that occurs exclusively at night, waking the affected individual from sleep.
A structural anomaly of the inferior portion of the vermis of cerebellum.
The presence of bacteria in the urine.
Involuntary and irregular twitches of the chin.
An above normal level of saturation of serum transferrin with iron.
A below normal level of saturation of serum transferrin with iron.

terms.it: Elevata concentrazione di ferro nel fegato
terms.def_en: An increased level of iron in liver tissues.

Longstanding impairment in ventilation such that the partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO2) is elevated above the upper limit of the reference range (more than 45 mm Hg), with a normal or near-normal pH secondary to renal compensation and an elevated serum bicarbonate levels (more than30 mEq/L).

Sudden onset of impairment in ventilation such that the removal of carbon dioxide by the respiratory system is less than the production of carbon dioxide in the tissues, leading to an elevation of the partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO2) above the normal limits (more than 45 mm Hg) with an accompanying acidemia (pH less than 7.35).
Longstanding abnormal acid accumulation or depletion of base.
Infantile spasms represent a subset of "epileptic spasms". Infantile Spasms are epileptic spasms starting in the first year of life (infancy).

An ophthalmologic sign in young children resulting from upward-gaze paresis. In this condition, the eyes appear driven downward, the sclera may be seen between the upper eyelid and the iris, and part of the lower pupil may be covered by the lower eyelid.
Increased width of the skin of vermilion border region of upper lip.
A turning outward of the lip or lips, that is, eversion of the lips.
Wasting of the tongue.
Complete obstruction of a carotid artery.

Reduced ability of the immune system to produce targeted, protective antibodies (immunoglobulins) against specific pathogens or vaccines in the setting of normal or near-normal serum levels of total IgG, IgA, and IgM and normal absolute counts of B cells and T cells.
syn_en: Decreased circulating level of specific antibodies

terms.en: Decreased circulating specific pneumococcal antibody concentration
terms.it: Diminuzione del livello di anticorpi specifici contro lo pneumococco
terms.def_en: The concentration in the blood circulation of specific immunoglobulins directed against pneumococci is below the lower limit of normal.

A wavering, unsteady voice that reflects involuntary and approximately sinusoidal oscillation of motor unit firings of laryngeal muscles. Vocal tremor results in low frequency modulations of voice frequency or amplitude and intermittent voice instability.
Bony fusion of the mandibular condyle to the base of the skull, resulting in limitation of jaw opening.
Noises from the temporomandibular joint during mandibular movement (e.g., chewing). Temporomandibular joint crepitus is often described as a clicking, popping, grating sound.
An anomaly of cerebral veins.

A congenital malformation of veins which drain normal brain characterized by a caput medusae or an umbrellalike convergence of multiple venules on a single, or occasionally multiple, enlarged parenchymal or medullary vein, like the trunk of a tree or the shank of an umbrella. This dilated terminal vein penetrates the cortex to drain either (a) superficially to cortical veins or sinuses, (b) deeply to subependymal veins of the lateral ventricle and then into the galenic system, (c) to the fourth ventricle and then to the pontomesencephalic vein, or (d) to the precentral cerebellar vein and into the galenic system.
A venous angioma of the frontal lobe of the brain.
Defective structure, size or content of alpha granules, platelet organelles that contain several growth factors destined for release during platelet activation at sites of vessel wall injury.

Defective structure, size or content of dense granules, platelet organelles that contain granules proaggregatory factors such as adenosine diphosphate (ADP), adenosine triphosphate (ATP), ionized calcium, histamine and serotonin.

An anomaly of the invaginations of the surface membrane that form the open canalicular system (OCS). The OCS serve as the pathway for transport of substances into the cells and as conduits for the discharge of alpha granule products secreted during the platelet release reaction.
Inflammation of the spinal cord.
An arachnoid cyst located at the margin of the cerebellum and pons.
An arachnoid cyst located within the ventricular system.

An arachnoid cyst that progressively enlarges from an abnormality in the membrane of Liliequist or in the interpeduncular cistern, and typically, expands from the prepontine space, displacing the floor of the third ventricle upwards, the pituitary stalk and optic chiasm upwards and forwards, and the mammillary bodies upwards and backwards.
Inflammation of subcutaneous adipose tissue.
An anomaly of the intracellular membrane complexes known as the dense tubular system.
Narrowing or constriction of the inner surface (lumen) of a cerebral artery.
Narrowing or constriction of the inner surface (lumen) of the middle cerebral artery.
Narrowing or constriction of the inner surface (lumen) of the anterior cerebral artery.
Narrowing or constriction of the inner surface (lumen) of the posterior cerebral artery.
A decrease in the maximum amount of negative pressure a person can generate during an inhalation.
A decrease in the maximum amount of pressure of expired air achieved by a person after a full inspiration.
A complication of pregnancy and delivery in which the umbilical cord wraps around the fetal neck once or multiple times.

A separation of the layers within the wall of the descending aorta. Tears in the intimal layer result in the propagation of dissection (proximally or distally) secondary to blood entering the intima-media space.
A wartlike (with multiple small elevated projections) papule.
An anomaly of the white matter of brainstem.
syn_en: Abnormality of the brainstem white matter

terms.def_en: An anomaly of the internal capsule, which is an area of white matter in the brain that separates the caudate nucleus and the thalamus from the putamen and the globus pallidus.
An anomaly of the pituitary gland.
A deviation from the normal size of the pituitary gland.
An abnormally increased size of the pituitary gland.
An abnormally decreased size of the pituitary gland.
Reduced strength of the orbicularis oculi, the circumorbital muscle in the face that closes the eyelid.
A visual anomaly in which images appear distorted. A grid of straight lines appears wavy and parts of the grid may appear blank.
An increased amount of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in the subarachnoid space.
A pale yellow discoloration of the temporal (lateral) portion of the optic disc.
A pale yellow discoloration of the entire optic disc.
An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the arm.
An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the leg.
Reduced ability to flex the femur, that is, to pull the knee upward.

terms.en: Tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia
terms.def_en: An extreme form of tetralogy of Fallot characterized by absence of flow from the right ventricle to the pulmonary arteries.
Activity or concentration of catalase in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
An anomaly of the circle of Willis, also known as the cerebral arterial circle.
syn_en: Abnormality of the cerebral arterial circle

terms.def_en: A developmental anomnaly characterized by underdevelopment of the posterior communicating artery.

Increased dimensions of the Virchow-Robin spaces (also known as perivascular spaces), which surround the walls of vessels as they course from the subarachnoid space through the brain parenchyma. Perivascular spaces are commonly microscopic, and not visible on conventional neuroimaging. This term refers to an increase of size of these spaces such that they are visible on neuroimaging (usually magnetic resonance imaging). The dilatations are regular cavities that always contain a patent artery.
Congenital absence of the optic nerve.

A form of telangiectasis characterized by a central elevated red dot the size of a pinhead, representing an arteriole, with numerous small blood vessels that radiate out thereby resembling the legs of a spider. Characteristically, compression of the central arteriole causes the entire lesion to blanch, and the lesion quickly refills once the compression is released.

Reluctance or refusal of a child to be breastfed or eat, manifested as gagging, vomiting, turning head away from food, or avoidance of sensation in or around the mouth (i.e. toothbrushing or face-washing).
A deviation from the normal discoid platelet shape.
An anomalous location and arrangement of platelet alpha granules.
A lack of platelet alpha granules. This typically results in the gray appearance of platelets in giemsa stained blood smears.

A deviation from the normal contents of the platelet alpha granules, which normally contain hemostatic proteins such as fibrinogen, von Willebrand factor, and growth factors such as platelet-derived growth factor.
A deviation from the normal count of alpha granules per thrombocyte.

A deviation from the normal contents of the platelet alpha granules, which normally contain adenosine triphosphate (ATP), adenosine diphosphate (ADP), serotonin, calcium, and pyrophosphate, which are secreted when platelets are activated.
A deviation from the normal count of dense granules per thrombocyte.
An unpleasant sensory and emotional experience associated with actual or potential tissue damage, or described in terms of such damage.
Persistent pain, usually defined as pain that has lasted longer than 3 to 6 months.
Pain due to a stimulus that does not normally provoke pain.

Painful sensations elicited by a nonpainful cutaneous stimulus such as a light touch or gentle stroking over affected areas of the body. Sometimes referred to as hyperpathia or hyperalgesia. Often perceived as an intense burning, dyesthesias may outlast the stimulus by several seconds.

An anomaly in the communication from a neuron to a target across a synapse. This is a four step process, comprising (i) synthesis and storage of neurotransmitters; (ii) neurotransmitter release; (iii) activation of postsynaptic receptors by the neurotransmitter; and (iv) inactivation of the neurotransmitter. Thus, this term is defined as an anomaly of neurotransmitter metabolic process.
A detrimental reaction to a food, beverage, food additive, or compound found in foods that produces symptoms in one or more body organs and systems that is not mediated by an immune reaction.
A detrimental reaction to the presence of gluten in food, which may include abdominal pain, fatigue, headaches and paresthesia, or celiac disease.
A type of lymphoma characterized microscopically by the absence of multinucleated Reed-Sternberg cells.
An epidermoid cyst in the armpit.
Hemorrhage between the skull and periosteum of a newborn resulting from rupture of blood vessels that cross the periosteum.
Thickened nails without deformity.
The presence of hemosiderin in the urine.

terms.it: Elevata concentrazione di aldolasi in circolo
terms.def_en: Concentration of fructose 1,6-bisphosphate aldolase in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
Concentration of fructose 1,6-bisphosphate aldolase in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
Anomalous movements of the eyes that occur without the subject wanting them to happen.
Muscle fibers degeneration resulting in fatty replacement of skeletal muscle fibers
A lipoma (a benign tumor composed of adipose tissue) located in the conjunctiva.
The presence of varices (enlarged and convoluted blood vessels) in the colon.
Lack of specific granules in neutrophils.
Presence of an elevated number of projections from nuclei of neutrophils. These projections can have the shape of hooks, tags, or clubs.
A thumbnail that is diminished in length and width, i.e., underdeveloped thumb nail.
Absence of thumb nail.
Absent nail of big toe.
The concentration of beta-alanine in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.en: EEG with centrotemporal focal spike waves
terms.it: EEG con onde di spike focali centrotemporali
terms.def_en: EEG with focal sharp transient waves in the centrotemporal region of the brain (also known as the central sulcus), i.e., focal sharp waves of a duration less than 80 msec followed by a slow wave.
A ratio of serum triiodothyronine (T3) to thyroxine (T4) in the blood that deviates from normal.
A ratio of serum triiodothyronine (T3) to thyroxine (T4) in the blood that is higher than normal.
A ratio of serum triiodothyronine (T3) to thyroxine (T4) in the blood that is lower than normal.
The presence of an aortic valve with one instead of the normal three cusps (flaps).

Stop of growth at the epiphyseal plate the hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at one or more long bones in the hand, at an earlier than normal age, resulting in growth arrest and shortening of the involved bone.

Stop of growth at the epiphyseal plate the hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at one or more long bones in the foot, at an earlier than normal age, resulting in growth arrest and shortening of the involved bone.

Stop of growth at the epiphyseal plate the hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at one or more long bones in the tibia, at an earlier than normal age, resulting in growth arrest and shortening of the involved bone.

Stop of growth at the epiphyseal plate the hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at one or more long bones in the fibula, at an earlier than normal age, resulting in growth arrest and shortening of the involved bone.

Stop of growth at the epiphyseal plate the hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at one or more long bones in the radius, at an earlier than normal age, resulting in growth arrest and shortening of the involved bone.

Stop of growth at the epiphyseal plate the hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at one or more long bones in the ulna, at an earlier than normal age, resulting in growth arrest and shortening of the involved bone.
Edema in the region of the Lower eyelid.
First period after the age of 15 years.
A type of mesenchymal tissue cell tumor that exhibits epithelial differentiation, which most frequently arises in the extremities.
A partial duplication of the ureter where the duplicated ureters fuse to a single ureter before their insertion into the bladder.
A complete duplication of the ureter, where the duplicated ureters have separate insertions into the bladder.

A type of proximal renal tubulopathy characterized by resorption defects leading to glycosuria, aminoaciduria, tubular proteinuria, renal hypophosphatemia, and urate tubular hyporeabsorption with bicarbonate loss and resulting acidosis.

Increased numbers of mesangial cells per glomerulus, defined as more than 3 nuclei fully surrounded by matrix in one or more mesangial areas, not including perihilar region, on a standard 3-micron-thick tissue section, best evaluated on periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain.
A structural anomaly of the nephron.
The presence of complement 3 deposits in the glomerulus.

Decreased thickness of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), measured from endothelial to visceral epithelial plasma membrane and mainly attributable to a decrease in thickness of the lamina densa, generally to an overall thickness more than 2 standard deviations less than that of the normal mean GBM thickness for health age- and sex matched individuals. May be focal or diffuse, although the term thin GBMs generally implies thinning of over 50% of GBMs.
A type of glomerulonephropathy characterized by thickening of the basement membrane and deposition of immune complexes in the subepithelial space.
The presence of minimal changes visible by light microscopy but flattened and fused podocyte foot processes on electron microscopy in a person with nephrotic range proteinuria.
The presence of calcium- and phosphate-containing calculi (stones) in the kidneys.
An isolated cyst of the kidney.
A bilateral form of developmental dysplasia of the kidney.
One sided hypoplasia of the kidney.
Two sided hypoplasia of the kidney.
Atrophy of the kidney.
A two-sided form of atrophy of the kidney.
Hematuria that is visible upon inspection of the urine.

A form of nephrotic syndrome that does not respond to treatment with steroid medication, defined as persistent proteinuria despite 60mg/m2 or 2mg/kg for 8 weeks, after insuring no infection or non-adherence to medication.
A form of nephrotic syndrome that does not respond to any immunosuppresive treatment.
An abnormal amount of urine production.
An abnormality in the concentration of electrolytes in the urine.
Increased concentration of albumin in the urine.
Severely increased amount of excretion of protein in the urine, defined as 3.5 grams per day or more in adults and 40 mg per meter-squared body surface area per hour in children.
The presence of moderately increased concentrations of albumin in the urine, defined as and albumin-creatinine ratio (ACR) of 30 to 299 mg/gm (3.4 to 34 mg/mmol).
Mildly increased levels of protein in the urine (150-500 mg per day in adults).
Moderately increased levels of protein in the urine (500-1000 mg per day in adults).
Severely increased levels of protein in the urine (1000-3000 mg per day in adults).
An abnormal concentration of potassium(1+) in the urine.
An abnormal phosphate concentration in the urine.
An abnormal concentration of chloride in the urine.
An decreased concentration of chloride in the urine.
High urine chloride in the presence of hypochloridemia.
An abnormal concentration of sodium in the urine.
An abnormally decreased sodium concentration in the urine.
An increased concentration of sodium(1+) in the urine.
An abnormally increased sodium concentration in the urine in the presence of hyponatremia.
An abnormal concentration of magnesium the urine.
An increased concentration of magnesium the urine.
An decreased concentration of magnesium the urine.

terms.en: Abnormality of urinary uric acid level
terms.it: Anomalia del livello di acido urico urinario
terms.def_en: Abnormal amount of urate in the urine.
Abnormal concentration of sulfate in the urine.
Elevated concentration of SO4(2-), i.e., sulfate, in the urine.
An anomalous finding in the examination of the urine for cells.
The presence of renal casts (cylindrical, cigar-shaped structures produced by the kidney in certain disease states) in the urine.
Presence of leukocyte casts (cylindrical structures produced by the kidney in certain disease states) in the urine.
Presence of erythrocyte casts (cylindrical structures produced by the kidney in certain disease states) in the urine.
A cyst located along the allantois canal.
Presence of a many diverticula (sac or pouch) in the wall of the urinary bladder.
A developmental anomaly associated with the failure of rectum, vagina, and bladder to separate.
Developmental anomaly in which the vagina, bladder, and rectum fuse resulting in a common channel.
Functional anomaly of the kidney persisting for at least three months.

terms.it: Insufficienza renale cronica al primo stadio
terms.def_en: A type of chronic kidney disease with normal or increased glomerular filtration rate (GFR at least 90 mL/min/1.73 m2).

terms.it: Insufficienza renale cronica al secondo stadio
terms.def_en: A type of chronic kidney disease with mildly reduced glomerular filtration rate (GFR 60-89 mL/min/1.73 m2).

terms.it: Insufficienza renale cronica al terzo stadio
terms.def_en: A type of chronic kidney disease with moderately reduced glomerular filtration rate (GFR 30-59 mL/min/1.73 m2).

terms.it: Insufficienza renale cronica al quarto stadio
terms.def_en: A type of chronic kidney disease with severely reduced glomerular filtration rate (GFR 15-29 mL/min/1.73 m2).
Deposition of fibrillar material that can be found on all anterior segment structures bathed by aqueous humor.

terms.en: Abnormal suspensory ligament of lens morphology
terms.def_en: An anomaly of the suspensory ligament of lens, also known as the ciliary zonule. These ligaments represent a series of fibers connecting the ciliary body and lens of the eye, holding the lens in place.
syn_en: Abnormality of the suspensory ligament of lens

terms.def_en: Tremulousness (trembling) of the lens of the eye.

An anomaly of the trabecular meshwork, which is the porelike structure surrounding the entire circumference of the anterior chamber at the base of the cornea and near the ciliary body. The trabecular mesh work is responsible for draining the aqueous humor into the canal of Schlemm.

terms.en: Pigment deposition in the trabecular meshwork
terms.def_en: Accumulation of abnormal amounts of pigment within the trabecular meshwork.
An anomaly in the amount of force per unit area exerted by the intraocular fluid within the eye.
A difference in the amount of intraocular pressure in the right and left eye.
Shedding of the pigment granules that normally adhere to the back of the iris into the aqueous humor.
Reduction in the amount of blood flow to the iris.
Blockage of a retinal vein or venule, occurring typically at an arteriovenous crossing. Typically presenting with dilated veins, retinal hemorrhages and in some cases non-perfusion.
High urine calcium in the presence of hypocalcemia.
A functional anomaly of the nervous system.
A structural anomaly of the nervous system.
A deviation from the norm of the intracranial pressure.
A reduction of the pressure inside the cranium (skull) and thereby in the brain tissue and cerebrospinal fluid.
Cerebellar agenesis is defined by the near complete absence of cerebellar tissue with only remnants of the anterior vermis, flocculus, and/or middle cerebellar peduncles.
Decreased amount of pigmentation in the fovea.
An elevated concentration of lactate in the caudate nucleus. This finding can be elicited by magnetic resonance spectroscopy imaging.
Increase in size of a peripheral nerve. This finding can be appreciated by palpation along the axis of the nerve.

A testis that is located at the upper scrotum or lower inguinal canal and that can be made to descend completely into the scrotum without resistance by manual reduction but returns to its original position by the cremasteric reflex.

Any anomaly of the inflammatory response, a response to injury or infection characterized by local vasodilation, extravasation of plasma into intercellular spaces and accumulation of white blood cells and macrophages.
An abnormal reduction in the inflammatory response to injury or infection.
A abnormal increase in the inflammatory response to injury or infection.

Polymicrogyria (an excessive number of small gyri or convolutions) that is maximal in perisylvian regions (the regions that surround the Sylvian fissures), which may be symmetric or asymmetric and may extend beyond perisylvian regions. The Sylvian fissures often extend posteriorly and superiorly.
A severe form of gait ataxia such that an affected person cannot walk at all.
Asthma attacks following exercise.
Severe asthma unresponsive to repeated courses of beta-agonist therapy such as inhaled albuterol, levalbuterol, or subcutaneous epinephrine.
Abnormal concentration of dopamine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).
Increased concentration of dopamine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).
Decreased concentration of dopamine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

A functional brain anomaly detectable by positron emission tomography (PET). PET scanning is a method for functional brain imaging, and its measurements reflect the amount of brain activity in the various regions of the brain.

terms.en: Abnormal brain FDG positron emission tomography
terms.it: Tomografia ad emissione di positroni FDG cerebrale anormale
terms.def_en: An anomaly detectable in [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) brain scans. Glucose uptake measured with FDG-PET is a marker of neuronal metabolic activity.
Reduced uptake of [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) in the prefrontal cortex as measured by positron emission tomography (PET) brain scan.
Reduced uptake of [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) in the thalamus as measured by positron emission tomography (PET) brain scan.
Reduced uptake of [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) in the hypothalamus as measured by positron emission tomography (PET) brain scan.
Reduced uptake of [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) in the parietal cortex as measured by positron emission tomography (PET) brain scan.

terms.en: Mildly reduced left ventricular ejection fraction
terms.it: Frazione di eiezione ventricolare sinistra lievemente ridotta
terms.def_en: A small reduction in the fraction of blood pumped from the left ventricle with each cardiac cycle. The normal range in adults is at least 50 percent, and a mild reduction is defined as 40-49 percent.

terms.it: Riduzione della frazione di eiezione ventricolare sinistra
terms.def_en: A diminution of the volumetric fraction of blood pumped out of the ventricle with each cardiac cycle.

terms.en: Moderately reduced left ventricular ejection fraction
terms.it: Frazione di eiezione ventricolare sinistra moderatamente ridotta
terms.def_en: A medium reduction in the fraction of blood pumped from the left ventricle with each cardiac cycle, defined as a left ventricular ejection fraction of 30-39 percent.

terms.en: Severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction
terms.it: Frazione di eiezione ventricolare sinistra gravemente ridotta
terms.def_en: A large reduction in the fraction of blood pumped from the left ventricle with each cardiac cycle. The normal range in adults is at over 50 percent, and a severe reduction is defined as less than 30 percent.

terms.en: Regional left ventricular wall motion abnormality
terms.def_en: An abnormal motion of a segment of the left ventricle during the cardiac cycle.

A vasovagal episode or vasovagal syncope is the most common form of reflex syncope. Reflex syncope is a general term used to describe types of syncope resulting from a failure in autoregulation of blood pressure, and ultimately, in cerebral perfusion pressure resulting in transient loss of consciousness. The mechanisms responsible for this are complex and involve both depression of cardiac output as well as a decrease in vascular tone.
An exaggerated response to carotid sinus baroreceptor stimulation resulting in syncope from transient diminished cerebral perfusion.
Syncope following a quick change in position from lying down to standing.

Abulia is characterized by difficulty in initiating and sustaining spontaneous movements; the person often appears frozen but will move hesitantly on request. There are frequently substantial reductions in emotional responsiveness, spontaneous speech, and social interaction. The individual appears to be content to remain still and inactive with minimal movement, but moves or reacts hesitantly in response to interactions.

The combined absence of spontaneous movement (akinesia) and speech (mutism). There may be eye movements consistent with visual tracking and the person may remember the events occurring at the time of the experience of stupor.
A failure to develop of the upper vagina.
A failure to develop of the lower part of the vagina.
An abnormal build up of iron (Fe) in brain tissue.
An anomalous build up of copper (Cu) in the brain.
An anomalous build up of iron (Fe) in the substantia nigra.

An increase in the distance between vertebral pedicles, which are the two short, thick processes, which project backward, one on either side, from the upper part of the vertebral body, at the junction of its posterior and lateral surfaces.
An anomaly of the pineal gland,a small endocrine gland in the brain that produces melatonin.
A structural abnormality of the pineal gland.
Accumulation of calcium salts in the pineal gland.
A glial uniloculated or multiloculated fluid-filled sac that either reside within or completely replace the pineal gland.
An abnormal increase or decrease in the quantity of three-dimensional space taken up by the pineal gland.
An abnormal reduction in the quantity of three-dimensional space taken up by the pineal gland.
An abnormal elevation in the quantity of three-dimensional space taken up by the pineal gland.
Failure to develop of the pineal gland, defined clinically as the absence of the pineal gland with no indication of the pineal gland even having been present.
A functional abnormality of the pineal gland.
An anomaly in the amount or timing of melatonin secretion by the pineal gland. Note that melatonin is also synthesized by multiple tissues outside of the pineal gland.
A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the thalamus. This term refers to a diffuse hypointensity affecting the entire thalamus.
A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the thalamus. This term refers to a localized hypointensity affecting a particular region of the thalamus.
A lighter than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the thalamus. This term refers to a localized hyperintensity affecting a particular region of the thalamus.
Deviation from the normal range of size of the thalamus.
An increase in the quantity of space occupied by the thalamus.
A reduction in the quantity of space occupied by the thalamus.
A deviation from normal signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the thalamus.
Decreased size of the basal ganglia.
Focal proliferation of glial cells in the cerebellum.
A structural abnormality of a diaphysis of the leg.
lay_en: Anomaly of shaft of long bone of lower limb

terms.def_en: A functional anomaly of the large intestine.
A sudden, irresistible need to have a bowel movement.
A repeated, painful urge to defecate without excreting stool.
Abnormality in the space in the meninges beneath the arachnoid membrane and above the pia mater that contains the cerebrospinal fluid.
An increase in size of the anatomic space between the arachnoid membrane and pia mater.

terms.en: Abnormal metabolic brain imaging by MRS
terms.def_en: An anomaly of metabolism in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

terms.en: Elevated brain choline level by MRS
terms.def_en: An increase in the level of choline-containing compounds in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

terms.en: Elevated brain lactate level by MRS
terms.it: Elevato livello di lattato cerebrale mediante MRS
terms.def_en: An increase in the level of lactate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

terms.en: Reduced brain N-acetyl aspartate level by MRS
terms.it: Ridotto livello di N-acetil aspartato cerebrale mediante MRS
terms.def_en: A decrease in the level of N-acetyl aspartate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
syn_en: MR Spectroscopy: N-acetylaspartate low in brain
Reduced brain N-acetyl aspartate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

terms.en: Abnormal brain choline/creatine ratio by MRS
terms.def_en: A deviation from normal in the ratio of choline to creatine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
Excessive growth of a nail laterally into the nail fold.
A delay in the process of formation and maturation of the epiphysis of one or more vertebrae.
lay_en: Delayed maturation of the end part of the vertebral bone

terms.def_en: A mild form of hearing impairment (26-40 dB) in which individuals can hear speech at a normal volume from about one meter away but may struggle with softer sounds, such as whispers or quiet conversations. Understanding speech in noisy environments can also be challenging.

A moderate form of hearing impairment (41-60 dB) in which speech must be spoken at a raised volume from one meter away for individuals to hear clearly. Normal conversations, particularly in the presence of background noise, may be difficult to follow.
A severe form of hearing impairment (61-80 dB) in which individuals can only hear a few words spoken at a high volume and experience significant difficulty perceiving speech at normal levels.
A profound (essentially complete) form of hearing impairment (over 80 dB) in which speech is inaudible, even when spoken loudly.
The presence of a moderate form of conductive hearing impairment.
A severe form of conductive hearing impairment.
Abnormal structure of the gastrointestinal tract.
lay_en: Abnormal shape of the digestive system
syn_en: Morphological abnormality of the GI tract
Morphological abnormality of the gastrointestinal tract
Morphological anomaly of the digestive system

terms.en: Functional abnormality of the gastrointestinal tract
terms.def_en: Abnormal functionality of the gastrointestinal tract.
syn_en: Functional abnormality of the GI tract

terms.def_en: Tumor (An abnormal mass of tissue resulting from abnormally dividing cells) of the nasal cavity.

A vascular malformation resulting from a developmental error of venous tissue composed of dysmorphic channels lined by flattened endothelium and exhibiting slow turnover. A venous malformation may present as a blue patch on the skin ranging to a soft blue mass. Venous malformations are easily compressible and usually swell in thewhen venous pressure increases (e.g., when held in a dependent position or when a child cries). They may be relatively localized or quite extensive within an anatomic region.
Impaired conduction of cardiac impulse occurring anywhere along the conduction pathway.
Disturbance in the atrial activation that is caused by transient failure of impulse conduction from the sinoatrial node to the cardiac atria.
Edema in the region of the upper eyelid.

A soft tissue continuity in the A/P axis between two digits that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints, or a soft tissue continuity in the A/P axis between two digits that lies significantly distal to the flexion crease that overlies the metacarpophalangeal or metatarsophalangeal joint of the adjacent digits.
An abnormally decreased potassium concentration in the blood occurring periodically with a return to normal between the episodes.
An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the thoracic aorta.
A concentric abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the descending thoracic aorta that involves the full circumference of the vessel wall
An eccentric abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the descending thoracic aorta that involves only a portion of the circumference of the vessel wall
Absence of the tongue owing to a developmental abnormality.
Abnormal anatomic location of the anterior pituitary gland.
An abnormality of the anus or rectum.
A flat, distinct, discolored area of skin less than 1 cm wide that does not involve any change in the thickness or texture of the skin.
Low blood glucose is accompanied by elevated levels of ketone bodies in the body.
A sudden, audible expulsion of air from the lungs through a partially closed glottis, preceded by inhalation.
A profound delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child.
A discrete abnormal tissue mass that protrudes into the lumen of the small intestine and is attached to the intestinal wall either by a stalk, pedunculus, or a broad base.
Agenesis of canine tooth.
syn_en: Failure of development of eye tooth

terms.def_en: Failure to develop of the small intestine.
A tumor of the skin or mucous membrane with finger-like projections.
Absence of a testis from the scrotum on one side owing to failure of the testis or testes to descend through the inguinal canal to the scrotum.
Fingernail that appears thin when viewed on end.
Excessive fat around the stomach and abdomen.
Failure of the femur to develop.
Distance between the medial and lateral canthi is more than 2 SD below the mean for age (objective); or, apparently reduced length of the palpebral fissures.
Toenail that appears thin when viewed on end.

terms.it: Intensità anomala del segnale RM del tronco encefalico
terms.def_en: A deviation from normal signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brainstem.

terms.it: Lesione focale T2 iperintensa del tronco encefalico
terms.def_en: A lighter than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brainstem. This term refers to a localized hyperintensity affecting a particular region of the brainstem.
A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brainstem. This term refers to a localized hypointensity affecting a particular region of the brainstem.
A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brainstem. This term refers to a diffuse hypointensity affecting the entire brainstem.

terms.en: Abnormal basal ganglia MRI signal intensity
terms.it: Intensità anomala del segnale della risonanza magnetica dei gangli della base
terms.def_en: A deviation from normal signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the basal ganglia.

terms.en: Focal T2 hypointense basal ganglia lesion
terms.def_en: A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the basal ganglia. This term refers to a localized hypointensity affecting a particular region of the basal ganglia.

terms.it: Gangli della base ipointensi in T2
terms.def_en: A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the basal ganglia. This term refers to a diffuse hypointensity affecting all of the basal ganglia.
Increased amount of myelin in the central nervous system.
Abnormal increase in size of the brainstem.
An increased polymorphonuclear cell count in the cerebrospinal fluid.

A structural anomaly of a neuron. Neurons are electrically excitable cells that transmit signals throughout the body. Neurons employ both electrical and chemical components in the transmission of information. Neurons are connected to other neurons at synapses and connected to effector organs or cells at neuroeffector junctions.

Neurodevelopmental delay (NDD) refers to delays in the maturation of the brain and central nervous system; infants and young children with NDD may experience delays in the development of one or more skills including gross motor abilities, fine-motor coordination, language abilities and ability to solve increasingly complex problems.
A deviation from normal of the neurological development of a child, which may include any or all of the aspects of the development of personal, social, gross or fine motor, and cognitive abilities.

A reduced ability to participate in the back-and-forth flow of social interaction appropriate to culture and developmental level, which is normally characterized by an influence of the behavior of one person on the behavior of another person. This results in difficulty interacting with others through emotional, physical, or verbal communication.
A developmental anomaly in which the mastoid process fails to form and is thus found to be congenitally absent.
The presence of atrophy (wasting) of the cerebral white matter.
A sudden attack of dyspnea that occurs while the affected person is at rest.
A sensation of breathlessness in the recumbent position, relieved by sitting or standing.
An increase in size of the anatomic space between the arachnoid membrane and pia mater in the region surrounding the cerebellum.
An increase in size of the anatomic space between the arachnoid membrane and pia mater in the region surrounding the cerebrum.
A deviation from normal size of the placenta.
Respiratory failure in the newborn.

A deviation from normal of the length of the arm span (length from one end of an individual's arms measured at the fingertips to the other when raised parallel to the ground at shoulder height at a one-hundred eighty degree angle)

Decreased length of the arm span (length from one end of an individual's arms measured at the fingertips to the other when raised parallel to the ground at shoulder height at a one-hundred eighty degree angle).

Increased length of the arm span (length from one end of an individual's arms measured at the fingertips to the other when raised parallel to the ground at shoulder height at a one-hundred eighty degree angle).

terms.en: Abnormal upper to lower segment ratio
terms.it: Rapporto anormale tra segmento superiore e inferiore
terms.def_en: A deviation from normal of the relation between the upper and the lower segment of the body, where the lower segment is defined as the length between the top of pubic symphysis to floor, and the upper segment is defined as the top of head to top of pubic symphysis.

terms.en: Reduced upper to lower segment ratio
terms.it: Riduzione del rapporto tra segmento superiore e inferiore
terms.def_en: Decreased ratio between the upper and the lower segment of the body, where the lower segment is defined as the length between the top of pubic symphysis to floor, and the upper segment is defined as the top of head to top of pubic symphysis. Consider the term Disproportionate tall stature (HP:0001519) if tall stature is also present.

terms.en: Increased upper to lower segment ratio
terms.def_en: Elevated ratio between the upper and the lower segment of the body, where the lower segment is defined as the length between the top of pubic symphysis to floor, and the upper segment is defined as the top of head to top of pubic symphysis.
A lacy pattern or iris pigmentation that resembles the spokes of a bicycle wheel.
A structural anomaly of the ciliary body.
A benign or malignant tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the retina.
A glial tumor of the retinal nerve fiber layer arising from a retinal astrocyte.
Hearing loss that occurs acutely and resolves completely.
A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the ear.
A type of hearing impairment affecting primarily the middle frequencies of sound (1000 Hz to 3000 Hz).
A type of nephrogenic rest associated with multiple lesions in the periphery of the renal lobe.
A type of nephrogenic rest usually representing single lesions within the renal lobe, renal sinus, or calyceal walls.
Inflammation of the connective and adipose tissues surrounding the kidney.
Chronic loss of joint motion in a finger due to structural changes in non-bony tissue.
Repeated infections of the urinary bladder.
Repeated episodes of pyelonephritis.
A net-like pattern of increased pigmentation of the oral cavity.
syn_en: Reticulate pigmentation of oral mucous membrane

terms.def_en: Underdevelopment of the heel bone.
An anomaly in the process of intramembranous ossification by which flat bones (cranial bones of the skull, i.e., the frontal, parietal, occipital, and temporal bones, and the clavicles) are formed.
An anomaly of the process of formation of bone in the humerus.
lay_en: Abnormal maturation of long bone in upper arm

terms.en: Absent ossification of thoracic vertebral bodies
terms.def_en: A lack of bone mineralization of one or more body of thoracic vertebra.
A kinked appearance of the brainstem, i.e., an exaggerated flexure.
Multiple areas of darker than expected signal on magnetic resonance imaging emanating from the cerebral white matter that surrounds the cerebral ventricles.
A morphological abnormality of the optic disc, i.e., of the portion of the optic nerve clinically visible on fundoscopic examination.

An elevation in the ratio of the diameter of the cup of the optic disc to the total diameter of the disk. The optic disc has an orange-pink rim with a pale center (the cup) that does not contain neuroretinal tissue. An increase in this ratio therefore may indicate a decrease in the quantity of healthy neuroretinal cells.
A benign or malignant neoplasm arising from the lymphatic vessels.

Infiltration of smooth muscle-like cells in lymph vessels as well as the lung (pleura, alveolar septa, bronchi, pulmonary vessels and lymphatics as well as lymph nodes, especially in posterior mediastinum and retroperitoneum). Focal emphysema can develop because of airway narrowing, and the thoracic duct may be obliterated. Pulmonary lymphangiomyomatosis may lead to multiple small cysts with a hamartomatous proliferation of smooth muscle in their walls.
One-sided weakness of the muscles of facial expression and eye closure.
lay_en: Paralysis of one side of the face
Weakness of one side of the face

terms.def_en: A cranial suture that is in addition to canonical membrane-covered openings in the incompletely ossified skull of the fetus or newborn infant.

Bigonial distance (lower facial width) more than 2 standard deviations below the mean (objective); or an apparently decreased width of the lower jaw (mandible) when viewed from the front (subjective).
Bigonial distance (lower facial width) more than 2 SD above the mean (objective); or an apparently increased width of the lower jaw (mandible) when viewed from the front (subjective).
Inequality of refractive power of the two eyes.
Disruption of the epithelial layer of the cornea with involvement of the underlying stroma.
Transmission of light through the iris as visualized upon slit lamp examination or infrared iris transillumination videography. The light passes through defects in the pigmentation of the iris.
A fleshy, tube-like structure usually located in the midline of the face or just to one side of the midline.
Insertion of the posterior columella superior to the nasal base.
An anomaly of the nasal base, which can be conceived of as an imaginary line between the most lateral points of the external inferior attachments of the alae nasi to the face.
Decreased distance between the attachments of the alae nasi to the face.
lay_en: Decreased width of base of nose

terms.def_en: Increased distance between the attachments of the alae nasi to the face.
lay_en: Increased width of base of nose

terms.def_en: Increased width of the nasal ridge.
syn_en: Increased width of dorsum of nose

terms.def_en: Increased bulk of tissue alongside the nose. The fullness can be caused by both bony and soft tissues.
lay_en: Fullness of tissue around the nose

terms.def_en: Underdevelopment of the breast on one side only.
Underdevelopment of the breast on both sides.
Underdevelopment of part or all of the female external reproductive organs (which include the mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, Bartholin glands, and clitoris).
A predominantly right ventricular variant of isolated noncompaction cardiomyopathy.
A type of cardiomyopathy characterized anatomically by deep trabeculations in the ventricular wall, which define recesses communicating with the main ventricular chamber.
Noncompaction cardiomyopathy that affects both ventricles.
Inflammation of the myocardium.
A loss of the ability to move the vocal fold on both sides.
Decreased strength of the vocal fold on one side.
Decreased strength of the vocal fold on both sides.
An increased number of twists and turns of the retinal blood vessels. This can affect either arteries, veins or both.
A benign or malignant neoplasm that arises from the hair follicles, sebaceous glands, or sweat glands.
An uncontrolled autonomous cell-proliferation originating in a hair follicle, which is an epidermal adnexal structures responsible for hair growth.
A benign tumor originating from the outer root sheath of the hair follicle.
Presence of a unitary trichilemmoma, a benign tumor originating from the outer root sheath of the hair follicle.
Presence of multiple trichilemmomata, a benign tumor originating from the outer root sheath of the hair follicle.

Epilepsia partialis continua (also called Kojevnikov's or Kozhevnikov's epilepsia) is a type of focal motor status epilepticus characterized by repeated stereotyped simple motor manifestations such as jerks, typically of a limb or the face, recurring every few seconds or minutes for extended periods (days or years).
The narrowing or partial blockage of a portion of the small intestine.
Bleeding from the small intestine.

Abnormal small intestinal contractions, such as spasms and intestinal paralysis related to the loss of the ability of the gut to coordinate muscular activity because of endogenous or exogenous causes.
A narrowing of a segment of colon whereby bowel continuity is maintained.
Hepatic fibrosis that reaches from a portal area to another portal area.
Hypospadias with location of the urethral meatus in the scrotum.
Hypospadias with location of the urethral meatus in the middle of the inferior shaft of the penis.
Increased pigmentation (skin color) of the scrotum.
Anomaly of the folded ridges (wrinkles) of skin of the scrotum.
Increased number or density of the folded ridges (wrinkles) of skin of the scrotum.
Decreased number or density of the folded ridges (wrinkles) of skin of the scrotum.
A white patch or plaque occurring on the surface of the esophageal mucous membranes that cannot be rubbed off and cannot be characterized clinically as any other disease.
Formation of excess connective tissue in the testicle.
A gonad that contains both ovarian follicles and testicular tubular elements.
Any structural anomaly of a reproductive cell.
syn_en: Abnormal shape of a reproductive cell

terms.def_en: A structural anomaly of a male reproductive cell.
A structural anomaly of sperm.

terms.it: Morfologia anomala della testa degli spermatozoi
terms.def_en: A structural abnormality of the sperm head.
A structural abnormality of the sperm neck.
A structural abnormality of the sperm mid-piece.
A structural abnormality of the sperm tail.
Spermatozoa with very small cranial ends devoid of any nuclear material, that is, lacking a typical sperm head.

A condition which is considered to be due to the subsequent atrophy and disappearance in fetal life of an initially normal testis. In the presence of spermatic cord structures is evidence of the presence of the testis in early intrauterine life. When associated with a blind-ending spermatic cord, this entity is named as his absence of a testis in an otherwise normal 46XY male is usually unilateral and is assumed to be a consequence of intrauterine or perinatal torsion or infarction.

A varicocele is a widening of the veins along the spermatic cord, leading to enlarged, twisted veins in the scrotum, and manifested clinically by a painless testicle lump, scrotal swelling, or bulge in the scrotum.
A structural anomaly of the secretory duct of the testicle that carries spermatozoa from the epididymis to the prostatic urethra where it terminates to form ejaculatory duct.
Aplasia (congenital absence) of the vas deferens.
syn_en: Congenital absence of the vas deferens

terms.def_en: An abnormal functionality of the male genital system.
Abnormality in the process of ejection of semen (usually carrying sperm) from the male reproductive tract.
The emission of semen and seminal fluid during the act of preparation for sexual intercourse, i.e. before there is penetration, or shortly after penetration.
The emission of semen and seminal fluid into the bladder instead of through the penis during orgasm.
Difficulty of a male in achieving orgasm.
Inability to ejaculate.
An anomaly of the labia minora, the folds of skin between the outer labia.
lay_en: Abnormality of the inner vaginal lips

terms.def_en: An anomaly of the outer labia.
Overgrowth of the outer labia.
A fluid filled sac located in the Fallopian tube.
A twisting of the Fallopian tube. Sudden onset with sharp, colicky pelvic pain associated with nausea, vomiting, bowel, and bladder symptoms is the usual presentation.
The presence of a supernumerary Fallopian tube.
An abdominal mass formed by bleeding into a follicular ovarian cyst or corpus luteum cyst.
A cystic tumor of the ovary, containing thin, clear, yellow serous fluid and varying amounts of solid tissue.
An anomaly of the neck of the uterus (lower part of the uterus), called the uterine cervix.
Abnormal growth of endometrial cells (which are normally limited to the uterus) within the cervix.
Posterior malposition of the anus.
Hair on the neck extends less inferiorly than usual.
lay_en: High hairline at back of head

terms.def_en: Hypertrophy of one or more muscles innervated by the facial nerve (the seventh cranial nerve).
Muscle hypertrophy affecting the muscles of the neck.
Muscle hypertrophy affecting the paraspinal muscles.
Muscle hypertrophy affecting the scapular muscles.

An anomaly identified by motor evoked potentials (MEPs). MEPs are measured following single-pulse or repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation and can be used for the assessment of the excitability of the motor cortex and the integrity of conduction along the central and peripheral motor pathways.
An anomaly identified by motor evoked potentials (MEPs) in the arm.
syn_en: Abnormal motor evoked potentials in the upper limb

terms.def_en: An anomaly identified by motor evoked potentials (MEPs) in the leg.
syn_en: Abnormal motor evoked potentials in the lower limb

terms.def_en: Difficulty releasing one's grip associated with prolonged first handgrip relaxation times.
Slowed relaxation of muscles in the face.
Slowed relaxation of muscles in the jaw.
Slowed relaxation of muscles in the leg.
Slowed relaxation of muscles in the arm.
An involuntary and painless delay in the relaxation of skeletal muscle following contraction or electrical stimulation that is induced by exposure to cold.

Euryblepharon is a congenital eyelid anomaly characterized by horizontal enlargement of the palpebral fissure. The eyelid is shortened vertically compared with the horizontal dimension, with associated lateral canthal malpositioning and lateral ectropion abnormally wide lid opening.

Congenital anophthalmos is a rare ocular anomaly in which histologically detectable eyeball structures are absent due to poor development of the primary optic nerve vesicle. However, with appropriate imaging or intraoperatively, rudimentary remains of this structure can usually be detected. Therefore, the term clinical congenital anophthalmos seems more appropriate and denotes a phenotypic range between microphthalmos and anophthalmos.
A pathological narrowing of the ileum that is caused by the development of a ring of scar tissue that constricts the ileal lumen.

A failure of an embryo to progress through the early stages of preimplantation development (typically from fertilization, i.e., 1-cell zygote, to blastocyst on day 5-6), and is used clinically when embryos fail to reach transferable stages in assisted reproductive technologies (ARTs) such in vitro fertilization (IVF). Arrested embryo development is characterized by downregulation of metabolic activity and cessation of cell division. In order for an embryo to be characterized as non-viable, i.e., arrested, it should present with a lack of cleaving activity and fail to show a sign of mitotic cellular division for at least 24 hours. One can observe failure of a zygote to cleave, cleavage stage arrest either on day 2 or day 3 when the embryo is expected to be between the 2 and 8-cell stage, failure to compact to morula, or failure to form a blastocyst.
The concentration of guanidinoacetic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is outside the limits of normal.
The concentration of guanidinoacetic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is below the lower limit of normal.
A coloboma of the ciliary body.

A disturbance in the processes by which emotional responses are initiated, modulated, sustained, or terminated in a contextually appropriate manner. Abnormal affect regulation involves maladaptive patterns in the generation, intensity, or control of affective experience and expression, leading to inconsistent, excessive, or insufficient modulation of emotion relative to situational demands.
Slough is a type of necrotic skin lesion that is characterized as being yellow, tan, green or brown in color and may be moist, loose and stringy in appearance.
Abnormal tingling, burning, or itching sensation localized to the site of an animal bite, typically occurring after the wound has healed.
Amyloid deposition categorized according to the anatomical site of deposition.

terms.en: Amyloid deposition by type of amyloid
terms.def_en: Amyloid deposition categorized according to the category of pathological amyloid fiber being deposited.
Deposition of misfolded transthyretin (TTR) protein in tissue.
Accumulation of misfolded transthyretin protein in brain tissue.
The concentration of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above or below the limits of normal.
The concentration of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is below the lower limit of normal.

A condition where the hip joint is limited in its range of motion due to the shortening of muscles that externally rotate the hip, causing the leg and foot to point outward when standing or walking. The knee is turned past neutral in the direction moving away from the midline, where the neutral position for the hip is with knee pointing directly anteriorly.
